dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-.technical:
This fact gathers series results the dark-matter paper relies on. The visible matter is the derived Standard Model generation. The three ladder pairs of the Fock structure of a conformal spinor form a Witt decomposition of the complexified conformal ambient $V_{\C}$: two of the pairs are realised by real hyperbolic planes of $\R^{2,4}$, the third only in $V_{\C}$.

The one-handed listing choice on this structure is the particle-antiparticle orientation, under Hypothesis (S) of the Standard-Model paper, which is carried here as a premise; the condensate's alignment is the one computed in the families paper. The only new step is to read the listing choice as the descent's flag, the Witt flag.
dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-.lay: The dark-matter paper borrows several earlier results of the series. The ordinary matter we see is one generation of the Standard Model as derived earlier. A basic spinor state of the conformal algebra carries three paired ladder operations; two of the pairs can be seen in real geometry and the third only once complex numbers are allowed. Choosing which member of each pair counts as particle rather than antiparticle is a single orientation choice, resting on the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S), which is carried here, and the dark-matter paper reads that choice as a flag on the structure.

__notes__.note.families.setting-koide-geometry:
The second-order breaking is a perturbation of the democratic vacuum, and the question this section makes precise is: which function of the physical masses is the natural \emph{linear} coordinate on face space? For a vector $v$ with non-negative components and $u = (1,1,1)/\sqrt{3}$,
\[
Q_{v} \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\sum_{k} v_{k}^{2}}{\bigl(\sum_{k} v_{k}\bigr)^{2}} \;=\; \frac{1}{3\cos^{2}\theta},
\]
with $\theta$ the angle of $v$ to the democratic direction. The method is the series' own: pre-registered refutation conditions, the natural conjecture first, the data deciding. Throughout, the charged-lepton pole masses are $m_{e} = 0.51099895$, $m_{\mu} = 105.6583755$, $m_{\tau} = 1776.93 \pm 0.09$ MeV \cite{PDG2024}. The charged leptons are the content of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s} that exists under Hypothesis (S) and only under it; everything this section and the next say about them carries (S) as a premise, and the levels of the results say so once more.
__notes__.note.lepton.what-was-assumed: Everything in Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space} rests on (C), and (C) is not a theorem. What makes it plausible is Fact \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder}'s form, $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j}Z^{j}$, which on bare conformal spinors (bare twistors) is the action of $A$ on a slot vector once; (C) extends that form to excited conformal spinors, and the extension is the premise. Nothing in (C) makes a slot a fermionic mode, and in $\Con$ every pair belongs to the conformal spinor in the slot; so (C) does not pay the second cost T12 lists for (S), a composite state space that does not record which pairs belong to which slot. It pays nothing for the composite because it says nothing about the composite.
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-machine-verification: Every computational identity asserted here is verified in exact arithmetic by the deposited script \cite{ButlerVerifyT12L}, \texttt{verify\_T12\_lepton.py}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: seventeen checks, all passing, no floating point. They are: the hypercharge generator built as an exact matrix on each $\Con_{k}$ with weight $3 - 2k$, and the lattice residues (Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space}(1), (4)); the $SU(3)$ contents of the halves and the dual weights $-(3-2k) = 3 - 2(3-k)$ (Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space}(2), (3)); the $K$-weights $1 - k$, the dual $K$-weights $k - 1$, their disagreement at matching content, and the biconditional of Proposition \claimref{lepton.self-conjugacy-forces-determinant-one-group} on five subgroups $G$ encoded by their trivial central characters, the $k = 0$ test alone passing on $SU(2) \times U(3)$ while $k = 1$ decides; the twist by $(\det A)^{m}$, its weights under $\mathsf{y}$ and $K$, the values $Y_{L} = -\tfrac52, \tfrac32$ at $m = \mp 2$, and the closure of the shifted weight multiset under negation only at $m = 0$; the twelve components of the five-mode ledger with their duals, exactly one (the vacuum) self-dual and none of the constituents' duals present (Observation \claimref{lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-thirteenth}); the ranks of the $SU(2)$-orbits of single-row states under the cell action ($k + 1$ for $k = 1, 2, 3$, computed in the wedge basis of $\Lambda^{k}\C^{6}$) and under the unit action ($2$), the cell weights $k$, and the full spans as ranks, $6, 9, 4$ against $6, 6, 2$ (Proposition \claimref{lepton.unit-action-cell-action}); the $(2,1)$ at weight $-3$ inside $(2,3) \otimes (3,\bar{3})$ as a dimension identity (Remark \claimref{note.lepton.operator-route-why-it-not-one}); and the two anomaly lists, $(0, 0, 0, 0)$ and $(\tfrac23, 0, 0, -\tfrac49)$, with the two lists conjugate in their free parts (Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors}). What the script does not check: the Facts, verified in their own papers' scripts; and the readings of Remark \claimref{note.lepton.what-was-assumed}, Observation \claimref{lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-thirteenth} and Remark \claimref{note.lepton.what-kind-fact-relative-handedness}, which are not computations.
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-constituent-space-hy:
The tensor ledger of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton} treats the six cells as independent fermionic modes: a state is an occupation pattern of cells, and a mixing of slots acts on each occupied cell separately. It is worth saying what this ledger is in the language of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations}: $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes W) = \Lambda^{\bullet}(W_{1} \oplus W_{2}) \cong \Sp_{1} \otimes \Sp_{2}$, the tensor product of the Dirac modules of the two twistors, each twistor excited by its own pair operators. Read on two twistors, Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations} produces the ledger, not something else. A lepton doublet, $(2,1)$ of weight $-3$, needs a space in which the slot vector appears once and the pair state carries the full system; the ledger has no such space (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton}), and the natural candidate, $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$ with the slot mixing acting on the slot alone, is not produced by the two theorems one would like to produce it. Fact \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} is proved for bare twistors, from their spinor parts, and says nothing about how a mixing acts on an excited twistor; Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations} concerns one twistor and carries no slot index. The step between them is a premise, and the note states it as one.

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hypothesis (C), the constituent hypothesis.} A constituent of the composite is a Dirac state in a slot, a twistor or its partner with any of its pairs excited: its state space is
\[
\Con := \C^{2} \otimes \Sp = \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W,
\]
sixteen-dimensional, with a pair $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acting as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(B)$: $A$ acts on the slot vector once, and on nothing else; $B$ acts on the Dirac state. The chirality of a constituent is that of the Dirac spinor it holds (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations}) up to one overall sign $\epsilon = \pm 1$ for the slotted sector relative to the free sector: $\epsilon = +1$ means a slot leaves the half alone, $\epsilon = -1$ that it reverses it. (C) leaves $\epsilon$ open; Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors} fixes $\epsilon = -1$. Write $\Con_{k} := \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$.
\end{quote}

Hypothesis (C) with $\epsilon = -1$ is the one-constituent row $j = 1$ of T12's Hypothesis (S), the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$: there the $(1, k)$ component is $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ with exactly this action, and (S)'s chirality, the parity of $j + k$, is on that row the parity of $1 + k$, the reversed half, which is $\epsilon = -1$. With $\epsilon = +1$ the two would contradict each other on the chirality clause, which is why the bit is left open in (C) and fixed by an argument rather than stipulated. So fixed, (C) is weaker than (S) in the plain sense that (S) implies it: (C) says nothing about states with two slot modes, nothing about the statistics of pairs of constituents, and nothing about a composite state space at all. The note claims no minimality for (C) over any class of hypotheses; what it shows is that (C) is enough for the lepton (Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space}) and exactly where any space holding one must depart from the ledger (Proposition \claimref{lepton.unit-action-cell-action}).

The automorphism group of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-automorphism-group-section-hypercharge-generator} acts on $\Con$ through its canonical section: an automorphism is a $K$-coset of pairs, the coset's representative with $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ is unique, and that representative acts as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(B)$. the section “The group on the constituents, and the one remaining choice” shows that among the actions of the automorphism group on $\Con$ this is the only one compatible with conjugation.
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-group-constituents-o: What remains is one binary choice. The doublets are the $\CSm{}$ constituents, $\C^{2} \otimes \CSm{}$; the free sector $\Sp$ of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-free-sector-anomaly-conditions} has its own halves; and the anomaly conditions require every fermion to be listed in one handedness. Which half of the free sector is listed with the $\CSm{}$ half of the slot sector is not decided by Hypothesis (C).
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-position-series: This note is a companion to T12 of the series and belongs with its Section 5. \emph{It relies on:} the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the hierarchy, the ladder theorem, the automorphism group and its section, the hypercharge generator, the tensor ledger and its no-lepton clause, the free sector and the anomaly Fact (Facts \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} to \claimref{lepton.imported-free-sector-anomaly-conditions}); the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the Fock model and the pure-spinor theorem behind Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations}; and the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} for the orientation bit that Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors} identifies. \emph{Papers that would rely on it:} T12 itself, if (C) is adopted in place of (S), and its companion note on the transport tower, which restates (S) as a hypothesis about the tower and prices (S) at Tier C; and through T12 the families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13} and the neutrino paper T15 \cite{ButlerT15}, whose imports of the content would then rest on (C) rather than on (S).
__notes__.note.lepton.operator-route-why-it-not-on: The ledger's states contain no $(2,1)$, but its operators do: $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda^{4}, \Lambda^{1}) = \Lambda^{1} \otimes (\Lambda^{4})^{*} \supseteq (2,3) \otimes (3,\bar{3})$, and $2 \otimes 3 = 2 \oplus 4$, $3 \otimes \bar{3} = 1 \oplus 8$ \cite[\S 11.2, \S 13.2]{FultonHarris1991}, so a $(2,1)$ of weight $1 - 4 = -3$ sits among the operators that annihilate four cells and create one; likewise in $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda^{5}, \Lambda^{2})$. One might hope to read T12's premise that elementary fermions are generators, not states, as admitting such an operator as the lepton. The note has no argument that closes this route, and does not claim one: what it observes is that the operator is a composite of five cell operators, that $\operatorname{End}(\Lambda^{\bullet})$, of dimension $64^{2}$, contains a great many representations of the group, and that the note knows no principle that would select this one among them and call it elementary. The route inside the ledger is closed at the level of states by Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton}; at the level of operators it is not closed but unresolved, for want of a selection principle, and the script records the representation-theoretic fact that the $(2,1)_{-1/2}$ is there.
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-what-changes-t12-wha:
The answer to the question the note was asked is no: inside the two-level hierarchy as T12 defines it, the tensor ledger, there is no lepton doublet at the level of states, by Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton}; at the level of operators the question is unresolved rather than closed (Remark \claimref{note.lepton.operator-route-why-it-not-one}); and no theorem of the series extends the ladder's action from bare twistors to excited ones. What the note adds is the exact shape of a hypothesis that does supply the lepton, and the exact point at which it departs from the ledger. Hypothesis (C), with its bit fixed by Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors}, is (S) restricted to one constituent: if T12 were to adopt (C) in place of (S), the existence and hypercharge of the lepton (Proposition 5.3(2), equation (4)), the common chirality of the doublets (Theorem 5.5(1)) and the two twistor-level doublets as a doublet and its antiparticle (Proposition 5.6, last clause) would rest on (C), a weaker premise, and the second cost T12 lists for (S), a composite state space that does not record which pairs belong to which slot, would not be paid, because (C) has no composite state space. The relative handedness of the two sectors would remain, under (C), a consistency condition fixed by the anomalies (Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors}), which is what it already is in T12 Theorem 5.5(3).

Two results of this note hold under (C) and (S) alike. Proposition \claimref{lepton.self-conjugacy-forces-determinant-one-group} and Observation \claimref{lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-thirteenth} address the first cost T12 listed for (S), the thirteenth generator: under either hypothesis, in the untwisted action, the constituent spectrum is self-conjugate only for the determinant-one group, so the automorphism rule, read with conjugation, gives twelve generators, not thirteen, at the level of the CPT premise the Observation prints. T12 now settles the point differently at proposition level \cite[Prop.~5.8(3), Prop.~10.7]{ButlerT12}: in the untwisted action the anomaly conditions exclude the generator, but the state space carries the twisted action, in which it is anomaly-free, the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, broken at the intermediate scale with the rest of the Pati-Salam algebra; so it is not a cost of (S) either way. That proposition's untwisted clause assumes (S) and computes over the five-mode charges; under (C) the singlets are the conjugated odd free states, so the charge list differs and the three linear sums are $2\alpha + 3\beta$, $4\alpha + 6\beta$ and $8\alpha + 12\beta$, with the same vanishing direction and the same conclusion. And Proposition \claimref{lepton.unit-action-cell-action} locates the departure from the ledger exactly: on twistors with two or more pairs excited, and nowhere else.

What (S) is still needed for, and (C) does not give: the composite's state space as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$, hence $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ as the Bogoliubov group of five modes and the derived $3/8$ (T12 Proposition 5.8(2), Remark 5.9). Under (C), $Q \oplus L = \Con_{1} \oplus \Con_{3}$ is the $j = 1$ part of the even half of that Fock space and $\Con_{0} \oplus \Con_{2}$ the $j = 1$ part of the odd half, and the free sector is the row $j = 0$; the row $j = 2$ is (S)'s alone. Successor problem (6) of T12 stands. It is sharpened, not narrowed: of its five outcomes this note closes the one that would derive the lepton inside the two-level hierarchy, and prices two of the others, the lepton needing at least (C) and $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ needing all of (S).
__notes__.note.lepton.what-kind-fact-relative-hand: Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors} is a consistency condition, not a kinematic derivation: gauging $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ on the constituents together with the free sector is possible only for the listing in (1). __notes__.note.neutrino.abstract: We identify the right-handed neutrino as the hypercharge-zero state of the framework's derived content, the empty twistor at grade zero, and prove that anomaly cancellation could not have fixed its hypercharge: with a fourth singlet free and $Y_{Q} \neq 0$, the anomaly-free spectra are exactly the span of $Y$ and $B - L$. The cosmological term of the deformed bracket cannot supply the neutrino mass (the sixteenth refutation: it lies below the flat term by $\Lambda l^{2}/6$ at extent $l$). Gauge invariance makes the Majorana bilinear of the total singlet the one mass term needing no condensate, a textbook fact about which the framework's own bracket, computed only on slot states, says nothing; with its scale a premise, the seesaw follows. Indifference makes the Majorana matrix $S_{3}$-invariant, hence $\alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J$ ($\J$ the all-ones matrix), aligned with the democratic Dirac matrix, and the light matrix is rank one at leading order with $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{3}$: normal ordering, and, as consequences of $m_{1} \approx 0$ and real phases, the sum at the oscillation floor $\mnu \approx 0.059$ eV and $m_{\beta\beta}$ at $1.5$ or $3.7$ meV. That sum is at the centre of the sharpest tension in cosmology, and the framework, which predicts $w = -1$, cannot relax the bound in the standard way: one joint prediction. Leptogenesis is suppressed under a reheating premise at the cost of a registered stance, $\delta_{CP} \in \{0, \pi\}$. Tier B/C with every premise named, a prediction table, and exact machine verification.
__notes__.note.neutrino.setting-introduction:
The neutrino was the largest gap in the framework's derived content. This paper addresses it using only parts already present in the series, and ends by registering the framework's most precise and most exposed prediction: this is, by design and by declaration, the series' fastest-falsifiable paper, published while the prediction is still open.

The chain. The Standard-Model paper T12's derived content always contained a fourth colour singlet: the single-twistor sector carries \emph{two} singlets, at grades zero and three of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{3}$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$), and the observed comparison column always had two. The right-handed neutrino is the grade-zero state, the \emph{empty twistor}, the pair system with no rung occupied, whose hypercharge the weight rule computes as zero. Anomaly cancellation could not have fixed it: with a fourth singlet of free hypercharge and $Y_{Q} \neq 0$ the anomaly-free spectra are exactly the two-dimensional span of the derived spectrum and $B - L$, a fact we prove in closed form, so the zero is a computation of the content derivation and not a consistency condition, and the Standard Model's ambivalence about $\nu_{R}$ is the ambivalence of a bottom-up construction that has only anomalies to go on. The natural small-mass mechanism is refuted first (the sixteenth refutation): the cosmological term of the mass paper T11's deformed bracket lies below the flat term by $\Lambda l^{2}/6$ for a composite of extent $l$, and can dominate only at horizon size. Gauge invariance then singles out the Majorana bilinear of the total singlet as the one fermion mass term that carries no charge and needs no condensate, an elementary fact proved outright and using nothing from the framework; whether the framework's own mass bracket, which T12 computes only on slot states and about which it says nothing for slot-free states, realises that term, and at what scale $M$, is a premise this paper names rather than derives, and with it the light masses follow by block inversion. Indifference makes the Majorana matrix $S_{3}$-invariant, which we show means $\alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J$ with $\J$ the all-ones matrix and, in the Gram-square reading, $\alpha = 0$ at leading order: the democratic vector is an eigenvector, and the seesaw of the democratic Dirac matrix is rank one at leading order and scalar on the democratic block, $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{3}$, whatever $\alpha$ is. Three numbers follow: the ordering is normal (inverted excluded by rank plus small corrections, not by fit); the sum is bounded below by the oscillation floor and is at it, $\mnu \approx 0.059$ eV, if the second stage of the breaking is hierarchical; and the effective double-beta mass is one of two values, $1.5$ or $3.7$ meV, if the breaking is real. These are consequences of $m_{1} \approx 0$ and real phases, shared with any model having those two features; what the framework adds is the structure that produces them. The sum is at the exact centre of the sharpest tension in current cosmology, and the framework cannot use the community's standard way of relaxing the bound (a varying dark-energy equation of state) because it predicts $w = -1$: the two stances are one joint prediction. Finally, the heavy states that make the masses are the textbook mechanism of leptogenesis, and that mechanism is suppressed in three steps (alignment, a reheating premise at the lower heavy scale, phases), at the cost of a fifth registered stance: $\delta_{CP} \in \{0, \pi\}$.
__notes__.note.neutrino.setting-prior-art: The prior work, acknowledged once. The seesaw mechanism is classic \cite{Minkowski1977, GRS1979, Yanagida1980, MohapatraSenjanovic1980}; what the framework adds is the identification of the state that carries it, a proof of which parts of the mechanism are forced by gauge invariance and which are premises, and an $S_{3}$-invariant texture with consequences. That anomaly cancellation with a right-handed neutrino leaves hypercharge undetermined up to $B - L$ is textbook, and T12 already exhibits the family and runs it at four values; we prove in-paper that the family is the whole solution set, because the argument is short and the point carries the paper's claim that the zero is computed, not forced. The oscillation splittings and angles are the global fits' \cite{PDG2024, NuFIT2024}; the cosmological bounds and their tensions \cite{DESI2025, HouWangZhaoZhang2026}, the long-baseline record \cite{T2KNOvA2025}, and the double-beta limits and projections \cite{KamLANDZen2023, LEGEND2021} are the experimental record's, refreshed at submission and tracked in the prediction table of the section “The predictions”. Democratic mass matrices are the flavour literature's \cite{HHW1978}, inherited through the families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13}. The leptogenesis results of the section “The predictions” (the decay-asymmetry interference formula, the washout parameter and equilibrium mass, the resonant enhancement of a degenerate pair, and the asymmetry a successful mechanism needs) is standard and is imported at that level \cite{FukugitaYanagida1986, DavidsonNardiNir2008, PilaftsisUnderwood2004}. What this paper claims as new is the identification of $\nu_{R}$ as the empty twistor, the sixteenth refutation at its exact scope, the $S_{3}$-invariance lemma and the exact rank-one seesaw it yields with the breaking relation that follows, the three numbers with their premises named, the joint prediction with the dark-energy stance, and the three-step suppression of leptogenesis with its falsifiable phase corollary.
__notes__.note.neutrino.setting-contribution: (1) The empty twistor: $\nu_{R}$ identified, its hypercharge computed, and the proof that anomalies could not have computed it (the section “The empty twistor”). (2) The sixteenth refutation at its scope, the gauge-invariance computation with its premise named, the $S_{3}$ lemma, the exact rank-one seesaw and the breaking relation: ordering, the sum, the double-beta values (the section “The seesaw, and its premises”). (3) The joint prediction with $w = -1$, and leptogenesis suppressed, with the fifth stance (the section “The predictions”). (4) The prediction table: what decides each stance, and when (the section “The predictions”). __notes__.note.neutrino.setting-position-series:
This paper is T15 of the series. \emph{It relies on six predecessors:} the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the transport principle and the series' method; the dark-energy paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} for the registered $w = -1$ with its condition (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}); the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} for the exact join, with its massless locus in place of a floor, and the bracket's dimensions (Fact \claimref{mass.exact-join}); the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the derived content, the hypercharge per grade, the mass bracket's quantum numbers, the unification scale on its conditional branch and the unconditional pairwise meetings (\cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT12}, at that paper's assembly level, cited inline in Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.valuation-m-both-ends-hypothesis-u}), the Pati-Salam chain's scales and the requirement it places on the neutrino sector (\cite[Props.~10.10, 11.2]{ButlerT12}, at record level, inline in the same remark), and Hypothesis (S), on which this paper's doublet content depends and which it records as open (Facts \claimref{neutrino.imported-derived-content-singlets}, \claimref{neutrino.imported-mass-bracket-quantum-numbers}; status now, 7 November 2026: the store derives (S) from a weaker postulate, Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}, in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}); the families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13} for the indifference instrument, the faces, the democratic alignment and its registered open problem (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-indifference-faces-democratic-alignment-rank}, Observation 7.1 there); and the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} for the ceiling range under Hypothesis (U), the arrow as a declared stance with Premise P4, the flag covariance, and the reheating assumption (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-ceiling-under-hypothesis-u-arrow}).

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} cites the sixteenth refutation (Proposition \claimref{neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-proves-what}(1), whose scope is the cosmological term of the deformed bracket, not a floor) and the flag covariance of the $\nu_{R}$ identification, $\nu_{R}$ being the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero of T12's listing (Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}); its seeding appendix's reheating is read here at the lower heavy scale (Premise (R)), about two to five orders below the top of the range across which that appendix quotes its numbers, so the numbers quoted at the top of that range do not apply on this paper's branch; the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} refers the massless locus of its join to this paper; the families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13} refers to this paper the neutrino exemption from its Koide relation, whose mechanism (seesaw-composed masses) holds under Premise (M); the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers, carries the sixteenth refutation in its refutation table at the scope of Proposition \claimref{neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-proves-what}(1), numbers the framework's stances (the joint prediction fourth, the phase fifth), and maintains the series-wide table of falsifiable claims of which the section “The predictions” is the neutrino sector's entry; what it takes from this paper is the refutation at that scope (the cosmological term, not a floor), the seesaw as premised under (M) rather than derived, the empty twistor at grade zero, the branch of Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3}, and Premises (M), (H), (R) with the results that depend on each.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-intermediate:
Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run} leaves two ways for the running between the weak and structural scales to differ from that of the derived content. the section “The partner sector quantified” took the first, partner-like content. The ten Majorana generators of the module are
\[
\gamma_{2a-2} = w_{a} + v_{a}, \qquad \gamma_{2a-1} = I_{4}(v_{a} - w_{a}), \qquad a = 1, \ldots, 5,
\]
six pair Majoranas $\gamma_{0}, \ldots, \gamma_{5}$ and four slot Majoranas $\gamma_{6}, \ldots, \gamma_{9}$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors). __notes__.note.rungs.setting-fallback-s-tier-c-pre:
If the missing statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.where-leaves-r} is not supplied, the series' own rule for a structural premise that resists derivation is to register it at Tier C, with its predictions and its kill conditions priced. The registration, in the form T12 uses for its stances:

\begin{quote}
\emph{Registered premise (S), equivalently (R).} The internal state space of the minimal massive composite is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$, the two-rung transport of the twistor completion, with the gauge group below the intermediate scale acting through Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) on its determinant-one part (the thirteenth generator, anomaly-free in the action the state space carries, being broken at that scale, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}) and chirality the parity of the mode number.
\end{quote}

\noindent\emph{What it predicts.} (i) Exactly one generation per composite, the sixteen of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$: quark and lepton doublets, four singlets, the fourth at hypercharge zero (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); that the composite carries no further chiral state is the registration's own reading of "the state space is this Fock space", not a clause of Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}. (ii) The $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice of T12 Theorem 4.2; this is unconditional in T12 and is not a test of (S), and is listed because (S) must respect it and does (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}). (iii) Unification into $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ with $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$ at the unification scale, hence, with the desert dead (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}), a change in the running between the weak and unification scales: partner-like content, or an intermediate symmetry such as T12's Pati-Salam route, on which $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ is an input. (iv) Baryon and lepton number violation by the thirty-two generators of $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ outside $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ (Proposition \claimref{rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra}): twelve that move an excitation between a rung and a pair (the leptoquark directions of $\uu(5)$), and twenty that create or annihilate two modes at once.

\noindent\emph{What kills it.} (a) A confirmed chiral fermion outside the sixteen per generation, or a fourth colour singlet with nonzero hypercharge (the anomaly conditions would then admit a family, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}). (b) A fractionally charged colour singlet, off the lattice; this kills the exclusion stance of T12 Theorem 4.2 whether or not (S) holds, so it is a kill shared with T12, not one that discriminates (S). (c) A measured $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ at a scale where the three couplings can be shown, with the observed spectrum plus any partner content compatible with the sixteen, not to meet: the two-loop run with thresholds, T12 successor problem (2). (d) A proton lifetime bound incompatible with any $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ breaking scale allowed by (iii); the framework does not yet fix that scale, so this condition is priced as inherited from the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ literature rather than sharpened. (e) Internally: a proof that the composite's internal algebra closes on the three pair modes alone, with the slots as labels (the tensor ledger reading of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}), which would refute (R) directly and leave (S) without its only structural reading.

\noindent\emph{Level.} A structural premise with priced kill conditions is Tier C by the series' definition; T12 is declared Tier B, and if (S) is registered rather than derived the sections that rest on it (T12 Proposition 5.3(2), Theorem 5.5(1), the consistency clause of (3), the last clause of Proposition 5.6, Proposition 5.8, Remark 5.9, and Proposition 6.1's values $3/8$ and $3/4$, which are taken over a generation containing the lepton; without the lepton the ratio is $9/26$) carry Tier C and the abstract should say so. The sections that do not rest on it, the algebra, the global form, the converse, the quark doublet, the singlet spectrum as a computation on the single-twistor Fock space, the uniqueness arithmetic given a charge list, the trace ratios as arithmetic over any tabulated content with $9/10$ over the fibre, and the run, stay at Tier B.

__notes__.note.rungs.where-leaves-r: Three things are now exact that were not. The five-mode ledger is the tower's two-rung module, so (S) is a statement about the tower. The ladder group is the rung-mixing group on the one-constituent sector. And the mass bracket is the frozen point's grip on the slot-antisymmetric bivector, at $\Lambda = 0$, which is a null vector of the ambient space that invites the next rung. What is missing is a single mechanism: why a conformal spinor constituent (a twistor) occupies a rung. The count is the obstacle. Null momenta invite one rung in total (Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}); the bivectors of two conformal spinors invite one more, together (Proposition \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}); neither gives one rung per constituent, and the second gives the right vector space with a $U(2)$ that mixes chirality. The precise form of the missing statement is this: the composite's internal algebra is generated by $3 + n$ anticommuting mode pairs, the three pairs of $W$ shared and one new pair per constituent. Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung} then supplies everything else, the module, the grading and the groups. Why a conformal spinor constituent should contribute exactly one mode to the composite, rather than none (the tensor ledger of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}, where the slots are labels and the pairs are shared) or three (a copy of $W$ per constituent, the product state that Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector} excludes), is the question, and the note has no argument for it. It belongs to the tower paper, where the mode count is a theorem about the real Witt index and where a statement about what a conformal spinor constituent contributes to a composite's algebra would have to be made.
__notes__.note.rungs.what-identifies-what-it-does-: Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one} is exact, and it is the one place where the tower and the Standard-Model paper's objects are literally the same thing: the ladder's $U(n)$, derived from momentum and helicity preservation, and the tower's rung-mixing group, derived from the completion, agree on $\C^{n} \otimes \CS$, $\CS$ the conformal spinor space (twistor space). But the identification is on that sector only. The ladder theorem says nothing about the other sectors ($j \neq 1$, or $k$ odd), and the tower says nothing about momentum. To say that the composite's state space is the whole module is a hypothesis, stated next.
__notes__.note.rungs.setting-part-does-not-close-n: Proposition \claimref{rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two} replaces one hypothesis by another of the same strength, and the gain is only that (R) is a sentence about the tower, an object the series has theorems about, rather than a sentence about slot statistics, which it does not. A derivation of (R) would need a mechanism producing one rung per twistor. Three candidates present themselves, and none works as stated.
__notes__.note.standard-model.reading-automorphism: Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}'s rule takes the automorphisms of $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ that preserve the partition. Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are} applies it to the canonical anticommutation relations of the five-mode state space and preserves the slot/pair split there without preserving the mode number. The reading is canonical, since Pati-Salam is exactly the stabiliser of the rung parity, but it is a reading: the rule as stated for the tensor hierarchy does not select it, and the paper registers it as such. Pati-Salam unification, with lepton number as a fourth colour, is Pati and Salam's \cite{PatiSalam1974}. What the framework adds is the reason for this group: it is what the composite's own slot/pair split preserves, with the slot mixing as the weak $\su(2)$ and the full or empty pair system as the fourth colour.
__notes__.note.standard-model.second-doublet-coupl: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.bidoublet-complex} says that $m_{t} \ne m_{b}$ needs a second independent doublet coupling and that a complex bidoublet, carrying two electroweak doublets, supplies one. Read with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.second-doublet-of-one-family-coupling-gives-no-quark-mixing}, "independent" must mean a second family matrix, not a second vev of the same one. If every coupling entering $M_{u}$ and $M_{d}$ is a multiple of one family matrix $Y$ (one rung coupling read through $c^{*}$ with any number of doublet vevs, or a complex bidoublet with a single Yukawa matrix), then $M_{u} = rM_{d}$ for one complex number $r$: every family has the same up/down mass ratio and the CKM matrix is the identity, against the record. So the complex bidoublet with one Yukawa matrix supplies the up/down scale ratio ($m_{t}/m_{b}$ through the ratio of its two vevs) but not the family pattern; the up/down split family by family, and any quark mixing, need a second family matrix not proportional to the first, with $\det[H_{u}, H_{d}] \ne 0$ for three families (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jarlskog-commutator-identity}). __notes__.note.standard-model.what-chain-decides-w: Three measured couplings fix $M_{I}$, $M_{U}$ and $\alpha_{U}$, so on this route $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ is an input that fixes $M_{I}$, not a prediction. __notes__.note.standard-model.setting-machine-veri:

\emph{Part A: the ladder.} The polarisation step of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} at $n = 3$: the nine rank-one constraints $v^{\dagger}Mv = 0$ span the nine-dimensional real space of Hermitian forms on $\C^{3}$, so only $M = 0$ survives; and the nine products $\pi^{j}\bar\pi^{k}$ of an explicit three-twistor configuration have rank four, not nine, the dependence the proof must avoid (the $n = 2$ configuration has rank four of four). __notes__.note.standard-model.weakness-examined-ex: Three consequences, at three declared levels. First, at proposition level, the exotic representations of \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space} are accounted for without projection: $(1,6)$, $(2,8)$, $(4,1)$ and their partners are multi-quantum states (the $(1,6)$ is a two-pair composite, the $(4,1)$ a full row) and are no more in need of removal from the elementary content than two-particle states are anywhere in quantum theory; Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.eighth-refutation-split-conclusion-decisive-test}'s miss list was a list of composites. What the tensor state space does not account for is the absence of the lepton, which is Hypothesis (S)'s to supply. Second, at open-question level, the colour content of the sector of a single conformal spinor is $3 \oplus \bar{3}$ against the observed $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3}$ of the two quark singlets, a single conjugation, which Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spinor-module-conjugation} resolves by the handedness of the listing; the particle-antiparticle orientation behind it is the descent's one undetermined bit, shown underivable in the dark-matter paper T14 \cite[Prop.~5.2]{ButlerT14}. __notes__.note.standard-model.point-contact-grand-: $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}\C^{5}$ restricted to $S(U(2) \times U(3)) \subset SU(5) \subset \mathrm{Spin}(10)$ being one Standard Model generation with a right-handed neutrino is the exterior-algebra presentation of grand unification expounded by Baez and Huerta \cite{BaezHuerta2010}, and Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor} arrives at it with the slot space of the conformal spinors (the twistor-slot space) as the $\C^{2}$ summand, the pair space $W$ as the $\C^{3}$ summand, and the duality of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spinor-module-conjugation} as its Hodge star. __notes__.note.standard-model.setting-introduction:
The mass paper of this series proves that mass first exists at two twistor constituents: a single twistor is null, and a two-twistor composite's mass is set by the symplectic area of its constituents' misalignment \cite{ButlerT11}. This paper asks what symmetries such composites carry, and finds that the question answers most of particle physics. The internal mixings of an $n$-twistor system form exactly $U(n)$; the minimal \emph{massive} hierarchy, two twistors of three ladder pairs each, is $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$; and the automorphisms of that tensor structure have Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$, dimension $4 + 9 - 1 = 12$: the Standard Model's, exactly. The global group comes out $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the full $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ quotient, the smallest of the Standard Model's global forms; and conversely (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse}(2)) the Standard Model algebra is the automorphism algebra of a two-factor hierarchy only for a two-by-three one. The fermion content is the quark doublet at the pair level, unconditionally, as the cells of the hierarchy's own state space, and the lepton doublet one level higher in the hierarchy under one declared hypothesis, that the twistor slots are fermionic modes like the pairs; without it the state space contains no lepton at all, and the paper proves that too. Under that hypothesis the object carrying the states has a thirteen-dimensional automorphism algebra, one abelian generator more than the twelve; in the action the state space carries, the extra generator is anomaly-free, the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, and the right-handed neutrino's Majorana mass breaks it (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(3)): the twelve are what survives below that scale. Colour neutrality of the lepton is then the exact statement that a lepton is a complete twistor, its pair system full, while a quark is a fractional one. Hypercharge is the weight of the global form's own abelian generator, and pair counting reads it off: one pair has weight one unit, so the quark doublet is at $Y = 1/6$; the single-twistor Fock space, listed by one handedness, gives the four singlets at $Y = 0, -2/3, 1/3, 1$ (a computation on that Fock space, which is not a subspace of the tensor state space; under the hypothesis it is the state space's slot-free row); and under the slot-statistics hypothesis a slot with its pair system full has weight minus three, so the lepton doublet is at $Y = -1/2$. Three anomaly conditions then hold as identities, the fourth confirms the orientation, and, given that content, they admit no other spectrum. Chirality is the handedness of the two halves of the single-twistor spinor module $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, and under the hypothesis the parity of the five-mode state space, whose even half is the generation as the half-spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}). The connection is forced, not chosen. And the numerical layer compresses. The mixing angle at the unification scale, over that generation, is $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$, a value that rests on the hypothesis with the lepton (without the lepton the ratio is $9/26$); the one-loop run from the scale where the couplings meet (the structural scale, $M_{U}$ below) refutes the desert and demands that the running between the scales change, either by partner-like content or by a gauge symmetry enlarged at an intermediate scale, and the composite's split between slots and pairs supplies the second (the section “An intermediate symmetry: the slot/pair split”); and the framework's three smallness problems are powers of the single largeness $N = M_{P}/H$, which the paper's closing trichotomy classifies: under the action as written, with the frozen point's norm fixed before variation, $N$ is a parameter of the laws (an import from the action paper); under the promotion of that norm to a Lagrange-multiplier field, a decision the series records open, it is initial data of the descent, a state-count fixing the universe's own boundary-mode count (about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$) rather than a coupling. The exhaustiveness of the alternatives is not proved.

Seven of this paper's results began as natural conjectures that failed and were refuted into better questions, and each failure is carried as a result that makes precise the question the next result answers. The refutation narrative itself belongs to the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17}, which numbers these seven as the sixth, seventh, eighth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth and fourteenth of the series; here the results are stated neutrally and the remarks say which conjecture each one refuted. The paper is Tier B for its unconditional results: the algebra, the quark doublet, the singlet spectrum, the anomaly arithmetic given a content, the run and the compressions are proved or derived at the series' standard from named premises; the identification of the derived structures with the observed forces is declared at observation level wherever it occurs; and the registered stances (the $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice, the refutation of the desert) are flagged with their falsification conditions. The results that rest on the slot-statistics hypothesis, the lepton doublet, the common handedness of doublets and singlets, the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ spinor and the values $3/8$ and $3/4$, are proved from that hypothesis at the same standard and carry its level, that of a declared and underived structural premise: until the hypothesis is derived or registered with refutation conditions (successor problem (6)), those results are conditional, and the list of levels in the section “The levels of the results, and successor problems” sets them apart. (Status now, 7 November 2026: the store derives (S) from a weaker postulate, Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}, in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}; the results that need (S) rest on that premise.)
__notes__.note.standard-model.point-contact-what-k: Three groups appear in nature and three groups appear on the ladder, but the derivation does not proceed by matching lists. The chain is: mass begins at two constituents (a theorem of the mass paper); a constituent carries three pairs (a theorem of T09, the twistor paper, on the conformal spinor space, with the three tied to dimension four); so the smallest composite that can have mass is $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$; and the forces are the freedom to rotate its internal structure without changing what it is. Each link carries its own level, itemised where it occurs, and the final identification of the automorphism group with the observed gauge group is at observation level and says so. What makes the derivation falsifiable rather than numerological is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}(iii): the global form is forced along with the algebra, and the $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ lattice it imposes is an exclusion statement current experiments can violate.

__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-gauge-algebr: The corrected conjecture of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.sixth-refutation-ladder-not-gauge-group} names a group: the automorphisms of the two-level hierarchy. Throughout, an \emph{automorphism of the hierarchy} $\C^{m} \otimes \C^{k}$ is a unitary of the product that preserves the tensor factorisation, acting as $A \otimes B$ with $(A, B) \in U(m) \times U(k)$; this is the definition of respecting both levels of the partition (twistor slots and pair slots), and it is also, for $m \neq k$ and $m, k \ge 2$, the full symmetry of the decomposable states, by Lemma \claimref{standard-model.segre-lemma-automorphisms-preserving-decomposable-tensors}; for $m = k$ the swap that lemma notes is excluded here by the requirement that twistor slots and pair slots are distinguished levels of the partition.

Two readings, at observation level and flagged as such. The natural completion of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.sixth-refutation-ladder-not-gauge-group}'s corrected conjecture, that the maximal hierarchy $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ carries the gauge group, fails on the seventeen; the framework's own correction, that mass begins at two, selects $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$; the capstone \cite[Table~1]{ButlerT17} records this refutation. __notes__.note.standard-model.setting-content-char:
The comparison of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.eighth-refutation-split-conclusion-decisive-test} set the Standard Model's elementary fermions against the state space's entire Fock space. The corrected comparison needs one definition and one declared hypothesis, stated here so that the propositions below are about defined objects and so that the reader can see exactly which results rest on which.

\emph{The hypercharge generator.} The Lie algebra of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}'s group is $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)) = \{(X, X') : \tr X + \tr X' = 0\}$, and its centre is one-dimensional, spanned by
\[
\mathsf{y} := (3I_{4}\,\mathbf{1}_{2},\; -2I_{4}\,\mathbf{1}_{3}),
\]
the unique trace-free combination of the two scalar generators up to scale (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors; $\mathbf{1}_{n}$ is the identity). The one-parameter subgroup $\exp(\theta\mathsf{y}) = (\lambda^{3}\mathbf{1}_{2}, \lambda^{-2}\mathbf{1}_{3})$, $\lambda = e^{I_{4}\theta}$, is the image of the $U(1)$ factor of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}'s second isomorphism, so $\mathsf{y}$ acts on an irreducible constituent by $I_{4}q$ where $q$ is the abelian weight of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}(ii). \emph{Hypercharge} is $Y := q/6$: the normalisation in which the lattice condition reads $t/3 + \delta/2 + Y \in \mathbb{Z}$, and in which, as computed below, a single pair has weight one unit. The sign of $\mathsf{y}$ is not fixed by the algebra: $(a, b, \lambda) \mapsto (\lambda^{-3}a, \lambda^{2}b)$ is an equally good second isomorphism with the same $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ kernel, and it reverses every weight. The sign chosen here is the one in which the pair-level generators of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(1) have weight $+1$; the opposite sign gives the conjugate listing throughout, and the choice is part of the particle-antiparticle orientation of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(1). This is a definition of the symbol $Y$; that the symbol so defined is the hypercharge of the Standard Model is the observation-level identification of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}'s reading, and is not claimed by the definition.

\emph{The tensor state space, and what it does not contain.} The state space of the minimal massive hierarchy is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$, generated from its vacuum by the six creation operators of the cells of a figure of the original; a cell is one pair of one twistor, and an automorphism acts on the cells as $A \otimes B$. On this state space the $U(1)$ factor $(\lambda^{3}, \lambda^{-2})$ acts on a cell by $\lambda^{3}\lambda^{-2} = \lambda$, so a state with $k$ cells occupied has weight $k$, and Proposition \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space} lists every representation that occurs: $(2,3)$ at one cell, and in every degree only the representations of \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space}. In particular no $(2,1)$ occurs anywhere in the tensor state space, and the states that fill a whole row of the figure, $(v \otimes f_{1}) \wedge (v \otimes f_{2}) \wedge (v \otimes f_{3})$ for $v \in \C^{2}$, are cubic in $v$ and span $S^{3}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}\C^{3} = (4, 1)$, the quadruplet of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space}'s degree three, of weight $+3$. A lepton doublet, $(2,1)$ of weight $-3$, is therefore not an object of the tensor state space, and no reading of its generators produces one. The same computation shows more: every cell has weight $+1$, so the state space contains no state of negative weight at all, and \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space} contains no $(1, \bar{3})$ in any degree; so the single-twistor sector of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3), with its negative weights $-2k$ and its $\bar{3}$ at grade two, is not a subspace of the tensor state space either. What is unconditional is the state space's own content, the quark doublet as its cells and the negative theorem; the single-twistor sector is a computation on the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ of one twistor's pairs, which under the hypothesis below is the slot-free row of one object holding both. The lepton needs a hypothesis, stated here.

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} The twistor slots of the composite are fermionic modes on the same footing as its pairs: the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; and, as in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov} supplies the structure: $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ is the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$ and its parity grading is that module's chirality).
\end{quote}

Hypothesis (S) is a structural premise, not a theorem of the series, and the paper carries it as one: every result below that needs it says so, and successor problem (6) records what deciding it would settle and what it would cost. (Status now, 7 November 2026: the store derives (S) from a weaker postulate, Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}, in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}; the results that need (S) rest on that premise.) Two remarks on its content. Under (S) a cell of the tensor state space, one slot with one pair, is the state with one slot mode and one pair mode occupied, of weight $3 - 2 = 1$, so the pair-level content of the tensor state space is recovered; but (S) does not record which pairs belong to which slot, so it is not a refinement of the two-level hierarchy but a different state space with the same one-cell sector. And under (S) the automorphisms preserving the slot-pair split act faithfully: the kernel $K$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined} acts on the $(j, k)$ component by $\lambda^{j - k}$, so the automorphism group of the five-mode state space that preserves the slot-pair split and the mode number is $U(2) \times U(3)$ itself, thirteen-dimensional, and the framework's rule that the gauge group is the automorphism group then yields one abelian generator more than Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}'s twelve. The extra generator, the total mode number $j + k$ (or equivalently $j - k$), cannot be gauged: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(3) proves that over the derived generation every abelian generator in the span of the two mode numbers except hypercharge fails three of the four anomaly conditions, so the automorphism rule read with anomaly cancellation returns the twelve. (Status now, 7 November 2026: that holds for the action $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; in the action the state space carries, through $\Lambda^{\bullet} \otimes \det^{-1/2}$, every abelian generator in that span is anomaly-free, Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(3)(b), and the rule read with anomaly cancellation returns thirteen.) What (S) still costs is the second item: a state space that is not a refinement of the two-level hierarchy.

__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-partner-sect: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run} states that the framework's $3/8$ survives experiment only if the running between the weak scale and the structural scale changes, by partner-like content or by an intermediate gauge symmetry, and names the pair and tower structure as the place to look for the first; the dark-matter paper carries the same as an open successor problem of its own, and the section “An intermediate symmetry: the slot/pair split” takes up the second. What the one-loop run demands of whatever supplies it is a question about three linear equations, answered exactly as a criterion any candidate spectrum can be held against, at one threshold and then at two. __notes__.note.standard-model.what-settled-what-gr: Two consequences. The towers do not. The answer does not depend on the odd towers' content, on their coupling rule, which the dark-matter paper shows not to be derivable \cite[Prop.~A.4]{ButlerT14}, or on their scales: it depends only on superselection, and it holds for any content whatever in the other seven sectors. What remains of the routing is the pair structure of this tower, taken up in the section “What is left in this tower”. Second, the one coupling the towers do share, the metric, contributes to the running of a gauge coupling only through graviton loops, which are suppressed by $(\mu/M_{P})^{2}$ and are not part of the one-loop gauge $\beta$-function at all; at the meeting scales of the section “The exact criterion at one threshold”, some two to five orders below $M_{P}$, this is at most a part in $10^{4}$, below the record's precision. The gravitational channel is therefore not an exception to Proposition \claimref{standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contributes-towers}; it is quoted at assembly level, as the framework's gravitational sector is not quantised in this series.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-what-left-to: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contributes-towers} returns the question to this tower, and the section “The exact criterion at one threshold” says what the content must do. This section says what the tower's own state space can and cannot do about it.
__notes__.note.standard-model.sensitivity-one-loop: Two-loop running and threshold corrections for content of this kind shift the effective $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ at the level of a few times $10^{-4}$ \cite{Amaldi1991, DimopoulosRabyWilczek1981}; at the record point $dR/d\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = -18.1$, so a shift of $3 \times 10^{-4}$ moves $R$ by $0.0054$, which is the whole of the supersymmetric content's gap $7/5 - R = 0.0055$. The one-loop table therefore neither admits nor excludes that content, and the one-loop table draws no conclusion about it; the section “Two loops” does, at record level, since the exact-rational discipline of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.one-threshold-exact-criterion} does not survive the two-loop terms, which are not rational in the inputs. The conclusions the table does deliver are those whose gaps exceed the two-loop scale by an order of magnitude: the gauginos ($r_{\Dl} - R = 0.48$), the higgsinos ($0.16$), a second doublet ($0.41$) and the gaugino-higgsino spectrum ($0.084$) fall short, and gluino-type content moves the ratio in the wrong direction, by margins ten to eighty times the shift. The record's central values $(127.951, 0.23122, 0.1180)$ in place of the rounded inputs move $R$ by $1.5 \times 10^{-4}$ and change no conclusion; the script checks both. The gaugino-higgsino row is the light content of a split spectrum with its scalars at or above $M_{U}$; the split spectra of the literature \cite{GiudiceRomanino2004, ArkaniHamedDimopoulos2005} place the scalars between the two scales, a two-threshold problem the section “Two thresholds” quantifies at one loop, and rest their unification on two-loop running.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-what-pattern: The tree relations of Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern}, $m_{\nu} = m_{u}$ and $m_{e} = m_{d}$, are the relations of a single $10$, and the observed second family needs the factor three of Georgi and Jarlskog at the unification scale \cite{GeorgiJarlskog1979}. The families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13} locates that factor in the module, in the operator $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch} at the end of this section, imported there with its provenance: with $B - L := 1 - \tfrac23 N_{W}$ and $\chi := -(-1)^{N_{R}}$ the rung parity, $T_{\mathrm{GJ}} = w_{4}(B - L)\chi$ is pure grade five, its mass form is the $126$ component, and its Clebsches have ratio $|y_{e}/y_{d}| = 3$, Georgi-Jarlskog's. The script recomputes the closed form, the grade and the Clebsches before using them. Three theorems then say, on the one-generation module, that the family structure cannot supply the factor, that the frozen point and its lifts cannot, and that the mass bracket cannot either; for an odd element $T$ of the Clifford algebra of the ten the \emph{mass form} is $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ on the sixteen, symmetrised.
__notes__.note.standard-model.what-condition-does-: The condition covers the gauge-mediated channel only. In supersymmetric content the partners of the colour triplets mediate proton decay through operators of dimension five, whose rate depends on the triplets' masses and on flavour structure this paper does not compute; Proposition \claimref{standard-model.proton-condition-candidates}(2) and (3) say nothing about that channel.
__notes__.note.standard-model.eighth-refutation-sp: Comparing \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space} with one Standard Model generation (the grid of a figure of the original is the object being decomposed) returns neither confirmation nor total failure but the framework's eighth refutation, a split conclusion. The exact agreement: the first excitation of the minimal massive hierarchy is $(2,3)$, the quark doublet, the Standard Model's most distinctive representation, appearing as the one-pair state. The near agreement: the massless sector's colour content $3 \oplus \bar{3} \oplus 1 \oplus 1$ against the observed $SU(2)$-singlet fields' $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3} \oplus 1 \oplus 1$, a single conjugation of discrepancy, definite enough to be decided rather than debated. The definite disagreements: the lepton doublet $(2,1)$ appears nowhere in the raw spectrum; exotic representations appear that nature does not show (a colour sextet, an octet-doublet, an $SU(2)$ quadruplet); and the abelian charges are pair numbers, not hypercharges. The refutation relocates the test rather than ending it: the raw Fock space was never the physical spectrum, because elementary fermions are \emph{generators}, not states, and the corrected comparison is Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}'s. The list of disagreements is a specification of what the corrected comparison must supply.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-content-char: The decisive test the algebra invites is the representation computation: decompose what the hierarchy actually contains and compare with one Standard Model generation. As elsewhere in the series, the computation does not confirm the first conjecture put to it and gives a more informative result instead.
__notes__.note.standard-model.scope: A single common threshold for all superpartners is the crudest model of a supersymmetric spectrum; the known result that a degenerate spectrum needs a few TeV to meet at $\alpha_{s} = 0.118$ is reproduced here, not discovered, and the actual thresholds, split as in the section “Two thresholds”, move $M_{U}$ and $\alpha_{U}$ by amounts the two-threshold theorem quantifies at one loop. What the proposition settles within this paper is narrower and exact in its logic: Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.sensitivity-one-loop-decides-nothing-about} left one row of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact} undecided because its one-loop gap equalled the two-loop scale, and at two loops that row is admissible. The other rows' conclusions were ten times outside the two-loop scale and stand.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-vector-modul: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point-doublet-datum-not} ends with a rung component whose mass-term couplings are the Yukawa pairs. This subsection asks where, in the framework's own objects, a doublet of hypercharge one half lies, and finds it in the most literal place: among the vectors of the transported algebra, as the directions transport adjoined.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-frozen-point: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are} says where the doublet's representation lies. This subsection asks whether the series already possesses a vector pointing along it, and finds that its scale tractor does, once carried into the completion by the transport principle's own construction.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-two-threshol: The one-threshold criterion admits an exact two-threshold extension, which is what the split spectra of the literature need.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.why-s-fails-three: In both cases the slot-level states are charged under the kernel of the action on the hierarchy. In five dimensions the kernel is the common scalar $U(1)$, and the subgroup $S(U(1) \times U(3)) = \{((\det B)^{-1}, B)\}$ maps isomorphically onto the quotient $U(3)$: the exterior algebra of slot and pair modes is a representation of that section, as T12 uses $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ in four dimensions. In three dimensions the kernel $\{\pm(1,1)\}$ is discrete inside the torus $SO(2) \times SO(2)$, and no subgroup maps isomorphically onto the quotient, so the slot-level states are not representations of the global form. Under (S) the five-dimensional state space has a tenth abelian automorphism, the slot number, beyond the nine of $\uu(3)$; this paper takes it as a global symmetry, not gauged (a choice: T12 counts the corresponding extra generator in four dimensions and finds it anomaly-free, broken by the right-handed neutrino's Majorana mass \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT12}); here it is broken only by a mass term for $N$ off the pair unit's axis.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-content-char: At observation level, and flagged as such: minimal coupling is on this reading a holonomy constraint rather than an ansatz, the gauge fields of the Standard Model algebra being exactly the freedom to rotate the pair hierarchy independently from point to point. The gauging of the internal factors is Yang-Mills, not MacDowell-Mansouri, by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}: the internal forces are conformal-level, gravity alone is pre-metric, and the $\theta$-terms are what survives the singularity. The coupling constants $g_{i}$ are normalisations this proposition does not determine; the numerical layer of the section “Unification and the desert” takes them up. Under Hypothesis (S) the hierarchy bundle would have fibre $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ and the split-and-number-preserving structure group $U(2) \times U(3)$, with the thirteenth generator settled in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(3); the proposition as stated is the tensor state space's.

families.imported-one-derived-generation.formal: Under the global group $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ of the minimal massive composite: unconditionally, the pair-level generators transform as $(2,3)$ with $Y = 1/6$, the quark doublet, and the singlets of a single conformal spinor (the single-twistor singlets) carry the hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, \tfrac13, 1$, the latter as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, which is not a subspace of the tensor state space. Under Hypothesis (S) (the slots of the conformal spinors are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs, so the composite's state space is the five-mode Fock space), and only under it, the lepton doublet $(2,1)$ with $Y = -\tfrac12$ exists, and, given the content (the two doublets and the singlets listed in one handedness, with a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or none) and the normalisation $Y_{Q} = 1/6$, the hypercharge spectrum of the generation is unique from the four anomaly conditions, the pair $\{Y_{u^{c}}, Y_{d^{c}}\}$ as an unordered set; the fourth-singlet and common-handedness hypotheses are both necessary there, and without the lepton doublet the anomaly conditions are different equations and the uniqueness is not claimed. Chirality is the parity grading of the Fock module, whose two halves carry inequivalent content. Hypothesis (S), a premise of the Standard-Model paper, is derived in the store from the weaker slot-module premise (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, from Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}), on which every statement of this paper about the charged leptons rests. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[\S4-\S5, in particular Prop.~5.3, Thm.~5.5, Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12}.

Chirality is the parity grading of the Fock module, whose two halves carry inequivalent content. Hypothesis (S), a premise of the Standard-Model paper, is derived in the store from the weaker slot-module premise, on which every charged-lepton statement of the families paper rests.
families.imported-one-derived-generation.lay: The families paper imports what the series has derived about one generation of matter. The quark doublet and the charges of single free spinor states come out with no extra assumption; the lepton doublet appears only if one adopts a stated hypothesis about how the slots those states occupy behave. The store derives that hypothesis from a weaker stated premise about the constituents, and everything that paper says about charged leptons depends on that premise.

lepton.content-constituent-space.formal:
Assume Hypothesis (C), and let $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ act through its canonical section. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Con_{k}$ transforms as $(2, \Lambda^{k}\C^{3})$ with abelian weight $q = 3 - 2k$, so
\[
\Con_{0} = (2,1)_{1/2}, \qquad \Con_{1} = (2,3)_{1/6}, \qquad \Con_{2} = (2,\bar{3})_{-1/6}, \qquad \Con_{3} = (2,1)_{-1/2}.
\]
\item The odd half is one generation's doublets, in the same chirality half, writing $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ for the conformal spinor space and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ for its partner (twistor and dual twistor space):
\[
\C^{2} \otimes \CSm{} \;=\; \Con_{1} \oplus \Con_{3} \;=\; (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \;=\; Q \oplus L.
\]
The lepton doublet is a slot holding the full pair system; the quark doublet is a slot holding one excited pair; and they lie in the same chirality half because one and three are both odd, whichever sign $\epsilon$ takes.
\item The even half is the dual of the odd half, constituent by constituent: $\Con_{k}^{*} \cong \Con_{3-k}$, so $\C^{2} \otimes \CS = \Con_{0} \oplus \Con_{2} = L^{*} \oplus Q^{*}$, the antiparticles, in the opposite chirality half. A slot holding a bare conformal spinor, the Fock vacuum $u$ itself, is the antilepton.
\item The lattice condition $2t + 3\delta + q \equiv 0 \pmod 6$ of \cite[Thm.~4.2(ii)]{ButlerT12} holds on every $\Con_{k}$.
\end{enumerate}
lepton.content-constituent-space.technical:
Under Hypothesis (C), with $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ acting through its canonical section, the constituent $\Con_{k} = \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ transforms as $(2, \Lambda^{k}\C^{3})$ with abelian weight $q = 3 - 2k$, so $\Con_{0}, \Con_{1}, \Con_{2}, \Con_{3}$ are $(2,1)_{1/2}$, $(2,3)_{1/6}$, $(2,\bar{3})_{-1/6}$, $(2,1)_{-1/2}$.

The odd half $\Con_{1} \oplus \Con_{3} = Q \oplus L$ is one generation's doublets, in the same chirality half whatever the sign $\epsilon$. The even half is its dual, $\Con_{k}^{*} \cong \Con_{3-k}$, the antiparticles, in the opposite half; a slot holding the bare Fock vacuum is the antilepton. Every $\Con_{k}$ satisfies the lattice condition $2t + 3\delta + q \equiv 0 \pmod 6$. The proof reads the weights off the section's action and uses the duality of exterior powers with $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ on the section.
lepton.content-constituent-space.lay: Under a stated hypothesis about how a basic spinor state sitting in a slot transforms (Hypothesis (C)), this result lists the charges of the four kinds of constituent. Two of them are exactly the quark doublet and the lepton doublet of one Standard Model generation, and they share a handedness; the other two are their antiparticles. A slot holding an unexcited spinor state is the antilepton, and all four have charges on the series' charge lattice.

proofs.main: (1) The representative $(\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$ acts on $v \otimes \omega \in \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ as $\lambda^{3}av \otimes \lambda^{-2k}\Lambda^{k}(b)\omega$: the $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ content is $(2, \Lambda^{k}\C^{3})$, which is $(2,1), (2,3), (2,\bar{3}), (2,1)$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, 3$ (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-duality-pair-system} for $\Lambda^{2}\C^{3} \cong \bar{3}$), and the weight is $3 - 2k$. (2) is (1) read at $k = 1, 3$, with the chirality clause of Hypothesis (C) (\claimref{lepton.hyp-c-constituent}). (3) By Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-duality-pair-system}, $\Con_{k}^{*} = (\C^{2})^{*} \otimes (\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \det(A)^{-1} \otimes \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes \det(B)^{-1}$, and on the section $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$, so this is $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3-k}W = \Con_{3-k}$; the weights confirm it, $-(3 - 2k) = 3 - 2(3-k)$, and irreducibles are determined by content and weight (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-automorphism-group-section-hypercharge-generator}). Parity flips because $k$ and $3 - k$ have opposite parity. (4) With $\delta = 1$ on every $\Con_{k}$ and $t = 0, 1, -1, 0$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, 3$: $3 + 3 = 6$, $2 + 3 + 1 = 6$, $-2 + 3 - 1 = 0$, $3 - 3 = 0$. The script builds $\mathsf{y}$ on each $\Con_{k}$ and reads off the weights, and checks the residues.

lepton.hyp-c-constituent.formal:
\emph{Hypothesis (C), the constituent hypothesis.} A constituent of the composite is a Dirac state in a slot, a conformal spinor or its partner (a twistor or its dual) with any of its pairs excited: its state space is
\[
\Con := \C^{2} \otimes \Sp = \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W,
\]
sixteen-dimensional, with a pair $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acting as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(B)$: $A$ acts on the slot vector once, and on nothing else; $B$ acts on the Dirac state. The chirality of a constituent is that of the Dirac spinor it holds (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations}) up to one overall sign $\epsilon = \pm 1$ for the slotted sector relative to the free sector: $\epsilon = +1$ means a slot leaves the half alone, $\epsilon = -1$ that it reverses it. (C) leaves $\epsilon$ open; Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors} fixes $\epsilon = -1$. Write $\Con_{k} := \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$.
lepton.hyp-c-constituent.technical:
Hypothesis (C) takes a constituent of the composite to be a Dirac state in a slot: a conformal spinor or its partner with any of its pairs excited. Its state space is $\Con = \C^{2} \otimes \Sp = \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, sixteen-dimensional, with $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acting as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(B)$, so the slot mixing acts on the slot vector once and on nothing else.

The chirality of a constituent is that of the Dirac spinor it holds, up to one overall sign $\epsilon = \pm 1$ for the slotted sector relative to the free sector. The hypothesis leaves $\epsilon$ open; a separate argument fixes $\epsilon = -1$. The graded pieces are $\Con_{k} = \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$.
lepton.hyp-c-constituent.lay: This is an assumption, not a result: each building block of a composite particle is one basic spinor state, with any of its internal pairs excited, sitting in one of two slots, and mixing the slots acts on that block as a whole rather than on each of its parts separately. It leaves open one sign, the relative handedness of slotted and free states, which is settled by a later argument. The companion note's results on the lepton hold under it.
