lepton.imported-automorphism-group-secti.formal: The automorphisms of the hierarchy, the unitaries $A \otimes B$ of $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ with $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$, form $(U(2) \times U(3))/K$ with $K = \{(\lambda I_{2}, \lambda^{-1}I_{3})\}$, and each $K$-coset contains exactly one pair with $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$, so the group is $S(U(2) \times U(3)) \cong (SU(2) \times SU(3) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the $U(1)$ factor acting as $(\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$. The centre of its Lie algebra is spanned by $\mathsf{y} = (3I_{4}\,I_{2}, -2I_{4}\,I_{3})$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors; $I_{2}$ and $I_{3}$ are identity matrices); on an irreducible representation $\mathsf{y}$ acts as $I_{4}q$ with $q$ the abelian weight, and hypercharge is $Y = q/6$. Irreducible representations of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ are determined by their $SU(2)$ content, $SU(3)$ content and weight. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~4.1, 4.2, and the definition before Prop.~5.3]{ButlerT12}.
lepton.imported-automorphism-group-secti.technical:
The automorphisms of the hierarchy $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ are the unitaries $A \otimes B$, $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$, modulo the kernel $K = \{(\lambda I_{2}, \lambda^{-1}I_{3})\}$. Each $K$-coset contains exactly one pair with $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$, which gives the canonical section and the group $S(U(2) \times U(3)) \cong (SU(2) \times SU(3) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the $U(1)$ factor acting as $(\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$.

The centre of the Lie algebra is spanned by $\mathsf{y} = (3I_{4}\,I_{2}, -2I_{4}\,I_{3})$, with $I_{4}$ the field theory's unit and $I_{2}$, $I_{3}$ identity matrices, which acts as $I_{4}q$ on an irreducible representation of abelian weight $q$, and hypercharge is $Y = q/6$. Irreducible representations are determined by their $SU(2)$ content, $SU(3)$ content and weight.
lepton.imported-automorphism-group-secti.lay: The symmetries of the structure of two spinor states with three internal pairs form exactly the Standard Model's gauge group in its smallest global form. Each symmetry can be written in many ways, and there is one canonical choice among them. The group's single abelian direction defines hypercharge as one sixth of a whole-number weight, and a particle type is fixed by three labels: its weak content, its colour content and that weight.

lepton.imported-duality-pair-system.technical:
Two dualities of representation theory are used. As $U(3)$-modules, the dual of an exterior power of $W = \C^{3}$ is the complementary power twisted by the inverse determinant, $(\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes \det^{-1}$; as a $U(2)$-module, $(\C^{2})^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \det^{-1}$.

Both are standard, taken from the series' Cauchy-decomposition import and the textbook treatment of exterior powers.
lepton.imported-duality-pair-system.lay: Taking the dual of a representation, which turns it inside out, gives back a familiar representation for these small symmetry groups, up to a determinant factor. In three complex dimensions the dual of the $k$-fold wedge products is the $(3-k)$-fold products; in two dimensions the dual is the space itself. These standard facts let particles be matched with antiparticles.

lepton.imported-free-sector-anomaly-cond.formal: The sector of a single conformal spinor (the single-twistor sector; massless, free) is $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ with the pair-slot factor acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\lambda^{-2}b)$: its grade-$k$ states transform as $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3} = 1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$ with weight $-2k$, that is $(1)_{0}, (3)_{-1/3}, (\bar{3})_{-2/3}, (1)_{-1}$. For a gauge group with a $U(1)$ factor acting on Weyl fermions listed in one handedness, the four anomaly-cancellation conditions are those of \cite[Fact~2.7]{ButlerT12}; a fermion of the opposite handedness enters as its conjugate, with the conjugate representation and the opposite hypercharge. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~5.3(3), Fact~2.7]{ButlerT12}; \cite[\S 22.4]{WeinbergQFT2}.
lepton.imported-free-sector-anomaly-cond.technical:
The sector of a single conformal spinor (massless, free), $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, with the pair-slot factor acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\lambda^{-2}b)$, has grade-$k$ states $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ of weight $-2k$, that is $(1)_{0}, (3)_{-1/3}, (\bar{3})_{-2/3}, (1)_{-1}$.

For a gauge group with a $U(1)$ factor acting on Weyl fermions listed in one handedness, the four anomaly-cancellation conditions are the series' standard ones; a fermion of the opposite handedness enters as its conjugate, with the conjugate representation and the opposite hypercharge.
lepton.imported-free-sector-anomaly-cond.lay: A single free spinor state of the conformal algebra carries four kinds of state, with hypercharges zero, minus one third, minus two thirds and minus one. To check that a gauge theory with an abelian (hypercharge-type) factor, built on such particles, is consistent at the quantum level, one uses four standard anomaly sums over the particles, all listed with the same handedness. A particle of the other handedness is counted through its antiparticle.

lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-n.formal: The tensor ledger $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$, the Fock space generated by the six cells $e_{i} \otimes f_{a}$ with the automorphisms acting cell by cell as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \otimes B)$, decomposes under $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ as $(1,1) \oplus (2,3) \oplus [(3,\bar{3}) \oplus (1,6)] \oplus [(4,1) \oplus (2,8)] \oplus [(3,3) \oplus (1,\bar{6})] \oplus (2,\bar{3}) \oplus (1,1)$, graded by cell number, which is also the abelian weight; no $(2,1)$ occurs; and the states that fill a whole row, $\bigwedge_{a}(v \otimes f_{a})$ for $v \in \C^{2}$, are cubic in $v$ and span $S^{3}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}\C^{3} = (4,1)$, of weight $3$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~5.1 and Prop.~5.3(2)]{ButlerT12}.
lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-n.technical:
The tensor ledger $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$ is the Fock space of the six cells $e_{i} \otimes f_{a}$, with the automorphisms acting cell by cell as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \otimes B)$. Under $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ it decomposes, graded by cell number (which is also the abelian weight), as $(1,1) \oplus (2,3) \oplus [(3,\bar{3}) \oplus (1,6)] \oplus [(4,1) \oplus (2,8)] \oplus [(3,3) \oplus (1,\bar{6})] \oplus (2,\bar{3}) \oplus (1,1)$, and no $(2,1)$ occurs.

The states that fill a whole row, $\bigwedge_{a}(v \otimes f_{a})$, are cubic in $v$ and span $S^{3}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}\C^{3} = (4,1)$, of weight $3$, a quadruplet and not a doublet.
lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-n.lay: If the states of the structure of two spinor states are counted cell by cell, as ordinary multi-particle states of its six cells, no state has the symmetry content of a lepton doublet. The obvious candidate, one spinor state's whole row filled, turns out to transform as a four-component object rather than a doublet. So the lepton does not live in this state space.

lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-.technical:
Under Hypothesis (C), list the doublets $Q = \Con_{1}$ and $L = \Con_{3}$ in one handedness and add the free sector $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ in one of two ways. Listing the free half $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ (grades $0$ and $2$) with the slot sector's $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$, and conjugating the free $\CSm{}$ half, gives $Q, L, \nu^{c}, u^{c}, d^{c}, e^{c}$ with hypercharges $(\tfrac16, -\tfrac12, 0, -\tfrac23, \tfrac13, 1)$, and all four anomaly sums vanish. The other listing gives $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1) = \tfrac23$ and a cubic sum of $-\tfrac49$.

So anomaly cancellation fixes the bit of (C) at $\epsilon = -1$: a slot reverses the chirality half. Physically the free fields are $\nu^{c}$ and $u^{c}$ from $\CS$ and $d_{R}$ and $e_{R}$ from $\CSm{}$, with no conjugation applied; a bare free conformal spinor is the neutrino singlet and a bare conformal spinor in a slot is the antilepton. The arithmetic is the Standard-Model paper's; what is new is its reading under (C).
lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-.lay: Under Hypothesis (C), the quark and lepton doublets come from basic spinor states sitting in slots, while further particles come from free ones, and there are two ways to match the handedness of the two groups. Only one of them gives a theory free of quantum anomalies, and it is exactly one Standard Model generation with a right-handed neutrino. So a consistency requirement, rather than a separate assumption, fixes this one-bit choice.
lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-.typing_note: Added the constituent-content proposition, which supplies the doublets Q, L and their hypercharges used in the sums; the Standard-Model hypercharge theorem in context_refs is cited only as having the same arithmetic, so it was not added, and no standard-route applies since the result is a reading under (C). Hypothesis pass: assumes lepton.hyp-c-constituent added because its statement assumes Hypothesis (C). Levels pass: the lay level now names Hypothesis (C) instead of 'a stated hypothesis'.

\[
(\tfrac16,\; -\tfrac23,\; \tfrac13,\; -\tfrac12,\; 1,\; 0):
\] $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1) = \tfrac13 - \tfrac23 + \tfrac13 = 0$; $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1) = \tfrac12 - \tfrac12 = 0$; gravitational $1 - 2 + 1 - 1 + 1 + 0 = 0$; cubic $\tfrac{1}{36} - \tfrac89 + \tfrac19 - \tfrac14 + 1 + 0 = 0$. (2) With the free $\CSm{}$ states $(3)_{-1/3}$, $(1)_{-1}$ listed unconjugated and the $\CS$ states conjugated to $(1)_{0}$, $(3)_{+2/3}$: $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1) = 2 \cdot \tfrac16 - \tfrac13 + \tfrac23 = \tfrac23$; $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1) = 0$ (the doublets are unchanged); gravitational $1 - 1 - 1 + 2 - 1 + 0 = 0$; cubic $\tfrac{1}{36} - \tfrac14 - \tfrac19 + \tfrac89 - 1 + 0 = -\tfrac49$. Both lists are verified exactly by the script. The physical reading: the $\CS$ half of the free sector listed as left-handed gives $\nu^{c}$ and $u^{c}$ directly, and the $\CSm{}$ half, being of the other handedness, is $d_{R} = (3)_{-1/3}$ and $e_{R} = (1)_{-1}$ as right-handed fields, the fields whose left-handed conjugates are $d^{c}$ and $e^{c}$. Both lists are drawn up under Hypothesis (C) (\claimref{lepton.hyp-c-constituent}), whose bit $\epsilon$ is the relative handedness the two lists decide.

lepton.self-conjugacy-forces-determinant.formal: As a representation of $U(2) \times U(3)$, $\Con$ is not self-dual: $\Con_{k}^{*} \cong \Con_{3-k} \otimes (\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1}$, and no $\Con_{j}$ is isomorphic to $\Con_{k}^{*}$, since the $K$-weights $1 - j$ and $-(1 - k)$ never agree for $j, k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with matching content. As a representation of a subgroup $G \subseteq U(2) \times U(3)$ containing $SU(2) \times SU(3)$, $\Con$ is self-dual if and only if $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ on $G$, that is $G \subseteq S(U(2) \times U(3))$. In particular the largest subgroup of $U(2) \times U(3)$ under which the constituent spectrum is closed under conjugation is exactly the automorphism group of the hierarchy, $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, twelve-dimensional. All of this is for the untwisted action, the one in which the first display holds: if every component is twisted by $t = (\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1/2}$, then $(\Con_{k} \otimes t)^{*} \cong \Con_{3-k} \otimes t$, the twisted spectrum is closed under conjugation for the whole group (on the double cover on which $t$ is a character), and the conclusion does not hold there (Observation \claimref{lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-thirteenth}).
lepton.self-conjugacy-forces-determinant.technical:
As a representation of $U(2) \times U(3)$ the constituent space $\Con$ is not self-dual: $\Con_{k}^{*} \cong \Con_{3-k} \otimes (\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1}$, and the $K$-weights, $1 - j$ on $\Con_{j}$ and $k - 1$ on $\Con_{k}^{*}$, never agree where the $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ contents match.

For a subgroup $G \subseteq U(2) \times U(3)$ containing $SU(2) \times SU(3)$, $\Con$ is self-dual if and only if $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ on $G$, that is $G \subseteq S(U(2) \times U(3))$. So the largest subgroup under which the constituent spectrum is closed under conjugation is exactly the twelve-dimensional automorphism group of the hierarchy. This is a statement about the untwisted action: in the action twisted by $(\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1/2}$, which the Standard-Model paper shows the generation's state space carries, the dual of every component is a component and self-conjugacy no longer removes the thirteenth generator.
lepton.self-conjugacy-forces-determinant.lay: A symmetry group that makes physical sense should send every particle's antiparticle back into the list of particles. Among groups that contain the weak and strong symmetry groups, for the constituent space this works only when a determinant condition holds, which cuts the naive thirteen-dimensional group down to twelve dimensions. That twelve-dimensional group is exactly the symmetry group of the two-level structure. This holds for the plain way the groups act; in the slightly twisted action the series now uses, the argument no longer removes the thirteenth direction.

proofs.main: The first isomorphism is Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-duality-pair-system} as in the proof of Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space}(3), without setting the determinants to one. For the non-isomorphism, compare $K$-weights, $K$ the kernel of \claimref{lepton.imported-automorphism-group-section-hypercharge-generator}: $\Con_{j}$ has $K$-weight $1 - j$ and $\Con_{k}^{*}$ has $-(1 - k) = k - 1$; equality needs $j + k = 2$, so $(j, k) \in \{(0,2), (1,1), (2,0)\}$, but the $SU(3)$ contents of $\Con_{0}, \Con_{1}, \Con_{2}$ are $1, 3, \bar{3}$ and those of $\Con_{2}^{*}, \Con_{1}^{*}, \Con_{0}^{*}$ are $3, \bar{3}, 1$, which never match. If $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ on $G$ the twist is trivial and $\Con_{k}^{*} \cong \Con_{3-k}$; if not, some $(A, B) \in G$ has $\det A \cdot \det B = \mu \neq 1$, and then $\Con_{1}^{*} \cong \Con_{2} \otimes \mu^{-1}$, whose $SU(3)$ content $\bar{3}$ is matched by $\Con_{2}$ alone among the $\Con_{j}$, is not isomorphic to $\Con_{2}$ (they differ on that element), so $\Con$ is not self-dual. (The case $k = 0$ would not do: $\Con_{0}$ and $\Con_{3}$ share the content $(2,1)$, and for $G = SU(2) \times U(3)$ one has $\Con_{0}^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes (\det A)^{-1} = \Con_{0}$, so the dual of $\Con_{0}$ is present there although $\Con$ as a whole is not self-dual; $k = 1$ or $k = 2$, whose $SU(3)$ contents are matched by one constituent each, decide.) Since $G \supseteq SU(2) \times SU(3)$, the condition $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ on $G$ is the condition $G \subseteq S(U(2) \times U(3))$. The script checks the $K$-weights and the dual weights, and tests the biconditional on five subgroups $G$, through the lattice of central characters trivial on $G$, including the one on which the $k = 0$ test alone would fail to decide.

lepton.unit-action-cell-action.technical:
Identify the single-row $k$-pair states $R_{k} \subset \Lambda^{k}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$ with $\Con_{k}$ by $\bigwedge_{a \in S}(e_{i} \otimes f_{a}) \mapsto e_{i} \otimes f_{S}$. At $k = 1$ the cell action $A \otimes B$ and the unit action coincide, so the pair-level generators are the one-pair constituents.

At $k = 2, 3$ the cell action does not preserve $R_{k}$: it spans $S^{k}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$, that is $(3,\bar{3})$ and $(4,1)$, with weight $k$, while under the unit action $\Con_{k} = (2, \Lambda^{k}\C^{3})$ has dimension $2\binom{3}{k}$ and weight $3 - 2k$. Hence the constituent space is not a subrepresentation of the tensor ledger: the ledger is the Fock space of the pairs, counted cell by cell, not the space of the composite's constituents.
lepton.unit-action-cell-action.lay: The slot symmetry can act on a basic spinor state with several excited pairs in two ways: once on the state as a whole, or separately on each pair. For one excited pair the two agree. For two or three they give different representations of the same states, so the space of constituents is genuinely different from the cell-by-cell state space, and the difference sits exactly at multiply excited spinor states.
lepton.unit-action-cell-action.typing_note: Removed the ladder Fact (cited only as silent on excited twistors, deciding neither way) and the pair-system Fact (cited as agreeing with the ledger's definition, which alone carries clause (3)); the second removal is the less certain. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: (1) Both actions send $e_{i} \otimes f_{a}$ to $Ae_{i} \otimes Bf_{a}$. (2) Under the cell action a mixing $A$ sends $\bigwedge_{a \in S}(e_{i} \otimes f_{a})$ to $\bigwedge_{a \in S}(Ae_{i} \otimes f_{a})$, which is the image of $(Ae_{i})^{\otimes k} \otimes f_{S}$ under the projection $(\C^{2})^{\otimes k} \otimes \Lambda^{k}\C^{3} \to \Lambda^{k}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$; as $Ae_{i}$ ranges over $\C^{2}$ the tensors $v^{\otimes k}$ span $S^{k}\C^{2}$, so the span is $S^{k}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$, of dimension $(k+1)\binom{3}{k}$, which is $9$ at $k = 2$ and $4$ at $k = 3$, exceeding $\dim R_{k} = 2\binom{3}{k}$ ($6$ and $2$) so $R_{k}$ is not preserved. Its $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ content is $(k+1, \Lambda^{k}\C^{3})$, that is $(3,\bar{3})$ and $(4,1)$, the representations Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton} lists in degrees two and three; and the weight is $k$, one per cell. Under the unit action $A$ acts once on the slot vector, so the span is $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W = \Con_{k}$ with the weight of Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space}. The script confirms the ranks: the $SU(2)$-orbit of a fixed pair subset $S$ under the cell action has rank $k + 1$ ($2, 3, 4$ for $k = 1, 2, 3$) and under the unit action rank $2$. (3) A subrepresentation would have to be preserved by the cell action; by (2) $R_{2}$ and $R_{3}$ are not, and by Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton} the ledger contains no $(2,1)$ at all. The reading of the ledger as the Fock space of pairs is the definition of the ledger, and is what Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations} gives on two conformal spinors; what (2) adds is the exact point at which (C) departs from it: on a conformal spinor with two or more pairs excited, the ledger lets a mixing of slots act on each pair separately, and (C) lets it act on the spinor once. Fact \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} is silent on excited conformal spinors, so it decides neither way; that is why (C) is a hypothesis.

lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-th.formal: A gauge symmetry of a theory with antiparticles must map the spectrum to itself and commute with conjugation: the conjugate of a state in the spectrum is in the spectrum, with the conjugate quantum numbers. The premise, printed: that $\Con$ is the whole constituent state space and is already closed under conjugation, the constituents' antiparticles being constituents; the observed one-handed content of the Standard Model is a complex representation, and the requirement applies to its CPT completion, so the premise is that $\Con$ is that completion. Under $U(2) \times U(3)$ the constituent spectrum $\Con$ fails self-conjugacy (Proposition \claimref{lepton.self-conjugacy-forces-determinant-one-group}): the conjugate of a bare conformal spinor (twistor) in a slot, $\Con_{0}^{*}$, is not a constituent, and the full conformal spinor $\Con_{3}$, which has the conjugate content, carries the wrong $K$-charge. So on that premise $K$ is not a symmetry of the constituents, and the group acting on them is $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the same group Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-automorphism-group-section-hypercharge-generator} derives from the cells, on which $K$ is trivial. The two agree, and the canonical section of the section “The constituent space: the hypothesis that holds a lepton, and where it leaves the ledger” is the only action of the automorphism group on $\Con$ compatible with conjugation. The same argument applies to the five-mode ledger $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of T12's Hypothesis (S) in its untwisted action, whose $(j,k)$ component has $K$-weight $j - k$: its dual is the $(2-j, 3-k)$ component twisted by $(\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1}$, so self-conjugacy forces the determinant-one group there too. T12 now shows that the state space carries the action twisted by $(\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1/2}$, in which the $(j,k)$ component has central character $\alpha^{j-1}\beta^{k-3/2}$ on $(\alpha I_{2}, \beta I_{3})$ and the dual of every component is again a component, so there self-conjugacy does not exclude the thirteenth generator: it is the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, anomaly-free and broken at the intermediate scale by the Majorana term of $\nu^{c}$ \cite[Prop.~5.8(3), Prop.~10.7]{ButlerT12}. Either way it is not a cost of (S). Two limits, stated. This is a statement about consistency with conjugation, at the level of the CPT theorem it invokes and of the premise just printed, and is recorded as an Observation for that reason; T12 reaches the untwisted half of this at proposition level, without that premise, from the anomaly conditions: in the untwisted action every abelian generator in the span of the two mode numbers other than hypercharge fails three of the four conditions over the derived generation \cite[Prop.~5.8(3)(a)]{ButlerT12}. Self-conjugacy also singles out the canonical section among the actions of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ on $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$ that differ from it by a character: twisting the section by $(\det A)^{m}$, $m \in \mathbb{Z}$, shifts every weight by $6m$ (on the section $\det A = \lambda^{6}$) and every hypercharge by $m$, giving $Y_{L} = -\tfrac12 + m$; but the twisted space is self-dual only if $\Con \cong \Con \otimes (\det A)^{-2m}$, and $\det A$ is onto $U(1)$ on the section, so only $m = 0$ survives, as the weight multiset $\{3, 1, -1, -3\}$ shifted by $6m$ is closed under negation only at $m = 0$. The agreement $Y_{Q} = \tfrac16$ with the ledger's one-cell states (Proposition \claimref{lepton.unit-action-cell-action}(1)) is then a check, not the argument. The script checks the twisted values $Y_{L} = -\tfrac52, \tfrac32$ at $m = \mp 2$ and the closure of the shifted multiset under negation for $m \in [-3, 3]$.
lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-th.technical:
On the printed premise that the constituent space $\Con$ is the CPT completion of the observed content, closed under conjugation, its failure of self-conjugacy under $U(2) \times U(3)$ means the kernel $K$ is not a symmetry of the constituents, so the acting group is $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the same group derived from the cells, and the canonical section is the only action compatible with conjugation. The same argument forces the determinant-one group on the five-mode ledger of Hypothesis (S) in its untwisted action.

In the action twisted by $(\det A \cdot \det B)^{-1/2}$ that the Standard-Model paper now uses, the dual of every component is a component, so self-conjugacy does not exclude the thirteenth generator: it is the anomaly-free $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, broken at the intermediate scale by the Majorana term of $\nu^{c}$. Self-conjugacy also excludes twisting the section by $(\det A)^{m}$ for $m \neq 0$, since the weights $\{3, 1, -1, -3\}$ shifted by $6m$ are closed under negation only at $m = 0$. The argument stands at the level of the CPT premise.
lepton.what-self-conjugacy-says-about-th.lay: Assume the constituents already include their own antiparticles. Then requiring the symmetry to respect particle-antiparticle conjugation picks out the twelve-dimensional Standard Model group and a unique way for it to act. In the version of the state space the series now prefers, this argument no longer rules out a thirteenth symmetry direction, which turns out to be a known one from grand unification, broken at a high scale by the right-handed neutrino's mass. This is a consistency argument resting on a stated premise, not a full derivation.

neutrino.imported-derived-content-single.formal: The minimal massive hierarchy's fermion content is $(2,3) \oplus (2,1)$, the doublets under the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S); the sector of a single conformal spinor (the single-twistor sector) $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{3} = 1 \oplus 3 \oplus \bar{3} \oplus 1$, graded zero through three, carries the weight $q = -2k$ at grade $k$ and hence the hypercharge $Y = -k/3$, that is $0, -\tfrac13, -\tfrac23, -1$, unconditionally as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor with the pair-slot factor acting alone (that Fock space is not a subspace of the tensor state space, and under (S) it is the row $j = 0$); listed by the handedness that keeps the even grades, the singlet spectrum is $(1)_{0} \oplus (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \oplus (1)_{+1}$, that is $\nu^{c}, u^{c}, d^{c}, e^{c}$, with the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero; the four anomaly conditions hold on this spectrum, and determine it (up to the $u^{c}, d^{c}$ relabelling) given the content, $Y_{Q} = \tfrac16$, and a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or none; and the physical representations are confined to the $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ lattice. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~5.1, Prop.~5.3, Thm.~5.5, Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT12}; Hypothesis (S) is declared in the Standard-Model paper and is derived in the store from the weaker slot-module premise (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, from Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}), on which the lepton doublet rests.

neutrino.imported-derived-content-single.lay: The neutrino paper imports the series' derivation of one generation of matter. The quark and lepton doublets come from the structure of two basic spinor states, the lepton doublet only under a stated hypothesis, which the store derives from a weaker stated premise about the constituents, and four single-particle states come from one free spinor state. One of those singlets has zero charge, the right-handed neutrino, and it sits at the lowest grade. The anomaly conditions confirm this spectrum and fix it, up to swapping the two coloured singlets, once the doublets, the quark doublet's hypercharge and at most one neutral singlet are given.

obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectru.formal:
A \emph{one-threshold spectrum} consists of the derived content with one Higgs doublet, coefficients $b = (b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3})$ (under Hypothesis (S) the content of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency} with its lepton doublet, $b = (\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$, the value used throughout this section), active from $M_{Z}$ upward, together with further content, coefficient shifts $\Dl = (\Dl_{1}, \Dl_{2}, \Dl_{3})$ by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices}, active from a threshold $M_{I}$ upward. Write $x = \ln(M_{U}/M_{Z})/2\pi$ and $y = \ln(M_{U}/M_{I})/2\pi$, so that the one-loop equations read
\begin{equation}
a_{i}(M_{Z}) \;=\; a_{U} + b_{i}\,x + \Dl_{i}\,y, \qquad i = 1, 2, 3,
\end{equation}
with $a_{U}$ the common inverse coupling at $M_{U}$. The spectrum is \emph{admissible} for given record values $a_{i}(M_{Z})$ if \claimref{obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectrum-admissible} has a solution with $x > 0$, $0 \le y \le x$ and $a_{U} > 0$: the couplings meet at one scale above $M_{Z}$, the threshold lies between $M_{Z}$ and $M_{U}$, and the unified coupling is positive. The \emph{threshold fraction} is $f = y/x = \ln(M_{U}/M_{I})/\ln(M_{U}/M_{Z})$. Write $b_{12} = b_{1} - b_{2}$, $b_{23} = b_{2} - b_{3}$, $\Dl_{12} = \Dl_{1} - \Dl_{2}$, $\Dl_{23} = \Dl_{2} - \Dl_{3}$, $D_{12} = a_{1} - a_{2}$ and $D_{23} = a_{2} - a_{3}$ at $M_{Z}$, and
\[
R \;=\; \frac{D_{12}}{D_{23}}, \qquad r_{0} \;=\; \frac{b_{12}}{b_{23}}, \qquad r_{\Dl} \;=\; \frac{b_{12} + \Dl_{12}}{b_{23} + \Dl_{23}}.
\]
$R$ is the record's ratio, $r_{0}$ the Standard Model's, $r_{\Dl}$ the ratio of the whole spectrum as if it were active from $M_{Z}$.
obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectru.technical:
A one-threshold spectrum is the derived content with one Higgs doublet, with one-loop coefficients $b = (b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3})$ active from $M_{Z}$ upward (under Hypothesis (S), $b = (\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$), plus further content that shifts the coefficients by $\Dl = (\Dl_{1}, \Dl_{2}, \Dl_{3})$ from a threshold $M_{I}$ upward. With $x = \ln(M_{U}/M_{Z})/2\pi$ and $y = \ln(M_{U}/M_{I})/2\pi$ the inverse couplings obey $a_{i}(M_{Z}) = a_{U} + b_{i}\,x + \Dl_{i}\,y$.

The spectrum is admissible for given record values $a_{i}(M_{Z})$ if these equations have a solution with $x > 0$, $0 \le y \le x$ and $a_{U} > 0$. The threshold fraction is $f = y/x$, and the ratios $R = D_{12}/D_{23}$ of the record, $r_{0} = b_{12}/b_{23}$ of the Standard Model and $r_{\Dl} = (b_{12} + \Dl_{12})/(b_{23} + \Dl_{23})$ of the whole spectrum as if active from $M_{Z}$ compare data with running.
obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectru.lay: This definition sets up a simple model of how the strengths of the three forces change with energy: the known particles act from low energy upward, and some extra particles join in above one threshold. The model counts as admissible if the three strengths meet at a single higher energy, with the threshold between the two scales and a positive common strength. A few ratios are defined to compare the measured couplings with what the running gives.

obj.standard-model.two-rung-module-secto.formal:
Let $R_{2} = \operatorname{span}(v_{4}, v_{5})$ be the span of the two rungs' creation modes over $\C$ and $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2})$ the Fock module of the five mode pairs, three of $W$ and two of $R_{2}$, with the Hermitian structure induced by $*$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} on the rung factor and by a fixed $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$-invariant Hermitian form on the pair factor. The \emph{sector} $(j, k)$ is $\Lambda^{j}R_{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$, $j$ the rung (slot) number and $k$ the pair number; the \emph{slot-singlet sectors} are $j \in \{0, 2\}$ and the \emph{slot-doublet sectors} $j = 1$. For an orthonormal basis $(e_{a})$ of $\Lambda^{j}R_{2}$, the \emph{slot components} of a state $\Psi_{j} = \sum_{a} e_{a} \otimes \psi_{a}$ in rung sector $j$ are the $\psi_{a} \in \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, $\binom{2}{j}$ of them. A \emph{product form} on the module is a Hermitian form with $\ip{e_{a} \otimes \psi}{e_{b} \otimes \varphi} = \ip{e_{a}}{e_{b}}_{R}\,\ip{\psi}{\varphi}_{W}$; the structure just described is one. The \emph{moment} of a bivector $X \in \Lambda^{2}V_{\C}$ on a state $\Psi$ is $M_{X}(\Psi) = \ip{\Psi}{X\Psi}$, and for $I \in V$ the grip and the mass-squared of $\Psi$ are Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-grip-area-casimir-form}(i) with this moment.
In the same module write the mode operators $v_{a}$ (creation) and $w_{a}$ (annihilation), $a = 1, \ldots, 5$, modes $1, 2, 3$ those of $W$ and $4, 5$ those of $R_{2}$; \emph{the ten} is their span, the complexified transported ambient space $V_{\C} \oplus R_{2} \oplus \overline{R}_{2}$; \emph{rung vectors} are $v_{4}, v_{5}, w_{4}, w_{5}$ and \emph{pair vectors} $v_{1}, v_{2}, v_{3}, w_{1}, w_{2}, w_{3}$. The hypercharge generator is $y = 3N_{R} - 2N_{W}$ and $2T_{3} = N_{4} - N_{5}$ in occupation numbers.
obj.standard-model.two-rung-module-secto.technical:
Let $R_{2} = \operatorname{span}(v_{4}, v_{5})$ and take the Fock module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2})$ of five mode pairs, three of $W$ and two rung (slot) modes, with a product Hermitian structure. The sector $(j, k)$ is $\Lambda^{j}R_{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$, with $j \in \{0, 2\}$ the slot-singlet sectors and $j = 1$ the slot-doublet sectors; a state in rung sector $j$ has $\binom{2}{j}$ slot components in $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$.

The moment of a bivector $X \in \Lambda^{2}V_{\C}$ on a state is $M_{X}(\Psi) = \ip{\Psi}{X\Psi}$, which defines the grip and the mass-squared of $\Psi$. The ten mode operators span $V_{\C} \oplus R_{2} \oplus \overline{R}_{2}$, split into rung vectors and pair vectors, and in occupation numbers the hypercharge generator is $y = 3N_{R} - 2N_{W}$ and $2T_{3} = N_{4} - N_{5}$.
obj.standard-model.two-rung-module-secto.lay: This definition sets up the state space used for matter with two extra rungs of the transport tower: five pairs of creation and annihilation operations, three from the conformal spinor's own pairs and two from the rungs. States are sorted by how many rung modes and how many pair modes are occupied, and a state's pieces along the rung directions are its slot components. Hypercharge and weak isospin are then simple counts of occupied modes.

pred.z6-charge-lattice.formal: The $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice: no fractionally charged colour singlet exists.
pred.z6-charge-lattice.technical:
The global form of the gauge group derived in the series is $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the full $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ quotient. Its representations satisfy $2t + 3\delta + q \equiv 0 \pmod 6$, equivalently $t/3 + \delta/2 + Y \in \mathbb{Z}$, for colour triality $t$, weak parity $\delta$ and hypercharge $Y = q/6$, so a colour singlet cannot carry fractional electric charge.

One confirmed fractionally charged colour-singlet particle would refute the identification of the gauge group with the automorphism group of minimal massive compositeness.
pred.z6-charge-lattice.lay: The series derives not only the Standard Model's symmetries but the precise way they fit together, and that restricts the charges particles can have. In particular, a particle that feels no strong force must have a whole-number electric charge. Finding even one such particle with a fractional charge would refute this part of the framework; searches so far have found none.
pred.z6-charge-lattice.typing_note: Kept the global-form basis; the source says the stance inherits the gauge-algebra theorem's premise, carried through the global-form result, and gives no standard-physics route.

refuted.the-number-n-is-a-coincidence-di.formal: The number N is a coincidence (Dirac)
refuted.the-number-n-is-a-coincidence-di.technical: Refuted at observation level only, and in part: the refuting Observation \claimref{standard-model.one-number-explain} is conjectured, unlike the refuters of the other refutations, which are proved. The corrected statement, that $N$ is one number appearing in every smallness problem, holds for the cosmological-constant problem ($G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$) and for gravity's weakness at the Hubble scale ($N^{-2}$), which are one number by the definition of $N$. It does not hold for the mass hierarchy: $\operatorname{Im} w = N\,(m/M_{P})$, to relative order $H^{2}/m^{2}$, carries the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2.0 \times 10^{-17}$, which, granting as Proposition \claimref{families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail} does that $m/M_{P}$ is invariant under the rescaling, is a second modulus kinematically not a function of $N$. What the series rejects is Dirac's reading of the coincidence as a law ($N$ a clock, $\Lambda$ decaying as $1/t^{2}$), on its registered and conditional prediction $w = -1$; the coincidence itself, $N$ equal to the present age of the universe in Planck units, the series holds to be a coincidence of the present epoch (Observation \claimref{standard-model.what}(iii)), and so too the Zel'dovich-Weinberg relation $m_{h}^{3} \sim M_{P}^{2}H$ (Proposition \claimref{families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail}).
refuted.the-number-n-is-a-coincidence-di.lay: Dirac noticed that some enormous numbers in physics have about the same size and asked whether this was chance. In this framework the tiny cosmological constant and the weakness of gravity are one number, N, the ratio of the Planck mass to the Hubble scale, though only by how N is defined, and particle masses need a second number besides. Dirac's own coincidence, that N matches the present age of the universe, is read as a feature of our era, not a law; the series rejects Dirac's law on a prediction that is itself conditional. So this entry is refuted only at the level of an observation, and only in part.

And the reading places every count between $2^{256}$ and $2^{2^{256}}$ between the same two levels: the corrected statement held when the mode space was put at order $10^{60}$ (between the second and third levels) and holds at $10^{122}$, so the count does not test it.
refuted.the-number-n-is-a-mystery-of-lar.lay: It once seemed natural to think that the very large number $N$, which appears in every smallness problem of physics, needs a special explanation because it is so large. That turned out to be the wrong question. On one unproved reading of the tower the programme builds, large numbers appear as a matter of course, so the puzzle becomes why the universe's horizon holds as few basic modes as it does, about $10^{122}$, roughly the square of $N$. The refutation stands only at the level of an observation: on the tower the series does prove, modes are added one at a time, and the reading would call almost any number small.

rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra.formal: Under (R) or (S), of the forty-five generators of $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ acting on the composite's modes, exactly thirteen preserve the slot-pair split and the mode number, spanning $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$; exactly twenty-five preserve the mode number, spanning $\uu(5)$; so thirty-two lie outside $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$, twelve of them inside $\uu(5)$, moving one excitation between a rung and a pair, and twenty changing the mode number by two.
rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra.technical:
Under the rung reading (R) or the slot-statistics hypothesis (S), the composite has five fermionic modes, two slots (the rungs) and three pairs, and the forty-five Majorana bilinears $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$ span $\so(10)$. Twenty-five of them commute with the total mode number and span $\uu(5)$; of these, the thirteen that also preserve the slot number and the pair number separately span $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$.

So thirty-two generators lie outside $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$: twelve inside $\uu(5)$, each moving one excitation between a rung and a pair, and twenty of the form $a_{i}a_{j} \pm a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j}^{\dagger}$ (up to factors of $I_{4}$), which change the mode number by two. The two centralisers are computed as exact kernels, of dimensions $25$ and $13$.
rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra.lay: Under the paper's rung reading (R), or equivalently Hypothesis (S), the composite's internal states are built from five on-off modes, two of one kind and three of another. Of the forty-five basic symmetry moves available on such a system, thirteen keep the two kinds separately counted, and these form the Standard Model's symmetry together with one extra charge. The other thirty-two either move an excitation from one kind of mode to the other, or create or remove two excitations at once.

proofs.main: Here the imaginary unit is $I_{4}$, which commutes with every mode operator (on the five-mode Fock module numbers, $I_{4}$ among them, act as scalars; as Clifford elements $I_{4}$ commutes with the rung vectors, and the pair vectors of $V_{\C}$ are complexified by $I_{7}$, which is not used here). The Majorana generators $\gamma_{2i} = a_{i} + a_{i}^{\dagger}$, $\gamma_{2i+1} = I_{4}(a_{i} - a_{i}^{\dagger})$ of the five modes (by \claimref{rungs.hyp-r-rung-reading} or \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) satisfy the Clifford relations, and the forty-five bilinears $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$, $p < q$, span $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}). The bilinears from one mode, $\gamma_{2i}\gamma_{2i+1} = I_{4}(2a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{i} - 1)$, five of them, and from two modes $i \neq j$ the two combinations $a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j} - a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{i}$ and $I_{4}(a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j} + a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{i})$, twenty of them, commute with the total number operator and span $\uu(5)$, of dimension twenty-five; the remaining two combinations from each pair of modes, $a_{i}a_{j} \pm a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j}^{\dagger}$ up to factors of $I_{4}$, twenty of them, change the mode number by two. Of the twenty-five, those with $i, j$ both rungs or both pairs commute with the rung and pair numbers separately: $5 + 2 + 6 = 13$, spanning $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$; the other twelve, with one rung index and one pair index, move an excitation across the split. The script computes the two centralisers as exact kernels, of dimensions $25$ and $13$, and exhibits the spanning sets.

rungs.hyp-r-rung-reading.formal: \emph{Hypothesis (R), the rung reading.} The internal state space of a composite of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor composite) is the spinor module of the $n$-th rung of the tower above $\Cl(2,4)$, $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{n})$, on which the transported algebra acts as in Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}: each conformal spinor of the composite occupies one new rung, and the constituents are the states with one rung occupied.
rungs.hyp-r-rung-reading.technical:
Hypothesis (R) reads the internal state space of a composite of $n$ conformal spinors as the spinor module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{n})$ of the $n$-th rung of the tower above $\Cl(2,4)$, with the transported algebra acting as it does on the tower. Each conformal spinor of the composite occupies one new rung, and the constituents are the states with one rung occupied.

It is a structural premise phrased in the language of the tower rather than of the composite's slots, and is taken as given by the results stated under it.
rungs.hyp-r-rung-reading.lay: This is an assumption, not a result: a composite of several basic spinor states is described by climbing the series' tower of algebras, one rung for each of them. rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group.formal: The mixings of a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) preserving momentum and helicity for every configuration are exactly $U(n)$, acting on the $n$-tuple $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n}) \in \C^{n} \otimes \CS$, $\CS$ the conformal spinor space, as $U \otimes 1$; the automorphism group of the hierarchy $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ is $(U(2) \times U(3))/K \cong S(U(2) \times U(3))$, and that of $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ has Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$, dimension seventeen; the tensor ledger $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$ contains no $(2,1)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~3.1, Thms.~4.1, 4.2, Prop.~5.3(2)]{ButlerT12}.
rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group.technical:
Three results imported from the Standard Model paper. The mixings of $n$ conformal spinors that preserve momentum and helicity for every configuration are exactly $U(n)$, acting on the tuple $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n}) \in \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ as $U \otimes 1$. The automorphism group of the hierarchy $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ is $(U(2) \times U(3))/K \cong S(U(2) \times U(3))$, while that of $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ has Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$, of dimension seventeen.

Finally, the tensor ledger $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3})$ contains no $(2,1)$: the exterior algebra of the hierarchy alone has no state with the $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ content of a lepton doublet.
rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group.lay: This entry collects three earlier results that the rung note builds on. Rotations that mix a set of basic spinor states of the conformal algebra without changing their total momentum or helicity form the unitary group. The symmetry group of the two-by-three structure is the Standard Model's group, while the three-by-three structure has a larger symmetry algebra, of dimension seventeen. And the simplest state space built on the two-by-three structure has no room for a lepton doublet.

rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registra.formal: The slot factor of the mass bracket transforms as $(1,1)_{1}$, unconditionally, and under (S) the state at $(2,0)$ is that same one-dimensional representation $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2}$. Given the content, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero or absent, the hypercharge assignment satisfying the anomaly conditions is unique; with a fourth singlet of free hypercharge a one-parameter family $Y + t(B - L)$ appears. Over the derived generation, which contains the lepton doublet, the trace ratio is $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$ (over the quark doublet and the singlets alone it is $9/26$), and the one-loop run with the measured couplings and the observed spectrum does not meet: the desert is dead and the running between the scales must change, through partner-like content or an intermediate symmetry. Under (S), in the untwisted action every abelian generator in the span of the two mode numbers except hypercharge fails three of the four anomaly conditions over the derived generation; in the action the state space carries, twisted by $\det^{-1/2}$, every abelian generator is anomaly-free, and the thirteenth generator of the five-mode ledger's automorphism algebra is the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, broken with the Pati-Salam algebra at the intermediate scale by the Majorana term of $\nu^{c}$, which leaves the determinant-one part of $U(2) \times U(3)$ as the gauge group below that scale. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~3.2, Prop.~5.8(1), (3), Thm.~5.5(3), Props.~6.1, 6.2, 10.7]{ButlerT12}.

rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one.formal: The $U(n)$ of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton} acts on the $n$-tuple $\Psi \in \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ of conformal spinors (twistors), $\CS$ the conformal spinor space, as $U \otimes 1$. Under Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) the rung-mixing $U(n)$ acts on the sector $\Lambda^{1}R_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W = \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ as $A \otimes 1$. The two actions coincide: the ladder of the Standard-Model paper is the mixing of the new rungs of the tower, restricted to the states with exactly one new mode occupied and an even number of old pairs. The same holds for the pair-mixing $U(3)$, which acts on $\CS$ by $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(B)$ in both.
rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one.technical:
The ladder $U(n)$, derived from preserving momentum and helicity, acts on the conformal-spinor tuple $\Psi \in \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ as $U \otimes 1$. The tower's rung-mixing $U(n)$ acts on the sector $\Lambda^{1}R_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W = \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ of the rung module as $A \otimes 1$. Identifying the slot basis with the new rung modes $v_{1}, \ldots, v_{n}$, the two actions coincide.

So the ladder is the rung mixing restricted to the states with exactly one new mode occupied and an even number of old pairs, and the same holds for the pair-mixing $U(3)$, which acts on $\CS$ by $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(B)$ in both. The content is that the identification of slots with rungs is available, not that it is forced.
rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one.lay: Two independent constructions produce a group that mixes several basic spinor states: one from requiring that total momentum and helicity are unchanged, the other from the algebraic tower the programme builds. On the states with exactly one new mode occupied and an even number of old pairs, and once the slots those states occupy are matched with the tower's new rungs, the two groups act in exactly the same way. This shows that the match between slots and rungs is available, not that it is forced, and it holds only on that part of the state space.

proofs.main: Both are $A \otimes 1$ on $\C^{n} \otimes \CS$ by construction, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton} for the first and Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) at $j = 1$, $k$ even, for the second; the identification $\Lambda^{1}R_{n} = \C^{n}$ sends the slot basis to the new modes $v_{1}, \ldots, v_{n}$. The $U(3)$ statement is Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) at $j = 1$ read on the $W$ factor. The proposition is definitional once the slot basis is identified with the rung basis; its content is that this identification is available, not that it is forced, and the script computes the rung operators of $\uu(2)$ on the sector and finds the ladder action and nothing leaving the sector.

rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two.formal: Given Facts \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung} and \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, Hypothesis (R) at $n = 2$ implies Hypothesis (S); and (S), together with the identification of the two slots with the two rungs, implies (R) at $n = 2$. At $n = 2$ that identification is a relabelling of two basis vectors, so (R) and (S) are equivalent up to it. Under either, the constituent hypothesis of T12's successor problem (6), a slot vector times a Dirac state with the slot mixing acting once, holds as the $j = 1$ sector; the derived generation is the even half of the module (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); the mass bracket is the pairing of Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}; and $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is the Bogoliubov group of the composite's modes.
rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two.technical:
Given the tower's one-qubit-per-rung structure and the Fock representation with its Bogoliubov group, the rung reading (R) at $n = 2$ implies the slot-statistics hypothesis (S), and (S) together with the identification of the two slots with the two rungs implies (R) at $n = 2$. At $n = 2$ that identification relabels two basis vectors, so the hypotheses are equivalent up to it: they share the module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$, its $(j,k)$ grading, the group action and the chirality $(-1)^{j+k}$.

Under either hypothesis, the constituent hypothesis (a slot vector times a Dirac state, with the slot mixing acting once) holds as the $j = 1$ sector, the derived generation is the even half of the module, the mass bracket is the frozen-point pairing, and $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is the Bogoliubov group of the composite's modes.
rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two.lay: The rung note offers two ways of saying what the internal states of a composite of two basic spinor states are: one in the language of the algebraic tower, one in the language of fermionic modes. This result shows that they say the same thing, apart from one relabelling that matches the two slots with the two new rungs. Either way, one generation of matter is the even half of the state space.

(S) speaks of the automorphism group of the hierarchy (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}) acting by $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ (the $U(n)$ action on the Fock space of \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}); the two groups are identified on the one-constituent sector by Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one}, and (R)'s clause that each conformal spinor occupies one rung extends the identification of slots with rungs, hence of the hierarchy's $U(2) \times U(3)$ with the rung-and-pair mixing group, to the whole module. With that identification the module, grading, action and chirality are (S) clause by clause. rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one.formal: The configuration space of two conformal spinors (two twistors) of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-mass-symplectic-area}, as a vector space, is $\CS \oplus \CS = \C^{2} \otimes \CS$, $\CS$ the conformal spinor space, eight-dimensional, carrying the continuous data $(\omega^{i}, \pi^{i})$, the parts of each spinor in the $E = -1$ and $E = +1$ eigenspaces at the origin; it is the sector $(j, k) \in \{(1,0), (1,2)\}$ of the two-rung module, which under $U(2) \times U(3)$ is, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, $(2,1)_{1/2} \oplus (2,\bar{3})_{-1/6}$, the antiparticle doublets $L^{*} \oplus Q^{*}$ in the orientation of T12's listing or $L \oplus Q$ in the opposite one. The two-particle tensor product $\CS \otimes \CS$, by contrast, has no $U(3)$-equivariant embedding in the module: it contains $S^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W)$, the six-dimensional $SU(3)$-irreducible $\bar{6}$, while every sector of the module is a multiple of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, whose $SU(3)$ content is $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$. And the mass bracket, the $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{2}\CS$ component of $\Psi \odot \Psi$ (Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}), is quadratic in $\Psi$ and lives in $S^{2}$ of the module, not in the module. So the module treats the composite as T12 does, as one tuple $\Psi$ with a slot index, and not as a product state of two conformal spinors.
rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one.technical:
The configuration space of two conformal spinors, as a vector space, is $\CS \oplus \CS = \C^{2} \otimes \CS$, eight-dimensional. In the two-rung module it is the sector $(j,k) \in \{(1,0), (1,2)\}$, which under $U(2) \times U(3)$ is $(2,1)_{1/2} \oplus (2,\bar{3})_{-1/6}$: the antiparticle doublets $L^{*} \oplus Q^{*}$ in one orientation, or $L \oplus Q$ in the other.

The two-particle product $\CS \otimes \CS$ has no $U(3)$-equivariant embedding in the module: it contains $S^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W)$, the irreducible $\bar{6}$ of $SU(3)$, whereas every sector of the module is a multiple of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, whose $SU(3)$ content is $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$. The mass bracket, quadratic in $\Psi$, lives in $S^{2}$ of the module rather than in the module. So the module holds the composite as one tuple $\Psi$ with a slot index, not as a product of two conformal-spinor states.
rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one.lay: A pair of basic spinor states of the conformal algebra could be described either as a single object with two slots or as two separate particles combined. The transported state space only accommodates the first description: it contains the two-slot object as one of its sectors, but has no room for a six-dimensional colour pattern that the two-particle description would bring. rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-.formal: For conformal spinors (twistors) $Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n} \in \CS$, where $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ is the conformal spinor space with complex unit $I_6$ (not the Dirac module $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ below), every pairwise bivector $Z^{i} \wedge Z^{j} \in \Lambda^{2}\CS \cong V_{\C}$ is a null vector of the complexified ambient space of $\Cl(2,4)$, decomposable by construction, and for $n = 2$, $m^{2} = 2|\varepsilon(n_{\infty} \wedge Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2})|^{2}$ by Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}. The transport principle iterates on the real ambient space $\R^{2,4}$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), and Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion} applied to it gives one further hyperbolic plane, unique, with a reciprocal total on the whole real cone, whatever $n$: the mechanism is a completion of one quadratic space and depends on no count of conformal spinors. The one-rung module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C v)$, of dimension sixteen, is $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$ as a vector space, the constituent space of (C), and the transported algebra does supply a $U(2)$ on the $\C^{2}$ factor: the unitary group of the rung's own Clifford algebra $B_{1} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{2}(\C)$, the commutant of the ground algebra. But that $U(2)$ contains the odd elements $v \pm w$ of the rung, which anticommute with the chirality operator; its chirality-preserving part is the abelian $\{1, vw\}$-span, a torus. So one rung gives (C)'s vector space with a $U(2)$ that mixes the chirality of the two constituent states, while (C), (S) and the ladder need a $U(2)$ acting within one chirality, which is the rung-mixing $U(2)$ on $\Lambda^{1}R_{2}$ of Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2), available at two rungs.
rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-.technical:
Each pairwise bivector $Z^{i} \wedge Z^{j} \in \Lambda^{2}\CS \cong V_{\C}$ of conformal spinors, $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, is decomposable, hence a null vector of the complexified ambient space of $\Cl(2,4)$, and for two spinors $m^{2} = 2|\varepsilon(n_{\infty} \wedge Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2})|^{2}$. Completing the real ambient space $\R^{2,4}$ adds one hyperbolic plane, unique, with a reciprocal total on the whole real cone, whatever the number of spinors.

The resulting one-rung module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C v)$, of dimension sixteen, is $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$, and the commutant of the ground algebra supplies a $U(2)$ on the $\C^{2}$ factor, the unitary group of $B_{1} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{2}(\C)$. Its odd elements $v \pm w$ anticommute with chirality, so its chirality-preserving part is only the torus spanned by $1$ and $vw$. A $U(2)$ acting within one chirality, as the constituent hypothesis, (S) and the ladder require, is the rung-mixing $U(2)$ available at two rungs.
rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-.lay: Any two basic spinor states of the conformal algebra define a null direction in the complexified larger space the programme works in, and completing that space adds exactly one new rung, whatever the number of such states. That single rung gives a state space of the right size for a two-state constituent, with a two-by-two unitary symmetry. But that symmetry mixes left- and right-handed states, whereas the constituent hypothesis, Hypothesis (S) and the ladder need one acting within a single handedness, as the weak force does; a symmetry of the right kind appears only with two rungs.
rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-.typing_note: Removed the null-momenta corollary, cited only as the parallel case (the completion applies "exactly as to R^{1,3}"); the other five edges are premises of the proof. Whether a given complex null bivector lies on the real cone is the nullity of its line for the reversion form $\Sigma$, the twistor form (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}), which a massive pair need not satisfy; the argument does not need it, since it is the real quadratic space $\R^{2,4}$ that is completed, and $\R^{2,4}$ is nondegenerate of mixed signature, so Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion} applies to it exactly as to $\R^{1,3}$ in Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}. One rung above $\Cl(2,4)$ has module $\Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C v) = \Sp \otimes \C^{2}$ and $T_{1} \cong A_{1} \otimes B_{1}$ with $B_{1} \cong \Cl(1,1) \cong \mathrm{M}_{2}(\R)$ acting irreducibly on the qubit and commuting with the twisted ground algebra $A_{1}$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}); after complexification $A_{1} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$, so the commutant of $A_{1}$ in $\mathrm{End}(\Sp \otimes \C^{2}) = \mathrm{M}_{8} \otimes \mathrm{M}_{2}$ is $1 \otimes \mathrm{M}_{2}(\C)$, whose unitary group is $U(2)$. standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-sl.formal:
Under Hypothesis (S), the bivectors $\tfrac12\gamma_{m}\gamma_{n}$ of the ten that preserve the split of the ten Majoranas into four slot and six pair generators are $6 + 15 = 21$ of the $45$. They close under the commutator and form $\su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$, with
\[
\su(2)_{L} = \operatorname{span}\bigl\{v_{4}w_{5},\ v_{5}w_{4},\ \tfrac12(N_{4} - N_{5})\bigr\}, \qquad
\su(2)_{R} = \operatorname{span}\bigl\{v_{4}v_{5},\ w_{5}w_{4},\ \tfrac12(N_{4} + N_{5} - 1)\bigr\},
\]
and $\su(4)$ the fifteen pair bivectors, which contain $\su(3)$ and $B - L$. The weak $\su(2)$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} is $\su(2)_{L}$, the slot mixing, and
\[
Y \;=\; T_{3R} + \tfrac12\,(B - L)
\]
exactly, with $T_{3R} = \tfrac12(N_{4} + N_{5} - 1)$. The other $24$ bivectors mix slots with pairs. On the sixteen, the commutant of the $21$ is spanned by $1$ and the rung parity $\chi$ ($+1$ on the slot-doublet states, $-1$ on the slot-singlet states). Hence the automorphisms of the five-mode state space induced by orthogonal maps of the ten that preserve the slot/pair split, but not the mode number, form $\mathrm{Spin}(4) \times \mathrm{Spin}(6)$, the Pati-Salam group, the stabiliser of the rung parity; preserving the mode number as well gives the $U(2) \times U(3)$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(2).
standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-sl.technical:
Under (S), write the ten Majorana generators of the five modes as four slot and six pair Majoranas. The bivectors $\tfrac12\gamma_{m}\gamma_{n}$ that preserve this split are $6 + 15 = 21$ of the $45$; they close into $\su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$, with $\su(2)_{L}$ the slot mixing, $\su(4)$ the fifteen pair bivectors, containing $\su(3)$ and $B - L$, and hypercharge exactly $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ with $T_{3R} = \tfrac12(N_{4} + N_{5} - 1)$.

The other $24$ bivectors mix slots with pairs. On the sixteen, the commutant of the $21$ is spanned by $1$ and the rung parity $\chi$. So the automorphisms induced by split-preserving orthogonal maps of the ten form $\mathrm{Spin}(4) \times \mathrm{Spin}(6)$, the Pati-Salam group, the stabiliser of the rung parity; preserving the mode number as well gives $U(2) \times U(3)$.
standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-sl.lay: Under the slot-statistics hypothesis, the composite's states are built from ten basic generators, four belonging to the slots of its two basic spinor states and six to the pairs. The symmetries that never mix the two groups form the Pati-Salam group, a known candidate for unifying quarks and leptons in which lepton number acts as a fourth colour. Within it, hypercharge comes out as an exact combination of a right-handed charge and baryon minus lepton number.

proofs.main:
The bivectors with both indices in one block span $\mathfrak{so}(4) \oplus \mathfrak{so}(6)$, which is Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}(a). The script builds the ten Majoranas as $32 \times 32$ matrices over $\mathbb{Q}(I_{4}) = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{Q}}\{1, I_{4}\}$, on the five-mode state space of Hypothesis (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), and confirms the Clifford relations, the independence of the $45$ bivectors, the closure of the $21$, that the displayed generators lie in the span of the slot bivectors and the identity and commute with each other, that $\su(3)$ and $B - L$ lie in the span of the pair bivectors and the identity, and $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ as matrices.

For the commutant: the five occupation numbers, shifted by $\tfrac12$, lie in the span of the $21$, and they take distinct values on the sixteen basis states, so a matrix commuting with the $21$ is diagonal in that basis. The off-diagonal entries of the $21$ connect the sixteen states into two classes of eight, the slot-doublet and the slot-singlet states, so the diagonal is constant on each class; $\chi$ is $+1$ on the first and $-1$ on the second. The script performs both steps.

The last sentence restates the first in the language of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(2): the orthogonal maps of the ten preserving the split form $S(O(4) \times O(6))$, whose identity component is implemented on the state space by $\mathrm{Spin}(4) \times \mathrm{Spin}(6)$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}).

standard-model.bidoublet-complex.formal: Under Hypothesis (S), a real vector of a rung plane, $x\,\gamma_{6} + y\,\gamma_{7}$ with $x$ and $y$ real, equals $a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$ with $b = \bar{a}$, so $|a| = |b|$. By Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern}, with the up-type masses read through the conjugate $c^{*}$, one rung vector $c = a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$, real or complex, gives $m_{u} = m_{d}$ at tree level. So $m_{t} \ne m_{b}$ needs a second independent doublet coupling, and a complex bidoublet, carrying two electroweak doublets, supplies one.
standard-model.bidoublet-complex.technical:
Under (S), a real vector of a rung plane, $x\,\gamma_{6} + y\,\gamma_{7}$ with $x, y$ real, equals $(x + yI_{4})\,v_{4} + (x - yI_{4})\,w_{4}$, with the imaginary unit $I_{4}$, which commutes with the rung modes, so its coefficients $a, b$ on $v_{4}, w_{4}$ satisfy $b = \bar{a}$ and $|a| = |b|$. Under the one-vev relations, with the up-type masses read through the conjugate vector $c^{*}$ as the Standard Model uses the conjugate doublet, a single rung vector gives $m_{u} = m_{d}$ at tree level whether it is real or complex.

Since $m_{t} \neq m_{b}$, a second, independent doublet coupling is needed; a complex bidoublet carries two electroweak doublets and so supplies one.
standard-model.bidoublet-complex.lay: Assuming the slots of the composite's basic spinor states behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), the field that gives quarks their masses in this construction points along the rung directions. Read as the Standard Model reads it, with the up-type quarks taking their masses from the mirror image of the field, a single such field gives the up-type and down-type quarks equal masses at the simplest level, whether the field is real or complex. The top and bottom quarks have very different masses, so a second, independent coupling is needed; a complex field of this kind, which carries two Higgs-like doublets rather than one, can supply it.

standard-model.chain.formal:
Under Hypothesis (S), take the derived content with one Higgs doublet from $M_{Z}$ to $M_{I}$, and above $M_{I}$ Pati-Salam with three generations, the bidoublet, the complex $(10,1,3)$ whose vev breaks it at $M_{I}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}) and, where named, the complex $(15,2,2)$; left-right parity is broken at $M_{U}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.left-right-parity-what-breaks-it}), so the $(\overline{10},3,1)$ is not light, and nothing else is light (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}(b)). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} gives $(b_{4}, b_{2L}, b_{2R}) = (-\tfrac{23}{3}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, \tfrac72)$ with a real bidoublet, $(-\tfrac{23}{3}, -3, \tfrac{11}{3})$ with a complex one, and $(-\tfrac73, 2, \tfrac{26}{3})$ with a complex bidoublet and the $(15,2,2)$; Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-two-loop-gauge-coefficients}'s generic formula gives, in the last case, the two-loop matrix $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2435/6 & 105/2 & 249/2 \\ 525/2 & 73 & 48 \\ 1245/2 & 48 & 779/3 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ (rows $4$, $2L$, $2R$).
\item[(2)] At one loop, with Lemma \claimref{standard-model.matching-traces} at $M_{I}$ and the inputs of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run}, the three couplings meet. With $x = \ln(M_{I}/M_{Z})/2\pi$ and $y = \ln(M_{U}/M_{I})/2\pi$ the solutions are exact rationals:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llllll@{}}
\toprule
bidoublet & $x$ & $y$ & $\alpha_{U}^{-1}$ & $M_{I}$ (GeV) & $M_{U}$ (GeV) \\
\midrule
real & $\tfrac{11901069}{3355625}$ & $\tfrac{5610391}{3355625}$ & $46.12$ & $4.3 \times 10^{11}$ & $1.6 \times 10^{16}$ \\[2pt]
complex & $\tfrac{25548992}{7116875}$ & $\tfrac{11220782}{7116875}$ & $45.69$ & $5.7 \times 10^{11}$ & $1.1 \times 10^{16}$ \\[2pt]
complex, with $(15,2,2)$ & $\tfrac{22055284}{6305625}$ & $\tfrac{11220782}{6305625}$ & $37.11$ & $3.2 \times 10^{11}$ & $2.3 \times 10^{16}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\item[(3)] In the language of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.one-threshold-exact-criterion}, the real-bidoublet chain is the one-threshold shift $\Dl = (-\tfrac{76}{15}, 0, -\tfrac23)$ at threshold fraction $f = \tfrac{5610391}{17511460} = 0.320$: the extra gauge bosons contribute $(-\tfrac{154}{15}, 0, -\tfrac{11}{3})$ and the $(10,1,3)$ contributes $(\tfrac{26}{5}, 0, 3)$, the bidoublet's light doublet being the Standard Model's. It satisfies Corollary \claimref{standard-model.direction-demanded-content-doublet-heavy}. Negative entries, which no added matter in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact} can have, are what gauge bosons supply.
\item[(4)] At two loops, from the record's central values, at record level:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llllll@{}}
\toprule
bidoublet & $M_{I}$ (GeV) & $M_{U}$ (GeV) & $\alpha_{U}^{-1}$ & $M_{U}$/bound & $\tau_{p}$ (yr) \\
\midrule
complex, with $(15,2,2)$ & $1.9 \times 10^{10}$ & $3.4 \times 10^{16}$ & $32.4$ & $6.4$ & $4 \times 10^{37}$ \\
complex & $1.4 \times 10^{11}$ & $7.9 \times 10^{15}$ & $45.1$ & $1.8$ & $2 \times 10^{35}$ \\
real & $9.2 \times 10^{10}$ & $1.2 \times 10^{16}$ & $45.6$ & $2.7$ & $1 \times 10^{36}$ \\
real, $(\overline{10},3,1)$ light & $4.4 \times 10^{13}$ & $8.9 \times 10^{14}$ & $40.7$ & $0.2$ & $3 \times 10^{31}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The bound is Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-proton-condition}'s; the last row keeps left-right parity down to $M_{I}$. With the $(15,2,2)$, $M_{I}$ moves between $1.8$ and $2.2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV across $\alpha_{s} = 0.1180 \pm 0.0009$. Keeping left-right parity down to $M_{I}$ fails the proton condition.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (one doublet or two, 2 November 2026).} The chain runs with one Higgs doublet from $M_{Z}$ to $M_{I}$, while the rung field is recorded as the elementary linear field with two doublets of hypercharge $\tfrac12$ (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}); above $M_{I}$ a complex bidoublet already carries two. standard-model.chain.technical:
Under (S), take the derived content with one Higgs doublet from $M_{Z}$ to the intermediate scale $M_{I}$, and above $M_{I}$ Pati-Salam with three generations, the bidoublet, the complex $(10,1,3)$ whose vev breaks it at $M_{I}$ and, where named, the complex $(15,2,2)$, with left-right parity broken at $M_{U}$ and nothing else light. The index formula gives the one-loop coefficients $(b_{4}, b_{2L}, b_{2R})$, and with the trace matching at $M_{I}$ the three couplings meet, with $x = \ln(M_{I}/M_{Z})/2\pi$ and $y = \ln(M_{U}/M_{I})/2\pi$ exact rationals; with a real bidoublet, for instance, $M_{I} \approx 4.3 \times 10^{11}$ GeV and $M_{U} \approx 1.6 \times 10^{16}$ GeV.

The real-bidoublet chain is the one-threshold shift $\Dl = (-\tfrac{76}{15}, 0, -\tfrac23)$ at threshold fraction $f \approx 0.320$, which satisfies the doublet-heavy direction; its negative entries are supplied by gauge bosons. At two loops, at record level, the chain with the $(15,2,2)$ meets the proton condition with $M_{U}$ a factor $6.4$ above the bound, while keeping left-right parity down to $M_{I}$ fails it. (Note, 2 November 2026: the chain uses one doublet below $M_{I}$, while the rung field is recorded as two doublets, the second heavy, about $2.5$ to $3.5$ TeV, on the working branch; the scales are not recomputed with the second doublet between a few TeV and $M_{I}$, an open item.)
standard-model.chain.lay: This result tests whether the three force strengths of the Standard Model can meet at a single high energy when the symmetry first enlarges to the Pati-Salam group at an intermediate scale. Assuming the slots of the composite's basic spinor states behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), and with the particle content the framework then supplies, left-right symmetry broken only at the unification scale and nothing else light, they do meet, with the intermediate scale roughly between $10^{10}$ and $10^{12}$ GeV and the unification scale near $10^{16}$ GeV. At two loops, from the measured couplings' central values, the most favourable version passes the proton-decay limit comfortably, while a version that keeps left-right symmetry down to the intermediate scale does not.

proofs.main: (1) to (3) are exact. The script builds the coefficients and the two-loop matrices from the component listings by the formulas of Facts \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} and \claimref{standard-model.imported-two-loop-gauge-coefficients}, solves the three linear equations of the one-loop chain exactly, with the matching of \claimref{standard-model.matching-traces} at $M_{I}$ and the inputs of \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run}, and substitutes the solutions back, and computes $\Dl$, $f$ (in the form of \claimref{standard-model.one-threshold-exact-criterion}) and the inequality of Corollary \claimref{standard-model.direction-demanded-content-doublet-heavy}. The content run rests on \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}, the $(10,1,3)$ whose vev breaks Pati-Salam at $M_{I}$, on \claimref{standard-model.left-right-parity-what-breaks-it}, which breaks left-right parity at $M_{U}$ so that the $(\overline{10},3,1)$ is not light, and on \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}(b), by which nothing else is light; the bound in (4) is the proton condition of \claimref{standard-model.imported-proton-condition}. standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spin.formal: The conformal spinor space $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ (twistor space) and its partner $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves of the ascended Dirac module (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the sector of a single conformal spinor $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ is their direct sum. Under $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ the two halves carry different content: $\CS$ carries $(1)_{0} \oplus (\bar{3})_{-2/3}$ and $\CSm{}$ carries $(3)_{-1/3} \oplus (1)_{-1}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3)), so the two halves are inequivalent representations of the group: the chirality split is visible to the internal symmetry, not only to the grading. The singlet spectrum listed by a single handedness is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(2)'s, and in particular the colour content $3 \oplus \bar{3}$ of the two halves becomes $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3}$ under it, which is the conjugation of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.weakness-examined-exotics-conjugation-hypercharge}. Moreover the conjugation is an operation inside the pair system: the dual of the grade-$k$ state is the grade-$(3-k)$ state with the full-system phase removed, $(\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes (\Lambda^{3}W)^{*}$, of weight $+2k$; and the two doublets at the level of one conformal spinor of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) are each other's duals, $(\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{0}W)^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}W$, and under (S) have opposite parity. Under (S) they are therefore one doublet and its antiparticle, not two candidates, and Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(1)'s listing choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.weakness-examined-exotics-conjugation-hypercharge}.
standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spin.technical:
The conformal spinor space $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and its partner $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves of the ascended Dirac module, the parity of the Fock grade, each four-dimensional (not the spacetime chiral halves $\Som$, $\Spi$ at a point, which split $\CS$). Under $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ they carry inequivalent content, $(1)_{0} \oplus (\bar{3})_{-2/3}$ on $\CS$ and $(3)_{-1/3} \oplus (1)_{-1}$ on $\CSm{}$, so the internal symmetry sees the chirality split, not only the grading. Listing by a single handedness turns the colour content $3 \oplus \bar{3}$ of the two halves into $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3}$.

Conjugation is a duality inside the pair system: $(\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes (\Lambda^{3}W)^{*}$, of weight $+2k$, and the two doublets at the level of one conformal spinor are each other's duals, $(\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{0}W)^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}W$. Under (S) they have opposite parity, so they are one doublet and its antiparticle, and the choice of listing is the particle-antiparticle orientation.
standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spin.lay: The internal states of a single basic spinor state of the conformal algebra split into two halves of opposite handedness, and the Standard Model symmetry treats the two halves differently, so handedness is visible to the forces. Describing everything in one handedness, as is conventional in particle physics, turns the colour pattern into the observed one. Under the slot-statistics hypothesis, the two candidate doublets are mirror images of each other, a particle and its antiparticle, rather than two separate particles.

proofs.main: The chirality statement is Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}. The content of each half is Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3) sorted by parity of grade: even grades $0$ and $2$ give $(1)_{0}$ and $(\bar{3})_{-2/3}$; odd grades $1$ and $3$ give $(3)_{-1/3}$ and $(1)_{-1}$. The two halves are inequivalent as representations (their $SU(3)$ contents $1 \oplus \bar{3}$ and $3 \oplus 1$ differ, and so do their weight sets $\{0, -4\}$ and $\{-2, -6\}$), so no intertwiner exists. The one-handed listing is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(2); conjugating the odd half turns its $3$ into $\bar{3}$, so the colour content becomes $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3}$. The duality: by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power}, $(\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes \det^{-1}$ as $U(3)$-modules, and under $B = \lambda^{-2}b$ the right side has weight $-2(3-k) + 6 = 2k$, the negative of the grade-$k$ weight, as a dual must. For the doublets, $(\C^{2})^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \det(A)^{-1}$ as a $U(2)$-module (the $2$ of $SU(2)$ is self-dual, $\varepsilon$ being the intertwiner), and under $A = \lambda^{3}a$ this has weight $3 - 6 = -3$ with $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ content $(2, 1)$, which is the content and weight of $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}W$; irreducible representations of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ are determined by their $SU(2)$ content, $SU(3)$ content and abelian weight (they are the irreducibles of $SU(2) \times SU(3) \times U(1)$ trivial on $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$), so the two are isomorphic. Their total mode numbers under (S, \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) are $1$ and $4$, of opposite parity. The script checks the weights $+2k$ and $-3$ on the explicit duals.
