standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder.formal: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. The ladder therefore reads: one conformal spinor, massless, internal group $U(1)$; two, the first massive step, internal group $U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$; three, internal group $U(3)$, with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$. (The groups are $U(n)$ themselves, not products: the map $SU(n) \times U(1) \to U(n)$, $(a, \mu) \mapsto \mu a$, is onto, and its kernel is $\{(\mu^{-1}I_{n}, \mu) : \mu^{n} = 1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by the determinant, so $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$; the distinction is treated in the section “The gauge algebra and the global form”.)
standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder.technical:
For $n$ conformal spinors, put the spinor parts $\pi^{i}$ (the $E = +1$ parts) in the columns of a $2 \times n$ matrix $\Pi$, so that the total momentum is $p = \Pi\,\Pi^{\dagger}$. A linear mixing $U$ preserves $p$ for every configuration exactly when $U^{\dagger}U = 1$, as testing on rank-one configurations and polarisation show, and unitary mixings also preserve the total helicity form $\sum_{i}\bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the summed reversion form.

So the internal group is exactly $U(n)$: $U(1)$ for one massless conformal spinor, $U(2)$ with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$ at the first massive step, and $U(3)$ with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ at three. Each is $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$, not a direct product.
standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder.lay: In this description a massless particle is one basic spinor state of the conformal algebra and a massive one at least two. Mixing the spinor states of a system among themselves without changing its total momentum or total helicity is possible only through unitary transformations. So one spinor state has a circle of internal symmetry, two have the group $U(2)$, and three have $U(3)$. These are genuine unitary groups, not simple products of a special unitary group with a circle.
standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder.typing_note: Self-contained computation; no edges needed, and the paper states no standard route.

proofs.main: Write $\Pi$ for the $2 \times n$ matrix whose $j$-th column is the spinor part $\pi^{j}_{A}$, so that the total momentum is the $2 \times 2$ matrix $p = \Pi\,\Pi^{\dagger}$, and write the mixing as $\pi^{i} \mapsto \sum_{j} U_{ij}\pi^{j}$, that is $\Pi \mapsto \Pi\,U^{T}$. Then $p \mapsto \Pi\,U^{T}\bar{U}\,\Pi^{\dagger}$, and preservation for every configuration is the condition $\Pi\,M\,\Pi^{\dagger} = 0$ for every $\Pi$, where $M = U^{T}\bar{U} - 1$ is Hermitian. (The products $\pi^{j}_{A}\bar\pi^{k}_{A'}$ themselves cannot be compared coefficient by coefficient: they are $n^{2}$ elements of a four-dimensional space, and are dependent as soon as $n \ge 3$.) Take the rank-one configurations $\Pi = a\,v^{\dagger}$ with $a \in \C^{2}$ and $v \in \C^{n}$ arbitrary: then $\Pi M \Pi^{\dagger} = (v^{\dagger}Mv)\,a\,a^{\dagger}$, so $v^{\dagger}Mv = 0$ for every $v \in \C^{n}$, and a Hermitian form vanishing on every vector is zero by polarisation ($v = e_{j}$ gives $M_{jj} = 0$; $v = e_{j} + e_{k}$ and $v = e_{j} + e_{k}I_{6}$ then give the real and $I_{6}$ parts of $M_{jk}$; the entries of $v$ and $U$ multiply twistor components, so numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{6}\}$, the conformal spinors' unit acting by right multiplication). Hence $U^{T}\bar{U} = 1$, that is $U^{\dagger}U = 1$. The helicity form $\sum_{i}\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot Z^{i}$ (the reversion form summed over the spinors) transforms by the transposed matrix $U^{\dagger}U$ and imposes the same condition by the same polarisation with $Z^{i} = c_{i}Z$ for a conformal spinor $Z$ that is not null for the reversion form (a null $Z$ gives no constraint, which is why the momentum argument, needing no such choice, is the one relied on). Conversely every unitary $U$ preserves both sums, since $\Pi U^{T}\bar{U}\Pi^{\dagger} = \Pi\Pi^{\dagger}$ when $U^{T}\bar{U} = 1$. Hence the group is exactly $U(n)$. The script confirms the polarisation step at $n = 3$: the nine constraints $v^{\dagger}Mv = 0$ for the nine vectors listed span the nine-dimensional real space of Hermitian forms on $\C^{3}$, so only $M = 0$ survives; it also confirms that the nine products $\pi^{j}\bar\pi^{k}$ of a generic configuration of three conformal spinors have rank four, not nine, which is why the argument must go through rank-one configurations.

standard-model.invariant-operators-modul.formal: The commutant of $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ acting on the two-rung module is fourteen-dimensional: the twelve sectors $(j,k)$ are pairwise inequivalent as representations except the two singlets $(1,1)_{0}$ at $(0,0)$, the vacuum, and $(2,3)$, the filled state, so an invariant operator is one scalar on each of the ten other sectors and an arbitrary $2 \times 2$ block on the span of the vacuum and the filled state. Those two states lie in opposite chirality halves, so the one off-diagonal invariant operator is chirality-changing. Restricted to the sixteen-dimensional even half alone the commutant is six-dimensional; under Hypothesis (S) that half is the generation, and an invariant mass operator on it is exactly one number per species, $(m_{\nu^{c}}, m_{u^{c}}, m_{Q}, m_{L}, m_{e^{c}}, m_{d^{c}})$, and the framework imposes no relation among the six.
standard-model.invariant-operators-modul.technical:
Under $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ acting on the two-rung module, the twelve sectors $(j,k)$ are pairwise inequivalent except the vacuum $(0,0)$ and the filled state $(2,3)$, both singlets $(1,1)_{0}$. The commutant is therefore fourteen-dimensional, $14 = 10 \cdot 1^{2} + 1 \cdot 2^{2}$: one scalar on each of the ten other sectors and a $2 \times 2$ block on the vacuum and the filled state, whose off-diagonal part changes chirality because the two lie in opposite chirality halves.

On the sixteen-dimensional even half the commutant is six-dimensional. Under Hypothesis (S) that half is the generation, and an invariant mass operator on it is exactly one free number per species, $(m_{\nu^{c}}, m_{u^{c}}, m_{Q}, m_{L}, m_{e^{c}}, m_{d^{c}})$, with no relation imposed among them.
standard-model.invariant-operators-modul.lay: The paper asks which operators on the composite's state space respect its full gauge symmetry. Almost every block of states is distinguishable from every other, so such an operator can only multiply each block by its own number, with one exception where two blocks look alike and can be mixed. Restricted to one generation of matter, under the paper's hypothesis about the state space (Hypothesis (S)), this leaves six independent numbers, one per species, and the framework places no relation among them.

proofs.main: The Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ is the traceless diagonal matrices on $\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3}$, so the weight of an occupation state is its five occupation numbers modulo $(1,1,1,1,1)$; the only two states with a common weight are the vacuum and the filled state, both of weight zero. An operator commuting with the Cartan is block-diagonal in weights, and the script imposes commutation with the ten off-diagonal generators $v_{a}w_{b}$, $a \ne b$, on such operators by exact sparse elimination, finding a solution space of dimension $14 = 10 \cdot 1^{2} + 1 \cdot 2^{2}$ on the module and $6$ on the even half, where the filled state, of odd total mode number, is absent. The chirality of the two singlets is the parity of $j + k$ (Hypothesis (S), \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), $0$ and $5$. The last sentence is the content of ``commutant'': the six scalars are free parameters of any invariant operator, and nothing in Facts \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} to \claimref{standard-model.imported-grip-area-casimir-form} or in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor} constrains them.

standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-mo.formal:
On $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2})$ define, in the occupation basis $e_{S}$, $S \subseteq \{1, \ldots, 5\}$,
\[
B(\psi, \varphi) \;=\; \sum_{S} (-1)^{|S|(|S|-1)/2}\,\varepsilon(S, S^{c})\,\psi_{S}\,\varphi_{S^{c}},
\]
$\varepsilon(S, S^{c})$ the sign of $e_{S} \wedge e_{S^{c}} = \varepsilon\, e_{12345}$. Then $B$ is nondegenerate, pairs each state with its complement only (even degree with odd, the $16$ with the $\overline{16}$), and is invariant under $\so(10)$: $B(X\psi, \varphi) + B(\psi, X\varphi) = 0$ for every bivector $X$ of the ten. In particular $B(\psi, \varphi) = 0$ for $\psi, \varphi$ both in the $16$: two sixteens have no invariant pairing without a vector between them.
standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-mo.technical:
On the five-mode exterior algebra $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2})$, define $B(\psi, \varphi) = \sum_{S}(-1)^{|S|(|S|-1)/2}\,\varepsilon(S, S^{c})\,\psi_{S}\varphi_{S^{c}}$ in the occupation basis, with $\varepsilon(S, S^{c})$ the sign of $e_{S} \wedge e_{S^{c}}$ relative to $e_{12345}$.

Then $B$ is nondegenerate, pairs each basis state only with its complement, so even degree with odd and the $16$ with the $\overline{16}$, and is invariant under the forty-five bivectors spanning $\so(10)$. In particular two states of the $16$ always pair to zero: two sixteens have no invariant pairing without a vector between them.
standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-mo.lay: The paper builds a natural way of pairing two states of a five-mode system: each pattern of occupied modes is matched with its complementary pattern, with a carefully chosen sign. This pairing respects the large $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ symmetry. Because complementary patterns have opposite parity, it never pairs two states from the same sixteen-state half, so a mass term between two such states needs an extra ingredient in the middle.
standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-mo.typing_note: Removed the twistor Fock-model fact: the proof only compares the pairing with that fact's three-mode version and verifies invariance directly. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: The forty-five elements $v_{i}w_{j}$ ($i \ne j$), $v_{i}v_{j}$, $w_{i}w_{j}$ ($i < j$) and $v_{i}w_{i} - \tfrac12$ are linearly independent (the script computes their rank as $45$) and span the bivectors of the ten, which is $\so(10)$ (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}). Invariance under a basis of the Lie algebra is invariance under the connected group, so it suffices to check $B(Xe_{S}, e_{T}) + B(e_{S}, Xe_{T}) = 0$ for the forty-five generators on all $32 \times 32$ basis pairs, which the script does exactly, all $46080$ identities holding. Nondegeneracy and the complement structure are read off the definition, since $\varepsilon(S, S^{c}) = \pm 1$; the degrees $|S|$ and $5 - |S|$ have opposite parity, so the $16$ pairs only with the $\overline{16}$, and the bare pairing of two sixteens vanishes, which the script also confirms on all $16 \times 16$ pairs. This is Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-model-twistor-space}'s pairing with five modes in place of three; the reversal sign $(-1)^{|S|(|S|-1)/2}$ is what makes the pair-creation and pair-annihilation bivectors act skewly.

standard-model.left-right-parity-what-br.formal: Under Hypothesis (S), let $D = \gamma_{5}\gamma_{9}$, one pair Majorana times one slot Majorana. Then $D^{2} = -1$ and $D = \exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\gamma_{5}\gamma_{9})$, a half-turn generated by a slot-pair mixing bivector; conjugation by $D$ exchanges $\su(2)_{L}$ and $\su(2)_{R}$ and maps the eight states of $Q$ and $L$ onto the eight singlet states; and $D$ anticommutes with $\chi$. Among the $210$ grade-four elements of the Clifford algebra of the ten, the Pati-Salam singlets form a one-dimensional space, spanned by $\gamma_{6}\gamma_{7}\gamma_{8}\gamma_{9}$, the product of the four slot Majoranas, which acts on the module as $\chi$. Hence a vev along the rung parity breaks $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ to Pati-Salam and, the rung parity being odd under $D$, breaks left-right parity at the same scale.
standard-model.left-right-parity-what-br.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), $D = \gamma_{5}\gamma_{9}$, one pair Majorana times one slot Majorana, satisfies $D^{2} = -1$, so $D = \exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\gamma_{5}\gamma_{9})$ is a half-turn generated by a slot-pair mixing bivector. Conjugation by $D$ exchanges $\su(2)_{L}$ and $\su(2)_{R}$ and maps the eight states of $Q$ and $L$ onto the eight singlet states, and $D$ anticommutes with the rung parity $\chi$.

Among the $210$ grade-four elements of the Clifford algebra of the ten, the Pati-Salam singlets form a one-dimensional space spanned by $\gamma_{6}\gamma_{7}\gamma_{8}\gamma_{9}$, which acts on the module as $\chi$. So a vev along the rung parity breaks $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ to Pati-Salam and, since $\chi$ is odd under $D$, breaks left-right parity at the same scale.
standard-model.left-right-parity-what-br.lay: In the Pati-Salam picture there is a symmetry that exchanges left-handed and right-handed matter. Under Hypothesis (S), the paper's hypothesis about the state space, this exchange is a half-turn that mixes one pair direction with one slot direction. The only Pati-Salam invariant of a certain kind is the rung parity, and the exchange flips its sign. So giving the rung parity a background value breaks the large symmetry down to Pati-Salam and breaks left-right symmetry at the same energy.

standard-model.majorana-element.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), $T = v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}v_{4}v_{5}$ sends the empty state $
u^{c}$ to the full state and annihilates every other state, so the mass form $B(\psi, T\varphi)$ on the sixteen has only the $
u^{c}
u^{c}$ entry: a Majorana mass for the right-handed neutrino. $T$ commutes with $\su(3)$, $\su(2)_{L}$ and $Y$, with $[B - L, T] = -2T$; inside the real span of the $21$ Pati-Salam generators its stabiliser is exactly the twelve-dimensional $\su(3) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \uu(1)_{Y}$, and its orbit spans the thirty-dimensional $(10,1,3)$.

So a vev along $T$ breaks Pati-Salam to the Standard Model algebra and gives $
u^{c}$ its Majorana mass at the same scale. It also breaks the thirteenth generator, which lies in $\su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ as $X = 2T_{3R} - 	frac32(B - L)$.
standard-model.majorana-element.lay: Assuming the slots behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), a particular element built from all five creation operators turns the empty state, the right-handed neutrino, into the completely filled state and does nothing else. Used as a mass term it gives only the right-handed neutrino a mass, of the kind a neutral particle can have on its own. Among the Pati-Salam symmetries, those that leave the element unchanged are exactly those of the Standard Model, so a background value along it breaks the larger Pati-Salam symmetry to the Standard Model and gives that neutrino its mass at the same energy.

standard-model.matching-traces.formal:
On the sixteen,
\[
\tr T_{3L}^{2} \;=\; \tr T_{3R}^{2} \;=\; 2, \qquad \tr\,(B - L)^{2} \;=\; \tfrac{16}{3}, \qquad \tr Y^{2} \;=\; \tfrac{10}{3}.
\]
Consequently, at a scale where $\su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ breaks to $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)_{Y}$, the inverse couplings in the normalisation of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-one-loop-running-trace-ratio}(a) match as
\[
a_{1} \;=\; \tfrac35\, a_{2R} + \tfrac25\, a_{4}, \qquad a_{2} \;=\; a_{2L}, \qquad a_{3} \;=\; a_{4}.
\]
standard-model.matching-traces.technical:
On the sixteen, $\tr T_{3L}^{2} = \tr T_{3R}^{2} = 2$, $\tr (B - L)^{2} = \tfrac{16}{3}$ and $\tr Y^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3}$. In the trace normalisation of the one-loop running fact, the $\su(4)$ generator along $B - L$ is $T_{BL} = \sqrt{3/8}\,(B - L)$ and $Y = T_{3R} + \sqrt{2/3}\,T_{BL}$.

Hence, where $\su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ breaks to $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)_{Y}$, the inverse couplings match as $a_{1} = \tfrac35 a_{2R} + \tfrac25 a_{4}$, $a_{2} = a_{2L}$ and $a_{3} = a_{4}$; the weights are the trace ratios $\tr T_{3R}^{2}/\tr Y^{2} = \tfrac35$ and $\tfrac14\tr(B - L)^{2}/\tr Y^{2} = \tfrac25$.
standard-model.matching-traces.lay: When the larger Pati-Salam symmetry breaks to the Standard Model at some energy, the strengths of the forces on either side must be joined up correctly. The paper reads the joining rule off simple traces of the charges over one generation. The hypercharge force takes three fifths of its inverse strength from the right-handed weak force and two fifths from the four-colour force, while the left-handed weak force and colour carry straight through.

standard-model.module-factorises-even-gr.technical:
The five-mode Fock module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2}) = \Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{2}$ is the irreducible module of the complexified two-rung algebra $T_{2} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{32}(\C)$. With the pair modes ordered before the rung modes, every vector of $V_{\C}$ acts as $x_{W} \otimes 1$, so every element of the even ground subalgebra, including every generator of $\so(2,4)$, acts on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ alone.

A rung vector acts as $(-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R}$, so ground and rung vectors anticommute while products of two rung vectors act as $1 \otimes Y_{R}$. Consequently $\so(V_{\C})$ and $\so(R_{2} \oplus \overline{R}_{2})$ commute elementwise, and $\so(V_{\C})$ commutes with the rung number $N_{R}$ and with the rung mixing $\uu(2)$.
standard-model.module-factorises-even-gr.lay: The paper's state space for a composite is built from five modes: three from the internal pairs of the original conformal spinor and two added by later steps of the transport construction. This result shows that the space splits cleanly into a pair part and a rung part. The original conformal symmetries act on the pair part only, and the symmetries of the added rungs act on the rung part only, so the two sets of symmetries never interfere.
standard-model.module-factorises-even-gr.typing_note: Added the imported Cauchy fact because the proof uses its direct-sum formula for exterior algebras (cited there to the same Fulton-Harris locator); kept the tower Fock-module fact.

proofs.main: By Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}, $T_{2} \cong \Cl(2,4) \otimes \mathrm{M}_{4}(\R)$, so $T_{2} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{8}(\C) \otimes \mathrm{M}_{4}(\C) = \mathrm{M}_{32}(\C)$, whose irreducible module is unique up to isomorphism and is the Fock module of any five anticommuting mode pairs; the three pairs of $W$ with $\overline{W}$ and the two rung pairs $(v_{a}, w_{a})$ are such a set, and their Fock module is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2}) = \Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{2}$ by the direct-sum formula for exterior algebras \cite[App.~B.2]{FultonHarris1991} (\claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power}). Realise the mode operators in the Jordan-Wigner form on the occupation basis, modes $1, 2, 3$ of $W$ before modes $4, 5$ of $R_{2}$: the creation and annihilation operators of mode $i$ carry the sign $(-1)^{\#\{\text{occupied modes below } i\}}$. For $i \le 3$ that sign involves pair modes only, so the operator is $x_{W} \otimes 1$; for $i \in \{4, 5\}$ it involves all three pair modes, giving $(-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R}$. This is (1) for vectors, and products of two vectors of $V_{\C}$ are products of operators of the form $x_{W} \otimes 1$, hence $X_{W} \otimes 1$; the even ground subalgebra is spanned by such products. (2): $(x_{W} \otimes 1)((-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R}) = -((-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R})(x_{W} \otimes 1)$ since a vector of $V_{\C}$ changes the pair number by one and so anticommutes with $(-1)^{N_{W}}$; two rung vectors give $((-1)^{N_{W}})^{2} \otimes Y_{R} = 1 \otimes Y_{R}$. (3) follows: operators of the forms $X_{W} \otimes 1$ and $1 \otimes Y_{R}$ commute, and $N_{R}$ and the $v_{a}w_{b}$ are of the second form. The untwisted bivectors used here are the twisted ones of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} up to sign, since $x\omega_{1}\omega_{2}\,y\omega_{1}\omega_{2} = \pm xy\,(\omega_{1}\omega_{2})^{2} = \pm xy$, so (3) is also the statement that $A_{2}$ and $B_{2}$ commute, read on the even part. The script builds the $32$-dimensional module exactly and checks: the Clifford relations of the five pairs; that every one of the fifteen bivectors of $V_{\C}$ has the block form $X_{W} \otimes 1_{4}$ (the same $8 \times 8$ block on each of the four rung states, no element between rung states); that every vector of $V_{\C}$ has that form and no rung vector does; that vectors of the two kinds anticommute; and that every bivector of $V_{\C}$ commutes with $N_{R}$, with the four $v_{a}w_{b}$, and with every bivector of the rung plane.

standard-model.no-spectator-slots.formal:
\emph{Premise (no spectator).} The slot operators of a composite are elements of the complexified floor $F_{\C}$, $F = \Cl(5,5)$, spanned by the composite's own five rungs, the three carrying its pair modes and the two carrying its slots: they borrow no generator from the conformal base $\Cl(2,4)$, nor from any other rung of the tower.

\emph{What it is for.} For two-level, $U(2)$-covariant slot operators that commute or anticommute with every pair operator, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(ii) and (iii) show that inside $F$ the slots are odd, and that the five modes then carry every clause of Hypothesis (S) with the tower grading as chirality; by clause (iv) there, one generator outside $F$, which every floor of the tower supplies (the base generators among them), already allows even slots, for which the tower grading is not the chirality (S) declares. This is a route to odd slots independent of the anomaly route of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content}, which fixes the same parity from anomaly freedom of the particle half under the slot-module hypothesis \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if the slot operators of a composite are shown to need a generator outside its five-rung floor: for example, if a derivation of the slot operators from the tower places them as Klein-twisted products $v_{k}g$ with a base generator $g$, or if an observable of the composite's slot sector is shown to be even in the tower grading. Its failure alone does not make the slots even: the anomaly route still forces odd slots wherever the slot-module hypothesis holds.
standard-model.no-spectator-slots.technical: The composite's three pair modes sit on three rungs of a floor of the tower, and its two slots on two more. The premise is that the slot operators are built from those five rungs alone, with no help from the four generators of the conformal base or from any other rung. Inside such a floor two fermionic slot modes cannot be even, since the even part of the pair algebra's commutant is eight-dimensional and two fermionic modes generate sixteen dimensions, so the slots are odd, and the composite's thirty-two states, its $U(2) \times U(3)$ action and its chirality, read as the tower grading, are those of Hypothesis (S). With one generator from outside, even slots exist and the tower grading stops being the chirality. Every floor contains such outside generators, so this is an assumption about where slot operators live, weaker than identifying slots with rung vectors. It gives odd slots by a route independent of anomaly cancellation. It would be refuted by a derivation that places the slot operators outside the composite's own floor.
standard-model.no-spectator-slots.lay: Each particle in this framework is built from a few basic quantum modes, sitting on a few levels of a ladder of mathematical structures. This assumption says that the operators describing two particular modes of a particle, its slots, are built only from the levels that particle itself occupies, and borrow nothing from the shared spacetime levels underneath. With that restriction the slots must behave like fermions of a particular kind, which gives the handedness of particles the framework needs. It is a second, independent argument for the same conclusion that anomaly cancellation gives.

standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contribu.formal: Under the sector decomposition of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-sectors-superselection-mirror-copy}, let $\phi$ be any field of a tower other than this one, of either statistics and any multiplicity. Then $\phi$ has index zero under each of $SU(2)$, $SU(3)$ and $U(1)_{Y}$ of this tower, and contributes zero to each of $b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ at every scale. Consequently the mirror tower and the four odd-dimensional towers together contribute $\Dl = (0, 0, 0)$ to this tower's one-loop run, and the partner-like content Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run} demands, if the framework supplies it, is supplied by this tower.
standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contribu.technical:
Under the sector decomposition of the superselection fact, a field $\phi$ of any other tower carries no component of this tower's hierarchy bundle $\mathcal{H}$, since such a component would give a non-gravitational coupling between towers, which the decomposition excludes. As this tower's gauge fields are connections on $\mathcal{H}$, every generator acts as zero on $\phi$.

So $\phi$ has index zero under each of $SU(2)$, $SU(3)$ and $U(1)_{Y}$ and, by the index formula, adds nothing to $b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ at any scale, for either statistics and any multiplicity. The mirror tower and the four odd-dimensional towers therefore contribute $\Dl = (0, 0, 0)$ to this tower's one-loop run, and any partner-like content the running demands, if the framework supplies it, is supplied by this tower.
standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contribu.lay: The framework contains several towers, separate copies of matter; under its sector decomposition they interact with one another only through gravity. A particle from another tower feels none of our tower's forces, so it cannot change how the strengths of our forces vary with energy. Any extra particles needed to make our forces' strengths meet must therefore come from our own tower, if the framework supplies them at all.
standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contribu.typing_note: All four edges are premises of the proof and were kept; the spectrum-run context reference only names what the conclusion is about, so it was not added. Levels pass: the lay level now presents gravity-only interaction between towers as the sector decomposition the result is stated under.

proofs.main: By Proposition \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}, this tower's gauge fields are connections on this tower's hierarchy bundle $\mathcal{H}$, and a field is charged under them, that is, has a nonzero index under any of the three factors, exactly when it carries a component of $\mathcal{H}$: the index of a representation is $\tr(\rho(X)^{2})$ for a normalised generator $X$, and $\rho(X) = 0$ on any field on which the connection acts trivially. By Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-sectors-superselection-mirror-copy}, a field of another tower is a section of that tower's soldered bundle and acts within that tower's sector; it carries no component of this tower's $\mathcal{H}$, since $\mathcal{H}$ is built from this tower's soldering (the hierarchy fibre is the ladder of two conformal spinors of this tower's conformal completion, Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}), and a component of $\mathcal{H}$ would make the minimal coupling $\bar{\phi}\,\mathcal{A}\,\phi$ a non-gravitational interaction between the two towers, which Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-sectors-superselection-mirror-copy} excludes: the only inter-tower coupling is gravitational. Hence $\rho(X) = 0$ on $\phi$ for every generator $X$ of the derived algebra, all three indices vanish, and by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} the contribution of $\phi$ to each $b_{i}$ is zero, whatever its statistics and multiplicity and at whatever scale it is light. The script checks the arithmetic of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} on a field with all indices zero, for both statistics. The sum over the seven other towers is a sum of zeros.

standard-model.one-threshold-exact-crite.formal:
Fix record values with $a_{1} > a_{2} > a_{3}$ at $M_{Z}$, so $D_{12}, D_{23} > 0$, and a one-threshold spectrum $(b, \Dl)$ with $b_{23} > 0$ and $b_{23} + \Dl_{23} > 0$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $b_{12}\Dl_{23} \ne b_{23}\Dl_{12}$, the system \claimref{obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectrum-admissible} has exactly one solution,
\[
x = \frac{D_{12}\Dl_{23} - D_{23}\Dl_{12}}{b_{12}\Dl_{23} - b_{23}\Dl_{12}}, \qquad
y = \frac{b_{12}D_{23} - b_{23}D_{12}}{b_{12}\Dl_{23} - b_{23}\Dl_{12}}, \qquad
a_{U} = a_{3} - b_{3}\,x - \Dl_{3}\,y,
\]
with threshold fraction
\[
f \;=\; \frac{y}{x} \;=\; \frac{R\,b_{23} - b_{12}}{\Dl_{12} - R\,\Dl_{23}},
\]
every one of them a rational function of the record values and the coefficients; the transcendental $\ln$ enters only in converting $x$ and $y$ to scales in GeV. If $b_{12}\Dl_{23} = b_{23}\Dl_{12}$ the system has no solution unless $R = r_{0}$.
\item[(ii)] (Inertness.) Replacing $\Dl$ by $\Dl + c\,(1,1,1)$ leaves $x$, $y$, $f$, $M_{U}$ and $M_{I}$ unchanged and lowers $a_{U}$ by $c\,y$. In particular, by Lemma \claimref{standard-model.complete-multiplets-shift-all-three-coefficients}, complete multiplets of a simple unifying group with a common threshold do not move the meeting condition; they lower the unified coupling, that is, raise $\alpha_{U}$.
\item[(iii)] (The interval criterion.) The threshold lies in $[M_{Z}, M_{U}]$, that is $0 \le f \le 1$, if and only if $R$ lies in the closed interval between $r_{0}$ and $r_{\Dl}$. Given that, $x > 0$ holds automatically, and admissibility reduces to $a_{U} > 0$.
\end{enumerate}
standard-model.one-threshold-exact-crite.technical:
Take record values with $a_{1} > a_{2} > a_{3}$ at $M_{Z}$, so $D_{12}, D_{23} > 0$, and a one-threshold spectrum $(b, \Dl)$ with $b_{23} > 0$ and $b_{23} + \Dl_{23} > 0$. Eliminating $a_{U}$ leaves a linear system in the logarithmic scales $(x, y)$ with determinant $b_{12}\Dl_{23} - b_{23}\Dl_{12}$. When it is nonzero the unique solution is rational in the inputs, with threshold fraction $f = y/x = (R\,b_{23} - b_{12})/(\Dl_{12} - R\,\Dl_{23})$, and the logarithm enters only in converting to GeV; when it vanishes there is no solution unless $R = r_{0}$.

Shifting $\Dl$ by $c(1,1,1)$, as complete multiplets of a simple unifying group with a common threshold do, leaves $x$, $y$, $f$, $M_{U}$ and $M_{I}$ unchanged and lowers $a_{U}$ by $cy$. The threshold lies in $[M_{Z}, M_{U}]$ exactly when $R$ lies in the closed interval between $r_{0}$ and $r_{\Dl}$, and then $x > 0$ automatically, so admissibility reduces to $a_{U} > 0$.
standard-model.one-threshold-exact-crite.lay: When extra particles appear at one intermediate energy, the question of whether the three forces' strengths meet at a single higher energy becomes a small problem in linear algebra. This result solves it exactly, giving the threshold position and the meeting point as simple fractions of the measured inputs. It shows that adding complete families of particles at the threshold never changes where the forces meet, only how strong they are there, and it gives a clean test for whether the threshold falls in the allowed energy range.
standard-model.one-threshold-exact-crite.typing_note: Removed the table proposition (E301 cycle): the proof only runs its script checks on the table's spectra, and it is the table that applies this criterion; kept the complete-multiplets lemma, which (ii) invokes.

proofs.main:
(i) Subtracting consecutive equations of \claimref{obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectrum-admissible} eliminates $a_{U}$ and gives the linear system $b_{12}x + \Dl_{12}y = D_{12}$, $b_{23}x + \Dl_{23}y = D_{23}$ in $(x, y)$, whose determinant is $b_{12}\Dl_{23} - b_{23}\Dl_{12}$; Cramer's rule gives the displayed $x$ and $y$, and the third equation gives $a_{U}$. Dividing, $f = (b_{12}D_{23} - b_{23}D_{12})/(D_{12}\Dl_{23} - D_{23}\Dl_{12})$, and dividing numerator and denominator by $D_{23}$ gives the form in $R$. When the determinant vanishes the two equations are proportional on the left, so a solution exists only if $D_{12}/D_{23} = b_{12}/b_{23}$. The script substitutes the closed forms back into \claimref{obj.standard-model.one-threshold-spectrum-admissible} for every spectrum of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact} and checks the identity for $f$.

(ii) $\Dl_{12}$ and $\Dl_{23}$ are unchanged by the shift, so the $(x, y)$ system and its solution are unchanged; $a_{U} = a_{3} - b_{3}x - (\Dl_{3} + c)y$ drops by $cy$. The script checks this for three values of $c$ on every spectrum. Lemma \claimref{standard-model.complete-multiplets-shift-all-three-coefficients} supplies the content with $\Dl \propto (1,1,1)$.

(iii) For $t \in [0, 1]$ set $r(t) = (b_{12} + t\Dl_{12})/(b_{23} + t\Dl_{23})$, so $r(0) = r_{0}$ and $r(1) = r_{\Dl}$. The denominator is positive at both ends and linear, hence positive on $[0, 1]$, so $r$ is a M\"obius function of $t$ without a pole on the interval, with derivative $(\Dl_{12}b_{23} - \Dl_{23}b_{12})/(b_{23} + t\Dl_{23})^{2}$ of constant sign: $r$ is strictly monotone on $[0, 1]$, or constant when the determinant vanishes. Now the two equations of (i) say precisely $D_{12} = x(b_{12} + f\Dl_{12})$ and $D_{23} = x(b_{23} + f\Dl_{23})$, so $R = r(f)$ and $x = D_{23}/(b_{23} + f\Dl_{23})$. Hence a solution with $f \in [0, 1]$ exists iff $R$ is a value of $r$ on $[0, 1]$, iff $R$ lies between $r(0)$ and $r(1)$ by monotonicity and continuity; and then $x > 0$ since $D_{23} > 0$ and the denominator is positive. standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-.formal:
Under Hypothesis (S), let $c = a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$ be a fixed vector of the rung plane and $M_{c}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, c\varphi)$ the resulting mass form on the sixteen. Then the nonzero entries of $M_{c}$ have magnitude $|a|$ on $(L, 
u^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$ and $|b|$ on $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$. The up-type masses, and with them the neutrino's Dirac mass, are read through the conjugate $c^{*} =  ar{b}\,v_{4} +  ar{a}\,w_{4}$ of the tower's conjugation ($v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$, Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}), as the Standard Model gives up-type masses through the conjugate doublet: they are the entries of $M_{c^{*}}$ on $(Q, u^{c})$ and $(L, 
u^{c})$, the coupling to $c^{*}$, of magnitude $|a(c^{*})| = |b|$ with $a(c^{*})$ the $v_{4}$ coefficient of $c^{*}$, while the down-type and charged-lepton masses are the entries of $M_{c}$. So at tree level $m_{
u} = m_{u} = |b|$ and $m_{e} = m_{d} = |b|$: one coupling gives all four Dirac masses equal, the relations of a single real $10$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-spinor-bilinears}), and the neutrino's Dirac mass is the up-type mass, as the neutrino paper's top-like valuation takes it (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-ceiling-under-hypothesis-u-arrow}). Read through $c$ itself the up-type entry would be $|a|$, with $m_{u}/m_{d} = |a|/|b|$ set by the direction of $c$; on the null-lift locus that reading gives the product law $m_{u}m_{d} = \Lambda/3$, which the observed top and bottom masses rule out (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)), and it is not the series' reading. Under the reading through $c^{*}$ the direction of $c$ no longer separates up-type from down-type masses: the observed up-down hierarchy needs a second coupling or another source. The $v_{4}$ term couples only the $T_{3} = -	frac12$ components of $L$ and $Q$ and the $w_{4}$ term only the $T_{3} = +	frac12$ components: a vector along one rung breaks the slot $SU(2) 	imes U(1)_{Y}$ to the $U(1)$ that fixes it, the electroweak pattern. And doublet-triplet splitting, the requirement that the triplet partner of the doublet not acquire a vev and not stay light, is the requirement that the vector lie in the rung directions and not in the ground ones: the split is between what transport adjoined and what the ground completion already had.

\emph{Note (the covariant completion, 2026-11-01).} The reading through $c^{*}$ stands for the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion of the coupling: one family matrix $Y$ on $c$ and one $	ilde{Y}$ on $c^{*}$, each on the whole vector, so that $M_{d} = bY +  ar{a}	ilde{Y}$ and $M_{u} = aY +  ar{b}	ilde{Y}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}, with the second family matrix $	ilde{Y}$ independent of $Y$). standard-model.pair-count-dimension.formal: Let the ambient space of the completion in spacetime dimension $n$ have signature $(2, n)$, so that $V_{\C}$ has dimension $n + 2$ and carries a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form. If $n$ is even, a maximal totally isotropic subspace of $V_{\C}$ has dimension $(n+2)/2$, so the pair system of a conformal spinor (a twistor's pair system) has $(n+2)/2$ pairs; in dimension four it has three.
standard-model.pair-count-dimension.technical:
In spacetime dimension $n$ the ambient space of the completion has signature $(2,n)$, so its complexification $V_{\C}$ has dimension $n+2$ and carries a nondegenerate symmetric form. For $n$ even every such form over $\C$ is equivalent to the split form, whose maximal totally isotropic subspaces have dimension $(n+2)/2$; none is larger, since an isotropic $U$ satisfies $U \subseteq U^{\perp}$ and so $2\dim U \le n+2$.

A conformal spinor is the Fock vacuum of the pair system built on a maximal isotropic subspace, one ladder pair per dimension, so its pair system has $(n+2)/2$ pairs: three in dimension four.
standard-model.pair-count-dimension.lay: A basic spinor state of the conformal algebra can be described as the empty state of a small set of paired switches, one pair for each independent direction of a special kind in the ambient space. This lemma counts those directions. In an even spacetime dimension n there are (n+2)/2 of them, which in our four-dimensional spacetime gives three pairs.
standard-model.pair-count-dimension.typing_note: Edge to the imported pair-system Fact kept as the source of the Fock-vacuum description; pure linear algebra with no completion dependence, so no standard-route derivation.

proofs.main: Here $V_{\C} = V \oplus I_{W}V$, with $I_{W} = I_{V}e$ the central pseudoscalar of the odd extension $W = V \oplus \R e$ of the ambient space $V$, which squares to $-1$ and commutes with every vector ($I_{7} = I_{6}e$ at $n = 4$; Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}), so its scalars are the field $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{W}\}$. Over that field a nondegenerate symmetric form on a space of even dimension $2r$ is equivalent to the split form, since every nondegenerate quadratic form over an algebraically closed field is equivalent to $x_{1}x_{2} + x_{3}x_{4} + \cdots$ (diagonalise, then pair the squares as $(y_{1} + I_{W}y_{2})(y_{1} - I_{W}y_{2})$). The split form on $\C^{2r}$ has the totally isotropic subspace spanned by $x_{1}, x_{3}, \ldots, x_{2r-1}$, of dimension $r$; and no totally isotropic subspace can exceed dimension $r$, because such a subspace $U$ satisfies $U \subseteq U^{\perp}$ and $\dim U + \dim U^{\perp} = 2r$. With $2r = n + 2$ the maximal isotropic dimension is $(n+2)/2$. A conformal spinor is the Fock vacuum of the pair system built on a maximal isotropic subspace (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), one pair per dimension, which is the count. In dimension four, $(4+2)/2 = 3$, the three pairs of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}.

standard-model.pair-mixing-not-colour.technical:
The pair mixing $U(3)$ is the unitary group of the Fock structure $v_{i}^{*} = w_{i}$ on a conformal spinor's own three modes. It is compact of dimension $9$, while the maximal compact subgroup of $SO_{0}(2,4)$ has dimension $7$, so it is not a subgroup of the conformal group; its generators $v_{i}w_{j}$ are bivectors and lie in $\so(6,\C)$, so the statement concerns real forms. Nor is it an internal symmetry: the commutant of $\so(2,4)$ on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ is two-dimensional, the scalars on $\CS$ and on $\CSm{}$, so no element of $\uu(3)$ commutes with the conformal algebra.

Hence the pair mixing is a Bogoliubov relabelling of which conformal spinor is called the vacuum. Colour acts on a separate label copy of the pair space carried by the hierarchy bundle, commuting with the conformal connection, so reading ``mass breaks colour'' off the pair mixing identifies two different copies of $\C^{3}$ and is a category error.
standard-model.pair-mixing-not-colour.lay: A basic spinor state of the conformal algebra has three internal modes that can be rotated into one another, and so does the colour label of a quark, which invites the idea that the two are the same and that mass breaks colour. This result shows that they are different. Rotating that state's own modes is neither a spacetime symmetry nor an internal symmetry; it only relabels which state counts as empty. Colour acts on a separate copy carried alongside, so the worry comes from confusing the two copies.

The script computes the commutant of the fifteen bivectors on the eight-dimensional Fock space by exact elimination and finds dimension two, and confirms that each $\uu(3)$ generator fails to commute with some bivector. standard-model.places-outside-state-spac.formal: The state space is not the whole of what this paper derives, and the demanded content, being split content, is more naturally sought where the series already has splits. Three places, in order of how much structure the series has for them, none of them a derivation. (a) \emph{The automorphism algebra.} The gauge fields lie in the adjoint of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, which is not a complete multiplet of any simple $G_{U}$ containing it (the $24$ of $SU(5)$ minus the $(2,3)_{-5/6}$ and its conjugate), and it is this incompleteness that gives the Standard Model's own $-\tfrac{11}{3}C_{2}$ its three unequal values. Fermionic content in the adjoint, the gauginos, is the split content the series' structure most nearly suggests, and Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact} says it is not enough alone: it needs the doublet content of the next place, and even then falls short at one loop. (b) \emph{The mass bracket.} Proposition \claimref{standard-model.mass-bracket-charged-singlet} shows the mass bracket to be a charged singlet under the $U(2)$ mixing two conformal spinors (the two-twistor $U(2)$), the order parameter whose condensate is the mass of the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11}; the Higgs doublet of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} is imported, not derived, and a derivation of the scalar sector would say how many doublets there are, which is the row ``second doublet'' of the table and the $\tfrac{1}{10}, \tfrac16$ of the higgsino row's scalar partner. (c) \emph{The slot/pair split.} Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-state-space-complete-multiplets} says the split must cut across the $SU(5)$ pieces and that the framework's one derived cut is between slots and pairs. The $\bar{5}$ of the scalar sector, a doublet and a colour triplet, is cut exactly there: the doublet is the slot part, the triplet the pair part, and a mechanism that gave the two different masses would be the framework's doublet-triplet splitting. No such mechanism is derived in the series. This is the structural form of the partner question after this subsection, and the section “The module's mass mechanism and the rung doublet” takes it up: not ``which tower'' but ``what sets a slot-mode mass apart from a pair-mode mass''. The same cut also enters as a gauge symmetry rather than as a mass difference: the automorphisms that preserve the split between slots and pairs are Pati-Salam (the section “An intermediate symmetry: the slot/pair split”).
standard-model.places-outside-state-spac.technical:
Since the state space alone cannot supply the split content the meeting condition demands, this observation lists three places where the series already has splits, none of them a derivation. (a) The gauge fields: the adjoint of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ is not a complete multiplet of any simple group containing it, and gauginos are the split content the structure most nearly suggests, though alone they are not enough and even with doublet content they fall short at one loop. (b) The mass bracket is a charged singlet under the $U(2)$ mixing two conformal spinors, while the Higgs doublet is imported; a derived scalar sector would fix how many doublets there are.

(c) The slot/pair split: the scalar $\bar{5}$ is cut exactly there, the doublet being the slot part and the colour triplet the pair part, so a mechanism giving slot modes and pair modes different masses would be the framework's doublet-triplet splitting. No such mechanism is derived in the series.
standard-model.places-outside-state-spac.lay: The particles of one generation cannot by themselves make the three forces meet, so something with uneven masses is needed. This note lists three places in the framework where such unevenness might come from: partners of the force carriers, the scalar sector that gives mass, and the split between the two kinds of mode in a composite. It is a list of places to look, not a result, and the paper derives none of them.

standard-model.proton-condition-candidat.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), at the record inputs, the meeting scales and unified couplings of the candidate spectra are the exact rationals of the one- and two-threshold criteria converted to GeV, and the lifetime is the imported estimate $\tau_{p} \propto \bigl(\alpha_{U}^{-1}M_{U}^{2}\bigr)^{2}$ set against the Super-Kamiokande limit. The three rows admissible at one loop meet at $M_{U} = 1.5$ to $2.5 \times 10^{14}$ GeV with lifetimes of about $2 \times 10^{28}$ to $2 \times 10^{29}$ yr, five to six orders of magnitude short: none meets the proton condition.

On the supersymmetric two-threshold segment the condition holds from the near-degenerate end down to $(f, f') = (0.868, 0.759)$, where $M_{U} = 5.6 \times 10^{15}$ GeV, and fails beyond it. The supersymmetric row at two loops, with $M_{U} = 1.1 \times 10^{16}$ GeV and $\alpha_{U}^{-1} = 25.7$, has $\tau_{p} \approx 3 \times 10^{35}$ yr and meets it.
standard-model.proton-condition-candidat.lay: If the forces unify, the heavy particles of the unified theory let protons decay, and experiments show that protons live longer than about ten to the thirty-four years. This result applies that test to the candidate particle spectra. The three that work at the simplest level of approximation make protons decay far too quickly, while part of a supersymmetric family of spectra, and the supersymmetric case treated more precisely, survive. All of it assumes the paper's hypothesis about the composite's modes.

standard-model.proton-decay-only-through.formal:
Under Hypothesis (S), write $n_{B}$ and $n_{L}$ for baryon and lepton number. On the sixteen
\[
n_{B} \;=\; \tfrac14\bigl((B - L) + \chi\bigr), \qquad n_{L} \;=\; \tfrac14\bigl(\chi - 3\,(B - L)\bigr), \qquad 3n_{B} + n_{L} \;=\; \chi,
\]
reproducing every species' baryon and lepton number. The $21$ generators of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are} commute with $\chi$, and the $24$ slot-pair mixing generators anticommute with it. The decay $p \to e^{+}\pi^{0}$ has $\Delta(B - L) = 0$ and $\Delta(3n_{B} + n_{L}) = -4$, so it is mediated only by the mixing generators, whose gauge bosons are massive at $M_{U}$.
standard-model.proton-decay-only-through.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), on the sixteen, baryon and lepton number are $n_{B} = \tfrac14\bigl((B-L) + \chi\bigr)$ and $n_{L} = \tfrac14\bigl(\chi - 3(B-L)\bigr)$, so that $3n_{B} + n_{L} = \chi$, and these reproduce every species' values. The $21$ Pati-Salam generators preserving the slot/pair split commute with $\chi$, and the $24$ slot-pair mixing generators anticommute with it.

The decay $p \to e^{+}\pi^{0}$ has $\Delta(B-L) = 0$ but $\Delta(3n_{B} + n_{L}) = -4$, so it changes $\chi$ and can be mediated only by the mixing generators, whose gauge bosons are massive at $M_{U}$.
standard-model.proton-decay-only-through.lay: In this framework each particle of a generation is a pattern of filled modes, and one operator counts a combination of baryon and lepton number. The symmetries that keep the two kinds of mode apart leave that count unchanged, while those that mix them flip it. The decay of a proton into a positron and a pion changes the count, so only the mixing symmetries, whose carriers are very heavy, can cause it. This holds under the paper's hypothesis about the composite's modes.

standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-.technical:
Under $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, with hypercharge $Y$ the abelian weight divided by six: (1) unconditionally, the cells of the tensor state space, $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$, transform as $(2,3)$ with weight $1$, so $Y = \tfrac16$, the quark doublet. (2) Under Hypothesis (S), the states with one slot mode occupied and the pair modes empty or full are $(2,1)$ with $Y = \pm\tfrac12$; without (S) the state space has no such states, its only row-filling states forming the $(4,1)$. (3) On the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{3}$, the grade-$k$ states are $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$ with $Y = 0, -\tfrac13, -\tfrac23, -1$.

So under (S) the fermion content at the particle handedness is $(2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2}$: a quark is one slot with one pair, and a lepton is one slot with the pair system full, which is why it is a colour singlet.
standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-.lay: The paper builds composite particles from basic spinor states of the conformal algebra, which have two kinds of internal mode, slots and pairs. One slot with one pair gives exactly the quantum numbers of a quark doublet, with no extra assumption. One slot with all three pairs filled gives a colourless doublet with the lepton's charges, but only if the slots are assumed to behave as fermionic modes like the pairs; without that assumption no lepton appears. A lone spinor state's modes give colourless and coloured states with hypercharges 0, -1/3, -2/3 and -1.

proofs.main: Write the $U(1)$ factor as $(A, B) = (\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$ with $a \in SU(2)$, $b \in SU(3)$, as in Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}. (1) On $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ it acts as $\lambda^{3}\lambda^{-2}\,(a \otimes b) = \lambda\,(a \otimes b)$: the $SU(2) \times SU(3)$ content is $(2,3)$ and the weight is $3 - 2 = 1$, so $Y = 1/6$. (2) Under (S, \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W) = \bigoplus_{j,k}\Lambda^{j}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power}), and on the $(j, k)$ component the $U(1)$ factor acts by $\lambda^{3j - 2k}$. The $SU(3)$-invariant lines of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ are $\Lambda^{0}W$ and $\Lambda^{3}W$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), on which $b$ acts trivially; so the $(1, 0)$ component is $\lambda^{3}a \otimes 1$, content $(2,1)$, weight $3$, and the $(1, 3)$ component is $\lambda^{3}a \otimes \det(\lambda^{-2}b) = \lambda^{-3}a$, content $(2,1)$, weight $-3$. The negative clause: by Proposition \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space}, $(2,1)$ occurs in no degree of \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space}; and the row-filling states are the image of the cubic map $v \mapsto \bigwedge_{a}(v \otimes f_{a})$, whose $SU(2)$-span is $S^{3}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}\C^{3}$ (the map is the composite of $v \mapsto v^{\otimes 3}$ with the projection to $\Lambda^{3}$, and its image spans the symmetric cube), the $(4,1)$ of degree three, of weight $3$ since three cells are occupied. The script confirms this: with the unipotent $A(s)$ acting on the slot index, the transform of a filled row has components on four independent degree-three states with coefficients $s^{3}, s^{2}, s, 1$, so the $SU(2)$-span has rank four and is not a doublet. (3) The pair-slot factor alone acts on a single conformal spinor's pair system, $\lambda^{-2}b$ on $W = \C^{3}$ (a lone conformal spinor occupies no slot; under (S) this is the row $j = 0$, and without (S) it is the definition of the sector of a single conformal spinor); on $\Lambda^{k}W$ it acts as $\lambda^{-2k}\Lambda^{k}b$, so the content is $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$, which is $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power}, $\Lambda^{2}\C^{3} \cong \bar{3}$), with weight $-2k$. Lattice membership, $2t + 3\delta + q \equiv 0 \pmod 6$: for (1), $t = 1$, $\delta = 1$, $q = 1$: $2 + 3 + 1 = 6$; for (2), $t = 0$, $\delta = 1$, $q = \pm 3$: $3 \pm 3 \in \{0, 6\}$; for (3), $(t, \delta, q) = (0, 0, 0), (1, 0, -2), (-1, 0, -4), (0, 0, -6)$: $0, 0, -6, -6$. The script builds the generator $\mathsf{y}$ as an exact matrix on each of these spaces and reads off the weights $1$, $3$, $-3$ and $0, -2, -4, -6$, and confirms the lattice residues.

standard-model.raw-representation-conten.technical:
Under $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$, with the abelian charge the pair number, the Cauchy decomposition of $\Lambda^{k}(A \otimes B)$ with $A = \C^{2}$ and $B = \C^{3}$ gives the full Fock space of the minimal massive hierarchy degree by degree: $(1,1)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,\bar{3}) \oplus (1,6)$, $(4,1) \oplus (2,8)$, $(3,3) \oplus (1,\bar{6})$, $(2,\bar{3})$ and $(1,1)$ for pair numbers $0$ to $6$, of dimensions $1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1$. The upper degrees are the duals of the lower ones.

The sector of a single conformal spinor (massless) is $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{3} = 1 \oplus 3 \oplus \bar{3} \oplus 1$, graded $0$ to $3$.
standard-model.raw-representation-conten.lay: The paper's composite of two basic spinor states has six internal cells, two slots times three pairs, each of which can be empty or filled, giving 64 states. This result sorts those states by how they behave under the weak and colour symmetries and by how many cells are filled. A single spinor state has only three cells and eight states, which sort into a colourless state, a colour triplet, an antitriplet and a second colourless state.
standard-model.raw-representation-conten.typing_note: Both imported edges are the proof's sources and are kept; representation theory with no completion dependence, so no standard-route derivation. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: The Cauchy decomposition (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power}) degree by degree with $A = \C^{2}$, $B = \C^{3}$, restricted to $SU(2) \times SU(3)$, under which the determinant characters are trivial. $\Lambda^{1}(A \otimes B) = A \otimes B = (2,3)$. $\Lambda^{2}(A \otimes B) = S^{2}A \otimes \Lambda^{2}B \,\oplus\, \Lambda^{2}A \otimes S^{2}B = (3, \bar{3}) \oplus (1, 6)$, dimension $9 + 6 = 15 = \binom{6}{2}$, using $\Lambda^{2}\C^{3} \cong \bar{3}$ and $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2} \cong 1$. $\Lambda^{3}(A \otimes B) = S^{3}A \otimes \Lambda^{3}B \,\oplus\, S_{(2,1)}A \otimes S_{(2,1)}B = (4, 1) \oplus (2, 8)$, dimension $4 + 2\cdot 8 = 20 = \binom{6}{3}$; the third Cauchy term $\Lambda^{3}A \otimes S^{3}B$ vanishes because $(1,1,1)$ has three parts and $\dim A = 2$, and $S_{(2,1)}\C^{2} \cong \C^{2}$, $S_{(2,1)}\C^{3} \cong 8$ by the Fact. Degrees $4$ through $6$: $\Lambda^{6-k}(A \otimes B) \cong (\Lambda^{k}(A \otimes B))^{*} \otimes \det$ by the last clause of the Fact, and the dual of $(3, \bar{3}) \oplus (1, 6)$ is $(3, 3) \oplus (1, \bar{6})$, of $(2, 3)$ is $(2, \bar{3})$ (the $2$ being self-dual), as displayed. The case of a single conformal spinor is the exterior algebra of $\C^{3}$ directly (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), with $\Lambda^{2}\C^{3} \cong \bar{3}$. The abelian grading is the pair number: the scalar $e^{I_{4}\theta}I_{3}$ of the pair slot ($I_{3}$ the identity) acts on $\Lambda^{k}$ by $e^{I_{4}k\theta}$. The script confirms the graded dimensions ($1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1$; total $64$), the two $\binom{6}{k}$ splits, and the degree-two and degree-three Cauchy identities as identities of symmetric functions at rational diagonal instances; the identification of the Schur functors with the named irreducibles is the Fact's, not the script's.

standard-model.segre-lemma-automorphisms.formal: Let $m, k \ge 2$ with $m \neq k$. A linear automorphism $T$ of $\C^{m} \otimes \C^{k}$ that maps the set of decomposable tensors onto itself (equivalently, that preserves the Segre variety; $T^{-1}$ then preserves it too) is of the form $T = A \otimes B$, and if $T$ is unitary then $A$ and $B$ may be taken unitary. When $m = k$ the factor swap $u \otimes v \mapsto v \otimes u$ is a further symmetry of the decomposable tensors.
standard-model.segre-lemma-automorphisms.technical:
For $m, k \ge 2$ with $m \neq k$, a linear automorphism $T$ of $\C^{m} \otimes \C^{k}$ that maps the decomposable tensors $u \otimes v$ onto themselves is a product $T = A \otimes B$, and if $T$ is unitary then $A$ and $B$ can be taken unitary. The proof uses the maximal linear subspaces made of decomposable tensors, $u \otimes \C^{k}$ and $\C^{m} \otimes v$, which $T$ must permute and which are told apart by their dimensions when $m \neq k$.

When $m = k$ the factor swap $u \otimes v \mapsto v \otimes u$ is a further symmetry of the decomposable tensors, not of product form.
standard-model.segre-lemma-automorphisms.lay: A tensor product of two spaces contains special simple elements, products of one vector from each side. This classical lemma says that if a transformation of the product sends simple elements to simple elements, and the two sides have different sizes, then it must act separately on each side. When the two sides have the same size, swapping them is one further possibility.
standard-model.segre-lemma-automorphisms.typing_note: Classical lemma proved in full in the source with no premises; pure algebra and not in the store as an import, so no standard-route derivation.

proofs.main:
First, a linear subspace consisting of decomposable tensors lies in a single $u \otimes \C^{k}$ or in a single $\C^{m} \otimes v$: two decomposable tensors $u \otimes v$ and $u' \otimes v'$ with $u 
parallel u'$ and $v 
parallel v'$ have a sum of rank two, so any two elements of such a subspace share a left factor or a right factor up to scale; and if $u \otimes v$, $u \otimes v'$ ($v 
parallel v'$) and $u'' \otimes v''$ ($u'' 
parallel u$) all lay in it, the third would have to share a right factor with each of the first two, forcing $v \parallel v''\parallel v'$, a contradiction; so one factor is common to the whole subspace. The maximal such subspaces are therefore exactly $u \otimes \C^{k}$ (dimension $k$) and $\C^{m} \otimes v$ (dimension $m$). Since $T$ and $T^{-1}$ both preserve the set of decomposable tensors, $T$ induces an inclusion-preserving bijection on the linear subspaces contained in it, so it maps maximal ones to maximal ones; and since $m 
eq k$ a maximal subspace is identified by its dimension, so $T(u \otimes \C^{k}) = u' \otimes \C^{k}$ and $T(\C^{m} \otimes v) = \C^{m} \otimes v'$ for some $u'$, $v'$ depending on $u$, $v$. Hence for fixed $v$ the map $u \mapsto T(u \otimes v)$ is linear with values in $\C^{m} \otimes v'$, so $T(u \otimes v) = A_{v}(u) \otimes v'$ with $A_{v}$ linear and injective; and for fixed $u$, $T(u \otimes v) = u' \otimes B_{u}(v)$ likewise. Comparing, $A_{v}(u)$ is proportional to $u'$ for every $v$, so $A_{v}(u) = \lambda(u, v)\,A_{v_{0}}(u)$ for a fixed $v_{0}$; linearity of $A_{v}$ in $u$ and injectivity of $A_{v_{0}}$ give $\lambda(u, v) = \lambda(u + u'', v) = \lambda(u'', v)$ for independent $u$, $u''$ (here $m \ge 2$ is used), so $\lambda$ depends on $v$ alone. Set $A := A_{v_{0}}$ and $B(v) := \lambda(v)\,v'$; then $T(u \otimes v) = A(u) \otimes B(v)$, and $B$ is linear because $T$ is linear in $v$ and $A(u) 
eq 0$. So $T = A \otimes B$; and if $T$ is unitary then $(A \otimes B)^{\dagger}(A \otimes B) = A^{\dagger}A \otimes B^{\dagger}B = 1$ forces $A^{\dagger}A = c\,1$ and $B^{\dagger}B = c^{-1}1$ with $c > 0$, so a scalar rebalancing makes both unitary. When $m = k$ the factor swap preserves the decomposable tensors and is not of product form. The script does not check this lemma; it is classical, and the proof is printed.

standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis.formal:
\emph{Premise (slot module).} The state space of a composite is $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Shape.)} $W$ is the pair space of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}, so $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ is one pair system, and $F = \bigoplus_{n \ge 0}F_{n}$ is a finite-dimensional polynomial representation of the slot mixing $U(2)$, graded by the slot number $n$ (the scalar $\mu I_{2}$ acting on $F_{n}$ as $\mu^{n}$); $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}B$.
\item[(b)] \emph{(Hypercharge from the centre.)} The hypercharge is the abelian factor of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}, so that $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ on $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$.
\item[(G)] \emph{(Generation from a unique vacuum.)} The slot vacuum is unique, $\dim F_{0} = 1$ (multiplicity one), and the slot module is generated from it by one doublet of slot creation operators: some $U(2)$-equivariant map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ is onto for every $n \ge 0$.
\item[(CPT)] \emph{(Chirality a CPT halving.)} The chirality is an involution $\Gamma$ of $V$ commuting with $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ whose eigenspaces $V_{\pm}$ form a CPT halving, $V_{-}$ isomorphic to the complex conjugate of $V_{+}$; the particle half is $V_{+}$, labelled so that it contains $(2,3)_{1/6}$ (a choice of names: the other label exchanges particles and antiparticles). When the slot module is fermionic, so that clause (f) applies, $\Gamma$ commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain: the $21$ bivectors $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$ of the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f) that preserve the split of the ten Majorana generators into four slot and six pair generators, $\su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}; the intermediate stage of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.chain}). (For a CPT halving commuting with $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ whose particle half is anomaly-free, this is equivalent to $\Gamma$ being the grading of the joint Clifford system, every Majorana generator $\gamma_{p}$ odd, $\Gamma\gamma_{p}\Gamma = -\gamma_{p}$, which is the form of this clause in the previous version of the premise: both admit exactly $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$, Theorems \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(iii) and \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(ii), (iii). Without anomaly freedom the two forms differ: the pair-parity halving $\pm(-1)^{k}$ is a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra and is anomalous.)
\item[(f)] \emph{(One group of signed directions.)} When the slot module is fermionic, $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, and the ten slot and pair Majoranas, with the slot operators Klein-twisted ($\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}(-1)^{k}$, $(-1)^{k}$ the pair parity, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}), are distinct directions of one group of signed directions, Premises (F2) and (F3) (\claimref{synthesis.premise-minimal-non-commutativity}, \claimref{synthesis.premise-superposition-over-the-integers}), the sign bit acting as $-1$. Equivalently (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-an-instance-of-the-signed-direction-postulates}(i)), the twisted slot creation and annihilation operators and the pair operators of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ together satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, each slot operator anticommuting with each pair operator; so the Majorana combinations of all five modes generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$. Reading the ten direction labels as the distinctions of Premise (F1) (\claimref{synthesis.premise-the-bit}) is a reading, not part of the clause: (F1) enters only as the index set, the configurations $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{10}$ of the labels, not the $2^{5}$ occupation configurations of $V$. On $V$ the clause so read holds for every fermionic slot module, canonically up to a central unit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(v)); its content is the choice of the ten directions inside the group, which the postulates do not make (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-an-instance-of-the-signed-direction-postulates}(iv)).
\end{enumerate}
Neither the slot statistics, nor a tower parity of the slots, nor the chirality as a tower grading is assumed. Clauses (c), (d) and (e) of the earlier form of this premise (slots of one tower parity, chirality the tower grading, a unique slot vacuum) are replaced by (G) and (CPT); the unique vacuum is kept, explicitly, in (G).

\emph{What it is for.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3), a slot module generated as in (G) admits a CPT halving only if $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$, and then slot creation obeys exclusion, with no anomaly condition used. So (G) and (CPT) make the slot module fermionic, clause (f) applies, and $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ is the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$. Anomaly freedom of the particle half, the consistency condition of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, forces the chirality $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ on every isotypic component except the twice-occurring $(1,1)_{0}$, spanned by the empty state $\Omega = F_{0} \otimes \Lambda^{0}W$ and the full five-mode state $\Omega^{\top}$, where it leaves any line (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4)). The Pati-Salam algebra contains a pair-creation bilinear and its adjoint (the two-slot creation and annihilation in $\su(2)_{R}$), and commuting with one such pair fixes that line to $\C\Omega$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(ii), (iii)). So the chirality is the parity of the total mode number, with the labelling of (CPT) the particle half is the even part, one generation and the neutral singlet $\Omega$: this is the chirality of Hypothesis (S), and Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics} follows. Fixing the neutral-singlet line is the clause's whole content beyond the other clauses and anomaly freedom (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}): (a), (b), (G), (f), the rest of (CPT) and anomaly freedom leave any line in the neutral block; a chirality that also commutes with the total mode number has that line equal to $\C\Omega$ or $\C\Omega^{\top}$, so there the content is one bit, whether the empty or the full state is the particle half's neutral singlet; the two choices are exchanged by the swap of $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$, a unitary commuting with the gauge algebra, so no gauge quantum number decides between them, and the vacuum-swapped halving satisfies every other clause and anomaly freedom but commutes with no pair-creation bilinear, so not with the Pati-Salam algebra. The Pati-Salam form places the choice on structure the series registers: any gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ that leaves the number-conserving $\uu(5)$ fixes the bit, and none inside $\uu(5)$ does (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(iii)); since the chain is itself derived under (S), this exchanges the choice of $\Omega$ for a requirement on the chain's intermediate gauge algebra rather than deriving it, and the clause remains a premise. The slot parity is no longer a premise: if the slot quanta are tower elements of one parity whose tower grading is the chirality, that parity is odd (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4)). (G) fixes by hypothesis that the one-slot space is a single doublet; with a unique vacuum and $b$ doublets, anomaly-free halvings exist for every odd $b$, the extra doublets entering in vectorlike pairs (the same theorem, (2)).

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if a composite's state space is shown not to factor as a slot module tensored with one pair system (for example if a derivation of the composite from the tower gives a state space with no single pair system, as the tensor state space of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) has none); if more than one slot vacuum is found, which would show itself as $m > 1$ copies of each Standard-Model species per composite; if the slot module needs more than one doublet of slot creation operators, which would show itself as vectorlike doublet pairs beside the generation; if the chirality is shown not to be a CPT halving, or, for fermionic slots, not to commute with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain (for example a particle half whose neutral singlet is not the slot-and-pair vacuum, such as the vacuum-swapped halving with the full five-mode state in its place); or if the slot operators are shown not to anticommute with the pair operators, so that slots and pairs do not form one Clifford system.
standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis.technical:
This is the weaker form of Hypothesis (S). It keeps the shape of (S), a representation of the slot mixing $U(2)$ graded by the number of occupied slots, tensored with one system of three pair modes, with the hypercharge read from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$. In place of a slot parity and the tower grading as chirality it assumes two things: the slot states are built from a unique empty state by one doublet of slot creation operators, and the chirality splits the states into a left-handed half and its CPT conjugate and, once the slots are fermionic, commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra $\su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ of the series' chain, the operators of the five-mode Clifford system that keep slots and pairs apart. With slots fermionic, the ten real Majorana combinations of the slot and pair operators, the slot operators twisted by the pair parity, are distinct directions of one group of signed directions in the sense of the foundation's postulates of minimal non-commutativity and integer superposition, the sign bit acting as minus one; equivalently, slot and pair operators form one Clifford system of five modes, as before. Reading the ten direction labels as the foundation's bits is a reading, not part of the clause, and the clause's content is which ten elements of the group are the directions. It does not assume that the slots are fermionic modes, nor any tower parity for them.

CPT closure of a generated slot module already forces exactly the fermionic slot module, with the exclusion principle for slot creation and no anomaly condition. The five modes then carry the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$. Anomaly freedom fixes the chirality as the parity of the total mode number except for a free line among the two neutral singlets, the empty and the full five-mode state; the Pati-Salam algebra contains an operator that creates two slots at once, and commuting with it and its adjoint fixes that line to the empty state. The result is everything (S) states. For an anomaly-free halving this requirement is equivalent to the earlier form of the clause, that the chirality is the grading of the joint Clifford system (every slot and pair creation or annihilation operator changes it), or that it commutes with $\Spin(10)$; without anomaly freedom it is weaker, since the pair-number parity also commutes with Pati-Salam. Fixing the neutral-singlet line is all the requirement adds to the other clauses and anomaly freedom: for a chirality that commutes with the total mode number the freedom is one bit, the empty rather than the full state as the particle half's neutral singlet, which no gauge quantum number can see. Any gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ that creates or destroys pairs of modes decides it, and none that conserves the mode number does; the requirement trades the bare choice for one about structure the series already uses, without deriving it. The premise would fail if a composite's state space did not factor this way, if there were several slot vacua, which would duplicate every species, if more than one doublet of slot creation operators were needed, which would add vectorlike doublets, if the chirality were not a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra, or if slot and pair operators did not anticommute.
standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis.lay: The framework's account of quarks and leptons needed an assumption, called (S), that two particular ingredients of each particle behave like fermions. This weaker assumption replaces it. It says how a particle's possible states are organised, that they are built from exactly one empty state by adding quanta of a single two-state kind, that handedness splits the states into particles and their mirror-image antiparticles in the way every theory of fermions requires, with that split respecting the intermediate Pati-Salam symmetry the framework already uses, and that, if the ingredients are fermions, they combine with the particle's other fermionic modes into one system, which is the framework's most basic rule for directions (distinct directions anticommute) applied to ten of them. Those requirements, with the standard consistency condition that the theory be free of anomalies, force the ingredients to behave like fermions and fix which states are left-handed, so (S) becomes a consequence rather than an assumption. Respecting the Pati-Salam symmetry does one job the others cannot: it decides that the completely empty state counts as a particle rather than an antiparticle.
