synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-an-in.formal:
Let $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, be the composite space of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space} with its Fock inner product, $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}$ the Klein-twisted slot annihilators, $a_{1}, a_{2}$ the untwisted ones and $b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ the pair annihilators. For five operators $\alpha_{1}, \dots, \alpha_{5}$ on $V$ with adjoints $\alpha_{k}^{*}$ put $\gamma_{2k-1} = \alpha_{k} + \alpha_{k}^{*}$, $\gamma_{2k} = \alpha_{k} - \alpha_{k}^{*}$, and let $G$ be the group generated by $\gamma_{1}, \dots, \gamma_{10}$ and $-1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The clause is the postulates; proved.)} The $\alpha_{k}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes exactly when $\gamma_{1}, \dots, \gamma_{10}$ with $c = -1$ satisfy Premise (F2), in the form of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}, with $\gamma_{2k-1}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{2k}^{2} = c$; then $|G| = 2^{11}$, the $2^{10}$ blades $\gamma_{S}$ are trace-orthogonal on $V$, $c$ acts as $-1$ (Premise (F3)), and $\Cl_{\Z}(5,5)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra} acts faithfully on $V$. For $(\alpha_{k}) = (\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3})$ both hold. The sign bits of the slot and the pair systems are both the operator $-1$ of $V$, so beyond the two separate systems the clause adds only (F2c) for the $24$ slot-pair pairs: clause (f) says exactly that the ten slot and pair Majorana directions are distinct directions of one group of signed directions whose sign bit acts as $-1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The signature; proved.)} (F2) allows every signature; for Majoranas of modes it is forced, one direction of square $1$ and one of square $c$ per mode, so $(5,5)$. Its Gauss sum $\sum_{S}\gamma_{S}^{2}$ is $2^{5}$, as for $(10,0)$, so $\Cl_{\Z}(5,5) \cong \Cl_{\Z}(10,0)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(viii)), the class of the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The adjoint; proved.)} On $V$, $g^{*} = g^{-1}$ for every $g \in G$, so on the image of $\Z[G]/(c + 1)$ the adjoint is the anti-involution induced by $g \mapsto g^{-1}$; and the commutant of $G$ on the rational span of the occupation basis is the scalars, so the $G$-invariant symmetric form is the Fock form up to a scalar. The adjoint in the CAR is the one the group fixes.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What the clause chooses; proved.)} The untwisted family ($a_{1}, a_{2}$ with the $b_{p}$) generates the same group $G$, with the same squares, since the pair parity is $-\gamma_{5}\gamma_{6}\cdots\gamma_{10} \in G$ and the untwisted slot Majoranas are the twisted ones times it; but its $24$ slot-pair pairs commute, so it is not a family of signed directions. The content of clause (f) beyond (F2) and (F3) is the choice of the ten directions inside $G$, canonical on $V$ up to a central unit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(iv)).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Computed.)} In the occupation basis of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$: $|G| = 2048$, $-1$ central, all $90$ ordered pairs of distinct twisted directions anticommuting, squares $1, -1$ alternating, the $1023$ nonempty blades traceless and the $1024$ blades distinct up to sign; $\tfrac12(\gamma_{2k-1} \pm \gamma_{2k})$ equal to the Fock operators, adjoint to each other, with the $50$ relations of the CAR; $g^{\mathsf T} = g^{-1}$ on all $2048$ elements; commutant of dimension $1$ (and $2$ for nine directions); the untwisted family generating $G$ with all $24$ cross pairs commuting; blade squares equal to GA's for the sign vector $(1, -1, \dots)$, Gauss sum $32$, against $32$ for $(10,0)$ and $-32$ for $(0,10)$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Once the ten Klein-twisted slot and pair Majoranas are declared the directions (the postulates do not choose them, (iv)), clause (f) is the instance $n = 10$ of Premises (F2) and (F3); Premise (F1) enters only as the index set, the configurations $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{10} = G/\langle c\rangle$ of the ten direction labels, not the $2^{5}$ occupation configurations of $V$, and reading these labels as the foundation's distinctions is a reading, not a theorem; it asks for no adjoint and no signature beyond what the modes and the group supply. Together with the Klein-convention result, the clause has no content on $V$ beyond a choice of directions fixed up to a central unit.
synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-an-in.technical: Clause (f) of the slot-module premise asks that the slot and pair operators form one system of five fermionic modes, the slot operators anticommuting with the pair operators. Written in their ten real Majorana combinations, the anticommutation relations of five modes are exactly the relations of a group of signed directions, the foundation's minimal non-commutativity premise for ten directions, with the sign bit acting as minus one: distinct directions anticommute, and each mode supplies one direction squaring to one and one squaring to the sign. The group has order $2^{11}$ and its blades are trace-orthogonal, so the integer Clifford algebra of signature $(5,5)$ acts faithfully, and its Gauss sum puts it in the class of $(10,0)$. Neither an adjoint nor a signature is extra: the Fock adjoint is the group inverse, the invariant form is unique up to scale, and the signature comes from the modes. The untwisted slot operators generate the same group but commute with the pairs, so the clause's only content is which ten elements of the group are the directions, which the Klein convention fixes up to a central unit.
synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-an-in.lay: One assumption of the series about how a composite particle's internal states are built says that two families of internal switches, the slot and pair switches, behave as one combined set of fermionic switches. The series' foundation starts from even simpler assumptions: independent yes-or-no distinctions, which become directions whose order matters by a single sign. This result shows that, once ten particular combinations of the switches are chosen as the directions, the assumption about the switches is exactly the foundation's assumption about directions applied to those ten, and nothing more: the rule for adjoints and the pattern of squares that the assumption seems to need are already supplied by the directions themselves. What the assumption fixes is only which ten elements of a given group are called directions, a choice made canonical earlier.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ with $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$ is the composite space of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}, with its Fock inner product (Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.fock-representation}); there the Klein-twisted slot operators $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}$ and the pair operators $b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, with adjoints the Fock adjoints (its (i), (ii)), and the untwisted $a_{i}$ commute with the $b_{p}$. In the occupation basis of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ these are the Jordan-Wigner operators of five modes (slots first), and the check works there: $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ has the rational occupation basis and every Majorana combination below is a signed permutation matrix in it, so all statements are about real matrices and need no imaginary unit.

\emph{(i).} Write $\gamma = \alpha + \alpha^{*}$, $\gamma' = \alpha - \alpha^{*}$ for each mode, so $\alpha = \tfrac12(\gamma + \gamma')$, $\alpha^{*} = \tfrac12(\gamma - \gamma')$. Then $\gamma^{2} = \alpha^{2} + \alpha^{*2} + \{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\}$, $\gamma'^{2} = \alpha^{2} + \alpha^{*2} - \{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\}$ and $\{\gamma, \gamma'\} = 2(\alpha^{2} - \alpha^{*2})$, and for two modes $\alpha$, $\beta$ the four anticommutators of $\gamma_{\alpha}, \gamma'_{\alpha}$ with $\gamma_{\beta}, \gamma'_{\beta}$ are the images of $\{\alpha, \beta\}$, $\{\alpha, \beta^{*}\}$, $\{\alpha^{*}, \beta\}$, $\{\alpha^{*}, \beta^{*}\}$ under an invertible linear map (the change of basis above, applied to each factor). So the CAR ($\alpha^{2} = 0$, $\{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\} = 1$, cross anticommutators zero, and the relations with $\alpha^{*}$ obtained by taking adjoints) hold exactly when $\gamma^{2} = 1$, $\gamma'^{2} = -1$ for every mode and every two distinct Majoranas anticommute. On $V$, $-1$ is central with square $1$. If the CAR hold, the group $G$ generated by the ten $\gamma$'s and $-1$ consists of the $\pm\gamma_{S}$, $\gamma_{S}$ the increasing products; a nonempty $\gamma_{S}$ is traceless on $V$ (it anticommutes with an invertible $\gamma_{j}$, $j \notin S$ when $|S|$ is odd, which exists since $|S| < 10$, and $j \in S$ when $|S|$ is even, so $\operatorname{tr}\gamma_{S} = \operatorname{tr}(\gamma_{j}^{-1}\gamma_{S}\gamma_{j}) = -\operatorname{tr}\gamma_{S}$), while $\pm1$ has trace $\pm32$, so no nonempty $\gamma_{S}$ is $\pm1$ and the $\gamma_{S}$ are pairwise trace-orthogonal ($\gamma_{S}^{-1}\gamma_{T} = \pm\gamma_{S \triangle T}$). Hence $G/\{\pm1\}$ is elementary abelian of order $2^{10}$ with basis the images of the $\gamma$'s, distinct directions satisfy $\gamma_{i}\gamma_{j} = (-1)\gamma_{j}\gamma_{i}$, and $-1 \ne 1$: (F2) holds for the ten directions with $c = -1$ and $e_{i}^{2} = c^{s_{i}}$, $s = (0, 1, 0, 1, \dots)$, and the representation of $\Z[G]$ on $V$ sends $c$ to $-1$, so it factors through $A = \Z[G]/(c + 1)$ (F3). By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(v), (vii), $A = \Cl_{\Z}(5,5)$, and it acts faithfully on $V$ by trace-orthogonality of the blades. Conversely, if the ten operators with $-1$ form a group of signed directions with these squares, the identities above give the CAR for $\tfrac12(\gamma + \gamma')$ and $\tfrac12(\gamma - \gamma')$; the factor $\tfrac12$ needs the rationals, which the coefficients of the operators on $V$ already are. For the given modes the CAR hold (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(ii), and Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} for each Fock system), so the twisted slot and pair Majoranas are a group of signed directions of order $2^{11}$, which the check confirms directly: closure of order $2048$, the $90$ ordered pairs of distinct directions anticommuting, the squares alternating, the $1023$ nonempty blades traceless, the $1024$ blades distinct up to sign, and the recovered $\tfrac12(\gamma \pm \gamma')$ equal to the Fock operators and satisfying the $50$ relations of the CAR. The two sign bits of the slot and pair systems are both the operator $-1$ of $V$, so sharing one sign bit is automatic on $V$; what (F2) adds to the two separate systems is the anticommutation of the $24$ slot-pair pairs.

\emph{(ii).} (F2) leaves the signature free, but a mode determines it: $\alpha^{2} = 0$ and $\{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\} = 1$ give $\gamma^{2} = 1$ and $\gamma'^{2} = -1$, so five modes give the signature $(5,5)$ and nothing in the clause chooses it. The check computes the squares of all $1024$ blades as operators, finds them equal to GA's blade squares for the sign vector $(1, -1, \dots)$ (the quadratic form $q$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}), and the Gauss sum $\sum_{S}\gamma_{S}^{2} = 32 = 2^{5}$, the value of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(viii) for $p - q \equiv 0, 2 \pmod 8$, shared with $(10,0)$ (also $32$) and not with $(0,10)$ ($-32$); so $\Cl_{\Z}(5,5) \cong \Cl_{\Z}(10,0)$ by (viii), the class of the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f) (whose generators over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ are the five $\gamma$'s and the five $I_{4}\gamma'$'s, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(ii)).

\emph{(iii).} $\gamma^{*} = \gamma = \gamma^{-1}$ and $\gamma'^{*} = \alpha^{*} - \alpha = -\gamma' = \gamma'^{-1}$; the adjoint and the inversion are both anti-automorphisms of $G$ agreeing on generators, so $g^{*} = g^{-1}$ on all of $G$ (the check confirms it on all $2048$ elements, as transposes of signed permutation matrices). The inversion $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ of $\Z[G]$ fixes $c$, hence preserves $(c + 1)$ and descends to an anti-involution of $A$: the adjoint on the image of $A$ is the group's own inversion. A symmetric bilinear form $B$ on the rational span of the occupation basis is $G$-invariant ($g^{\mathsf T}Bg = B$) exactly when $B$ commutes with $G$, since $g^{\mathsf T} = g^{-1}$; the check computes the commutant of the ten Majoranas in $M_{32}(\Q)$ by a signed union-find on the entries ($K_{\pi(i)\pi(j)} = s_{i}s_{j}K_{ij}$ for each signed permutation) and finds it one-dimensional (two-dimensional for nine of them, the control). So the $G$-invariant form is the Fock form up to a scalar, and the adjoint used in the CAR is the one the group fixes.

\emph{(iv).} The pair parity $P = (-1)^{k}$ commutes with the slot operators and anticommutes with the pair operators, and for each mode $\gamma\gamma' = (\alpha + \alpha^{*})(\alpha - \alpha^{*}) = \alpha^{*}\alpha - \alpha\alpha^{*} = -(-1)^{n}$, so $P = -\gamma_{5}\gamma_{6}\cdots\gamma_{10}$ (the six pair Majoranas) lies in $G$. The untwisted slot Majoranas are $\gamma_{i}P$ ($i \le 4$): they lie in $G$, have the same squares ($(\gamma_{i}P)^{2} = \gamma_{i}^{2}P^{2} = \gamma_{i}^{2}$) and commute with every pair Majorana. So the untwisted family generates a subgroup of $G$ of order $2^{11}$ (the check computes it), which is $G$ itself, but it is not a family of signed directions: the $24$ slot-pair pairs commute and (F2c) fails. The group, its sign bit, its signature and its inversion are therefore the same in both conventions, and the content of clause (f) beyond (F2) and (F3) is the choice of which ten elements of $G$ are the directions; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(iv) that choice is canonical on $V$ up to a central unit. This is the extraspecial central product $2^{1+4}\circ 2^{1+6} \cong 2^{1+10}$ of the slot and pair groups, read with two different generating sets (prior art; not used).

\emph{Status.} Transport-absent. (F1) enters only as the index set $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{10} = G/\langle c\rangle$ of the ten direction labels (not the $2^{5}$ occupation configurations of $V$); identifying these labels with the foundation's distinctions is a reading. The equivalence of the CAR with the Clifford relations of the Majoranas in (i) is classical (Jordan and Wigner), derived here for completeness. Nothing here derives clause (f) from tower structure; it shows that, on $V$, the clause is the statement of Premises (F2) and (F3) for the ten slot and pair Majorana directions, with no further content.

synthesis.majorana-scale-not-carried-by-.formal:
Let $v_{a}, w_{a}$ ($a = 1, \dots, 5$) be the mode vectors of the ten of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}, $v_{a}w_{b} + w_{b}v_{a} = \delta_{ab}$, with pair slots $a = 1, 2, 3$ and rung slots $a = 4, 5$, number operators $n_{a} = v_{a}w_{a}$, $N_{R} = n_{4} + n_{5}$, $T_{3R} = \tfrac12(N_{R} - 1)$, $B - L = -\tfrac23\sum_{a \le 3}(n_{a} - \tfrac12)$ and $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ (\claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-is-rung-vector-times-pair-part-of-majorana-square}), $*$ the tower's conjugation with $v_{a}^{*} = w_{a}$, $\|X\|_{*}$ the scalar part of $X^{*}X$, and $T = v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}v_{4}v_{5}$ the Majorana element. The frame boost of Theorems \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(4) and \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}(1) acts on one rung plane; here, for $s = e^{\eta} > 0$, $B_{s}$ is its $U(2)$-covariant extension, $v_{a} \mapsto sv_{a}$, $w_{a} \mapsto s^{-1}w_{a}$ on both rung slots and the identity on the pair slots, extended to the algebra. Units with $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$; the rung component has $\mathsf{N} = \|c\|_{*}$, $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}$ (as in \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}), and on the lift family $\mathsf{N} = H^{2}\cosh t$ with $t = 2\eta$, $\lambda = He^{\eta}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The boost is right-handed isospin at real rapidity.)} $B_{s}$ is the automorphism induced by an isometry of the ten, $B_{1/\lambda}c_{1} = c_{\lambda}$ on the lift family, and on every element $X$ with $[N_{R}, X] = qX$ it acts as $B_{s}X = s^{q}X$, where $q$ is twice the $\operatorname{ad} T_{3R}$ weight: $B_{e^{\eta}} = \exp(\eta\,\operatorname{ad} 2T_{3R})$.
\item \emph{(Majorana directions have weight two.)} On every hypercharge-neutral element of definite weights the frame weight is $q = -(B - L)$. The elements with $Y = 0$ and $B - L = \mp 2$, the directions giving a Majorana entry $\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$, are combinations of the $T$-type and $T^{*}$-type monomials, of frame weight $\pm 2$; the rung vectors have $Y = \pm\tfrac12$ and weight $\pm 1$.
\item \emph{(Chebyshev scaling.)} Distinct frame weights are $*$-orthogonal and $\|B_{s}X\|_{*} = s^{2q}\|X\|_{*}$ for weight $q$, while the pairing given by the scalar part of $\widetilde{X}X$ is frame-invariant. For the balanced rung component $c_{H} = H(v_{4} - w_{4})$ and the balanced Majorana element $D_{H} = H(T + T^{*})/\|T\|_{*}^{1/2}$, $\|B_{s}c_{H}\|_{*} = H^{2}\cosh t$ and $\|B_{s}D_{H}\|_{*} = H^{2}\cosh 2t = H^{2}\bigl(2(\|B_{s}c_{H}\|_{*}/H^{2})^{2} - 1\bigr)$; in general weight $q$ gives $H^{2}T_{q}(\|B_{s}c_{H}\|_{*}/H^{2})$ with $T_{q}$ the Chebyshev polynomial. The stored Majorana element $T$ alone is null for the pairing, and $\|B_{s}T\|_{*} = s^{4}\|T\|_{*}$ takes every positive value: the frame fixes no size for it.
\item \emph{(The weight-two tie is excluded.)} Let a Majorana vev lie in the weight $\pm 2$ span with its size fixed in Hubble units in one frame, by a frame-invariant pairing $\kappa^{2}$ times that of $D_{H}$, and let its size $M$ be its $*$-norm in the weak frame, where the rung component has $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}$ (fixed normalisations of $M$ absorbed in $\kappa$). Then $M^{2} = \kappa^{2}(v^{4}/(2H^{2}) - H^{2})$, so $M \ge \kappa v^{2}/(2H)$, a relation between the Majorana scale and $v/H$. With the stored record and $\kappa = 1$, $M > 2.1 \times 10^{46}$ GeV, above $1.7 \times 10^{27}M_{P}$ and above $4.05 \times 10^{34}$ times the perturbative cap $4\pi v_{R}$ of \claimref{synthesis.majorana-scale-free-on-pati-salam-route}(iii) ($v_{R} = 4.15 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}); under the imported seesaw (\claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}), with Dirac entries at most $\sqrt{4\pi}\,v$ and the Majorana matrix $M$ times a family coupling of smallest singular value $\sigma$, every light mass is below $8\pi H/\sigma$, so the stored $m_{3}$ needs $\sigma < 1/(1.38 \times 10^{30})$. Bringing $M$ under the cap needs $\kappa < 10^{-34}$; either rescue is a new hierarchy.
\item \emph{(Other extensions.)} Boosting rung slot $4$ alone gives $T$ weight $1$ and a tied size of order $\kappa v$; extending the boost as the complexified hypercharge on the whole algebra gives every $Y = 0$ element weight $0$ and a tied size of order $\kappa H$. For $\kappa$ of order one both are excluded by the stored $v_{R}$, which exceeds $v$ by more than $1.6 \times 10^{8}$ and $H_{0}$ by more than $2.8 \times 10^{52}$.
\end{enumerate}
So the frame boost does not tie the Majorana scale to $v/H$ through a weight-two vev of fixed Hubble-unit size, under any of the three extensions; the stored null Majorana element is not tied at all.
synthesis.majorana-scale-not-carried-by-.technical: The rung unit is a boost of the rung frame (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}); the same boost is read as the conformal dilatation of the ground point in the result \claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}(5), and the readings agree on the rung plane. Extended to both rung slots of the ten and as the identity on the pair slots, the boost is the real-rapidity flow generated by twice the right-handed isospin $T_{3R}$, so each element is rescaled by a power fixed by its charges; on hypercharge-neutral elements the power is minus the $B - L$ charge. The directions that give the right-handed neutrino its Majorana mass carry $B - L = \mp 2$ and no hypercharge, so they have weight two, where the rung vector, which carries the weak scale, has weight one. If a Majorana vev of weight two had its size fixed in Hubble units in one frame, as the lift's rung component has, and were read in the frame that gives the weak scale, then $\cosh 2t = 2\cosh^{2}t - 1$ with the stored $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}$ would force $M^{2} = \kappa^{2}(v^{4}/(2H^{2}) - H^{2})$, roughly $v^{2} \approx 2MH/\kappa$, a seesaw-type relation removing one free number. For $\kappa$ of order one the record rules it out: $M$ exceeds $2 \times 10^{46}$ GeV, far above the Planck mass and the stored range of the Majorana scale, and the seesaw then makes every light neutrino lighter than $8\pi H$ divided by the smallest Majorana family coupling, so the measured mass needs that coupling below $10^{-30}$. A rescue needs $\kappa$ below $10^{-34}$ or such a coupling, a new hierarchy either way. The other extensions of the boost (one rung slot only, or the full complexified hypercharge) tie the Majorana size to $v$ or to $H$, also excluded for $\kappa$ of order one; and the stored Majorana element is null, so the frame fixes no size for it. Whatever the status of $v/H$ (a parameter of the laws, or initial data under the promotion), the frame boost supplies no relation tying the Majorana scale to it.
synthesis.majorana-scale-not-carried-by-.lay: In this framework the strength of the weak force's symmetry breaking is set by how a particular reference frame in some extra directions is stretched. The same stretch acts on every quantity built from those directions, by an amount fixed by its charges. The quantity that gives the heavy neutrinos their mass carries twice the relevant charge of the Higgs field, so if its size were fixed once and then read through the same stretch, the heavy neutrino mass would come out as roughly the square of the weak scale divided by the expansion rate of the universe: about $10^{46}$ GeV, far beyond the Planck mass, and the ordinary neutrinos would be about $10^{30}$ times lighter than they are measured to be, unless some other coupling were itself absurdly small. Other ways of setting up the stretch give the opposite failure, heavy neutrino masses far too small. So the stretch that sets the weak scale does not set the heavy neutrino mass; that remains a separate number of the theory.

proofs.main:
The ten, its mode vectors, the number operators and the Majorana element $T = v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}v_{4}v_{5}$ are those of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}; $T_{3R}$, $B - L$ and $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ are as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-is-rung-vector-times-pair-part-of-majorana-square} and Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}(2), (4) (there $X = 2T_{3R} - \tfrac32(B - L) = 2Y - \tfrac52(B - L)$, which is this relation). The frame boost, the lift family and the $*$-norm of the rung component are those of Theorems \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(4) and \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}(1). The stored boost acts on the rung plane of slot $4$; the setting takes its $U(2)$-covariant extension to both rung slots, the identity on the pair slots, and (5) treats the two other extensions. The same boost is read as the conformal dilatation of the ground point in the result \claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}(5); on the rung plane the two readings coincide.

(1) Since $Q(v_{a}) = Q(w_{a}) = 0$ and $v_{a}w_{a} + w_{a}v_{a}$ is unchanged when $v_{a} \mapsto sv_{a}$, $w_{a} \mapsto s^{-1}w_{a}$, the map $B_{s}$ on vectors is an isometry, so it extends uniquely to an automorphism of the Clifford algebra; the check verifies that the images of the ten generators obey the Clifford relations for $s = 2, \tfrac32$. On the lift family, $c_{1} = -w_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}v_{4}$ is sent by $B_{1/\lambda}$ to $-\lambda w_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1}v_{4} = c_{\lambda}$. From the anticommutators, $[n_{a}, v_{b}] = \delta_{ab}v_{b}$ and $[n_{a}, w_{b}] = -\delta_{ab}w_{b}$, so on a product of mode vectors $\operatorname{ad} N_{R}$ has eigenvalue $q$, the number of rung $v$ factors minus the number of rung $w$ factors, and $B_{s}$ multiplies that product by $s^{q}$. Every element is a sum of such products, so $B_{s}$ acts on the $\operatorname{ad} N_{R}$ eigenspace of weight $q$ as $s^{q}$. Since $N_{R} = 2T_{3R} + 1$, $\operatorname{ad} N_{R} = 2\,\operatorname{ad} T_{3R}$, and $B_{e^{\eta}} = \exp(\eta\,\operatorname{ad} 2T_{3R})$: the frame boost is the flow of the right-handed isospin at real rapidity $2\eta = t$. (The compact flow $\exp(I_{4}\varphi\,\operatorname{ad} 2T_{3R})$ is the unitary one, numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(1) the hypercharge already acts on the real rung summand as a boost.) The check verifies the eigenvalue relation and $B_{s}X = s^{q}X$ on nine monomials, including $T$ and $T^{*}$.

(2) On a product of mode vectors let $p$ be the number of pair $v$ factors minus pair $w$ factors and $r$ the same for the rung slots. Then the weights are additive: $\operatorname{ad}(B - L)$ has weight $-\tfrac23 p$, $\operatorname{ad} T_{3R}$ has $\tfrac12 r$, $\operatorname{ad} N_{R}$ has $r$ and $\operatorname{ad} Y$ has $\tfrac12 r - \tfrac13 p$; the check verifies these four weights by direct commutators on all $3^{5}$ slot types (each slot $v$, $w$ or absent; factors $n_{a}$ or $w_{a}v_{a}$ in a slot have weight zero and change nothing). So $Y = 0$ if and only if $r = \tfrac23 p = -(B - L)$, which is (2)'s first statement. A Majorana entry $B(\psi, X\varphi)$ on the sixteen with $\psi = \varphi = \nu^{c}$, the empty state, needs $X$ to raise $B - L$ by the amount $T$ does, and a vev that preserves the Standard Model algebra has $Y = 0$; so the Majorana directions have $Y = 0$ and $B - L = \mp 2$. Then $|p| = 3$, every pair slot carries the same letter, and $r = \pm 2$, both rung slots carrying the same letter; with $Y = 0$ the letters agree, so the class is that of $T$ ($p = 3$, $r = 2$) or of $T^{*}$ ($p = -3$, $r = -2$), up to weight-zero factors. The check finds exactly these two classes among the $243$ and confirms $[B - L, T] = -2T$, $[T_{3R}, T] = T$, $[Y, T] = 0$, $[N_{R}, T] = 2T$ and the opposite weights for $T^{*}$. A single rung vector has $p = 0$, $r = \pm 1$, so $Y = \pm\tfrac12$ and weight $\pm 1$.

(3) The conjugation $*$ is antilinear and reverses products with $v_{a}^{*} = w_{a}$, so it sends weight $q$ to weight $-q$; the scalar part has weight zero, so the scalar part of $X^{*}Y$ vanishes unless $X$ and $Y$ have equal weight, and weight spaces are $*$-orthogonal. For real $s$, $(B_{s}X)^{*} = B_{1/s}(X^{*})$, so for weight $q$, $\|B_{s}X\|_{*} = s^{2q}\|X\|_{*}$. The balanced rung component $c_{H} = H(v_{4} - w_{4})$ (the lift at $\lambda = H$) has components of weights $\pm 1$ with $\|v_{4}\|_{*} = \|w_{4}\|_{*} = \tfrac12$, so $\|B_{s}c_{H}\|_{*} = \tfrac12H^{2}(s^{2} + s^{-2}) = H^{2}\cosh 2\eta = H^{2}\cosh t$, which is $\mathsf{N}$ on the lift family (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(4) with $\lambda = He^{\eta}$). For $D = T + T^{*}$, of weights $\pm 2$ with $\|T\|_{*} = \|T^{*}\|_{*} = \tfrac{1}{32}$ (computed exactly), $\|B_{s}D\|_{*}/\|D\|_{*} = \tfrac12(s^{4} + s^{-4}) = \cosh 2t = 2\cosh^{2}t - 1$. For weight $q$ the ratio is $\cosh qt = T_{q}(\cosh t)$. The pairing given by the scalar part of $\widetilde{X}X$ is preserved by every automorphism induced by an isometry; on $c$ it is $Q(c)$, equal to $-H^{2}$ on the lift family, and on $\alpha T + \beta T^{*}$ it is $\alpha\beta$ times the nonzero pairing of $T$ with $T^{*}$, while $T$ alone pairs to zero. The check verifies, for $s = 2, 3, \tfrac32$ and $H = 1$, the two norm formulas, the identity $\|B_{s}D\|_{*}/\|D\|_{*} = 2x^{2} - 1$ with $x = \|B_{s}c_{H}\|_{*}$, its form $\tfrac12 u^{2} - 1$ in $u = 2x = v^{2}/H^{2}$, the vanishing of the cross terms, the invariance of both pairings, and $\|B_{s}T\|_{*} = s^{4}\|T\|_{*}$, which takes every positive value as $s$ varies, so the stored null Majorana element has no size fixed by the frame and lies outside the class of (4).

(4) Under the hypothesis of (4) the Majorana vev is $\kappa D_{H}$ up to the frame and a phase, read in the frame $s = e^{\eta}$ in which the rung component has $\mathsf{N} = H^{2}\cosh t$, $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}$ (the stored normalisation of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}, in the Hermitian reading of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}; fixed normalisations of $M$ are absorbed in $\kappa$). By (3), $M^{2} = \kappa^{2}H^{2}\cosh 2t = \kappa^{2}H^{2}(2(v^{2}/(2H^{2}))^{2} - 1) = \kappa^{2}(v^{4}/(2H^{2}) - H^{2})$; the term $-\kappa^{2}H^{2}$ is exact and is not a normalisation. For $x = v^{2}/(2H^{2}) \ge 1$, $2x^{2} - 1 \ge x^{2}$, so $M \ge \kappa v^{2}/(2H)$. Record inputs (all stored quantities): $H \le H_{0}$ since $H^{2} = H_{0}^{2}\Omega_{\Lambda}$ with $\Omega_{\Lambda} \le 1$ (the convention of $N$; the two differ by a factor of order one); $\hbar H_{0} < 1.439 \times 10^{-42}$ GeV from the stored Hubble constant, $\hbar$ and megaparsec; $v^{2} = M_{W}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta_{W}\,\alpha^{-1}/\pi$ (the tree relation $M_{W} = gv/2$ with $g = e/\sin\theta_{W}$, cited from memory), above $6.08 \times 10^{4}$ GeV$^{2}$ with $\pi < \tfrac{22}{7}$, which the check proves from Machin's formula by alternating partial sums. Hence, for $\kappa = 1$, $M > 2.1 \times 10^{46}$ GeV, above $1.7 \times 10^{27}$ times the stored Planck mass and above $4.05 \times 10^{34}$ times $4\pi v_{R}$ with the stored $v_{R} = 4.15 \times 10^{10}$ GeV (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}), the upper end of the admissible range of the Majorana scale in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.majorana-scale-free-on-pati-salam-route}(iii). Under the imported seesaw, $m_{\nu} = -M_{\nu}M_{R}^{-1}M_{\nu}^{\mathsf{T}}$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}) with $M_{R} = Mf$, $f$ a family coupling of smallest singular value $\sigma$, and Dirac entries bounded by the perturbative $\sqrt{4\pi}\,v$, every light mass is at most $\|M_{\nu}\|^{2}\|M_{R}^{-1}\| \le 4\pi v^{2}/(\sigma M) \le 8\pi H/\sigma$, and $8\pi H_{0} < m_{3}/(1.38 \times 10^{30})$ with the stored $m_{3} = 0.050$ eV; so the measured $m_{3}$ needs $\sigma < 1/(1.38 \times 10^{30})$. Since $M \ge \kappa v^{2}/(2H)$, bringing $M$ under $4\pi v_{R}$ needs $\kappa < 1/(4.05 \times 10^{34}) < 10^{-34}$. Either rescue introduces a dimensionless number as far from one as $v/H$ is. Neither $N = M_{P}/H$ nor $M_{P}$ enters the relation, which would tie the Majorana scale to $v/H$ alone; since the tie is excluded, the status of the Majorana scale is unaffected by whether $v/H$ is a parameter of the laws or initial data.

(5) If the boost acts on rung slot $4$ only ($v_{4} \mapsto sv_{4}$, $w_{4} \mapsto s^{-1}w_{4}$, all else fixed, an isometry by the argument of (1)), its weight is the slot-$4$ number $n_{4}$, and $T$ has weight $1$; a vev of $T$-type with size fixed in Hubble units in one frame then scales like the rung component, of order $\kappa v$. If instead the boost is extended to the whole algebra as the complexified hypercharge, $\exp(\eta\,\operatorname{ad} Y)$ up to normalisation, every $Y = 0$ element has weight $0$ and is frame-blind, so a tied size stays of order $\kappa H$. A vev along $T$ is the Pati-Salam breaking vev (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), whose stored value is $v_{R} = 4.15 \times 10^{10}$ GeV; from the stored quantities, with $\pi > 3$ (Machin, partial sums), $v^{2} < 6.37 \times 10^{4}$ GeV$^{2}$, so $v_{R}^{2} > 2.7 \times 10^{16}v^{2}$ ($v_{R}/v > 1.6 \times 10^{8}$) and $v_{R} > 2.8 \times 10^{52}H_{0}$. For $\kappa$ of order one both alternatives are excluded; the check verifies the two weights and these bounds.

Computed, not part of the check: with $H = H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}} = 1.19 \times 10^{-42}$ GeV and $v = 246.2$ GeV, $v^{2}/(\sqrt{2}H) = 3.6 \times 10^{46}$ GeV, $35.9$ orders of magnitude above $v_{R}$.

synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by.formal:
Let $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ be the five-mode module of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, modes $1, 2$ the slots and $3, 4, 5$ the pairs, $N$ the total mode number, $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$, $\Omega$ the empty and $\Omega^{\top}$ the full state. Let $\so(10)$ be the span of all bilinears, $\uu(5)$ that of the number-conserving ones $a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$, and $\mathfrak{p}$ that of the pair-creation and pair-annihilation bilinears $a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}$, $a_{i}a_{j}$, so $\so(10) = \uu(5) \oplus \mathfrak{p}$. Let $\Gamma' = (-1)^{N} - 2P_{\Omega} + 2P_{\Omega^{\top}}$ be the vacuum-swapped halving of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}, and call a gauge-commuting CPT halving anomaly-free when it agrees with $\pm(-1)^{N}$ on the charged states (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Hypercharge grading.)} $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ is diagonal on the bilinear basis with eigenvalues $\{0, \pm\tfrac56\}$ on $\uu(5)$, $\{1, \tfrac16, -\tfrac23\}$ on pair creation and $\{-1, -\tfrac16, \tfrac23\}$ on pair annihilation, three disjoint sets. Hence every subspace $\mathfrak{g} \subseteq \so(10)$ stable under $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ is $(\mathfrak{g} \cap \uu(5)) \oplus (\mathfrak{g} \cap \mathfrak{p})$, and $\mathfrak{g} \cap \mathfrak{p}$ is spanned by pure creation and pure annihilation elements.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(One pair decides.)} $(-1)^{N}$ commutes with $\so(10)$; $\Gamma'$ commutes with $\uu(5)$, and $x \mapsto [\Gamma', x]$ is injective on $\mathfrak{p}$. For an involution equal to $s(-1)^{N}$ ($s = \pm1$) on the charged states and arbitrary on the neutral block, commuting with one nonzero pure creation element $x \in \mathfrak{p}$ forces $\Gamma\Omega^{\top} = -s\Omega^{\top}$ and $\Gamma\Omega \in s\Omega + \C\Omega^{\top}$, and commuting with $x$ and $x^{\dagger}$ forces $\Gamma = s(-1)^{N}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Dichotomy.)} Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be closed under adjoints with $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)) \subseteq \mathfrak{g} \subseteq \so(10)$. If $\mathfrak{g} \subseteq \uu(5)$, the vacuum-swapped halving commutes with $\mathfrak{g}$ and the bit is free. If $\mathfrak{g} \not\subseteq \uu(5)$, the anomaly-free gauge-commuting CPT halvings that commute with $\mathfrak{g}$ are exactly $\pm(-1)^{N}$, with no use of number conservation or of the grading clause. In particular the Pati-Salam algebra $\so(4) \oplus \so(6)$ of the split-preserving bivectors (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}), the left-right algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \uu(1)_{B - L}$, $\su(4) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \uu(1)$ and the flipped $\uu(5)$ fix the bit; the Georgi-Glashow $\uu(5)$, and the Standard Model algebra with $B - L$ or with $N$ adjoined, do not.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Yukawa forms.)} With the invariant pairing $B$ of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes}: for $(-1)^{N}$ the slot vectors pair the lepton doublet (one slot, three pairs) with $\Omega$; for $\Gamma'$ the full state $\Omega^{\top}$ has $B(\Omega^{\top}, X\psi) = B(\psi, X\Omega^{\top}) = 0$ for every other state $\psi$ of its half and every Clifford element $X$ of grade $1$, $3$ or $5$, keeps a nonzero self-pairing $B(\Omega^{\top}, X\Omega^{\top})$, and meets the lepton doublet only through grade four. The charged states of the two halves coincide. Hence, for Yukawa couplings that are odd-grade forms $B(\psi, X\varphi)$ (the $10$, $120$ and $126$ forms of the stored mass relations; under $\Gamma'$ the particle half is not an $\so(10)$ module, so these forms are an assumption there, not singled out), the rung coupling gives the particle half's neutral singlet a Dirac coupling to the lepton doublet under $(-1)^{N}$ and none under $\Gamma'$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(CPT blindness.)} $\Theta = U\kappa$, with $U = \prod_{k}(a^{\dagger}_{k} + a_{k})$ and $\kappa$ complex conjugation in the occupation basis (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors; $\kappa$ sends $I_{4}$ to $-I_{4}$), commutes with all ten Hermitian Majoranas, so with $\Spin(10)$, carries $\Omega$ to $\pm\Omega^{\top}$, commutes with the swap $S$ of $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$, and satisfies $\Theta(-1)^{N}\Theta^{-1} = -(-1)^{N}$ and $\Theta\Gamma'\Theta^{-1} = -\Gamma'$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, given the other clauses of the slot-module hypothesis (\claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}) and anomaly freedom, the grading form of its chirality clause (its earlier version) is equivalent to the chirality commuting with some gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ that leaves $\uu(5)$, the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain among them (the clause's current form), and is not implied by any that stays inside it.
synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by.technical: The stored ladder showed that symmetry, CPT and anomaly freedom leave one binary choice in the composite's chirality, whether the empty or the full five-mode state is the particle half's sterile singlet, and that only operators of $\so(10)$ that create or destroy two modes see it. This result asks which gauge algebras between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ contain such operators. Hypercharge sorts $\so(10)$ into three eigenvalue families that never overlap (number-conserving, pair-creating, pair-annihilating), so any gauge algebra containing hypercharge either stays entirely inside the number-conserving $\uu(5)$ or contains a pair-creation operator and its adjoint. One such pair, with the anomaly-fixed signs on the charged states, already pins the neutral block, and number conservation is not needed. So the Pati-Salam, left-right and flipped stages decide the bit and the Georgi-Glashow stage cannot. Two cross-checks: under the swapped choice the stored Yukawa forms (all of odd Clifford grade) leave the particle half's singlet uncoupled from the rest of the half, so the rung coupling gives no Dirac neutrino coupling; and the Clifford CPT antiunitary treats both choices alike. Since the stored chain, stated under (S), runs through Pati-Salam, the clause can be read as the chirality commuting with the chain's intermediate gauge algebra: an exchange of premises onto registered structure, not a derivation from nothing.
synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by.lay: Each matter particle of one family is a pattern of five filled or empty slots, and one yes-or-no choice in sorting patterns into particles and antiparticles had been left as an assumption: whether the completely empty pattern goes with the particles. This result shows which larger symmetries can settle that choice. Any symmetry that can create or remove two slots at once settles it, and the symmetries that only move slots around never do. The intermediate symmetry stage the series already uses, Pati-Salam, is of the first kind, so if the sorting respects that symmetry, the choice is fixed; this trades the assumption for that requirement rather than removing it. With the other choice, and mass couplings of the usual kind, the neutrino partner would have no ordinary mass coupling to the rest of its family.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} On the five-mode module of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, with $Y = \sum_{k} y_{k} n_{k}$, $y_{k} = \tfrac12$ on the slots and $-\tfrac13$ on the pairs, $[Y, a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}] = (y_{i} - y_{j})a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$, $[Y, a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}] = (y_{i} + y_{j})a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}$ and $[Y, a_{i}a_{j}] = -(y_{i} + y_{j})a_{i}a_{j}$. The differences $y_{i} - y_{j}$ are $0$ and $\pm\tfrac56$; the sums $y_{i} + y_{j}$ are $1$ (two slots), $\tfrac16$ (slot and pair) and $-\tfrac23$ (two pairs). The three sets $\{0, \pm\tfrac56\}$, $\{1, \tfrac16, -\tfrac23\}$, $\{-1, -\tfrac16, \tfrac23\}$ are disjoint, so each eigenspace of $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ on $\so(10)$ lies in $\uu(5)$, in the creation span or in the annihilation span. A subspace stable under $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ is the sum of its intersections with the eigenspaces, which gives the splitting. The check verifies every eigenvalue equation on the $45$ basis elements and the disjointness.

\emph{(ii).} Every bilinear changes $N$ by an even amount, so $(-1)^{N}$ commutes with $\so(10)$, and $\Gamma'$, which differs from it only by the projectors onto $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$ (both annihilated by every $a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$ with $i \ne j$ and eigenvectors of every $n_{i}$), commutes with $\uu(5)$. Write an involution as $s(-1)^{N}$ on the thirty charged states and $\Gamma\Omega = a\Omega + c\Omega^{\top}$, $\Gamma\Omega^{\top} = b\Omega + d\Omega^{\top}$. Let $x = \sum_{i<j} c_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j} \ne 0$ and pick $c_{ij} \ne 0$. Then $x\Omega$ is a nonzero charged state of degree two, $x\Omega^{\top} = 0$, so $[\Gamma, x]\Omega = s\,x\Omega - a\,x\Omega$ gives $a = s$. For $\varphi$ the degree-three state on the complement of $\{i, j\}$, $x\varphi = \pm c_{ij}\Omega^{\top}$ and $\Gamma x\varphi = \pm c_{ij}(b\Omega + d\Omega^{\top})$, while $x\Gamma\varphi = -s\,x\varphi$ has no $\Omega$ component; so $b = 0$ and $d = -s$. The entry $c$ is not constrained by $x$ (the involution with $c = 1$ commutes with the Standard Model and with $x$; checked). For $x^{\dagger}$, a pure annihilation element, $x^{\dagger}\Omega = 0$ and $x^{\dagger}\Omega^{\top} \ne 0$ is charged, so $[\Gamma, x^{\dagger}]\Omega = -c\,x^{\dagger}\Omega^{\top}$ gives $c = 0$. Hence $\Gamma = s(-1)^{N}$. Injectivity: for $x$ a nonzero creation element, $[\Gamma', x]\Omega = (+1 - (-1))x\Omega = 2x\Omega \ne 0$, and $x \mapsto x\Omega = \sum c_{ij}e_{i} \wedge e_{j}$ is injective; for annihilation elements use $\Omega^{\top}$; the creation and annihilation images lie in different degrees. The check solves the affine system for $(a, b, c, d)$ for every one of the ten basis pairs $x, x^{\dagger}$ and both $s$, finds rank $4$ with the solution $(s, 0, 0, -s)$, rank $3$ for $x$ alone, rank $2$ with $N$ in place of $x$ (diagonal block), rank $0$ for the Standard Model alone, and rank $20$ for the twenty columns of $[\Gamma', \cdot]$.

\emph{(iii).} The Standard Model algebra contains $Y$, so $\mathfrak{g}$ is $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$-stable and splits by (i). If $\mathfrak{g} \subseteq \uu(5)$, $\Gamma'$ commutes with it by (ii), and so does $-\Gamma'$; both are anomaly-free gauge-commuting CPT halvings (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(ii)), so the bit is not fixed. If not, $\mathfrak{g} \cap \mathfrak{p}$ is nonzero and spanned by pure creation and pure annihilation eigenvectors; closure under adjoints (a gauge algebra is the complexification of a compact real form, so it is closed under $x \mapsto x^{\dagger}$) supplies $x$ and $x^{\dagger}$ with $x$ pure creation. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4) an anomaly-free gauge-commuting CPT halving is $s(-1)^{N}$ on the charged states, and by (ii) commuting with $x, x^{\dagger}$ forces $\Gamma = s(-1)^{N}$, which does commute with $\mathfrak{g}$. The named algebras: Pati-Salam is the span of the slot bilinears ($\so(4)$, including $a^{\dagger}_{1}a^{\dagger}_{2}$) and the pair bilinears ($\so(6)$, including $a^{\dagger}_{3}a^{\dagger}_{4}$), the $21$ split-preserving bivectors of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}; the left-right algebra contains $\su(2)_{R} \ni a^{\dagger}_{1}a^{\dagger}_{2}$; $\su(4)$ contains the pair-pair brackets; the flipped $\uu(5)$ (number-conserving for the modes with the two slots' creation and annihilation exchanged) contains the slot-pair brackets $a_{i}a_{j}$, $a^{\dagger}_{j}a^{\dagger}_{i}$. The check verifies, for each named algebra, membership of $Y$, whether it lies in $\uu(5)$ (a span computation), that $(-1)^{N}$ commutes with it, that $\Gamma'$ commutes with it exactly when it lies in $\uu(5)$, and the neutral-block solution ($(1, 0, 0, -1)$ at rank $4$ for those leaving $\uu(5)$, rank below $4$ otherwise). $B - L$ is taken up to a central constant, $-k/3$, which does not change any commutator.

\emph{(iv).} The pairing $B$ of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes} pairs the state on a mode set $S$ only with the state on the complement, so $B(\psi, X\varphi) \ne 0$ needs $N(\psi) + N(X\varphi) = 5$. A Clifford monomial of grade $r$ changes $N$ by an amount of the parity of $r$. For $\psi = \Omega^{\top}$ ($N = 5$) and $\varphi$ a charged state of $\Gamma'$'s particle half ($N$ even), $X\varphi$ must be $\Omega$, impossible for odd $r$; the same for $B(\varphi, X\Omega^{\top})$ ($N(X\Omega^{\top})$ even, needs $N = 5 - N(\varphi)$ odd). For $r$ odd, $X\Omega^{\top}$ can be $\Omega$ (the product of the five annihilations has grade-five and lower odd components), which gives the self-pairing. The lepton doublet ($N = 4$) pairs with $\Omega^{\top}$ only if $N(X\Omega^{\top}) = 1$, a change of $-4$, even grade; with $(-1)^{N}$ it pairs with $\Omega$ through a slot vector ($N(X\Omega) = 1$). The check computes $B$ from the stored construction, confirms its invariance in this labelling of the modes, and evaluates all $382$ monomials of grades $1$, $3$, $5$ and the $210$ of grade $4$ on the relevant states. The $10$, $120$ and $126$ Yukawa forms of the stored mass relations are of grades $1$, $3$, $5$; so under $\Gamma'$ the rung coupling gives the particle half's singlet no Dirac coupling to the lepton doublet.

\emph{(v).} $U$ is a product of five mutually anticommuting real Majoranas, so it commutes with each of them and anticommutes with each $a^{\dagger}_{k} - a_{k}$; $\kappa$ fixes the real matrices and negates $I_{4}(a^{\dagger}_{k} - a_{k})$; so $\Theta$ fixes all ten Hermitian Majoranas and hence their bivectors. $U\Omega$ is the product of five creations on $\Omega$ up to sign, i.e. $\pm\Omega^{\top}$; $U$ is real, maps degree $d$ to degree $5 - d$ on each mode, so it reverses $(-1)^{N}$, exchanges $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$ and therefore commutes with $S$ and reverses $\Gamma' = S(-1)^{N}S$. All verified exactly.

The closing equivalence: by (iii) any gauge algebra leaving $\uu(5)$ forces $\pm(-1)^{N}$, which is the grading clause (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(iii)); conversely $\pm(-1)^{N}$ commutes with all of $\so(10)$; and an algebra inside $\uu(5)$ leaves the vacuum-swapped halving. Numerical work: none; all statements are exact.

Version 2, wording only: the closing sentence now names the grading form as the earlier version of the chirality clause and the Pati-Salam form as its current version (version 4 of the slot-module premise), and makes explicit that the equivalence uses anomaly freedom, as (iii) assumes. Mathematics unchanged.

synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-f.formal:
Let $S_{3}$ act on family matrices by $X \mapsto PXP^{\mathsf{T}}$ in the basis $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$ of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation}, let $S_{2}$ be the stabiliser of its breaking direction $e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ (the exchange of $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$), and put $u' = (1,1,1)$, $s = (1,1,-2)$, $a = (1,-1,0)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] No nonzero antisymmetric family matrix is $S_{3}$-invariant. The $S_{2}$-invariant antisymmetric matrices form a line, spanned by $u' \wedge s = u's^{\mathsf{T}} - su'^{\mathsf{T}} = -3\,(e_{1} + e_{2}) \wedge e_{3}$; it annihilates $a$. The $S_{3}$-invariant symmetric matrices form the plane of $\Pi$ and $\J$ (Lemma \claimref{neutrino.invariant-symmetric-matrices}), the $S_{2}$-invariant ones a four-dimensional space spanned by $u'u'^{\mathsf{T}}$, $ss^{\mathsf{T}}$, $aa^{\mathsf{T}}$ and $u's^{\mathsf{T}} + su'^{\mathsf{T}}$.
\item[(ii)] For every breaking $\J + \varepsilon\,e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$, $a$ is a null vector and $s$ is not: at the $S_{2}$ stage $a$ is the first family, $s$ the second and $u'$ (mixed with $s$) the third, with the charged-fermion family labels taken from the neutrino-sector breaking direction. Hence a $120$ coupling (antisymmetric, Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-spinor-bilinears}) that respects the residual $S_{2}$ couples exactly the second and third families and leaves the first uncoupled, and an $S_{3}$-symmetric stage admits no $120$ coupling.
\item[(iii)] Under Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}, if the Majorana matrix is $S_{3}$-invariant, $M_{R} = \alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3$ as in Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation}, then $f = M_{R}/v_{R}$ and $\mathrm{Sym}(M_{d} - M_{e}) = 4w_{d}f$ are $S_{3}$-invariant whatever the $10$s and the $120$: the $126$ enters the two light families through one scalar, $4w_{d}\alpha/v_{R}$ on the whole plane $u'^{\perp}$, and the third through $4w_{d}M_{3}/v_{R}$. A $126$ entry on the second family alone is not of this form.
\end{enumerate}
So, with an $S_{3}$-invariant Majorana sector and the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ breaking direction, the $126$ cannot supply a factor on the second family alone, the Georgi-Jarlskog texture is unavailable, and the registered route through the $120$ coupling of the second and third families with the $10$s is the route that remains; (i)-(ii) derive that coupling's family form. Its strength is not derived.
synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-f.technical:
Import the neutrino paper's family symmetry into the Pati-Salam Clebsch structure. Antisymmetric family matrices, the only ones a $120$ can carry, contain no $S_{3}$ singlet, so an unbroken permutation symmetry forbids the $120$ altogether. Under the residual $S_{2}$ of the store's breaking direction $e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ exactly one antisymmetric matrix survives, $u' \wedge s$: it couples the heavy direction $u'$ to the $S_{2}$-even light state $s$ and annihilates the $S_{2}$-odd state $a$. Since any breaking along $e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ leaves $a$ massless while $s$ acquires mass, $a$ is the first family and $s$ the second at that stage, so the residual symmetry selects precisely the antisymmetric coupling between the second and third families that the registered route uses.

For the $126$: the Majorana matrix is $v_{R}f$, and the symmetric part of $M_{d} - M_{e}$ is $4w_{d}f$ whatever the $10$s and the $120$. If the Majorana sector is $S_{3}$-invariant, as the neutrino paper takes it at leading order, the $126$ is family-blind on the light plane: it cannot put a factor $3$ on the second family alone, so the Georgi-Jarlskog texture is unavailable; any factor the $126$ supplies is shared by the first family. Under these premises the registered route through the $120$ and the $10$s is the route that remains, and its family form is derived; the coupling's size is still an input.
synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-f.lay: In the framework's grand-unified picture the muon is about three times heavier than the strange quark at high energy, while the electron and the down quark go the other way, and the series has had to choose how that factor of three arises. This result shows that if the heavy neutrinos are as symmetric among the three families as the neutrino paper assumes, the field that gives them mass cannot be the source of that factor for the second family alone: it treats the two lighter families identically. The remaining route takes the factor from a different field that links families in pairs, and the family symmetry left over after the first stage of breaking allows that field to link only the second and third families. That is the route the series had chosen by fitting; here its shape follows from symmetry, though its strength is still not derived.

synthesis.rung-field-charged-pair-decoup.formal:
In the setting of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}: the rung vector $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$ ($a = 4, 5$) on the null-lift locus $L = \{Q(c) = -H^{2}\}$, $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, $\mathsf{N}$, $m$, the Hermitian form $G$, the slot-mixing generators $T_{j}$, $Y$, the lift family $c_{\lambda}$ ($\alpha = (H^{2}/\lambda, 0)$, $\beta = (-\lambda, 0)$, $\lambda = He^{\eta}$), and the per-sector Yukawa reading of \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern} on the sixteen: the down-type and charged-lepton entries are those of $M_{c}$ on $(Q, d^{c})$ and $(L, e^{c})$, the up-type and Dirac-neutrino entries those of $M_{c^{*}}$ on $(Q, u^{c})$ and $(L, \nu^{c})$. This reading is not $\su(2)_{R}$ covariant; it is the leading mass reading of the covariant completion with one family matrix on $c$ and one on $c^{*}$, to which the clauses below do not apply. Let the vacuum be $c_{\lambda}$ with $\lambda^{2} > H^{2}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The per-sector readings see only $\beta$.)} Both readings vanish on every vector with $\beta = 0$ and are unchanged by any phase $\alpha \mapsto u\alpha$, $|u| = 1$; the sum of $|\text{entry}|^{2}$ over each of the two sectors is $8|\beta|^{2}$. Read through $c$ itself (not the series' reading) the up-type entries would see $\alpha$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Charged couplings under the per-sector reading.)} The physical charged plane at $c_{\lambda}$ is $\{\alpha' = a\,e_{5},\ \beta' = (H^{2}/\lambda^{2})\bar{a}\,e_{5}\}$, and for each of its directions $d$, in both sectors,
\[
\frac{\sum|\text{entries of } d|^{2}/\mathsf{N}(d)}{\sum|\text{entries of } c_{\lambda}|^{2}/\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})} = \Bigl(\frac{H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}}\Bigr)^{2} = e^{-4\eta}:
\]
in the two-doublet reading $\Phi_{1} = \alpha$, $\Phi_{2} = \bar{\beta}$, with $\Phi_{2}^{\dagger}\Phi_{1} = Q(c) = -H^{2}$, the pattern is that of one doublet coupling to every fermion, with $\tan\beta_{2} = |\Phi_{2}|/|\Phi_{1}| = \lambda^{2}/H^{2} = e^{2\eta}$, and the charged pair couples with $\cot\beta_{2}$ times the coupling of the neutral vev direction.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Gauge vertex.)} For $j = 1, 2$ the vector $T_{j}(dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda)$ lies in the charged sector, and its squared $G$-projection on the physical charged plane is $4H^{4}\lambda^{4}/(\lambda^{4} - H^{4})^{2} = 1/\sinh^{2}2\eta$ times its squared projection on the eaten plane spanned by $T_{1}c_{\lambda}$, $T_{2}c_{\lambda}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(A phase on $\alpha$.)} The map $\alpha \mapsto u\alpha$ keeps $\mathsf{N}$, $m$, $|Q|$, $\sum_{j}\mu_{j}^{2}$, $\mu_{Y}$ and $G$, commutes with every $T_{j}$ and $Y$, keeps both per-sector readings, and sends $Q$ to $uQ$: it keeps the kinetic term, the D-term action at every level, every added $W(\mathsf{N})$ and the per-sector Yukawa entries, and moves $L$ unless $H = 0$. At $H = 0$ the charged plane at $c_{\lambda}$ lies wholly in the $\alpha$ half.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Top decays.)} With the stored $m_{t}$, $M_{W}$, $\alpha^{-1}(M_{Z})$, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$, $\Lambda$ and $\hbar c$, $g^{2}H^{2}/(4M_{W}^{2}) < \cot\beta_{2} = H^{2}/\lambda^{2} < g^{2}H^{2}/(2M_{W}^{2})$ (with $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$ and the tree relation $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N}^{*}$), the lower end above $2.32 \times 10^{-89}$ and the upper end below $4.66 \times 10^{-89}$, and for $m_{\pm}^{2} \in [13702, 13803]$ GeV$^{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-charged-scalar-sum-rule}) the factor $K = (1 - x)^{2}/((1 - y)^{2}(1 + 2y))$, $x = m_{\pm}^{2}/m_{t}^{2}$, $y = M_{W}^{2}/m_{t}^{2}$, lies below $\tfrac12$, so $\Gamma(t \to bH^{+})/\Gamma(t \to bW^{+}) = K\cot^{2}\beta_{2} < 10^{-176}$ (the ratio formula of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-top-to-charged-higgs-width-ratio}).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.rung-field-charged-pair-decoup.technical: The rung field is two Higgs-like doublets tied by the lift constraint: $\alpha$ and the conjugate of $\beta$, with $\Phi_{2}^{\dagger}\Phi_{1} = -H^{2}$. The series reads down-type masses through $c$ and up-type masses through $c^{*}$. Taken sector by sector (down-type entries from $c$, up-type entries from $c^{*}$), both readings use only the $\beta$ half, so one doublet gives every fermion its mass; this per-sector reading is not $\su(2)_{R}$ covariant, and it is the leading mass reading of the covariant completion, which puts one family matrix on $c$ and one on $c^{*}$ as wholes. At the vacuum the $\beta$ half carries the weak scale $\lambda$ and the $\alpha$ half only $H^{2}/\lambda$, and the physical charged pair is almost entirely $\alpha$: its admixture of $\beta$ is $H^{2}/\lambda^{2} = e^{-2\eta}$, the rung unit's boost squared. Under the per-sector reading its couplings to quarks and leptons, and its vertex with the $W$ and the neutral mode, carry that factor, so $t \to bH^{+}$ is negligible; a phase on $\alpha$ alone keeps the kinetic term, the D-term action, every $W(\mathsf{N})$ and the per-sector entries, and is broken only by the constraint $Q(c) = -H^{2}$. Under the covariant completion the $\alpha$ half carries the same two family matrices, and the pair couples with the strength of the mass couplings.
synthesis.rung-field-charged-pair-decoup.lay: The series' candidate for the Higgs field comes with a pair of electrically charged partners. This result works out how those partners couple to quarks and leptons when the masses are read sector by sector, down-type quarks from the field and up-type quarks from its conjugate, which is the series' leading reading of the masses. Under that reading they hardly couple at all: their coupling is smaller than the ordinary one by a factor set by the ratio of the cosmological scale to the weak scale, so top quarks essentially never decay into them. The reason is an almost exact symmetry that only the cosmological constant breaks, and the partners then cannot decay quickly into anything. A left-right symmetric completion of the same reading gives the partners couplings of ordinary strength instead, and then searches in top-quark decays apply.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Coordinates, the Hermitian form $G$, the generators $T_{j} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{j}$ (the unit on the rung field and its coefficients is the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, which commutes with the rung vectors; $\C = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$) and $Y = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\mathbf{1}$ (acting by $X$ on $\alpha$ and by $\bar{X}$ on $\beta$), the lift family and the computation of the physical directions (the $G$-orthogonal complement of the gauge orbit in the tangent space of $L$, the neutral line $dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda$ removed) are those of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus} and \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}. The Yukawa form $M_{x}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, x\varphi)$ on the five-mode module and the species of its entries are those of \claimref{standard-model.yukawa-pattern-two-rung-module}: a rung creation vector $v_{a}$ ($Y = +\tfrac12$) has entries exactly on $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$, a rung annihilation vector $w_{a}$ ($Y = -\tfrac12$) exactly on $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$. The conjugation $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$, conjugate-linear, is that of \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}, and the readings are those of \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern}, taken sector by sector: down-type entries from $M_{c}$, up-type entries from $M_{c^{*}}$. This per-sector reading is not $\su(2)_{R}$ covariant: by (i) its kernel is the $\alpha$ half, which the $\su(2)_{R}$ raising generator carries into the $\beta$ half, and the kernel of an equivariant map is invariant. The covariant completion puts one family matrix $Y$ on $c$ and one $\tilde{Y}$ on $c^{*}$ as wholes, $M_{d} = \beta Y + \bar{\alpha}\tilde{Y}$, $M_{u} = \alpha Y + \bar{\beta}\tilde{Y}$, whose leading mass reading at $|\alpha| \ll |\beta|$ is the per-sector one (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}). Every clause below concerns the per-sector reading.

\emph{(i).} The down-type sectors $(Q, d^{c})$, $(L, e^{c})$ of $M_{c}$ receive only the $w_{a}$ terms of $c$, whose coefficients are $\beta_{a}$; the up-type sectors $(Q, u^{c})$, $(L, \nu^{c})$ of $M_{c^{*}}$ receive only the $v_{a}$ terms of $c^{*} = \sum_{a}(\bar{\beta}_{a}v_{a} + \bar{\alpha}_{a}w_{a})$, whose coefficients are $\bar{\beta}_{a}$. So both readings are functions of $\beta$ alone: zero for $\beta = 0$ and unchanged by $\alpha \mapsto u\alpha$. The check computes every entry on the $16 \times 16$ basis pairs for two pure-$\alpha$ vectors (zero), three generic Gaussian-rational vectors (nonzero, with $\sum|\text{entry}|^{2} = 8|\beta|^{2}$ in each sector) and two rational phases $u = \tfrac35 + \tfrac45I_{4}$, $\tfrac{5}{13} - \tfrac{12}{13}I_{4}$ (entries unchanged), and confirms that $M_{c}$ itself has nonzero up-type entries on pure $\alpha$: only the $c^{*}$ reading removes $\alpha$ from the up-type sector.

\emph{(ii).} At $c_{\lambda}$ the charged plane is $\{\alpha' = a\,e_{5},\ \beta' = (H^{2}/\lambda^{2})\bar{a}\,e_{5}\}$ (stored clause (3) of the D-term result; the check recomputes it from the tangent space and the gauge orbit and verifies the form of $\beta'$). By (i) the entries of a direction $d$ in either sector have $\sum|\cdot|^{2} = 8|\beta(d)|^{2}$, so the ratio in the statement is
\[
\frac{|\beta(d)|^{2}/\mathsf{N}(d)}{|\beta(c_{\lambda})|^{2}/\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})} = \frac{(H^{4}/\lambda^{4})|a|^{2}}{\tfrac12|a|^{2}(1 + H^{4}/\lambda^{4})}\cdot\frac{\tfrac12(H^{4}/\lambda^{2} + \lambda^{2})}{\lambda^{2}} = \frac{H^{4}}{\lambda^{4}}.
\]
Dividing by $\mathsf{N}$ normalises each direction for the Hermitian kinetic term, as in the stored mass computation. The check verifies the ratio exactly in both sectors for $(H^{2}, \lambda) = (1, 3), (1, \tfrac72), (2, 5), (\tfrac14, 9)$. In the two-doublet reading: $\Phi_{1} = \alpha$ transforms by $X$, and so does $\Phi_{2} = \bar{\beta}$, both with hypercharge $+\tfrac12$; $\Phi_{2}^{\dagger}\Phi_{1} = \beta^{\mathsf T}\alpha = Q(c)$; at $c_{\lambda}$, $|\Phi_{1}| = H^{2}/\lambda$ and $|\Phi_{2}| = \lambda$, so $\tan\beta_{2} = \lambda^{2}/H^{2} = e^{2\eta}$, every fermion entry comes from $\Phi_{2}$ (one doublet coupling to all fermions), and the charged direction $(\Phi_{1}', \Phi_{2}') = (a, (H^{2}/\lambda^{2})a)e_{5}$ is the orthogonal complement of the eaten direction, as in a two-doublet model with that angle; the ratio above is $\cot^{2}\beta_{2}$.

\emph{(iii).} The vertex of a $W_{j}$ with the neutral mode and a charged direction $d$ comes from the cross term of the Hermitian kinetic term, with coefficient proportional to $G(dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda, T_{j}d) = -G(T_{j}\,dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda, d)$, since $T_{j}$ is $G$-antisymmetric. For $j = 1, 2$, $T_{j}$ carries the slot-$4$ vector $dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda = (-H^{2}/\lambda^{2}, -1)e_{4}$ into slot $5$, where the four real directions are the two eaten ones $T_{1}c_{\lambda}$, $T_{2}c_{\lambda}$ and the two physical charged ones; the check verifies that the two planes are $G$-orthogonal and span the image ($|P_{\text{phys}}w|^{2} + |P_{\text{eaten}}w|^{2} = G(w, w)$), and that
\[
|P_{\text{phys}}w|^{2}(\lambda^{4} - H^{4})^{2} = 4H^{4}\lambda^{4}\,|P_{\text{eaten}}w|^{2}, \qquad w = T_{j}\frac{dc_{\lambda}}{d\lambda},
\]
in the four frames. Since $\sinh 2\eta = (\lambda^{4} - H^{4})/(2H^{2}\lambda^{2})$, the ratio is $1/\sinh^{2}2\eta$: in two-doublet language $\cos^{2}(\beta_{2} - \alpha_{2})/\sin^{2}(\beta_{2} - \alpha_{2})$ with the neutral mode as the light scalar.

\emph{(iv).} $\mathsf{N}$, $m$ and $G$ are sums of $|\alpha_{a}|^{2}$, $|\beta_{a}|^{2}$ and of $\bar{\alpha}_{a}\alpha'_{a}$, $\bar{\beta}_{a}\beta'_{a}$, kept by a common phase on $\alpha$; $u$ commutes with $X$ and so with $T_{j}$ and $Y$; the moment maps are $G(c, -I_{4}T c)$, kept; $|Q|$ is kept and $Q \mapsto uQ$. The check verifies each on three generic vectors and two phases, including $Q(uc) \ne Q(c)$, and that the locus $\{Q = 0\}$ is kept. The D-term action is a function of the $\mu$'s and of the level; every $W(\mathsf{N})$ is a function of $\mathsf{N}$; the kinetic term is built from $G$ and the generators; the Yukawa entries are (i). So the one term of the stored action that the phase does not keep is the constraint $Q(c) = -H^{2}$ that defines $L$. At $H = 0$ the vacuum is $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-\lambda, 0)$ on $\{Q = 0\}$, and the check finds the charged plane with $\beta' = 0$, $\alpha'_{5} \ne 0$ at $\lambda = 3, \tfrac72$.

\emph{(v).} $\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) = \tfrac12(H^{4}/\lambda^{2} + \lambda^{2}) < \lambda^{2}$ for $\lambda^{2} > H^{2}$, so $\cot\beta_{2} = H^{2}/\lambda^{2} < H^{2}/\mathsf{N}^{*} = g^{2}H^{2}/(2M_{W}^{2})$ with $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N}^{*}$ (stored gauge form). The check bounds $g^{2} = 4\pi\alpha/\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ above with $\pi < \tfrac{22}{7}$ and the stored $\alpha^{-1}(M_{Z}) = 127.951$, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 0.23122$, takes $H^{2} = \Lambda(\hbar c)^{2}/3$ from the stored $\Lambda = 1.09 \times 10^{-52}$ m$^{-2}$ and $\hbar c = 197.3269804$ MeV fm, and the stored $M_{W} = 80.3692$ GeV, and finds $g^{2}H^{2}/(2M_{W}^{2}) < 4.66 \times 10^{-89}$. Since $\lambda^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}^{*} - H^{4}/\lambda^{2} < 2\mathsf{N}^{*}$, also $\cot\beta_{2} > H^{2}/(2\mathsf{N}^{*}) = g^{2}H^{2}/(4M_{W}^{2})$, and the check, with $\tfrac{333}{106} < \pi < \tfrac{22}{7}$, puts this lower end in $(2.32, 2.33) \times 10^{-89}$; the two differ from $\cot\beta_{2}$ by relative orders $1$ and $H^{4}/\mathsf{N}^{*2}$, so $\cot\beta_{2} \approx 2.3 \times 10^{-89}$ (computed: $H^{2} \approx 1.41 \times 10^{-84}$ GeV$^{2}$, $g^{2} \approx 0.425$, $v = \sqrt{2\mathsf{N}^{*}} \approx 246.6$ GeV). Here $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, so $H$ is $H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, not $H_{0}$; the two differ by a factor of order one. For a charged scalar coupling to $t\bar{b}$ through one doublet with angle $\beta_{2}$, $\Gamma(t \to bH^{+})/\Gamma(t \to bW^{+}) = \cot^{2}\beta_{2}\,(1 - x)^{2}/((1 - y)^{2}(1 + 2y))$ with $m_{b}$ neglected (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-top-to-charged-higgs-width-ratio}, the standard tree formulas); the check finds $K < \tfrac12$ at both ends of the bracket $m_{\pm}^{2} \in [13702, 13803]$ GeV$^{2}$ of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-charged-scalar-sum-rule} (computed: $K \approx 0.33$), so the ratio is below $10^{-176}$ (computed: about $2 \times 10^{-178}$).

\emph{Reading (argued, not part of the statement).} (a) The ATLAS search for $t \to bH^{+}$, $H^{+} \to \tau\nu$ with $140$ fb$^{-1}$ at $13$ TeV bounds $\mathcal{B}(t \to bH^{+})\mathcal{B}(H^{+} \to \tau\nu)$ between $0.27\%$ and $0.02\%$ for $80$ to $160$ GeV (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-atlas-charged-higgs-top-decay-tau-nu-limits}); under the per-sector reading the branching is below $10^{-176}$ and the search says nothing. (b) Under the per-sector reading the phase on $\alpha$ is broken only through $Q(c) = -H^{2}$, and the charged pair is the lightest state carrying $\alpha$-number (the neutral component of $\alpha$ is fixed by the constraint): each of its couplings to lighter states computed here carries $H^{2}/\lambda^{2}$ or $1/\sinh 2\eta$, and its vertices with $W^{\pm}Z$ and $W^{\pm}\gamma$ vanish at tree level (the check computes the seagull coefficients at $c_{\lambda}$). Its partial widths are then of order $10^{-176}$ times a weak width, so it is stable on every time scale that matters. (c) A stable charged scalar near $117$ GeV is pair-produced through $\gamma^{*}/Z^{*}$ at hadron colliders and is not reached at LEP ($2m_{\pm} > 209$ GeV). CMS excluded Drell-Yan pair-produced long-lived staus below $339$ GeV at $7$ and $8$ TeV, with an observed limit $0.16$ of the predicted cross-section at the lowest tabulated mass $126$ GeV (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-long-lived-charged-particle-stau-limits}(i)); ATLAS at $13$ TeV with $36.1$ fb$^{-1}$ set $430$ GeV for staus, on a grid starting at $287$ GeV (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-long-lived-charged-particle-stau-limits}(ii)). The charged pair's $Z$ coupling, $\tfrac12 - \sin^{2}\theta_{W}$, is comparable to a right-handed stau's, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$, and its mass is lower, so its cross-section is comparable or larger. (d) The two readings then give two branches. Under the per-sector reading the couplings are suppressed by $e^{-2\eta}$ and the pair is stable, for every $W(\mathsf{N})$ and every level; near $117$ GeV it is excluded by the searches for stable charged particles of (c), a reinterpretation of the stau limits and not a dedicated analysis, and a population of stable charged particles left by a standard hot early universe is also excluded by searches for anomalous heavy hydrogen (memory, flagged). Under the covariant completion the $\alpha$ half carries the same $Y$ and $\tilde{Y}$ that give the masses, so the pair couples with the strength of the mass couplings, of order $m_{t}/v$ to $t$ and $b$, and searches in top decays apply: with a coupling of the size of the top's mass coupling the width ratio is $K$, about $0.33$ at $117$ GeV, a branching $K/(1 + K)$ of about $25\%$ (computed; the check brackets it in $(0.24, 0.25)$ at both ends of the mass bracket), far above the limits of (a) and of the corresponding searches in $H^{+} \to c\bar{s}$ (memory, flagged), so the $117$ GeV point is excluded on that branch too.
