synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus.formal:
Let $\mathcal{R}_{\C} = (H_{4} \oplus H_{5}) \otimes \C$, with $\C = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (the unit is the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, which commutes with the rung vectors, so $\mathcal{R}_{\C} = \mathcal{R} \oplus I_{4}\mathcal{R}$), be the complexified rung summand of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}, with mode vectors $v_{a}, w_{a}$ ($a = 4, 5$) of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}, and write $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$ with $\alpha, \beta \in \C^{2}$. The complex-bilinear extension of the quadratic form is $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, and the Hermitian norm of the tower's conjugation is $\mathsf{N}(c) = c^{*}\cdot c = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$. Let $X \in U(2)$, the slot mixing of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are}, act by $\alpha \mapsto X\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{X}\beta$, with generators $T_{1} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(E_{45} + E_{54})$, $T_{2} = \tfrac12(E_{45} - E_{54})$, $T_{3} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(E_{44} - E_{55})$ and hypercharge $Y = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(E_{44} + E_{55})$, in the slot generators $E_{ab} = v_{a}w_{b}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}, which act by commutator as the matrix unit on the $\alpha$-coefficients and as minus its transpose on the $\beta$-coefficients (on $\alpha$, the matrices $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{j}$ and $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\mathbf{1}$, a labelled reading); let $K = -2I_{4}Y$, so $Kv_{a} = v_{a}$ and $Kw_{a} = -w_{a}$, and let $m(c) = \operatorname{Re}(c^{*}\cdot Kc) = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})$, the hypercharge moment map. Let $\Lambda > 0$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, let $L = \{c \in \mathcal{R}_{\C} : Q(c) = -\Lambda/3\}$, the rung components $c$ for which $I + c$ is null with $I$ the frozen point, and let $c_{\lambda} = -\lambda w_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3\lambda}v_{4}$, $\lambda > 0$, be the rung component of the lift of $I$ in the frame $\lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}, Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i) at $\lambda = 1$); write $\eta = \log(\lambda/H)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The charge-preserving locus is the lift family.)} The stabiliser in $U(2)$ of $c \in L$ is trivial unless $\beta \in \C\bar{\alpha}$, and is then a circle. The points of $L$ with a circle stabiliser are exactly the $U(2)$-images of the $c_{\lambda}$, $\lambda > 0$; on them $|\beta| = \lambda$ and $|\alpha| = H^{2}/\lambda$, so $\lambda$ is a $U(2)$-invariant and $|\alpha||\beta| = \Lambda/3$. At $c_{\lambda}$ the unbroken generator is $Y - T_{3}$.
\item \emph{(Two readings of the gauge-boson masses.)} For gauge fields $(W^{j}, B)$ acting through $gT_{j}$ and $g'Y$, the quadratic forms in the gauge fields at $c_{\lambda}$ of the Hermitian kinetic term $\operatorname{Re}((Dc)^{*}\cdot Dc)$ and of the bilinear kinetic term $Q(Dc, Dc)$ are $\tfrac14 \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})P$ and $\tfrac14 Q(c_{\lambda})P$, with $P = \operatorname{diag}(g^{2}, g^{2}) \oplus \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} g^{2} & gg' \\ gg' & g'^{2}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, of eigenvalues $g^{2}, g^{2}, g^{2} + g'^{2}, 0$. The Hermitian reading has the electroweak pattern (one massless combination, $M_{Z}^{2}/M_{W}^{2} = (g^{2} + g'^{2})/g^{2}$) with scale $\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) = H^{2}\cosh 2\eta$; the bilinear reading has the same pattern with scale $-\Lambda/3$ in every frame.
\item \emph{(The rung unit is the neutral physical mode.)} The tangent space of $L$ at $c_{\lambda}$, of real dimension $6$, is the sum of the tangent space of the gauge orbit, of dimension $3$, and its orthogonal complement in it for $\operatorname{Re}(x^{*}\cdot y)$, of dimension $3$, on which the unbroken generator acts with charges $0, +1, -1$: the neutral line is spanned by $dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda$, and the charged plane is its orthogonal complement. Along the family $Q(dc_{\lambda}/d\eta) = \Lambda/3$ and $\mathsf{N}(dc_{\lambda}/d\eta) = \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})$.
\item \emph{(The rung unit is the imaginary hypercharge, fixed by the moment map.)} $e^{tK}c_{\lambda} = c_{\lambda e^{-t}}$, so the rung-unit boost $B_{s}$ on the plane $H_{4}$ is $e^{(\log s)K}$, the complexified hypercharge. Along every orbit $\mathsf{N}(e^{tK}c) = \tfrac12(e^{2t}|\alpha|^{2} + e^{-2t}|\beta|^{2})$, whose $t$-derivative is $2m(e^{tK}c)$; for $\alpha, \beta \ne 0$ it is strictly convex in $t$ and minimal exactly where $m = 0$. On the family $m(c_{\lambda}) = -H^{2}\sinh 2\eta$ and $\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) = H^{2}\cosh 2\eta$, so the frame is fixed by the value of $m$, and the balanced frame $\lambda = H$ is the zero of the hypercharge moment map.
\item \emph{(Product law, and the conjugation as mirror.)} For every $c$ with $\beta \in \C\bar{\alpha}$, $|Q(c)| = |\alpha||\beta|$ and $\mathsf{N}(c)^{2} = |Q(c)|^{2} + m(c)^{2}$; for every other $c$, $\mathsf{N}(c)^{2} > |Q(c)|^{2} + m(c)^{2}$. \emph{Reading through $c$:} by Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern}, the tree Dirac entries of the mass form of $c_{\lambda}$ itself are $H^{2}/\lambda$ on the up-type and neutrino pairs and $\lambda$ on the down-type and charged-lepton pairs: their product is $\Lambda/3$ in every frame and their ratio is $e^{2\eta}$. \emph{Reading through $c^{*}$:} if the up-type and neutrino entries are read from the mass form of $c_{\lambda}^{*} = \bar{\beta}\cdot v + \bar{\alpha}\cdot w$ and the down-type and charged-lepton entries from that of $c_{\lambda}$, the product law does not apply: both entries equal $\lambda$, their ratio is one in every frame, and their product is $\lambda^{2} = |\beta|^{2} = \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) - m(c_{\lambda}) = H^{2}e^{2\eta}$, a Hermitian quantity that the tractor norm does not fix. The conjugation $c \mapsto c^{*}$ preserves $L$, $\mathsf{N}$ and $Q$, reverses $m$, and sends $c_{\lambda}$ to $-c_{H^{2}/\lambda}$, so it acts on the charge-preserving orbits as $\eta \mapsto -\eta$.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (the Hubble unit).} Here $H$ is the de Sitter rate of $\Lambda$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, that is $H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, the $H$ of $N = M_{P}/H$; some texts quote $v/H$ with $H_{0}$, which differs from it by the factor $\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, of order one ($v/H \approx 2.1 \times 10^{44}$ against $v/H_{0} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{44}$; $\ln(v/H)$ changes by about $0.2$). The order $10^{-42}$ GeV of $H$ quoted in the proof holds for either.
synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus.technical: Write the rung component as a field with values in the complexified rung summand, a doublet $\alpha$ of hypercharge $+\tfrac12$ (the creation coefficients) and a conjugate doublet $\beta$ of hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ (the annihilation coefficients), and keep the one condition transport imposes: the frozen point's lift is null, so the field lies on $L$, where the complex bilinear invariant $\alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$ is fixed at $-\Lambda/3$. On $L$ electromagnetism survives exactly on the frozen point's lift family and its gauge images; there the two doublet lengths are $H^{2}/\lambda$ and $\lambda$, with product $\Lambda/3$ whatever the frame. Of the field's six real directions along $L$ three are gauge, one is neutral and two form a charged pair: the neutral one is the rung unit, so the radial Higgs mode of this field is the frame boost, not the tractor norm, which is frozen. The gauge-boson masses read the Hermitian norm $H^{2}\cosh 2\eta$ in the electroweak pattern, while a bilinear kinetic term would give the same pattern at the scale $\Lambda/3$ in every frame. The frame boost is the hypercharge rotation at imaginary angle; the Hermitian norm is convex along it, and its slope is the hypercharge moment map, which vanishes exactly at the balanced frame. On charge-preserving vectors the Hermitian norm, the tractor norm and the moment map satisfy $\mathsf{N}^{2} = |Q|^{2} + m^{2}$, and through the stored tree mass relations read through $c$ the up-type and down-type entries of the lift multiply to $\Lambda/3$ in every frame; if the up-type entries are read through the conjugate $c^{*}$ instead, as the Standard Model reads the conjugate doublet, the two entries are equal and their product is the Hermitian quantity $H^{2}e^{2\eta}$. The conjugation exchanges the frames $\lambda$ and $H^{2}/\lambda$.
synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus.lay: In the series the Higgs field sits in the extra directions that transport adds, and transport fixes one combination of its two halves, through the cosmological constant. Treating it as a field under that condition, the only direction in which it can change physically without breaking electromagnetism is the scale the earlier work called the rung unit, so the Higgs boson of this field is a ripple of that scale. The masses of the W and Z bosons come out in the right pattern if they are read with the quantum-mechanical (Hermitian) norm, which sees the scale; the geometric norm would give them a cosmologically small mass whatever the scale. Changing the scale is the hypercharge symmetry turned through an imaginary angle, and the scale is measured by a quantity that vanishes only at the frame matched to the cosmological scale. One consequence is sharp: if the quark masses come from this field through the series' single coupling and the up-type masses are read from the field itself rather than its conjugate, the up-type and down-type masses at tree level multiply to the coupling squared times the cosmological scale squared, whatever the scale chosen, which the observed top and bottom masses rule out; so one of those two readings has to go. Read through the conjugate, the up-type and down-type masses are equal and both grow with the scale.

proofs.main:
Conventions of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}: $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a}^{-} + e_{a}^{+})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a}^{+} - e_{a}^{-})$, so $Q(v_{a}) = Q(w_{a}) = 0$, $v_{a}\cdot w_{b} = \tfrac12\delta_{ab}$ and $v_{a}w_{b} + w_{b}v_{a} = \delta_{ab}$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}); the conjugation is $x^{*} = \theta(\bar{x})$ with $\theta$ fixing $e_{a}^{+}$ and negating $e_{a}^{-}$, so $\theta v_{a} = w_{a}$ and $v_{a}^{*} = w_{a}$. For $c = \alpha\cdot v + \beta\cdot w$ the complex-bilinear form is $Q(c) = 2\sum_{a}\alpha_{a}\beta_{a}\,(v_{a}\cdot w_{a}) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, and $c^{*} = \bar{\beta}\cdot v + \bar{\alpha}\cdot w$, so $c^{*}\cdot c = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$. The slot generators $E_{ab} = v_{a}w_{b}$ act on vectors by commutator as the matrix unit $e_{a}e_{b}^{\mathsf T}$ on the $v$-coefficients and as $-e_{b}e_{a}^{\mathsf T}$ on the $w$-coefficients, so $X = \sum X_{ab}E_{ab}$ acts by $(\alpha, \beta) \mapsto (X\alpha, -X^{\mathsf T}\beta)$, which for $X \in \uu(2)$ is $(X\alpha, \bar{X}\beta)$; the group $U(2)$ acts by $(\alpha, \beta) \mapsto (X\alpha, \bar{X}\beta)$ and preserves $Q$ (since $X^{\mathsf T}\bar{X} = \overline{X^{\dagger}X} = \mathbf{1}$) and $\mathsf{N}$. The hypercharge $Y = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\mathbf{1}$ has weight $+\tfrac12$ on $v$ and $-\tfrac12$ on $w$, as in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are}. The frozen point $I$ lies in the ground and the rung summand is orthogonal to it, so $Q(I + c) = \Lambda/3 + Q(c)$ and $I + c$ is null exactly when $c \in L$; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}(1) every lift $X_{\mu}(I)$ has rung component $c_{\mu} \in L$, and $c_{1}$ is the rung component of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i).

(1) $X$ fixes $c$ iff $X\alpha = \alpha$ and $\bar{X}\beta = \beta$, that is $X\bar{\beta} = \bar{\beta}$. On $L$, $\alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = -H^{2} \ne 0$, so $\alpha \ne 0 \ne \beta$. If $\alpha$ and $\bar{\beta}$ are independent they span $\C^{2}$ and $X = \mathbf{1}$. If $\bar{\beta} = \bar{\kappa}\alpha$, $X$ fixes the line of $\alpha$ pointwise and, being unitary, acts on its orthogonal line by a phase, which may be any phase: the stabiliser is a circle. Then $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\kappa\bar{\alpha} = \kappa|\alpha|^{2} = -H^{2}$, so $\kappa = -H^{2}/|\alpha|^{2}$ is real and negative. Put $u = \alpha/|\alpha|$ and choose $A \in U(2)$ with $Au = e_{1}$ (for instance the matrix with rows $\bar{u}^{\mathsf T}$ and $(-u_{2}, u_{1})$). Then $A\alpha = |\alpha|e_{1}$ and $\bar{A}\beta = \kappa\,\overline{A\alpha} = -(H^{2}/|\alpha|)e_{1}$, which is $c_{\lambda}$ with $\lambda = H^{2}/|\alpha| = |\beta|$. Conversely $c_{\lambda}$ has $\alpha = (H^{2}/\lambda)e_{1}$, $\beta = -\lambda e_{1} \in \C\bar{\alpha}$, and $U(2)$ preserves the alignment and the lengths. Since $|\beta|$ is $U(2)$-invariant, distinct $\lambda$ lie on distinct orbits. At $c_{\lambda}$ the stabiliser fixes $e_{1}$ and rotates $e_{2}$: it is generated by $I_{4}E_{55} = Y - T_{3}$, as $Y - T_{3} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(\mathbf{1} - \sigma_{3}) = \operatorname{diag}(0, I_{4})$.

(2) With $Dc = dc + \sum_{A}g_{A}A^{A}T_{A}c$ the gauge-field quadratic forms are $g_{A}g_{B}\operatorname{Re}((T_{A}c)^{*}\cdot T_{B}c)$ and $g_{A}g_{B}Q(T_{A}c, T_{B}c)$, $Q(\cdot,\cdot)$ the polarisation. At $c_{\lambda} = a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$ ($a = H^{2}/\lambda$, $b = -\lambda$ real), $T_{A}c = (aX_{A}e_{1}, b\bar{X}_{A}e_{1})$, so $\operatorname{Re}((T_{A}c)^{*}\cdot T_{B}c) = \tfrac12(a^{2} + b^{2})\operatorname{Re}(X_{A}^{\dagger}X_{B})_{11}$, and with $X_{A} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{A}$ ($\sigma_{0} = \mathbf{1}$ for $Y$), $X_{A}^{\dagger}X_{B} = \tfrac14\sigma_{A}\sigma_{B}$, whose $(1,1)$ entry has real part $\delta_{AB}$ for $A, B \in \{1,2,3\}$, $(\sigma_{3})_{11} = 1$ for the pair $(T_{3}, Y)$ and $1$ for $(Y, Y)$. This is $\tfrac14 \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})P_{0}$ with $P_{0} = \operatorname{diag}(1,1) \oplus \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, and the couplings make it $\tfrac14 \mathsf{N} P$. For the bilinear form, $Q(T_{A}c, T_{B}c) = ab\operatorname{Re}(X_{A}^{\mathsf T}\bar{X}_{B})_{11}$ and $X_{A}^{\mathsf T}\bar{X}_{B} = \overline{X_{A}^{\dagger}X_{B}}$ for anti-Hermitian $X_{A}$, giving $\tfrac14 ab P = \tfrac14 Q(c_{\lambda})P$. The block $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} g^{2} & gg' \\ gg' & g'^{2}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ has eigenvalues $0$ and $g^{2} + g'^{2}$. Finally $\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) = \tfrac12(H^{4}\lambda^{-2} + \lambda^{2}) = H^{2}\cosh 2\eta$, as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(4), and $Q(c_{\lambda}) = -\Lambda/3$.

(3) $T_{c}L = \{\delta : \alpha^{\mathsf T}\delta\beta + \delta\alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = 0\}$ is a complex hyperplane, of real dimension $6$, and the orbit has dimension $4 - 1 = 3$ by (1). At $c_{\lambda}$ the condition reads $a\,\delta\beta_{4} + b\,\delta\alpha_{4} = 0$ with $\delta\alpha_{5}, \delta\beta_{5}$ free. In the plane $H_{4}$ the solutions are $z(a, -b)$, $z \in \C$; $z$ real gives $(a, -b) = -\lambda\,dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda$, and $z$ imaginary gives $I_{4}(a, -b) = 2T_{3}c = 2Yc$, a gauge direction. In $H_{5}$ the gauge directions are $T_{1}c = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(a, -b)$ and $T_{2}c = -\tfrac12(a, b)$ (coefficients of $(v_{5}, w_{5})$), so the physical directions there form a real plane. The real vector $dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda$ is orthogonal to the purely imaginary $T_{3}c$, and its $H_{4}$ support makes it orthogonal to $T_{1}c, T_{2}c$; it is fixed by $Y - T_{3} = \operatorname{diag}(0, I_{4})$, which acts only on the $H_{5}$ coefficients, by $I_{4}$ on $\delta\alpha_{5}$ and $-I_{4}$ on $\delta\beta_{5}$, so it acts on the physical plane in $H_{5}$ as a rotation with $(Y - T_{3})^{2} = -1$: charges $\pm1$. With $dc_{\lambda}/d\eta = \lambda\,dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda = -(H^{2}/\lambda)v_{4} - \lambda w_{4}$, $Q = (H^{2}/\lambda)\lambda = H^{2}$ and $\mathsf{N} = \tfrac12(H^{4}\lambda^{-2} + \lambda^{2}) = \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})$.

(4) $e^{tK}$ multiplies $\alpha$ by $e^{t}$ and $\beta$ by $e^{-t}$, so $e^{tK}c_{\lambda} = (e^{t}H^{2}/\lambda)v_{4} - e^{-t}\lambda w_{4} = c_{\lambda e^{-t}}$; the boost $B_{s}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm} ($v \mapsto sv$, $w \mapsto w/s$ on $H_{4}$) is $e^{(\log s)K}$ there. $\mathsf{N}(e^{tK}c) = \tfrac12(e^{2t}|\alpha|^{2} + e^{-2t}|\beta|^{2})$ has derivative $e^{2t}|\alpha|^{2} - e^{-2t}|\beta|^{2} = 2m(e^{tK}c)$ and second derivative $2(e^{2t}|\alpha|^{2} + e^{-2t}|\beta|^{2}) > 0$, so it is strictly convex with its only minimum where $m = 0$. On the family $m(c_{\lambda}) = \tfrac12(H^{4}\lambda^{-2} - \lambda^{2}) = -H^{2}\sinh 2\eta$, strictly decreasing in $\lambda$, and zero exactly at $\lambda = H$, where $\mathsf{N} = H^{2}$.

(5) $\mathsf{N}^{2} - m^{2} = |\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2}$ identically, and $|Q|^{2} = |\alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta|^{2} = |\langle\bar{\alpha}, \beta\rangle|^{2} \le |\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2}$ by Cauchy-Schwarz, with equality iff $\beta \in \C\bar{\alpha}$. Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern} gives, for $c = a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$, tree entries $|a|$ on $(L, \nu^{c}), (Q, u^{c})$ and $|b|$ on $(L, e^{c}), (Q, d^{c})$; for $c_{\lambda}$, $|a| = H^{2}/\lambda$ and $|b| = \lambda$. Read through the conjugate instead, the same corollary applied to $c_{\lambda}^{*} = \bar{b}\,v_{4} + \bar{a}\,w_{4} = -\lambda v_{4} + (H^{2}/\lambda)w_{4}$ gives up-type entries $|\bar{b}| = \lambda$, while the down-type entries of $c_{\lambda}$ are $|b| = \lambda$; so the two are equal, with product $\lambda^{2} = |\beta|^{2} = \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) - m(c_{\lambda})$, since $\mathsf{N} - m = |\beta|^{2}$ identically, and $\lambda^{2} = H^{2}e^{2\eta}$. The tractor norm, $ab = -H^{2}$, enters only the reading through $c$. Finally $c_{\lambda}^{*} = \theta(c_{\lambda}) = -\lambda v_{4} + (H^{2}/\lambda)w_{4} = -c_{H^{2}/\lambda}$; the conjugation fixes $Q$ on $L$ (it conjugates $Q$, which is real there), preserves $\mathsf{N}$, exchanges $|\alpha|$ and $|\beta|$ and so reverses $m$; and since $-\mathbf{1} \in U(2)$, the orbit of $-c_{H^{2}/\lambda}$ is that of $c_{H^{2}/\lambda}$.

The script builds $\Cl(2,2)$ in GA.py, reads $Q$ and the Hermitian product from GA.dot and the slot generators from GA.mul, and checks: the pair relations, the frame involution and the generator action; for three values of $\Lambda$ and five frames, $Q(c_{\lambda}) = -\Lambda/3$, a one-dimensional stabiliser spanned by $Y - T_{3}$, trivial stabilisers at two misaligned points of $L$, and, at six aligned points of $L$ with complex coefficients, an explicit unitary matrix carrying them to $c_{H^{2}/|\alpha|}$; the two gauge quadratic forms entry by entry for five frames, with the characteristic polynomial $t(t - g^{2})^{2}(t - g^{2} - g'^{2})$ of $P$ at $g = 1$, $g' = \tfrac12$ evaluated at five points; the normal space of dimension $3$, the neutral line, the charged plane with $(Y - T_{3})^{2} = -1$ on it, and $Q(dc/d\eta) = \Lambda/3$, $\mathsf{N}(dc/d\eta) = \mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})$; the boost as $e^{(\log s)K}$ on the family, the closed forms of $\mathsf{N}$ and $m$ along it, the minimum at the balanced frame and $\mathsf{N}^{2} = Q^{2} + m^{2}$; and the product law read through $c$, the equal entries and the product $\mathsf{N} - m = \lambda^{2}$ read through $c^{*}$, the mirror $c_{\lambda}^{*} = -c_{H^{2}/\lambda}$, the identity $\mathsf{N}^{2} = |Q|^{2} + m^{2}$ at two aligned vectors off $L$ with complex $\kappa$ and the strict inequality at a misaligned vector.

Reading, argued and not part of the statement. (a) \emph{The quantum.} On $L$ the rung field has one neutral physical scalar, the rung unit $\eta$, and one charged scalar; the second neutral scalar and the pseudoscalar of a pair of doublets are removed by the complex constraint $Q(c) = -\Lambda/3$, and the tractor norm, which would be the radial mode of a doublet, is frozen. So the quantum of this field that plays the Higgs boson's part is a fluctuation of the frame boost, with Hermitian kinetic coefficient $\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda})$, and for $\lambda \gg H$ the canonical field is approximately $\lambda$ itself. (b) \emph{The potential.} Any $U(2)$-invariant potential restricted to the charge-preserving part of $L$ is a function of $\eta$ alone by (1), and a conjugation-invariant one is even in $\eta$ by (5), stationary at the balanced frame. A hypercharge D-term $\tfrac12 g'^{2}(m - \xi)^{2}$ puts the minimum at $m = \xi$; without a constant $\xi$ it is the balanced frame, where $\mathsf{N} = H^{2}$ and the weak scale would be the Hubble rate. With $\xi$, the number $v/H$ is traded for $\xi/H^{2}$: nothing here fixes it, so the premise \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number} is neither derived nor refuted. (c) \emph{A tension.} With one coupling $y$ through the pairing (a single $10$) and the up-type masses read through $c$, the product law says every charge-preserving vacuum on $L$ has tree masses with $m_{u}m_{d} = y^{2}\Lambda/3$, of order $y^{2}(10^{-42}\,\mathrm{GeV})^{2}$, whatever the frame; the observed third family has $m_{t}m_{b} \approx 700\,\mathrm{GeV}^{2}$ (record values, from memory). So either the electroweak vacuum is not on $L$, and the Higgs's tractor norm is a second quantity of order $m_{t}m_{b}/y^{2}$ rather than the frozen point's $-\Lambda/3$, or the up-type masses are read through $c^{*}$, as the Standard Model reads them through the conjugate doublet, so that they too are Hermitian readings; in the second case $c^{*} = \bar{\beta}\cdot v + \bar{\alpha}\cdot w$ puts $|\beta| = \lambda$ on the up-type pairs and both masses scale with the frame.

synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost.formal:
Let $\mathcal{R} = H_{4} \oplus H_{5}$ be the rung summand of the transported ambient space of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}, two adjoined hyperbolic planes with frame $e_{a}^{\pm}$, $Q(e_{a}^{\pm}) = \pm 1$, mode vectors $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a}^{-} + e_{a}^{+})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a}^{+} - e_{a}^{-})$ ($a = 4, 5$), so $v_{a}w_{b} + w_{b}v_{a} = \delta_{ab}$, and let $*$ be the tower's conjugate-linear antiautomorphism, on vectors $x^{*} = \theta(\bar{x})$ with $\theta$ fixing $e_{a}^{+}$ and negating $e_{a}^{-}$, so $v_{a}^{*} = w_{a}$. Let $E_{ab} = v_{a}w_{b}$ act on vectors by commutator, and let $\uu(2)$ be the real span of $I_{4}(E_{ab} + E_{ba})$, $E_{ab} - E_{ba}$, $I_{4}E_{aa}$, the slot mixing of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are}, acting on $\mathcal{R} \otimes \C = \mathcal{R} \oplus I_{4}\mathcal{R}$ ($\C = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the unit being the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, which commutes with the rung vectors) by $a\cdot v + b\cdot w \mapsto (Xa)\cdot v + (\bar{X}b)\cdot w$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The real summand carries the split form.)} The real span of the $E_{ab}$ is $\gl(2,\R) \subset \so(\mathcal{R}) = \so(2,2)$, acting on the real slice $\mathcal{R}$. The subalgebra of $\uu(2)$ preserving $\mathcal{R}$ is one-dimensional, spanned by $E_{45} - E_{54}$; in particular the compact $U(1)$ generated by the hypercharge does not preserve $\mathcal{R}$, on whose rung vectors the hypercharge acts with the real weights $\pm 3$, as a boost.
\item \emph{(No compact weak connection on the real summand.)} The trace form $\tr(XY)$ of $\so(2,2)$ on $\mathcal{R}$ has signature $(4,2)$, and $\so(2,2)$ contains no subalgebra isomorphic to $\su(2)$. Hence no group of isometries of $(\mathcal{R}, Q)$ is locally $SU(2)$, and no connection on the real rung summand preserving its metric, flat or curved, has holonomy containing an $SU(2)$.
\item \emph{(No positive invariant kinetic form.)} The symmetric bilinear forms on $\mathcal{R}$ invariant under $\gl(2,\R)$, and a fortiori under $\so(2,2)$, are the multiples of the metric, of signature $(2,2)$: a kinetic term $k\,Q(\nabla c)$ for an $\mathcal{R}$-valued field $c$ has two directions of each sign for either sign of $k$. The form $\ip{\theta x}{y}$ is positive definite, and needs $\theta$, that is, the frame.
\item \emph{(The rung unit is the frame's boost.)} Take the lift of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i) in the null pair $(n_{0}', n_{\infty}') = (-\lambda w_{4},\, 2\lambda^{-1}v_{4})$, $\lambda > 0$, the proposition's being $\lambda = 1$. Its rung component is $c_{\lambda} = -\lambda w_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1}v_{4}$, with
\[
Q(c_{\lambda}) = -\frac{\Lambda}{3}\ \text{ for every } \lambda, \qquad \ip{\theta c_{\lambda}}{c_{\lambda}} = \tfrac12\Bigl(\lambda^{2} + \frac{\Lambda^{2}}{9}\lambda^{-2}\Bigr) = \frac{\Lambda}{3} + \tfrac12\Bigl(\lambda - \frac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1}\Bigr)^{2}.
\]
\item \emph{(Unitary only when balanced.)} The $U(2)$-invariant real forms of $(\mathcal{R} \otimes \C, Q)$ on which $Q$ is real are $\mathcal{R}_{\mu} = \{a\cdot v + \mu\bar{a}\cdot w\}$, $\mu \in \R \setminus \{0\}$, of signature $(4,0)$ for $\mu > 0$ and $(0,4)$ for $\mu < 0$; the tower's $*$ fixes $\mathcal{R}_{1}$. For $\Lambda > 0$ the complex line $\C c_{\lambda}$ meets $\mathcal{R}_{1} \cup \mathcal{R}_{-1}$ if and only if $\lambda^{2} = \Lambda/3$, equivalently $\ip{\theta c_{\lambda}}{c_{\lambda}} = |Q(c_{\lambda})|$, and then $I_{4}c_{\lambda} \in \mathcal{R}_{1}$.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost.technical: The two hyperbolic planes that transport adjoins for the rungs form a real space of signature $(2,2)$, and the series' slot mixing, the group the Higgs doublet's representation is read from, acts on it only after complexification. On the real summand itself the slot generators span the split algebra $\gl(2,\R)$; only a one-dimensional rotation of the compact $\uu(2)$ preserves the real summand, and the hypercharge acts there as a boost. Since $\so(2,2)$ has trace form of signature $(4,2)$ and so no room for a compact $\su(2)$, no metric connection of the real rung summand, whatever its curvature, can be the weak gauge field, and the only invariant kinetic form is the metric itself, indefinite. A positive kinetic form and the compact real form on which the weak group acts both need the tower's $*$, that is, the frame. The store does not propose a metric connection of the real summand as the weak connection, the weak group acting on the complexification; clause (2) records why that reading is closed. The frame carries a scale. In the lift of the frozen point, a boost of the null pair leaves the tractor norm $-\Lambda/3$ of the rung component unchanged and changes its $*$-norm, which is $\Lambda/3 + \tfrac12(\lambda - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1})^{2}$; the rung component lies in a $U(2)$-invariant real form, up to a phase, only at the balanced boost $\lambda^{2} = \Lambda/3$, where its $*$-norm is $\Lambda/3$.
synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost.lay: The extra directions that transport adds, where the series finds the Higgs doublet, have a split geometry: two directions count positively and two negatively. The symmetry of the weak force is a rotation-like symmetry that needs an all-positive geometry, so it cannot act on these directions as they stand, and no energy expression built from their own geometry is positive. Both problems are cured by one extra choice the series already makes, a preferred frame. That frame comes with a scale, which the geometry of these directions does not see. On a reading argued in the proof but not proved, that scale is the unexplained ratio of the weak scale to the cosmological scale, and a frame matched to the cosmological scale would make the weak scale as small as the Hubble rate.

proofs.main:
The rung summand, its mode vectors and the involution $*$ are those of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}: the adjoined null pairs satisfy $v_{a}w_{b} + w_{b}v_{a} = \delta_{ab}$, and $*$ fixes the positive frame generators and negates the negative ones, so on a vector $x^{*} = \theta(\bar{x})$. In the basis $(v_{4}, v_{5}, w_{4}, w_{5})$ the metric is $\ip{v_{a}}{w_{b}} = \tfrac12\delta_{ab}$, all other pairings zero, and $\theta$ exchanges $v_{a}$ and $w_{a}$.

(1) From the anticommutators, $[v_{a}w_{b}, v_{c}] = \delta_{bc}v_{a}$ and $[v_{a}w_{b}, w_{c}] = -\delta_{ac}w_{b}$: $E_{ab}$ is the matrix unit on the $v$'s and minus its transpose on the $w$'s. These are real operators on $\mathcal{R}$, each preserving $Q$ (each $E_{ab}$ with $a \neq b$ is the real bivector $v_{a}\wedge w_{b}$, and $E_{aa} - \tfrac12$ is $v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$), so their real span is $\gl(2,\R)$ inside $\so(2,2)$. A real combination $\sum c_{k}G_{k}$ of the four $\uu(2)$ generators preserves $\mathcal{R}$ if and only if its matrix is real; the imaginary parts come only from the three generators carrying $I_{4}$ and are independent, so the coefficients of those three vanish and the solution space is spanned by $E_{45} - E_{54}$. The rung number $N_{R} = E_{44} + E_{55}$ acts as $+1$ on the $v$'s and $-1$ on the $w$'s, so the hypercharge $3N_{R} - 2N_{W}$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are} has the real weights $\pm 3$ on rung vectors, and its compact $U(1)$, $\exp(I_{4}\varphi\,y)$, multiplies $v_{a}$ by $e^{3I_{4}\varphi}$, which leaves $\mathcal{R}$ only for $\varphi \in \tfrac{\pi}{3}\mathbb{Z}$.

(2) The six bivectors $e_{i}e_{j}$ span $\so(2,2)$ acting by commutator; the two whose generators have equal square are rotations with $\tr(X^{2}) < 0$, the four mixed ones boosts with $\tr(X^{2}) > 0$, and the script computes the trace form's signature $(4,2)$ exactly by congruence diagonalisation (control: $\so(4)$ gives $(0,6)$). Suppose $\mathfrak{k} \subset \so(2,2)$ with $\mathfrak{k} \cong \su(2)$. The restriction of the trace form to $\mathfrak{k}$ is invariant, so it is a multiple of the Killing form of $\mathfrak{k}$. Take $X \in \mathfrak{k}$ nonzero; in $\mathfrak{k}\otimes\C \cong \mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$, $X = \tfrac{I_{4}\alpha}{2}H$ for an $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$-triple $(H, E, F)$ and real $\alpha \neq 0$, and on the faithful four-dimensional representation $H$ is diagonalisable with integer eigenvalues $m_{j}$, not all zero (imported: Fulton and Harris, Lecture 11, cited from memory). So $\tr(X^{2}) = -\tfrac{\alpha^{2}}{4}\sum_{j} m_{j}^{2} < 0$, and the trace form is negative definite on the three-dimensional $\mathfrak{k}$, which is impossible since its negative index on $\so(2,2)$ is $2$. A group of isometries of $(\mathcal{R}, Q)$ that is locally $SU(2)$ would have such a Lie algebra; and the holonomy algebra of a metric connection lies in $\so(\mathcal{R})$, whatever its curvature, so it contains no $\su(2)$.

(3) Let $K$ be symmetric and invariant under the $E_{ab}$. Invariance under $N_{R}$ gives $2K(v_{a}, v_{b}) = 0$ and $-2K(w_{a}, w_{b}) = 0$, so only the block $K(v_{a}, w_{b})$ survives; invariance under $E_{ab}$, $a \neq b$, makes that block a multiple of the identity. So $K = kQ$; the script solves the linear system exactly for $\gl(2,\R)$, for its $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\R)$ part and for $\so(2,2)$, finding a one-dimensional solution space each time. $Q$ on $\mathcal{R}$ has signature $(2,2)$. The form $\ip{\theta x}{y}$ is $\tfrac12$ times the identity in the basis $(v_{a}, w_{a})$ paired with its $\theta$-image, signature $(4,0)$ (script); it is not $\so(2,2)$-invariant, since a boost of a hyperbolic plane commutes with $\theta$ only when trivial.

(4) The lift of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i) is $X(I) = n_{0}' + I + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}n_{\infty}'$ for any null pair with $\ip{n_{0}'}{n_{\infty}'} = -1$; with $n_{0}' = -\lambda w_{4}$, $n_{\infty}' = 2\lambda^{-1}v_{4}$ the pairing is $-2\cdot\tfrac12 = -1$, and the rung component is $c_{\lambda} = -\lambda w_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1}v_{4}$; at $\lambda = 1$ it is the proposition's $-w_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}v_{4}$. Then $Q(c_{\lambda}) = 2(-\lambda)(\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1})\tfrac12 = -\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}$, and $\theta c_{\lambda} = -\lambda v_{4} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1}w_{4}$, so $\ip{\theta c_{\lambda}}{c_{\lambda}} = \tfrac12(\lambda^{2} + \tfrac{\Lambda^{2}}{9}\lambda^{-2})$, and subtracting $\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}$ leaves the square displayed. The script verifies both identities for twelve rational pairs $(\Lambda, \lambda)$. The boost $(n_{0}', n_{\infty}') \mapsto (e^{t}n_{0}', e^{-t}n_{\infty}')$ is an isometry of $\mathcal{R}$ fixing every vector of the ground space, so it changes no tractor norm; it changes $\theta$, and with it the $*$-norm.

(5) Let $\sigma$ be a conjugate-linear involution of $\mathcal{R}\otimes\C$ commuting with $U(2)$, with $Q$ real on its fixed set. The centre $\exp(I_{4}\varphi N_{R})$ multiplies $R_{2} = \mathrm{span}(v_{4}, v_{5})$ by $e^{I_{4}\varphi}$ and $\overline{R}_{2} = \mathrm{span}(w_{4}, w_{5})$ by $e^{-I_{4}\varphi}$, and $\sigma$ commutes with it, so $\sigma$ maps $R_{2}$ to $\overline{R}_{2}$; composing with complex conjugation of coefficients gives a $U(2)$-equivariant linear map of $R_{2}$, a scalar $\mu$ by Schur's lemma. So $\sigma(a\cdot v) = \mu\bar{a}\cdot w$, the fixed set is $\mathcal{R}_{\mu}$, and $Q(a\cdot v + \mu\bar{a}\cdot w) = \mu|a|^{2}$ is real exactly when $\mu$ is real. That $U(2)$ preserves each $\mathcal{R}_{\mu}$ is $\bar{X}(\mu\bar{a}) = \mu\overline{Xa}$; the script checks it for each generator and three values of $\mu$. The tower's $*$ sends $a\cdot v$ to $\bar{a}\cdot w$, so its fixed set is $\mathcal{R}_{1}$. Now $c_{\lambda} = a\cdot v + b\cdot w$ with $a = (\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\lambda^{-1}, 0)$, $b = (-\lambda, 0)$, and $zc_{\lambda} \in \mathcal{R}_{\pm 1}$ requires $|zb| = |za|$, that is $\lambda^{2} = \Lambda/3$; the action of $U(2)$ preserves $|a|$ and $|b|$ separately, so no element of $U(2)\cdot\C^{\times}$ helps. Conversely at $\lambda^{2} = \Lambda/3$, $a = (\lambda, 0) = -b$, and $I_{4}c_{\lambda}$ has $I_{4}b = -I_{4}\lambda = \overline{I_{4}a}$, so it lies in $\mathcal{R}_{1}$. By (4), $\lambda^{2} = \Lambda/3$ is exactly where the $*$-norm reaches its minimum $|Q(c_{\lambda})|$. The script checks membership at a balanced pair and non-membership, through $|a| \neq |b|$, at unbalanced ones.

Reading, argued and not part of the statement. Standard-Model paper Proposition 9.29(2) (\claimref{standard-model.what-derived-what-not}) calls the coefficient one of $-w_{4}$ the rung unit and reads a weak scale of $246$ GeV as that unit being about $10^{44}$ Hubble units. By (4) the tractor geometry does not see this unit at all, and the positive norm a kinetic term would use does: with $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$ and $\lambda = H e^{s}$, $\ip{\theta c_{\lambda}}{c_{\lambda}} = H^{2}\cosh 2s$. A weak scale of the observed size needs $e^{2s}$ of order $(v/H)^{2} \approx 10^{88}$, while the one choice that makes the frozen point's rung component itself a value of a unitary doublet, $s = 0$ by (5), gives a $*$-norm of $H^{2}$, a weak scale equal to the Hubble rate. So the transported frozen point does not fix the weak scale through unitarity; the open number is the frame's boost, and by (2) and (3) the same frame is what a positive kinetic term and a compact weak connection need. Whether the frame is a datum of the series beside $N$ is a decision for the premise register, not settled here.

synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number.technical:
In the lift of the frozen point to the rung directions, the scale of the rung component, which sets the weak scale, is the boost of the rung frame against the lift's null pair. Transport cannot see it: every clause of totality holds in every boosted frame, the rung component's tractor norm is $-\Lambda/3$ whatever the boost, and a change of the boost moves the component along a level set of that norm, transverse to the direction in which $\Lambda$, and so $N$, would move it. The one frame the structure singles out, the balanced one, would put the weak scale at the Hubble scale, which is off by about $10^{44}$. In the rung field's D-term action the frame is set by the level, a constant of the action.

This premise records the decision: the level, made dimensionless as $\xi G$, is a second free number of the laws beside $N$, not derived and not a function of $N$. Under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion, which the series adopts, $N$ is initial data; the D-term potential at the vacuum does not contain the Hubble rate, so the weak scale against the Planck mass, $v/M_{P}$, is the law up to a relative correction of order $(H/v)^{4}$, and the rung-frame boost $v/H$ is initial data. The relation $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ is an identity in the units used, not a law. Two models at equal $N$ with different levels satisfy every stored relation (\claimref{synthesis.d-term-level-free-at-fixed-n}), so nothing stored fixes $\xi G$, as the premise says. An earlier version held $v/H$ as the law; the D-term action read under the promotion met its refutation condition, and it is restated here. The premise would be refuted by a derivation of $\xi G$, from the transport structure, another premise, or a dynamics with no further free constant, by a proof that it is a function of $N$, or by a coupling of the rung action to the promoted $\Lambda$ that makes the level proportional to it.
synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number.lay: In this framework almost every hierarchy of scales comes from one huge number, N, the ratio of the Planck mass to the scale set by the cosmological constant. The strength of the weak force's symmetry breaking, about 246 GeV, does not: it is set by how a particular reference frame in the extra dimensions is stretched, and the framework's construction works equally well for every stretch. The only stretch the structure itself prefers gives a weak scale far too small, by 44 powers of ten. In the field theory written for the Higgs field the stretch is fixed by one constant, and this assumption accepts that constant as a second basic number of the laws, put in by hand beside N. Since the framework treats N as a fact about the universe's history, the weak scale measured against the Planck mass is then the law, and the weak scale measured against the cosmological scale is a historical fact. It would be overturned if anyone derived the constant, showed it follows from N, or tied it to the cosmological constant.

synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm.formal:
Let $I$ be a frozen point of the ground space with $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, let $(e_{+}, e_{-})$ be the orthonormal pair adjoined by the next completion, $v = \tfrac12(e_{-} + e_{+})$, $w = \tfrac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$, $\nO' = -w$, $\nInf' = 2v$ as in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}, and $*$ the conjugation of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} ($v^{*} = w$; on the real rung plane it fixes $e_{+}$ and negates $e_{-}$), with $\|y\|_{*} = y^{*}\cdot y$. For $\mu > 0$ let $X_{\mu}(x) = \mu\,\nO' + x + \frac{Q(x)}{2\mu}\,\nInf'$, $c_{\mu} = -\mu w + \frac{\Lambda}{3\mu}v$ the rung component of $X_{\mu}(I)$, and $B_{s}$ the boost $v \mapsto sv$, $w \mapsto w/s$ fixing the ground.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Transport cannot see the unit.)} $B_{s}$ is an isometry, $(B_{s}v, B_{s}w)$ again satisfies $v^{2} = w^{2} = 0$, $vw + wv = 1$, and $X_{\mu} = B_{1/\mu}\circ X_{1}$; every clause of Fact \claimref{transport.totality} holds for $X_{\mu}$ with $\iota_{\mu}[N] = [e_{+}^{(\mu)}Ne_{+}^{(\mu)}]$, $e_{+}^{(\mu)} = B_{1/\mu}e_{+}$. Every function of rung-plane vectors with both null components nonzero that is invariant under all $B_{s}$ is a function of the norm and the sign of the $w$-coefficient, and $Q(c_{\mu}) = -\Lambda/3$ for every $\mu$.
\item \emph{(The unit is transverse to the norm.)} $\bigl(\tfrac{d}{d\mu}c_{\mu}\bigr)\cdot c_{\mu} = 0$ and $\bigl(\tfrac{\partial}{\partial\Lambda}c_{\mu}\bigr)\cdot c_{\mu} = -\tfrac16$ (so $\tfrac{\partial}{\partial\Lambda}(Q(c_{\mu})) = -\tfrac13$): a change of the rung unit moves $c_{\mu}$ along a level set of the norm, Klein-orthogonally to $c_{\mu}$, and a change of $\Lambda$ moves it off.
\item \emph{(The two doublet lifts are mirror frames.)} $c_{1}$ and $c_{\Lambda/3}$ are the rung components of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i) and (ii), so for $\Lambda > 0$ the reciprocal's rung component is the lift's in the boosted frame, $c_{\Lambda/3} = B_{3/\Lambda}c_{1}$. With $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, the involution $\mu \mapsto H^{2}/\mu$ of the units exchanges $c_{1}$ and $c_{\Lambda/3}$, and its fixed point is the balanced frame $\mu = H$.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (the Hubble unit).} Here $H$ is the de Sitter rate of $\Lambda$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, that is $H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, the $H$ of $N = M_{P}/H$; some texts quote $v/H$ with $H_{0}$, which differs from it by the factor $\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, of order one ($v/H \approx 2.1 \times 10^{44}$ against $v/H_{0} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{44}$; $\ln(v/H)$ changes by about $0.2$). No number here depends on the choice.
synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm.technical: The lift that carries the frozen point into the next rung needs a unit $\mu$, and changing $\mu$ is a boost of the rung plane. The boost preserves the quadratic form, the anticommutation relations of the rung's mode pair, and the totality theorem clause by clause, so nothing transport defines can fix the unit; the rung component keeps the norm $-\Lambda/3$, the only invariant of its boost orbit. A change of unit moves the rung component along the level set of its norm, orthogonally to it in the tractor metric, while a change of $\Lambda$ moves it off that level set. So a dynamical rung unit, if there were one, would move along a direction orthogonal to the norm mode of the frozen point, which carries no local degree of freedom. The two doublet directions the transported frozen point produces, from the lift and from the reciprocal's lift, are the same component in two frames related by the boost $H^{-2}$, exchanged by the involution $\mu \mapsto H^{2}/\mu$, whose fixed point is the balanced frame $\mu = H$ singled out by the conjugation norm (filed alongside, synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost).
synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm.lay: In the series the Higgs field's size is measured in a unit that the step carrying the cosmological point into the next layer has to choose, and changing that unit is a hyperbolic rotation of the new layer. That rotation leaves every geometric statement of the step unchanged, so the geometry cannot choose the unit. It is also a different direction from a change of the cosmological constant, so if the unit were promoted to a field, its changes would point in a different direction from those of the cosmological constant. The two Higgs directions that the step produces turn out to be the same thing seen in two frames, mirror images of each other about the frame matched to the cosmological scale.

proofs.main:
Conventions of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}: $v = 	frac12(e_{-} + e_{+})$, $w = 	frac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$, so $Q(v) = Q(w) = 0$, $v\cdot w = 	frac12$, $vw + wv = 1$, $
O' = -w$, $
Inf' = 2v$, $
O'\cdot
Inf' = -1$. A rung-plane vector is $y = -\alpha w +  eta v$ with $Q(y) = -\alpha eta$. The conjugation $*$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} has $v^{*} = w$; on the real rung plane it fixes $e_{+} = v + w$ and negates $e_{-} = v - w$, so $y^{*} = -\alpha v +  eta w$ and $\|y\|_{*} = y^{*}\cdot y = 	frac12(\alpha^{2} +  eta^{2})$.

(1) $B_{s}$ multiplies $v$ by $s$ and $w$ by $1/s$ and fixes the ground, so it preserves $Q(v) = Q(w) = 0$, $v\cdot w = 	frac12$ and the orthogonality of the rung plane to the ground: it is an isometry, and the Clifford relations of the pair, which depend only on these products, hold for $(B_{s}v, B_{s}w)$. For a ground vector $x$, $B_{1/\mu}X_{1}(x) = B_{1/\mu}(-w + x + Q(x)v) = -\mu w + x + (Q(x)/\mu)v = X_{\mu}(x)$. An isometry extends to an automorphism of the Clifford algebra and of its quadric, so each clause of Fact \claimref{transport.totality}, proved for the completion with its adjoined orthonormal pair, holds verbatim for the completion with the adjoined orthonormal pair $(B_{1/\mu}e_{+}, B_{1/\mu}e_{-})$, whose lift is $X_{\mu}$ and whose involution is $\iota_{\mu}[N] = [e_{+}^{(\mu)}Ne_{+}^{(\mu)}] = B_{1/\mu}\,\iota[B_{\mu}N]$. The boosts act on coefficients by $(\alpha,  eta) \mapsto (\alpha/s, s eta)$; on the set $\alpha eta 
e 0$ the orbits are exactly the level sets of $\alpha eta$ with fixed signs of $\alpha$ and $ eta$, since $(\alpha',  eta')$ with $\alpha' eta' = \alpha eta$ and the same signs is reached with $s = \alpha/\alpha' > 0$. So an invariant function is a function of the norm $-\alpha eta$ and the sign of $\alpha$, the $w$-coefficient (the sign of $ eta$ is then fixed by the norm). This is the rung-plane version of the first-rung statement Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii). With $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $c_{\mu} = \mu
O' + 	frac{\Lambda}{6\mu}
Inf' = -\mu w + 	frac{\Lambda}{3\mu}v$ and $Q(c_{\mu}) = -\Lambda/3$.

(2) $	frac{d}{d\mu}c_{\mu} = -w - 	frac{\Lambda}{3\mu^{2}}v$, and the bracketed product $ igl(	frac{d}{d\mu}c_{\mu} igr)\cdot c_{\mu}$ is $(-w - 	frac{\Lambda}{3\mu^{2}}v)\cdot(-\mu w + 	frac{\Lambda}{3\mu}v) = -	frac{\Lambda}{3\mu}\cdot	frac12 + 	frac{\Lambda}{3\mu}\cdot	frac12 = 0$. And $	frac{\partial}{\partial\Lambda}c_{\mu} = 	frac{1}{3\mu}v$, with $ igl(	frac{\partial}{\partial\Lambda}c_{\mu} igr)\cdot c_{\mu} = 	frac{1}{3\mu}v\cdot(-\mu w) = -	frac16$, so that $	frac{\partial}{\partial\Lambda}(Q(c_{\mu})) = -	frac13$, as $Q(c_{\mu}) = -\Lambda/3$ requires. The first vector is tangent to the level set $\{y : Q(y) = -\Lambda/3\}$ at $c_{\mu}$, since the derivative of $Q(y)$ along it is $2\,	frac{d}{d\mu}c_{\mu}\cdot c_{\mu} = 0$; the second is not.

(3) At $\mu = 1$, $c_{1} = -w + 	frac{\Lambda}{3}v$ is Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i); at $\mu = \Lambda/3$, $c_{\Lambda/3} = -	frac{\Lambda}{3}w + v = 	frac{\Lambda}{3}
O' + 	frac12
Inf'$, the rung component of (ii). By (1), $c_{\mu} = B_{1/\mu}c_{1}$, so $c_{\Lambda/3} = B_{3/\Lambda}c_{1}$. For $\Lambda > 0$ put $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$; the map $\mu \mapsto H^{2}/\mu$ is an involution of $(0, \infty)$ sending $1$ to $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, so it exchanges $c_{1}$ and $c_{\Lambda/3}$, and its only fixed point is $\mu = H$. (The conjugation norm $\|c_{\mu}\|_{*} = 	frac12(\mu^{2} + H^{4}/\mu^{2})$, its invariance under this involution and its minimum $H^{2} = |Q(c_{H})|$ at $\mu = H$ are proved in the result filed alongside, synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost(4); the script recomputes them as a control.)

The script works in the Clifford algebra of $\R^{2,2}\oplus\R^{1,1}$ built with GA.py (a first-rung plane holding $I = 
Inf^{(1)} - 	frac{\Lambda}{6}
O^{(1)}$, the second rung, two further ground directions): it checks that $B_{s}$ preserves all products of generators and the pair relations, that $*$ commutes with $B_{s}$ only at $s = 1$, that $X_{\mu}(x) = B_{1/\mu}X_{1}(x)$ is null and that $e_{+}^{(\mu)}X_{\mu}(x)e_{+}^{(\mu)}$ is proportional to $X_{\mu}(x/Q(x))$ for three ground vectors and four units, the norm of $c_{\mu}$ for four values of $\Lambda$ (one negative), the conjugation norm as a control, the symmetry $\mu \mapsto H^{2}/\mu$, the identification of $c_{1}$ and $c_{\Lambda/3}$ with Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i), (ii), the orthogonality (2) and the value $-	frac16$.

synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-nee.formal:
In the setting of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}: the complexified rung summand with $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$, $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, $\mathsf{N} = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$, $m = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})$, the slot mixing $U(2)$, the conjugation $c \mapsto c^{*}$, the null-lift locus $L = \{Q(c) = -H^{2}\}$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, the lift family $c_{\lambda}$ with $\eta = \log(\lambda/H)$, $t = 2\eta$, and its physical half $\lambda \ge H$ (on which, read through $c^{*}$, every tree Dirac entry is $\lambda$, \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)), the gauge masses $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N}$, $M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac12(g^{2} + g'^{2})\mathsf{N}$, and $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}$. Call a potential \emph{scale-free} if it is a real $U(2)$-invariant polynomial on $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ homogeneous of degree four. Masses are Hessians on the locus divided by the kinetic coefficient of the stored Hermitian term.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Five couplings.)} The real scale-free potentials are $V = \sum_{i}k_{i}I_{i}$ over $I_{1..10} = |\alpha|^{4}, |\beta|^{4}, |\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2}, |\alpha|^{2}\operatorname{Re}Q, |\alpha|^{2}\operatorname{Im}Q, |\beta|^{2}\operatorname{Re}Q, |\beta|^{2}\operatorname{Im}Q, \operatorname{Re}Q^{2}, \operatorname{Im}Q^{2}, |Q|^{2}$. On $L$,
\[
V = a\mathsf{N}^{2} + bm^{2} + e\mathsf{N}m + H^{2}(d\mathsf{N} + fm) + c_{0}H^{4},
\]
with $a = k_{1} + k_{2} + k_{3}$, $b = k_{1} + k_{2} - k_{3}$, $e = 2(k_{1} - k_{2})$, $d = -(k_{4} + k_{6})$, $f = -(k_{4} - k_{6})$, $c_{0} = k_{8} + k_{10}$; the conjugation changes $(e, f)$ to $(-e, -f)$. The D-term action is scale-free exactly when its level $\xi$ vanishes, and then $(a, b, e, d, f, c_{0}) = (\tfrac18 g^{2}, \tfrac18 g'^{2}, 0, 0, 0, -\tfrac18 g^{2})$.
\item \emph{(The frame, and the flat condition.)} Along the family $V(c_{\lambda}) = H^{4}\bigl[a + c_{0} + (a + b)\sinh^{2}t - \tfrac{e}{2}\sinh 2t + d\cosh t - f\sinh t\bigr]$, and the joint rescaling $(c, H) \mapsto (sc, sH)$ maps $c_{\lambda}$ to $c_{s\lambda}$ and $V$ to $s^{4}V$: a scale-free potential sees the rung unit only through the frame $t$. Let $K_{\pm} = a + b \mp e$. If $K_{+} < 0$, $V$ decreases without bound along the physical half. At every critical point of $V$ along the family with $t \ge 0$,
\[
K_{+} \le 2(|d| + |f|)e^{-t} + |K_{-}|e^{-2t}, \qquad \text{and for } K_{+} > 0,\quad e^{t} \le \frac{2(|d| + |f|) + \sqrt{K_{+}|K_{-}|}}{K_{+}};
\]
since $\mathsf{N}^{*}/H^{2} = \cosh t \le e^{t}$, a charge-preserving tree-level critical point at $\mathsf{N}^{*} = \tfrac12 v^{2}$, $\mathsf{N}^{*}/H^{2} \approx 2 \times 10^{88}$ (with $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$; about $1.4 \times 10^{88}$ if $H$ is read as $H_{0}$, the two differing by a factor of order one), needs $K_{+} \le 2(|d| + |f|)H^{2}/\mathsf{N}^{*} + |K_{-}|H^{4}/\mathsf{N}^{*2}$. The half $t \le 0$ is the same with $K_{+}$ and $K_{-}$ exchanged and $f \mapsto -f$.
\item \emph{(The Gildener-Weinberg flat ray, on the cone $Q = 0$.)} On the cone $L_{0} = \{Q = 0\}$, the limit $H \to 0$, with orbit cone $|m| \le \mathsf{N}$, a scale-free potential is $V_{4} = a\mathsf{N}^{2} + bm^{2} + e\mathsf{N}m$. It is nonnegative on the cone and vanishes on the physical ray $m = -\mathsf{N}$ if and only if $K_{+} = 0$, $e \ge 0$ and $2a \ge e$; the mirror ray $m = \mathsf{N}$ then carries $V_{4} = 2e\mathsf{N}^{2}$, flat as well exactly when $e = 0$ (so for every $c^{*}$-even potential). On the flat physical ray of $L_{0}$ the neutral mode is massless, the charged pair has $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N} = (2a - e)v^{2}$, and the two do not mix.
\item \emph{(The norm quartic fails.)} For the level-zero D-term plus $\kappa \mathsf{N}^{2}$ the physical ray is flat only at $\kappa = -\tfrac18(g^{2} + g'^{2})$, and there $m_{\pm}^{2} = -\tfrac12 g'^{2}\mathsf{N} = M_{W}^{2} - M_{Z}^{2} < 0$ and $V < 0$ inside the cone: the potential is unbounded below and the family $W = \kappa \mathsf{N}^{2}$ is not a flat-ray endpoint. With a moment-map quartic $\kappa'm^{2}$ and $e\mathsf{N}m$ added the flat ray is admissible exactly when $e \ge 0$, $2a \ge e$, which requires $\kappa' \le \tfrac12 e - \tfrac18 g'^{2}$.
\item \emph{(The rung unit is the dilatation; a restatement.)} With the lift's null pair $n_{0}' = -w$, $n_{\infty}' = 2v$ and $X_{\mu}(x) = \mu n_{0}' + x + \tfrac{Q(x)}{2\mu}n_{\infty}'$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}), $X_{\mu}(x) = \mu X_{1}(x/\mu)$, which restates the stored $X_{\mu} = B_{1/\mu}\circ X_{1}$ through the standard fact that the null-plane boost is the dilator of the conformal model: a change of the rung unit is the conformal dilatation of the ground point by $1/\mu$, and the flat ray of (3) is the orbit of the rung unit.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (the transmutation branch excluded, 2 November 2026).} The flat physical branch of (iii) is the route by which a scale-free rung potential would reach the weak scale through one loop. Under the decided coupling reading of the rung field (the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion with complex symmetric family matrices), that transmutation branch is recorded as excluded, by the three strikes collected in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev}: the diphoton rate, neutral B-meson mixing and strong coupling of the quartics at a few TeV. The branch with a level is the working branch. The tree-level statements here are unchanged.
synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-nee.technical: A potential for the rung field with no dimensionful constant is a quartic form invariant under the slot mixing. On the locus where the frozen point's lift is null it reduces to a quadratic form in the Hermitian norm and the hypercharge moment map, plus terms of order $H^{2}$ and $H^{4}$ that the locus induces: five couplings. Rescaling the field together with the cosmological scale maps the lift family to itself, so such a potential sees the rung unit only through the frame. At tree level the frame it selects is a ratio of couplings: a tree-level vacuum at the weak scale, about $10^{88}$ in units of $H^{2}$, needs the coefficient of the physical branch to vanish to that precision. Exact vanishing is the Gildener-Weinberg condition, under which the physical branch is a flat direction and quantum corrections choose the scale by dimensional transmutation; the flat direction is the orbit of the rung unit, which in the conformal model is the standard dilatation of the ground point (a restatement of the stored boost). On the cone $Q = 0$, the limit of small $H$, the flat direction is bounded below exactly when two inequalities hold; then the neutral mode is massless at tree level and the charged pair has mass squared $(2a - e)v^{2}$. A potential even under the rung conjugation leaves the mirror branch flat too; under the per-sector reading (not su(2)_R covariant) the fermion entries there are tiny, under its su(2)_R-covariant completion they are not. The level-zero D-term with a norm quartic, the form behind the $117$ GeV point, cannot be made flat without a tachyonic charged pair, $M_{W}^{2} - M_{Z}^{2}$: a quartic in the moment map is needed.
synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-nee.lay: Could the weak scale come from nothing, as the strong-interaction scale does, by the slow running of a coupling? The first condition is a potential for the series' Higgs candidate with no built-in mass scale. This result lists all such potentials and shows that, without quantum effects, they put the weak scale at most a modest factor from the cosmological scale, unless one combination of couplings vanishes almost exactly. When it vanishes exactly the potential is flat along the very direction that changes the weak scale, which in the series' geometry is a rescaling; quantum corrections then pick the scale. The flat direction is stable only for some couplings, and the simplest choice, the one behind an earlier prediction of a charged scalar near 117 GeV, is not among them: it makes the charged scalar's mass squared negative.

proofs.main:
\emph{(1).} By \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(1) the $U(2)$-invariant polynomials are generated by $|\alpha|^{2}$, $|\beta|^{2}$, $Q$ and $\bar{Q}$, each of degree two in $c$, so the invariant polynomials homogeneous of degree four are spanned by the products of two generators; their real parts and imaginary parts give the ten $I_{i}$ (the products $|\alpha|^{2}\bar{Q}$, $\bar{Q}^{2}$ and so on add nothing over $\R$). On $L$, $Q = -H^{2}$, $|\alpha|^{2} = \mathsf{N} + m$ and $|\beta|^{2} = \mathsf{N} - m$, so $I_{1} = (\mathsf{N} + m)^{2}$, $I_{2} = (\mathsf{N} - m)^{2}$, $I_{3} = \mathsf{N}^{2} - m^{2}$, $I_{4} = -H^{2}(\mathsf{N} + m)$, $I_{6} = -H^{2}(\mathsf{N} - m)$, $I_{8} = I_{10} = H^{4}$ and $I_{5} = I_{7} = I_{9} = 0$; collecting terms gives the stated map $k \mapsto (a, b, e, d, f, c_{0})$. The conjugation $c^{*} = (\bar{\beta}, \bar{\alpha})$ exchanges $|\alpha|^{2}$ and $|\beta|^{2}$ and conjugates $Q$, so it exchanges $k_{1} \leftrightarrow k_{2}$, $k_{4} \leftrightarrow k_{6}$ on $L$, which reverses $e$ and $f$ and fixes the rest. The D-term $V_{D} = \tfrac12\bigl(g^{2}\sum_{j}\mu_{j}^{2} + g'^{2}(\mu_{Y} - \zeta)^{2}\bigr)$ has the terms $-g'^{2}\zeta\mu_{Y}$ of degree two and $\tfrac12 g'^{2}\zeta^{2}$ of degree zero, so it is homogeneous of degree four exactly when $\zeta = 0$; then on $L$ it is $\tfrac18 g^{2}(\mathsf{N}^{2} - H^{4}) + \tfrac18 g'^{2}m^{2}$ (stored clause (2)). The check verifies the invariance under five rational $U(2)$ elements, the restriction at four points of $L$ for three coefficient vectors, the conjugation rule, that the six monomials $\mathsf{N}^{2}, m^{2}, \mathsf{N}m, H^{2}\mathsf{N}, H^{2}m, H^{4}$ are independent on $L$ (rank six on six points), and the homogeneity test of $V_{D}$ for $\zeta = 0$ and $\zeta = \tfrac13$.

\emph{(2).} On the family $\mathsf{N} = H^{2}\cosh t$ and $m = -H^{2}\sinh t$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(4)), and substituting into (1) with $\cosh^{2}t = 1 + \sinh^{2}t$ gives the family formula. The rescaling $c_{\lambda}(H) \mapsto s\,c_{\lambda}(H) = c_{s\lambda}(sH)$ is immediate from $c_{\lambda} = -\lambda w + (H^{2}/\lambda)v$, and $V(sc) = s^{4}V(c)$ by homogeneity, so $V(c_{\lambda})/H^{4}$ is a function of $\lambda/H$, that is, of $t$. Write $X = e^{t}$, $u = \cosh t$, $s = \sinh t$, $F(t) = (a + b)s^{2} - esu + du - fs$. Then $F'(t) = (a + b)\sinh 2t - e\cosh 2t + ds - fu$ and $(a + b)\sinh 2t - e\cosh 2t = \tfrac12(K_{+}X^{2} - K_{-}X^{-2})$. If $K_{+} < 0$ the leading term $\tfrac14 K_{+}X^{2}$ of $F$ wins over the terms of order $X$ and $X^{-2}$, so $F \to -\infty$. At a critical point with $t \ge 0$, $K_{+}X^{2} = K_{-}X^{-2} + 2(fu - ds) \le |K_{-}| + 2(|d| + |f|)X$, since $u, s \le X$ and $X^{-2} \le 1$; dividing by $X^{2}$ gives the first inequality. For $K_{+} > 0$ put $D = |d| + |f|$, $R = \sqrt{K_{+}|K_{-}|}$ and $X_{0} = (2D + R)/K_{+}$: then $K_{+}X_{0}^{2} - 2DX_{0} - |K_{-}| = X_{0}R - R^{2}/K_{+} = 2DR/K_{+} \ge 0$, and $K_{+}X^{2} - 2DX$ is increasing for $X > X_{0}$, so $2F'(t) \ge K_{+}X^{2} - 2DX - |K_{-}| > 0$ there: no critical point lies above $X_{0}$. With $\cosh t \le e^{t}$, $e^{-t} \le H^{2}/\mathsf{N}^{*}$, which gives the stated condition at the weak scale; the observed weak scale gives $\mathsf{N}^{*}/H^{2} = \tfrac12(v/H)^{2} \approx 2 \times 10^{88}$ with $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$ ($v/H \approx 2.1 \times 10^{44}$), or about $1.4 \times 10^{88}$ if $H$ is read as $H_{0}$ ($v/H_{0} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{44}$, \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}, not used in the proof); the two readings differ by $\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, a factor of order one. The bound is attained up to a factor two: with $d < 0 < f$ and $f > |d|$ criticality gives $K_{+} = D/X + (f - |d|)X^{-3} + K_{-}X^{-4} > D/X$, so no bound of the form $K_{+} \le D/X$ holds. The half $t \le 0$ follows by applying the conjugation, which maps $t \mapsto -t$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)) and $(e, f) \mapsto (-e, -f)$. The check verifies the family formula at four frames for three coefficient vectors, the rescaling, the identity for the leading part of $F'$, $F'$ against a difference quotient of $F$, positivity of $F'$ on forty points above a rational upper bound of $X_{0}$ for three samples, the inequality at three exactly constructed critical points (with $f$ solved for criticality, one with $K_{+} = 10^{-3}$ and $X = 10^{3}$), two near-saturating critical points (with $K_{+}$ solved for criticality) at which $K_{+}$ exceeds $D/X$, and the runaway for two samples with $K_{+} < 0$.

\emph{(3).} As $H \to 0$ the terms $H^{2}(d\mathsf{N} + fm)$ and $c_{0}H^{4}$ drop, the locus becomes the cone $Q = 0$ and the orbit space $\mathsf{N}^{2} - m^{2} \ge H^{4}$ becomes $|m| \le \mathsf{N}$. Write $m = -\sigma \mathsf{N}$, $\sigma \in [-1, 1]$; then $V_{4} = \mathsf{N}^{2}\phi(\sigma)$ with $\phi(\sigma) = a + b\sigma^{2} - e\sigma$, the physical ray is $\sigma = 1$ and the mirror ray $\sigma = -1$. Vanishing on the physical ray is $\phi(1) = K_{+} = 0$. Given that, $\phi(-1) = 2e$, so $e \ge 0$ is necessary; $\phi'(1) = 2b - e = e - 2a$, and if it were positive $\phi$ would be negative just below $\sigma = 1$, so $2a \ge e$ is necessary. Conversely, if $b = e - a \le 0$ then $\phi$ is concave and its minimum on $[-1, 1]$ is at an endpoint, $\min(0, 2e) = 0$; if $b > 0$ the vertex $\sigma_{0} = e/(2b)$ satisfies $\sigma_{0} \ge 1$ exactly when $e \ge 2(e - a)$, that is $2a \ge e$, so $\phi$ decreases on $[-1, 1]$ to $\phi(1) = 0$. The masses: at $c = (0, (-\lambda, 0)) \in L_{0}$ the directions $d_{n} = (0, (-1, 0))$ (the rung unit) and $d_{c} = ((0, z), 0)$, $z \in \C$, are tangent to $L_{0}$ and orthogonal for $G$ to the gauge orbit, and the complement of the gauge orbit in the tangent space has dimension three (stored construction, \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(3), here on $L_{0}$). Along $d_{n}$, $V_{4} = K_{+}\mathsf{N}^{2} = 0$, so the neutral mode is massless. Along $d_{c}$ exactly, $\mathsf{N}$ and $m$ both increase by $\tfrac12\varepsilon^{2}|z|^{2}$, so $V_{4}$ increases by $\tfrac12\varepsilon^{2}|z|^{2}(\partial_{\mathsf{N}} + \partial_{m})V_{4} = \tfrac12\varepsilon^{2}|z|^{2}\cdot 2(a - b)\mathsf{N}$ at $m = -\mathsf{N}$; with the kinetic coefficient $2\mathsf{N}(d_{c}) = |z|^{2}$ this is $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2(a - b)\mathsf{N} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N}$, and $2\mathsf{N} = v^{2}$ by $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N} = \tfrac14 g^{2}v^{2}$. The check computes these Hessians on $L_{0}$ by exact interpolation along curves kept on $Q = 0$ to second order, for three admissible coupling sets and two points of the ray, and verifies that the mixed second derivative of neutral and charged directions vanishes.

\emph{(4).} By (1), the level-zero D-term plus $\kappa \mathsf{N}^{2}$ has $a = \tfrac18 g^{2} + \kappa$, $b = \tfrac18 g'^{2}$, $e = 0$, so $K_{+} = 0$ forces $\kappa = -\tfrac18(g^{2} + g'^{2})$ and then $2a - e = -\tfrac14 g'^{2} < 0$; by (3), $m_{\pm}^{2} = -\tfrac12 g'^{2}\mathsf{N} = M_{W}^{2} - M_{Z}^{2}$, which is the stored sum rule (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-charged-scalar-sum-rule}(ii)) at $m_{h} = 0$, and $\phi(0) = a < 0$ is a negative value inside the cone. With $\kappa'm^{2} + e\mathsf{N}m$ added, $b = \tfrac18 g'^{2} + \kappa'$; admissibility requires $b = e - a \le e - \tfrac12 e$. The check computes $V_{D}$ from the moment maps (not from the reduced form), on $L_{0}$, for $g = \tfrac23$, $g' = \tfrac12$: flatness along the ray, the charged mass squared $M_{W}^{2} - M_{Z}^{2}$ by exact Hessian, a negative value at an interior point of the cone, and with $\kappa' = -\tfrac18 g'^{2} - \tfrac15$ the positive charged mass $4a\mathsf{N}$.

\emph{(5).} This clause restates the stored $X_{\mu} = B_{1/\mu}\circ X_{1}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}(1)) through the standard fact, cited from memory (D. Hestenes; C. Doran and A. Lasenby, Geometric Algebra for Physicists), that a boost of the null pair is the dilator of the conformal model. $\mu X_{1}(x/\mu) = \mu n_{0}' + x + \tfrac{Q(x)}{2\mu}n_{\infty}' = X_{\mu}(x)$ by $Q(x/\mu) = Q(x)/\mu^{2}$; the map $x \mapsto X_{1}(x)$ is the conformal embedding of the ground with null pair $(n_{0}', n_{\infty}')$, and $X_{1}(x/\mu)$ is the embedding of the dilated point, projectively equal to $X_{\mu}(x)$. The rung component of $X_{\mu}(I)$ is $c_{\mu}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-transverse-to-norm}(1)), the family of (2). The same stored boost is read as the flow of $2T_{3R}$ at real rapidity on the ten in \claimref{synthesis.majorana-scale-not-carried-by-rung-frame-boost}; on the rung plane the two readings agree. The check builds the conformal model of a ground plane in the exact Clifford engine and verifies nullity of $X_{\mu}(x)$, the identity at six pairs $(x, \mu)$, and the rung component with $Q(c_{\mu}) = -H^{2}$.

\emph{Remarks.} (a) On $L$ itself the flat condition $K_{+} = 0$ with $d = f = 0$ leaves $F(t) = -\tfrac{e}{2}(1 - e^{-2t})$, a slope of relative order $H^{4}/\mathsf{N}^{2}$ along the boost hyperbola: the constraint's scale $H^{2}$ is negligible against any quantum correction at the weak scale, but it is a dimensionful input, and the flat direction on $L$ is the hyperbola $\mathsf{N}^{2} - m^{2} = H^{4}$, which (3) treats in its limit as a ray. (b) This result does not compute the running of $K_{+}$: dimensional transmutation trades the level $\xi$ for the scale at which $K_{+}$ vanishes, which is a further input unless a boundary value of the couplings at a fixed scale is supplied.

synthesis.second-doublet-of-one-family-c.formal:
Let $M_{u}$, $M_{d}$ be the up-type and down-type Dirac mass matrices at $M_{I}$ in the form of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}, $H_{q} = M_{q}M_{q}^{\dagger}$, and $V$ the CKM matrix, the overlap of the eigenbases of $H_{u}$ and $H_{d}$ (masses nondegenerate in each sector).
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Commuting squares.)} If $[H_{u}, H_{d}] = 0$, then $V$ is a permutation matrix up to phases and the Jarlskog invariant vanishes (a case of the common-eigenvector lemma of the result filed alongside, synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns).
\item \emph{(One coupling.)} Suppose every coupling entering $M_{u}$ and $M_{d}$ is a multiple of one family matrix $Y$. This covers one rung coupling read through $c^{*}$ as in Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern} with any number of doublet vevs, and a complex bidoublet with a single coupling (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.bidoublet-complex}). Then $M_{u} = rM_{d}$ for one complex number $r$, so $m_{u_{i}}/m_{d_{i}} = |r|$ for every family and $V = 1$.
\item \emph{($S_{3}$-invariant couplings.)} If every coupling is invariant under the family $S_{3}$ of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation}, then each coupling is $\alpha 1 + \beta\J$ and no $120$ is allowed (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-form}(i)), so every mass matrix and its square has eigenvalues $\alpha, \alpha, \alpha + 3\beta$: two degenerate families in every sector, which the record excludes, and the mixing is undetermined. (The general residual-$S_{2}$ case, of which this is a special case, is the result filed alongside, synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns.)
\item \emph{(Against the record.)} The record has three different up/down ratios, $|V_{us}| \approx 0.225$ and $J \ne 0$ (cited from memory). So under the $c^{*}$ reading the up/down split needs a second coupling that is a family matrix independent of the first, and for three families $\det[H_{u}, H_{d}] \ne 0$; a second vev of the rung coupling does not supply it, and an $S_{3}$-symmetric completion is already excluded by its degenerate spectrum.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.second-doublet-of-one-family-c.technical: Quark mixing measures how far apart the mass eigenbases of the up and down sectors are. A single rung coupling read through any number of doublet vevs makes $M_{u}$ a multiple of $M_{d}$. This includes the complex bidoublet with one Yukawa matrix, where the two doublets differ only by a ratio of vevs. The consequence is one up/down ratio for all three families and no mixing at all. Couplings invariant under the full family permutation group leave two families degenerate in every sector, which the record excludes before mixing is considered. The record has three very different up/down ratios and a nonzero Cabibbo angle. So the second coupling the up/down split needs must be a genuinely different family matrix, not a second vev of the same coupling. The residual-$S_{2}$ result filed alongside, synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns, shows that such a matrix must also break the residual $S_{2}$ to produce the Cabibbo angle.
synthesis.second-doublet-of-one-family-c.lay: Quarks of the up kind and the down kind mix with each other, by angles that are measured. Mixing happens only when the two kinds' mass patterns do not line up. One natural way to make up-type quarks heavier than down-type ones is to use the same coupling twice with two different strengths. That scales every up-type mass by one common factor and lines the patterns up exactly. The result would be the same mass ratio in every family and no mixing, and neither fits the measurements. So the series needs a genuinely different second coupling.

proofs.main:
\emph{(1).} This is the common-eigenvector lemma of the result filed alongside, synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns (its clause (ii)); recalled here. Let $U_{u}$, $U_{d}$ be unitaries with $U_{q}^{\dagger}H_{q}U_{q}$ diagonal, the columns ordered by mass; $V = U_{u}^{\dagger}U_{d}$. With nondegenerate masses each column of $U_{q}$ is fixed up to a phase. If $x$ is a common unit eigenvector, it is (up to phase) column $i$ of $U_{u}$ and column $k$ of $U_{d}$ for some $i$, $k$, so $V_{ik} = e_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}U_{u}^{\dagger}U_{d}e_{k}$ has modulus one, and unitarity forces the rest of row $i$ and column $k$ to vanish. Also $[H_{u}, H_{d}]x = H_{u}\lambda_{d}x - H_{d}\lambda_{u}x = 0$, so $\det[H_{u}, H_{d}] = 0$; by Jarlskog's identity $\det[H_{u}, H_{d}] = 2I_{4}J\prod_{i<j}(m_{u_{j}}^{2} - m_{u_{i}}^{2})\prod_{i<j}(m_{d_{j}}^{2} - m_{d_{i}}^{2})$ (cited from memory) the invariant $J$ is zero. If $H_{u}$ and $H_{d}$ commute they are simultaneously diagonal and every column of $U_{d}$ is a column of $U_{u}$ up to phase.

\emph{(2).} In Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw} each coupling enters $M_{u}$ and $M_{d}$ multiplied by complex vevs. If every coupling is $\mu_{a}Y$ for one matrix $Y$, then $M_{u} = (\sum_{a}\mu_{a}v^{a}_{u})Y$ and $M_{d} = (\sum_{a}\mu_{a}v^{a}_{d})Y$, so $M_{u} = rM_{d}$ with $r$ the ratio (when $M_{d} \ne 0$). Then $H_{u} = |r|^{2}H_{d}$: the eigenbases coincide, $V = 1$, and the singular values satisfy $m_{u_{i}} = |r|m_{d_{i}}$. This covers the one rung coupling of Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern} under the $c^{*}$ reading, where $r = 1$, and the complex bidoublet of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.bidoublet-complex} when its two doublets carry the same family matrix, where $|r|$ is the ratio of the two vevs (a $\tan\beta$). The check verifies $H_{u} = |v_{u}/v_{d}|^{2}H_{d}$ and $[H_{u}, H_{d}] = 0$ for a generic complex $Y$ and three pairs of vevs, and, as a control, that two independent family matrices give $\det[H_{u}, H_{d}] \ne 0$.

\emph{(3).} By Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation} and Proposition \claimref{synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-form}(i), the $S_{3}$-invariant symmetric family matrices are spanned by $1$ and $\J$ (equivalently $\Pi$ and $\J$), and no nonzero antisymmetric matrix is $S_{3}$-invariant, so no $120$ enters. Since $\J^{2} = 3\J$, this span is closed under products and adjoints (for complex coefficients), so $M_{u}$, $M_{d}$, $H_{u}$, $H_{d}$ all lie in it. $\J$ has eigenvalue $3$ on $u' = (1,1,1)$ and $0$ on its orthogonal plane, so $\alpha 1 + \beta\J$ has eigenvalues $\alpha$ (twice) and $\alpha + 3\beta$, and $H_{q}$ has $|\alpha_{q}|^{2}$ twice: two families of each sector are degenerate. Clause (1) then does not apply (it assumes nondegenerate masses) and the mixing is undetermined; the record's nondegenerate masses exclude this case outright. The check verifies the spectra for a complex instance, $H_{u}$ with $5, 5, 290$ and $H_{d}$ with $9, 9, 90$. The general residual-$S_{2}$ case, of which this is a special case, is the result filed alongside, synthesis.residual-s2-decouples-first-family-from-ckm-and-pmns.

\emph{(4).} Record values (cited from memory; running masses at $M_{Z}$ in MeV, from the table of Xing, Zhang and Zhou, Phys. Rev. D 77 (2008) 113016): $m_{u} \approx 1.27$, $m_{d} \approx 2.90$, $m_{c} \approx 619$, $m_{s} \approx 55$, $m_{t} \approx 1.717 \times 10^{5}$, $m_{b} \approx 2.89 \times 10^{3}$, so $m_{u}/m_{d} \approx 0.44$, $m_{c}/m_{s} \approx 11$, $m_{t}/m_{b} \approx 59$; $|V_{us}| \approx 0.225$ and $J \approx 3 \times 10^{-5}$ (Particle Data Group). Three different ratios contradict (2) at $M_{Z}$. To carry the conclusion to $M_{I}$: QCD running multiplies the up and down masses of each family by the same factor at one loop, and the electroweak and Yukawa corrections change the ratios by factors of order one, not by the factor of about $130$ between $m_{t}/m_{b}$ and $m_{u}/m_{d}$; and the one-loop running of the Yukawa matrices preserves $[H_{u}, H_{d}] = 0$ (the flow of $H_{u}$ and $H_{d}$ is generated by polynomials in them), so a vanishing mixing angle at $M_{I}$ stays zero at $M_{Z}$ (both cited from memory). So $V \ne 1$ at $M_{Z}$ rules out (2) and (3) as the source of the observed spectrum. Under the $c^{*}$ reading the second coupling must therefore be a family matrix not proportional to the first. For three families with $J \ne 0$ it must give $\det[H_{u}, H_{d}] \ne 0$. The stored record-level fits, whose complex couplings reproduce the CKM numbers, are of this kind.
