synthesis.slot-count-not-from-constituen.technical: Second quantising composites over the twistor attachment, with a label for each slot and the twistor as internal label, puts one copy of the twistor label on every constituent. Hypothesis (S) instead puts one pair system on the whole composite, beside the slot modes, so that a state with no slot occupied, or with both, still carries a full twistor or dual twistor. Central elements decide the matter: in any Fock-type space built from creation operators carrying a slot index and a twistor index, $-1$ in the slot group and $-1$ in the twistor group act by the same sign $(-1)^{n}$ on $n$-particle states. For an even number of slots an invariant of the slot group therefore has even particle number and is fixed by $-1$ in the twistor group, which acts as $-1$ on twistors and dual twistors. In the space of (S) the slot-invariant sectors, no slot or both slots occupied, are twistors and dual twistors, and they hold exactly the four singlet species $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $e^{c}$, $d^{c}$. So the count of (S) cannot come from constituents by any construction that respects the twistor group $SL(4)$, with any statistics; only the doublet sector can be matched. Under the gauge group $U(2) \times U(3)$ alone the obstruction disappears: the central element $-1 \in SL(4)$ is not a gauge transformation. The argument needs the even count: three bosonic constituents do produce one invariant dual twistor, their antisymmetrised product.
synthesis.slot-count-not-from-constituen.lay: The series' Hypothesis (S) says a composite particle has two places for its twistors plus one shared set of three internal modes. A natural way to derive such a space is to treat each twistor as a particle and build the many-particle space, each particle carrying its own internal label. This result shows that route cannot work for two twistors, whatever rule for identical particles one uses: a sign coming from the twistor symmetry, which both descriptions must agree on if the twistor symmetry is to be respected, comes out differently, and the states that disagree are exactly the four kinds of particle with no weak charge (the right-handed neutrino, up quark, electron and down quark). The shared internal modes must come from something attached to the composite as a whole.

proofs.main:
The one-particle space of the twistor attachment is built on $\CS$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}), and $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ with the action of $\mathrm{Spin}(6)$, complexified $SL(4)$, by Theorem \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}; $\Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ is the other half-spinor module, the dual $\CSm$. The element $-1 \in SL(4) = \mathrm{Spin}(6, \C)$ is the nontrivial element of the kernel of $\mathrm{Spin}(6) \to SO(6)$ and acts as $-1$ on both half-spinor modules, hence as $-1$ on $\CS$, on $\CSm$ and on all of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$.

(1) The $n$-particle vectors $a^{\dagger}(u_{1})\cdots a^{\dagger}(u_{n})\Omega$ span the image of the equivariant map $(\C^{K}\otimes U)^{\otimes n} \to F$ (equivariant because $\Omega$ is invariant and $a^{\dagger}$ is equivariant and linear), so $F$ is a sum of quotients of the tensor powers. On $(\C^{K}\otimes U)^{\otimes n}$ the central element $z_{K} = (-1_{K}, 1)$ acts by $(-1)^{n}$, and so does $z_{4} = (1, -1_{4})$, since $-1_{4}$ acts by $-1$ on $U$ in each of the three cases. Hence $z_{K}z_{4}$ acts trivially on every tensor power and on $F$. If $K$ is even, $-1_{K} \in SL(K)$, so $z_{K}$ fixes every $SL(K)$-invariant vector, and then $z_{4}$ fixes it too. But $z_{4}$ acts by $-1$ on every vector of an $SL(4)$-isotypic component of type $\CS$ or $\CSm$. So such a vector is zero.

(2) In $\mathcal{S}$ the slot $SL(2)$ acts on $\Lambda^{j}\C^{2}$, trivially for $j = 0$ and $j = 2$ (the determinant is $1$), and $SL(4)$ acts on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W = \CS \oplus \CSm$; so $\mathcal{S}_{0}$ and $\mathcal{S}_{2}$ are $SL(2)$-invariant, each $\CS \oplus \CSm$, and $\nu^{c}, u^{c}$ sit at $(j, k) = (0, 0), (0, 2)$ and $e^{c}, d^{c}$ at $(2, 0), (2, 2)$ in Theorem \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(1). An equivariant linear map carries $SL(2)$-invariant vectors of a given $SL(4)$-type to $SL(2)$-invariant vectors of the same type, which by (1) with $K = 2$ are zero in $F$; so it vanishes on $\mathcal{S}_{0} \oplus \mathcal{S}_{2}$. Dually, $z_{2}z_{4}$ acts trivially on $F$ and by $(-1)^{j}\cdot(-1) = -1$ on $\mathcal{S}_{0}\oplus\mathcal{S}_{2}$ and $+1$ on $\mathcal{S}_{1}$, so an equivariant map $F \to \mathcal{S}$ lands in the $+1$ eigenspace $\mathcal{S}_{1}$. An $SL(2)\times SL(4)$-equivariant subquotient of $F$ isomorphic to $\mathcal{S}$ would contain $z_{2}z_{4} = -1$ eigenvectors, impossible since $z_{2}z_{4} = 1$ on $F$ and on its subquotients.

(3) Computed by exact highest-weight counting. For $U = \CS$ realised as $\C^{4}$ with the standard $GL(4)$, an $SL(K)$-singlet copy of $\CS$ (of $\CSm$) is a $GL(K) \times GL(4)$ highest weight vector of weight $((m^{K}); (c+1, c, c, c))$ (respectively $(c+1, c+1, c+1, c)$) with $Km = 4c + 1$ (respectively $4c + 3$), and its multiplicity is the dimension of the joint kernel of the simple raising operators $E_{i,i+1} = \sum_{a}a^{\dagger}_{ia}a_{i+1,a}$ and $E_{a,a+1} = \sum_{i}a^{\dagger}_{ia}a_{i,a+1}$ on that weight space. For $K = 3$ the admissible weights in the exterior algebra (degree at most $12$) are $((1,1,1);(1,1,1,0))$ and $((3,3,3);(3,2,2,2))$, with six-dimensional weight spaces and multiplicity zero; in the symmetric algebra the first has multiplicity one (the vector $\sum_{\sigma}\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\,x_{1\sigma(1)}x_{2\sigma(2)}x_{3\sigma(3)}$ over bijections onto the first three twistor indices, the dual twistor of three constituents) and the second, with a $132$-dimensional weight space, multiplicity zero. For $K = 4$ no weight satisfies $4m = 4c + 1$ or $4c + 3$. For the exterior algebra and every $K \ge 2$ the same conclusion follows from skew Howe duality, $\Lambda(\C^{K}\otimes\C^{4}) = \bigoplus_{\lambda}S_{\lambda}\C^{K}\otimes S_{\lambda'}\C^{4}$ (imported, cited from memory): an $SL(K)$-singlet has $\lambda = (m^{K})$, and $S_{(K^{m})}\C^{4}$ is $K$ times the $m$-th fundamental weight, trivial for $m = 4$ and never $\CS$ or $\CSm$ for $K \ge 2$.

Remark. The obstruction needs $SL(4)$: no element of $U(2) \times U(3)$, acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$, acts as $-1$ on all of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, since $\Lambda^{0}W$ is fixed; for instance with $K = 2$ fermions and $\CS$ restricted to $U(3)$ as $\Lambda^{0}W \oplus \Lambda^{2}W$, $\Lambda^{2}(\C^{2}\otimes\CS) \supset \Lambda^{2}\C^{2}\otimes\mathrm{Sym}^{2}\CS \supset \det\otimes(\Lambda^{0}W\cdot\Lambda^{2}W) \cong \det\otimes\Lambda^{2}W$, the $d^{c}$-type component of $\mathcal{S}_{2}$ as a $U(2)\times U(3)$ module.

The script computes the highest-weight multiplicities of (3) and controls (one constituent: $\CS$ once in degree one; $K = 2$: the doublet copies of $\CS$ in degree one and of $\CSm$ at weight $((4,3);(2,2,2,1))$ found once each), checks that for $K = 2$ and $K = 4$ no target weight exists, and counts the sectors $\mathcal{S}_{0}$, $\mathcal{S}_{2}$ of $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2}\oplus\C^{3})$ by $W$-parity (four even and four odd states each).

clauses: (1) even K has no SL(K)-singlet CS or CS* component
(2) S_0 and S_2 carry CS + CS*
(3) K = 3 exterior and symmetric, K = 4

synthesis.slot-parity-decides-hypothesis.technical:
Hypothesis (S) asks that the two slots of a composite be fermionic modes on the same footing as its three pairs, with chirality the parity of the total mode number. Take any two slot operators inside the tower's canonical anticommutation algebra that are two-level, carry a linear $U(2)$ action, have definite tower parity $\pi$, commute or anticommute with the pair modes and share their vacuum. The $U(2)$ action alone forces the slots to anticommute with each other: two commuting two-level slots are not $U(2)$ covariant, since the rotated slot fails to square to zero and the doubly occupied state transforms by a permanent.

Whatever the parity, the resulting thirty-two states carry exactly the state space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ and the $U(2) \times U(3)$ action of (S). The only thing the parity changes is the tower grading: the component with $j$ slots and $k$ pairs occupied has grading $(-1)^{\pi j + k}$. For odd slots this is the chirality (S) declares. For even slots, Klein-twisted fermions $s = cK$ that the no-canonical-commutation theorem explicitly allows as bosons made of fermions, the doublets land at the opposite handedness to the singlets. Each chirality half is then $\bar{Q} \oplus \bar{L} \oplus u^{c} \oplus d^{c} \oplus e^{c} \oplus \nu^{c}$ or its conjugate, which fails the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ condition by $\tfrac23$ and the cubic condition by $\tfrac49$ (the sums Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(3) records for doublets listed at the opposite handedness from the singlets); the only anomaly-free abelian generators are multiples of $j - 1$, which do not separate quarks from leptons.

So (S) is independent of the statistics no-go plus tower membership, with the even-slot model as witness, and the obstruction that removes the witness is anomaly cancellation of the hypercharge, not the generation count. Read the other way, the premises (a) to (d), the tower grading as chirality, and the imported anomaly conditions derive (S).
synthesis.slot-parity-decides-hypothesis.lay: The framework's particle content rests on an assumption, called (S): the two places in a composite particle that its basic spinor states occupy behave like fermions, the same kind of quantum mode as the particle's internal pairs. It was hoped that a known result, that the framework has no room for elementary bosons, would force this. It does not: a slot can be built from two of the framework's fermions, which is allowed, and everything still works except one thing, which half of the states counts as left-handed. With such slots the left-handed states would have the weak doublets and the singlets at opposite handedness, and the resulting theory would be inconsistent, because its hypercharge would suffer a quantum anomaly. So (S) is a genuine extra assumption, but, if the slots are two-level and the framework's own grading is read as handedness, the requirement of an anomaly-free theory pins it down.

proofs.main:
The operators live in the tower's canonical anticommutation algebra; the check realises it in $\Cl(6,6)$ with six modes, $a_{m} = \tfrac12(e_{m} + f_{m})$, $a_{m}^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{m} - f_{m})$, $e_{m}^{2} = 1$, $f_{m}^{2} = -1$, so that $\{a_{m}, a_{n}^{*}\} = \delta_{mn}$ and $\{a_{m}, a_{n}\} = 0$, with the tower's grading the grade involution. Modes $3, 4, 5$ carry the pairs, which are odd as in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}; the sixth supplies a Majorana generator $K = e_{6}$, $K^{2} = 1$.

(i) Let $c, d$ be real with $c^{2} + d^{2} = 1$ and $cd \ne 0$, and let $s' = cs_{1} + ds_{2}$, the image of $s_{1}$ under a rotation in $U(2)$. By (b) for $s_{1}, s_{2}$, $s'^{2} = cd\{s_{1}, s_{2}\}$, and (c) requires $s'^{2} = 0$, so $\{s_{1}, s_{2}\} = 0$. Likewise $\{s', s'^{*}\} = 1 + cd(\{s_{1}, s_{2}^{*}\} + \{s_{2}, s_{1}^{*}\})$, so the bracket sum vanishes; repeating with $s'' = cs_{1} + I_{4} d s_{2}$ (the unit of the tower's canonical anticommutation algebra being the field theory's $I_{4}$, which commutes with every tower mode operator), also the image under an element of $U(2)$, gives $\{s_{2}, s_{1}^{*}\} - \{s_{1}, s_{2}^{*}\} = 0$, hence both vanish. If instead $s_{1}s_{2} = s_{2}s_{1}$ with $s_{1}s_{2} \neq 0$, then $s'^{2} = 2cd\,s_{1}s_{2} \neq 0$, and on the doubly occupied state $(cs_{1}^{*} + ds_{2}^{*})(-ds_{1}^{*} + cs_{2}^{*})\lvert 0 \rangle = (c^{2} - d^{2})s_{1}^{*}s_{2}^{*}\lvert 0 \rangle$, the permanent of the rotation, which is not multiplicative; the check realises this with $h_{1} = a_{1}$, $h_{2} = a_{2}(1 - 2n_{1})$ and $(c, d) = (\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$, permanent $-\tfrac{7}{25}$ against determinant $1$.

(ii) By (i) and (b) the slot operators generate a two-mode Fock system and the pair operators a three-mode one (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}). By (d) each $s_{J}^{*}b_{K}^{*}\lvert 0 \rangle$ is, up to a sign, the product state with $J$ slots and $K$ pairs occupied, and moving a slot operator past a pair operator only changes signs; so the thirty-two states are independent and span $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, on which $(A, B)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}B$. By Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power} this is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ with $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$. The check builds both parities: $s_{i} = a_{i}$ ($\pi = 1$) and $s_{i} = a_{i}K$, $s_{i}^{*} = Ka_{i}^{*}$ ($\pi = 0$), each also multiplied by $(-1)^{N_{\mathrm{pair}}}$ to realise the other mutual sign; it verifies (b), the mutual relation, the common vacuum, the rotated relations under $(\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$, the determinant law on the doubly occupied state, and rank thirty-two of the states.

(iii) The vacuum projector is even. A slot creator has parity $\pi$ and a pair creator is odd, so $s_{J}^{*}b_{K}^{*}\lvert 0 \rangle$ has parity $(-1)^{\pi j + k}$, independently of the mutual sign. This equals $(-1)^{j + k}$ on every component if and only if $\pi = 1$; for $\pi = 0$ it differs on $j = 1$. The check computes the grade involution of every state.

(iv) Writing the abelian factor as $(A, B) = (\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$, $a \in SU(2)$, $b \in SU(3)$, as in Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}, the component $(j, k)$ carries $\Lambda^{j}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$, content $1, 2, 1$ in $j$ and $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$ in $k$, with weight $3j - 2k$ and $Y = (3j - 2k)/6$; this uses only (ii), not Hypothesis (S). For $\pi = 0$ the even half is $(0,0) = \nu^{c}$, $(0,2) = u^{c}$, $(2,0) = e^{c}$, $(2,2) = d^{c}$, $(1,0) = (2,1)_{1/2} = \bar{L}$, $(1,2) = (2,\bar{3})_{-1/6} = \bar{Q}$. Taking it as left-handed, the conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} for $Y$ are: $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$, $2(-\tfrac16) - \tfrac23 + \tfrac13 = -\tfrac23$; $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$, $3(-\tfrac16) + \tfrac12 = 0$; gravitational, $6(-\tfrac16) + 2 \cdot \tfrac12 + 3(-\tfrac23) + 3 \cdot \tfrac13 + 1 = 0$; cubic, $6(-\tfrac16)^{3} + 2(\tfrac12)^{3} + 3(-\tfrac23)^{3} + 3(\tfrac13)^{3} + 1 = \tfrac49$. These two nonzero sums are the ones Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(3) records (``if the doublets were listed in the opposite handedness from the singlets the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ and cubic sums would be $-\tfrac23$ and $+\tfrac49$''); what is added here is that the even-slot model produces exactly that listing, and the analysis of a general generator below. That theorem is cited for agreement only and not used as a premise, since it holds under Hypothesis (S) and the present result must not rest on (S). The odd half is the conjugate and the sums change sign. For a general generator $\alpha j + \beta k + \gamma$ the three linear sums on the even half are $4\alpha + 8\beta + 4\gamma$, $4\alpha + 6\beta + 4\gamma$ and $16\alpha + 24\beta + 16\gamma$, of rank two, with kernel $\beta = 0$, $\gamma = -\alpha$; on that kernel the cubic sum is $\alpha^{3}(-4 + 4) = 0$, the four slot-free and four doubly occupied states entering with $j - 1 = \mp 1$. For $\pi = 1$ the even half is $\nu^{c}, u^{c}, Q, L, e^{c}, d^{c}$ and the linear sums are $4\alpha + 6\beta + 4\gamma$ (twice) and $16\alpha + 24\beta + 16\gamma$, of rank one, vanishing at $Y$ ($\alpha = \tfrac12$, $\beta = -\tfrac13$, $\gamma = 0$), where the cubic sum also vanishes (the standard cancellation, reproduced in the check). The check computes all of these sums exactly and scans the integer generators with $|\alpha|, |\beta|, |\gamma| \le 3$. (A remark not used: the cubic colour anomaly, triplets minus antitriplets weighted by $SU(2)$ multiplicity, cited from memory as a further condition, is $0$ for $\pi = 1$ and $-4$ for $\pi = 0$, the even half holding four antitriplets and no triplet.)

(v) The model with $\pi = 0$ lives in a finite floor, so by Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower} it contains no pair with $[a, a^{*}] = 1$; its slot operators are tower elements, even ones, which that proposition explicitly does not exclude. It satisfies (a) to (d), and by (iii) the tower grading is not the parity of the total mode number, so the chirality clause of Hypothesis (S) fails. Hence (S) is not a consequence of the no-go plus tower membership.

(vi) Under (a) to (d) with the tower grading as chirality, (iv) shows (for slot modules beyond the two-level case the same anomaly step is treated in the result filed alongside, synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content) that $\pi = 0$ violates the imported conditions for $Y$; so $\pi = 1$, and by (i) to (iii) the slots are fermionic modes generating with the pairs the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ with $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ and chirality the parity of the total mode number, which is every clause of Hypothesis (S). If the odd slots commute rather than anticommute with the pairs, the Klein transformation $s_{i} \mapsto s_{i}(-1)^{N_{\mathrm{pair}}}$ restores anticommutation without changing the states, the action or the grading (the check runs both signs at both parities).

synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-n.technical: The composite's state space under Hypothesis (S) is the sixteen-plus-sixteen states of five fermionic modes. Which states count as particles and which as antiparticles is a choice of involution that the premise fixes by asking it to commute with Spin(10). This result measures exactly how much that request does. The stored CPT theorem already gives the chirality on every charged state and leaves a free line in the two-dimensional neutral block; what is added is the cut of that line to two points and its resolution. Gauge symmetry alone allows thirty-two sign choices on the charged states and any split of the two neutral singlet states. Conserving the total mode number forces the split to be the empty state against the full one. The stored anomaly result then fixes all the charged signs. What remains is one bit: does the particle half contain the empty state or the full one. The two answers are carried into each other by swapping the two neutral states, a unitary that commutes with every gauge generator, so nothing with a gauge quantum number can decide it. Spin(10), through its operators that create two modes at once, makes it the empty state, and that is the same as saying that every creation and annihilation operator flips chirality. So the Spin(10) clause is one bit of premise, equivalent to the natural grading of the Clifford system, and cannot be derived from the other clauses.
synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-n.lay: In this model each matter particle of one family is a pattern of five occupied or empty slots, and the rule that sorts patterns into particles and antiparticles is assumed, not derived. The result counts what the assumptions actually decide: symmetry and consistency fix everything except one yes-or-no question, whether the completely empty pattern belongs with the particles or with the antiparticles. The remaining assumption decides that one question, and it amounts to saying that filling or emptying a slot always switches a particle to an antiparticle.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}(ii) and (v) give the module $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ with the two slot modes and three pair modes forming one system of five fermionic modes, the gauge group acting through its bilinears, and the Majorana combinations generating $\Cl(10)$ with $\Spin(10)$ the group of its bivectors (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}). Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4) gives the anomaly-free CPT halvings: the chirality is $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ on every charged component, with a free line in the neutral block. The twelve components $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ are irreducible and pairwise inequivalent except for $(n, k) = (0, 0)$ and $(2, 3)$, both $(1,1)_{0}$; conjugation pairs $(n, k)$ with $(2 - n, 3 - k)$. The check builds everything on the thirty-two-dimensional Fock space with exact sparse matrices (modes $0, 1$ slots, $2, 3, 4$ pairs), and computes each commutant as the solution space of $[X, g] = 0$ over all generators $g$ of the set, with $X$ supported on pairs of states of equal weight under the set's diagonal generators (which is where any solution lives), by exact elimination.

\emph{(i).} By Schur's lemma the commutant of a completely reducible action is $\bigoplus M_{m_{\rho}}(\C)$ over the isotypes, of dimension $\sum m_{\rho}^{2}$. For the gauge algebra the multiplicities are one on ten components and two on $(1,1)_{0}$, so the dimension is $10 + 4 = 14$; the check finds $14$, and that the only states of zero weight under all four diagonal generators are the empty and the full state (so the charged weight spaces are lines, a control). Under $\uu(5)$ the degrees $\Lambda^{d}\C^{5}$ are irreducible and inequivalent, dimension $6$. Under $\so(10)$ the two parities are the two inequivalent half-spin representations, dimension $2$. The Majoranas generate $\Cl(10)_{\C} = M_{32}(\C)$, dimension $1$. The product $\prod_{k}(a^{\dagger}_{k} + a_{k})(a_{k} - a^{\dagger}_{k}) = \prod_{k}(2N_{k} - 1) = \prod_{k}(-(-1)^{N_{k}}) = -(-1)^{N}$ (the pair factors are even and commute), as the check verifies; so the volume element is the parity up to sign, the stored statement.

\emph{(ii).} A gauge-commuting involution is a sign on each multiplicity-one component and an involution of the neutral block; a CPT halving needs $V_{-} \cong \bar{V}_{+}$, so the signs on conjugate charged components are opposite ($32$ patterns on the five pairs) and the block, self-conjugate, contributes one line to each half, any pair of complementary lines. The check enumerates the $32$ patterns. Commuting with $\uu(5)$ means commuting with the degree projectors: the signs are constant on each degree (degrees $1$ to $4$ carry only charged components, and CPT ties degree $d$ to $5 - d$), which the check finds leaves $4$ charged patterns, and the block involution is diagonal in degree, so the particle line is $\C\Omega$ or $\C\Omega^{\top}$: $8$ halvings. Anomaly freedom, the stored clause (4), fixes the charged signs to $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$: the check finds $2$ of the $4$ patterns, hence $4$ halvings with the neutral choice. An involution commuting with $\so(10)$ is $\alpha P_{\mathrm{even}} + \beta P_{\mathrm{odd}}$ by (i), with $\alpha, \beta = \pm1$; equal signs give $\Gamma = \pm1$, whose halves have dimensions $32$ and $0$, not a halving; so $\Gamma = \pm(-1)^{N}$ (the check enumerates). The vacuum-swapped halving $\Gamma' = (-1)^{N} - 2P_{\Omega} + 2P_{\Omega^{\top}}$ is an involution of trace zero commuting with every $a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$, is anomaly-free (it agrees with $(-1)^{N}$ on every charged component) and does not commute with $a^{\dagger}_{1}a^{\dagger}_{2}$, which carries $\Omega$ to degree two (checked). So the ladder is $32 \times$ (lines) $\to 8 \to 4 \to 2$. The check computes it from the operators: the gauge components as the cyclic submodules generated from the weight vectors (connectivity under the off-diagonal entries of the generators), the conjugate pairing from the negated weight multisets (five pairs and two self-conjugate single states), the $\uu(5)$ components (six, of sizes $1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1$) and the $\so(10)$ components (two of sixteen), and counts the sign patterns constant on each; removing the hypercharge from the gauge set changes the pairing and the count. Commuting with the total mode number $N$ alone, in place of $\uu(5)$, already splits the neutral block into $\C\Omega$ and $\C\Omega^{\top}$ (they have $N = 0$ and $N = 5$), and with the stored charged chirality gives the same four halvings; only the count $8$ uses $\uu(5)$. The two survivors are conjugate: the swap $S$ of $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$ (identity on the other thirty states) is an involution, commutes with every gauge generator (both states are gauge singlets of the same weight), and $S(-1)^{N}S = \Gamma'$ (checked); $S$ does not commute with $\so(10)$. So the bit is invisible to every gauge quantum number and is seen only by the pair operators of $\so(10)$, the $B - L$ charged direction of the Majorana element $\Omega \mapsto \Omega^{\top}$.

\emph{(iii).} If $\Gamma\gamma_{p}\Gamma = -\gamma_{p}$ for all $p$ then $\Gamma(-1)^{N}$ commutes with every $\gamma_{p}$ (since $(-1)^{N}$ anticommutes with each), hence with $M_{32}(\C)$ by (i), so it is a scalar, and $\Gamma = c(-1)^{N}$ with $c = \pm1$ from $\Gamma^{2} = 1$. Conversely $\pm(-1)^{N}$ anticommute with each $\gamma_{p}$ (checked for all ten), and the vacuum-swapped $\Gamma'$ fails for $\gamma_{1}$ (checked). The equivalence with the $\Spin(10)$ form: $\Gamma$ commutes with the bivectors iff it commutes with the even subalgebra they generate; a grading of the Clifford system commutes with the even part and anticommutes with the odd part, and conversely an involution commuting with the even part is $\alpha P_{\mathrm{even}} + \beta P_{\mathrm{odd}}$ by (i), which anticommutes with the generators iff $\alpha = -\beta$, the CPT condition. Independence: $\Gamma'$ satisfies clauses (a), (b), (G), the CPT halving, the joint Clifford system (it is an involution on the same module) and anomaly freedom, and differs from $(-1)^{N}$ exactly on the neutral block; so the clause is not a consequence of the others, and its content is the choice of $\Omega$ over $\Omega^{\top}$. The control repeats the counts on the three-mode pair system ($\uu(3)$: $4$; $\so(6)$: $2$; $\gamma_{1}\cdots\gamma_{6} = -(-1)^{N}$), the stored chirality of the pair system in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}'s language.

\emph{Scope.} Nothing here derives the clause; it locates it. Whether a further stated structure of the series (the Majorana element's action $\Omega \mapsto \Omega^{\top}$, which maps each half to the other under both candidate halvings and so does not decide; or the no-spectator route) selects $\Omega$ is left to the open problem. Transport-absent: finite Clifford algebra on the series' module.

synthesis.supersymmetric-splits-two-loop.formal:
Under Hypothesis (S), run the four splits of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-supersymmetric-splits} at two loops with the top Yukawa, from the record's central values and with the top Yukawa as in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops} ($y_{t}(M_{Z}) = 0.95$, matched by $1/\sin\beta$ at the heavy threshold, $\sin\beta = 1$): the Standard Model matrix below $M_{I}$, between $M_{I}$ and $M_{I}'$ the generic matrix of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-two-loop-gauge-coefficients} for the Standard Model content with the light set, as the Fact quotes it, that is without the gaugino-Higgs-higgsino Yukawa couplings of splits (a) and (d), above $M_{I}'$ the minimal supersymmetric matrix. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Exact.)} The middle-regime one-loop coefficients are $(\tfrac92, -\tfrac76, -5)$, $(\tfrac92, -\tfrac52, -7)$, $(\tfrac{23}{5}, -\tfrac73, -7)$ and $(\tfrac92, -\tfrac76, -7)$ for (a) to (d), and the two-loop matrices are the generic formula's for the listed content. At $f = f'$ every split is the full supersymmetric content at one threshold, so the four lines of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.two-threshold-criterion} share the diagonal point; at one loop it is $f = f' = 1.0116$, outside the triangle, the $1.2$ percent miss in $f$ (a threshold near $62$ GeV, below $M_{Z}$) of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact}(c), and this is why the lines of (a), (b) and (c) miss the triangle.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The decision.)} At two loops the diagonal point is admissible, $M_{I} = M_{I}' = 2.3$ TeV, $f = f' = 0.901$, $M_{U} = 1.1 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, $\alpha_{U}^{-1} = 25.7$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops}), and it meets the proton condition. So each of the four splits is admissible at two loops, and none is excluded by unification: the one-loop exclusion of (a), (b) and (c) does not survive.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Record, computed numerically; middle-regime matrices without the gaugino Yukawas.)} Each admissible set is a curve ending at the diagonal point. For (a), (b) and (c) the light set lies between $M_{Z}$ and $2.3$ TeV and the heavy set above, the far end at $f = 1$ having the heavy set at $1.0 \times 10^{8}$, $7.9 \times 10^{5}$ and $1.6 \times 10^{9}$ GeV and $M_{U} = 2.7 \times 10^{16}$, $2.8 \times 10^{15}$ and $4.8 \times 10^{14}$ GeV. For (d) the light set lies above $2.3$ TeV, the far end at $f' = 0$ having the light set at $3.5 \times 10^{9}$ GeV and $M_{U} = 1.2 \times 10^{14}$ GeV. Including the gaugino-Higgs-higgsino Yukawas at tree-level matching, through the general two-loop Yukawa term (not a Fact of the store), moves the far end of (a) to a heavy set at $5.4 \times 10^{7}$ GeV and that of (d) to $3.4 \times 10^{9}$ GeV, and leaves the diagonal point and every decision unchanged. The one-loop end $(f, f') = (1, 0.991)$, every partner near $M_{Z}$, is not admissible at two loops, and on the whole curve every partner of (d), the gluino included, lies above $2.3$ TeV.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Record, computed numerically; proton condition of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-proton-condition}, same matrices as (iii).)} (a) meets it on its whole curve; (b) and (c) meet it from the diagonal point down to the light set at about $490$ GeV and $1.2$ TeV respectively, the heavy set then at $3.7 \times 10^{4}$ GeV; (d) meets it from the diagonal point up to the light set at $1.7 \times 10^{4}$ GeV, the heavy set at $7.8 \times 10^{4}$ GeV and $M_{U} = 5.7 \times 10^{15}$ GeV, against $6 \times 10^{3}$ GeV at one loop (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.proton-condition-candidates}(2)).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Sensitivity, computed numerically.)} Across $\alpha_{s} = 0.1180 \pm 0.0009$ the diagonal point moves between $1.7$ and $3.0$ TeV and stays inside the triangle, so (ii) holds across the record's range; (d)'s far end moves between about $3$ and $4 \times 10^{9}$ GeV.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.supersymmetric-splits-two-loop.technical:
Under Hypothesis (S), at two loops and from the record's central values, the four ways of splitting the supersymmetric partners into a light and a heavy set all share one spectrum: both sets at the same scale. That spectrum is the supersymmetric row, which one loop places at $f = 1.0116$, a threshold of about $62$ GeV, below $M_{Z}$, and two loops place at $2.3$ TeV. One loop excluded three of the four splits only because their lines reach the diagonal outside the allowed triangle; at two loops the diagonal point is inside, so all four splits are admissible on curves ending there.

For the gaugino-higgsino split (a), the higgsino split (b) and the two-doublet split (c), the light set lies below $2.3$ TeV and the heavy set rises to $10^{8}$, $8 \times 10^{5}$ and $1.6 \times 10^{9}$ GeV at the far end. For split (d), the only one one loop admitted, the light set must lie above $2.3$ TeV, up to $3.5 \times 10^{9}$ GeV; its near-degenerate one-loop end is gone, so the gluino of (d) is above $2.3$ TeV automatically. The proton condition holds on all of (a), near the diagonal end of (b) and (c), and on (d) up to a light set at $1.7 \times 10^{4}$ GeV. The decision rests on the stored two-loop row; the curves are record-level integrations, with the generic matrix as the Fact quotes it, without the gaugino Yukawas; including them moves the far ends by a few percent in the logarithm, (a)'s heavy end by a factor of about two. Collider limits are not applied: in (a) the light set contains the gluino below $2.3$ TeV.
synthesis.supersymmetric-splits-two-loop.lay: Supersymmetric partner particles could come in two groups at two different energies. A simpler calculation had found that only one of four natural groupings lets the three forces meet. Redoing it one level more precisely, under the series' slot-statistics hypothesis (S) and with the measured coupling values, all four groupings work for the meeting of the forces and the proton's lifetime (limits from particle colliders are not applied here), because each of them includes the case where both groups sit together at about 2.3 TeV, which the more precise calculation already allowed. What changes between groupings is how far the two groups can be pulled apart. In the grouping the simpler calculation favoured, every partner now has to be heavier than about 2.3 TeV, and the proton lives long enough only while the lighter group stays below about 17 TeV.

proofs.main:
(i) The one-loop coefficients are Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices} applied to the component listings of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact} (gauginos one Weyl adjoint per factor, higgsinos a vector-like pair of doublets, the second doublet a complex scalar, the sfermions three scalar generations): the light sets add $\Dl = (\tfrac25, 2, 2)$, $(\tfrac25, \tfrac23, 0)$, $(\tfrac12, \tfrac56, 0)$ and $(\tfrac25, 2, 0)$ to $(\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$, and light plus heavy is the full content $(\tfrac52, \tfrac{25}{6}, 4)$ in every split. The two-loop matrices are the generic formula of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-two-loop-gauge-coefficients} on the listed Weyl fermions and complex scalars, which excludes gauge Yukawa couplings; the script rebuilds the Fact's Standard Model and supersymmetric matrices from components as controls, and prints the four middle-regime matrices. At $f = f'$ the middle regime has zero length, so the run is the one-threshold run of the full content; in Theorem \claimref{standard-model.two-threshold-criterion} the line $f(\Dl_{12} - R\Dl_{23}) + f'(\Dl'_{12} - R\Dl'_{23}) = Rb_{23} - b_{12}$ meets the diagonal at $f = (Rb_{23} - b_{12})/((\Dl + \Dl')_{12} - R(\Dl + \Dl')_{23})$, the same exact rational for all four splits, and at the inputs of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run} it is $1.0116\ldots > 1$, the threshold fraction of the full content in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.table-exact}(c). The script evaluates the four lines exactly, recovers the endpoints $(1, 0.99115)$ and $(0.4377, 0)$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-supersymmetric-splits}(d) and confirms that the lines of (a), (b) and (c) meet neither $f = 1$ nor $f' = 0$ inside the triangle; each passes through the diagonal at $1.0116$ and leaves the triangle on both sides.

(ii) A pair $(M_{I}, M_{I}')$ with $M_{I} = M_{I}'$ is admissible for a split exactly when the full content at the single threshold $M_{I}$ unifies, since the run is then identical; Proposition \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops} finds that it does at $M_{I} = 2.3$ TeV with $M_{U} = 1.1 \times 10^{16}$ GeV and $\alpha_{U}^{-1} = 25.7$, and states the spread $1.7$ to $3.0$ TeV across $\alpha_{s} = 0.1180 \pm 0.0009$. Since $M_{Z} < M_{I} = M_{I}' < M_{U}$, the point lies in the triangle $0 \le f' \le f \le 1$ for every split, so every split has a nonempty admissible set at two loops. Proposition \claimref{standard-model.proton-condition-candidates}(3) records that this point meets the proton condition.

(iii) to (v) are computed numerically, at record level, and are not part of the exact check; they are reproducible from the description that follows. The two-loop equations of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-two-loop-gauge-coefficients}, $da_{i}/d\ln\mu = -b_{i}/2\pi - \sum_{j}B_{ij}/(8\pi^{2}a_{j}) + c_{i}y_{t}^{2}/(32\pi^{3})$ with the middle-regime matrices of (i), are integrated from $M_{Z} = 91.1876$ GeV with the record's central values $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}^{-1} = 127.951$, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 0.23122$, $\alpha_{s} = 0.1180$, the top Yukawa running at one loop as the Fact gives it from $y_{t}(M_{Z}) = 0.95$, the thresholds as step functions and the matching $y_{t} \to y_{t}/\sin\beta$, $\sin\beta = 1$, at $M_{I}'$, by fourth-order Runge-Kutta in $\ln\mu$ with step $0.04$ (halving the step changes no printed digit). For each light threshold the heavy threshold is found by bisection on the mismatch $a_{2} - a_{3}$ at the crossing of $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$. Controls: with the two-loop terms off and the rounded inputs of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run}, the integrator returns the exact one-loop endpoint $f' = 0.99115$ of split (d) at $f = 1$ that the check computes in rationals; with them on, the diagonal point is $M_{I} = M_{I}' = 2259$ GeV, $M_{U} = 1.125 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, $\alpha_{U}^{-1} = 25.736$, $f = 0.9011$, the stored row's values. The numbers obtained, without the gaugino Yukawas: far ends at $f = 1$ with the heavy set at $9.74 \times 10^{7}$, $7.92 \times 10^{5}$ and $1.60 \times 10^{9}$ GeV and $M_{U} = 2.67 \times 10^{16}$, $2.80 \times 10^{15}$, $4.76 \times 10^{14}$ GeV for (a), (b), (c); the $f' = 0$ end of (d) at a light set of $3.50 \times 10^{9}$ GeV with $M_{U} = 1.18 \times 10^{14}$ GeV and $\alpha_{U}^{-1} = 39.97$. A light threshold half an e-fold beyond the diagonal point, above it for (a) to (c) and below it for (d), admits no heavy threshold, which fixes the side of the diagonal on which each curve lies; the curves were traced by a scan of light thresholds at half-e-fold spacing, each admitting one heavy threshold. The proton figure of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-proton-condition} changes sign between light thresholds $450$ and $530$ GeV for (b) (heavy set $4.3$ to $3.2 \times 10^{4}$ GeV), between $1.1$ and $1.3$ TeV for (c) (heavy set $4.6$ to $2.3 \times 10^{4}$ GeV), and between $1.6$ and $1.8 \times 10^{4}$ GeV for (d) (heavy set $6.7$ to $8.2 \times 10^{4}$ GeV, $M_{U}$ from $5.9$ to $5.7 \times 10^{15}$ GeV); bisection locates the crossings stated in (iv). It is positive at both ends of (a) and at the diagonal point, and negative at the far ends of (b), (c) and (d). With the gaugino-Higgs-higgsino Yukawas included at tree-level matching the far end of (a) moves to $5.4 \times 10^{7}$ GeV and that of (d) to $3.39 \times 10^{9}$ GeV. At $\alpha_{s} = 0.1171$ and $0.1189$ the diagonal point is at $2990$ and $1714$ GeV and (d)'s far end at $3.87$ and $3.16 \times 10^{9}$ GeV. Two independent reproductions agree: integrating the two-loop terms along the one-loop path (leading logarithms) gives the diagonal point at $2.2$ TeV and the far ends within twenty percent in the heavy scale, and an adaptive integration (relative tolerance $10^{-11}$) reproduced every number above to the printed precision. The run's content, three derived generations with their lepton doublets, rests on Hypothesis (S) through Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run}.

synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-fiel.formal:
Assume (GW) the Gildener-Weinberg one-loop formula (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}): on a flat direction of a scale-free tree potential, along which every field-dependent mass squared is proportional to $\varphi^{2}$ with $\langle\varphi\rangle = v$, the scalon has
\[
8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{S}^{2} = 3\sum_{\text{vectors}}M^{4} + \sum_{\text{real scalars}}M^{4} - 4N_{c}\sum_{\text{Dirac fermions}}M^{4};
\]
and assume (D) decoupling: the only states whose masses depend on the rung field are the Standard Model's and the rung field's charged pair (the Majorana and Pati-Salam sectors carry no coupling to the rung field that gives a rung mass term; (D) fails for order-one neutrino Dirac couplings with the stored $v_{R}$, see the proof). Apply (GW) to the rung field on its flat physical branch on the cone $Q = 0$ (the ray $m = -\mathsf{N}$ of a scale-free potential with $a + b = e$, $e \ge 0$, $2a \ge e$; \claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}, clause (3)), with the Hermitian gauge masses of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(2), the charged plane of (3), the fermion entries of (5) (on the physical ray of size $|\beta|$ in the per-sector reading and in its $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion alike), and $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Content.)} The gauge mass form has eigenvalues $g^{2}$ twice, $g^{2} + g'^{2}$ once and $0$ once, so the vectors contribute $6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4}$; the physical scalars are the scalon and the charged pair (two real directions), whose tree mass squared $2(2a - e)\mathsf{N}$ is proportional to $\mathsf{N}$, as are the gauge and fermion masses; the top contributes $-12m_{t}^{4}$. Hence $8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{h}^{2} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4} + 2m_{\pm}^{4} - 12m_{t}^{4} - \ell$, with $\ell = 12m_{b}^{4} + 12m_{c}^{4} + 4m_{\tau}^{4}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Standard Model content.)} Without the charged pair the right side is negative for every $m_{t} \in [162, 173]$ GeV, the range containing the stored pole and $M_{Z}$-scale top masses; at the stored pole mass $m_{h}^{2}$ lies between $-(47\ \mathrm{GeV})^{2}$ and $-(45\ \mathrm{GeV})^{2}$; the vector bosons alone would give $9.7 < m_{h} < 9.9$ GeV.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Threshold.)} $m_{h}^{2} > 0$ exactly when $2m_{\pm}^{4} > 12m_{t}^{4} + \ell - 6M_{W}^{4} - 3M_{Z}^{4}$; the threshold lies in $(249, 250)$ GeV at $m_{t} = 162$ GeV and in $(267, 268)$ GeV at $m_{t} = 173$ GeV, above $m_{t} - m_{b}$: the charged pair is not produced in top decays.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The measured Higgs mass.)} With $m_{h} \in [125, 125.4]$ GeV, $v \in [246, 247]$ GeV (containing the tree value from the stored $M_{W}$, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z})$ and $\alpha(M_{Z})$, and $246.22$ GeV), $m_{t} \in [162, 173]$ GeV and the stored $M_{W}$, $M_{Z}$, $m_{b}$, $m_{c}$, $m_{\tau}$: $450 < m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV, with $454 < m_{\pm} < 455$ GeV at $v = 246.22$ GeV, the stored $m_{h}$ and the stored pole $m_{t}$; the charged quartic is $3.2 < 2a - e = m_{\pm}^{2}/v^{2} < 3.5$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Diphoton rate.)} On the flat ray the charged pair couples to the scalon with $\partial m_{\pm}^{2}/\partial v = 2m_{\pm}^{2}/v$, so, with the standard one-loop amplitudes (cited from memory), $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} = \bigl((A_{1}(\tau_{W}) + \tfrac43 A_{1/2}(\tau_{t}) + A_{0}(\tau_{\pm}))/(A_{1}(\tau_{W}) + \tfrac43 A_{1/2}(\tau_{t}))\bigr)^{2}$, $\tau_{i} = m_{h}^{2}/4m_{i}^{2}$; with the stored $m_{h}$, $M_{W}$, pole $m_{t}$ and $m_{\pm} \in [450, 456]$ GeV, $0.898 < \mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$, below the measured signal strength (Particle Data Group average $1.10 \pm 0.06$; ATLAS full Run 2 alone $1.04^{+0.10}_{-0.09}$).
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (the elementary rung field, 2026-11-01).} The rung field is recorded as the elementary palatial linear field, with values in all eight real components of the complexified rung summand, two doublets of hypercharge $\tfrac12$ (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}). The count in (i) is that of the field constrained to the cone, the six directions tangent to it; for the linear field it is the case of a massless neutral normal pair. Counted in full, with the normal pair in the scalon sum (the standard two-doublet sum rule), the bracket of (iv) becomes an upper bound, $m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV (below $383$ GeV when the normal pair is the heavier), the normal pair lies below $542$ GeV, and $h \to \gamma\gamma$ stays below $0.900$ of the Standard Model rate for every charged mass in $(m_{h}/2, 456]$ GeV, under the same hypotheses (GW) and (D) (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}). The edge $450 < m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV, a massless normal pair, is excluded by the measured invisible width of the $Z$ (argued there). Clauses (i) to (v) stand as statements about the constrained field.

\emph{Note (the transmutation branch excluded, 2 November 2026).} Under the decided coupling reading of the rung field, the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion $Yc + \tilde{Y}c^{*}$ with complex symmetric family matrices (the rung $10$), the transmutation branch, for the constrained field here and for the elementary linear field (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}), is recorded as excluded, by three independent strikes: (1) $h \to \gamma\gamma$: the bound $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$ lies $3.3$ standard deviations below the Particle Data Group 2026 average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ (pdglive node S126SGG, read on 2 November 2026; inputs ATLAS 2023 $1.04^{+0.10}_{-0.09}$, CMS 2022 $1.13 \pm 0.09$, ATLAS and CMS Run 1 $1.14^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$); (2) $B$-meson mixing: tree-level exchange of the neutral normal pair, below $542$ GeV on this branch, exceeds the measured $B_{s}$ and $B_{d}$ mass differences more than $50$ times for every splitting of its two masses (more than $52$ and $50$), with quark mixing from tree-level determinations and three-family unitarity (\claimref{synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch}); (3) strong coupling: on the scalon-sum surface the quartic couplings reach $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV at one loop (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-strong-coupling-within-a-few-tev-on-the-transmutation-branch}). Clauses (i) to (v) and their mathematics are unchanged and stand as statements under (GW) and (D); what is excluded is this branch as the origin of the weak scale under that coupling reading. The branch with a level, on which the second doublet is heavy (about $2.5$ to $3.5$ TeV), is the working branch.
synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-fiel.technical: If the weak scale arises by dimensional transmutation, the tree potential of the rung field is flat along the physical branch and the Higgs mass comes entirely from one loop, from the fourth powers of the masses the vacuum gives to every particle that feels the rung field. This result assumes that those are the Standard Model's particles and the rung field's charged pair only; the series' Majorana and Pati-Salam sectors would otherwise feed the rung field a mass term of their own scale and lift the flat direction. Bosons push the Higgs mass up and fermions down; with the Standard Model's particles the top wins and the mass squared is negative, about $-(46$ GeV$)^{2}$. The rung field's charged pair restores it once heavier than about $250$ to $268$ GeV, and the measured $125$ GeV fixes the pair between $450$ and $456$ GeV, above the top, with a large quartic coupling. The pair does not decouple from the Higgs decay to two photons and lowers that rate to $0.90$ of the Standard Model's, below the measured value. The scale itself is not derived: it is where the physical-branch coupling runs through zero, an input of the same kind as the weak scale against the Planck mass. (Note, 2026-11-01: the rung field is recorded as the elementary linear field with two doublets, for which this count is the edge with a massless neutral pair; counted in full, the charged pair lies below $456$ GeV rather than in the $450$ to $456$ GeV bracket, and the diphoton rate stays below $0.900$ of the Standard Model's for every charged mass between $m_{h}/2$ and $456$ GeV, \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}.) (Note, 2 November 2026: under the series' coupling reading with symmetric family matrices this branch is excluded, by the diphoton rate, whose Particle Data Group 2026 average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ lies $3.3$ standard deviations above the bound $0.900$, by tree-level $B$-meson mixing more than fifty times the measured rate, and by quartic couplings that reach $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV; the branch with a level, with the second doublet at a few TeV, is the working branch.)
synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-fiel.lay: One way to explain why the weak scale is so far below the gravitational one is the mechanism that makes the proton's mass: a scale generated by the slow running of a coupling, with no mass put in by hand. For the Higgs this works only if the particles that feel the Higgs field supply the Higgs mass through quantum effects, and in the Standard Model the top quark spoils it. The series' Higgs field carries an extra electrically charged scalar, which rescues the mechanism if it weighs between $450$ and $456$ GeV, provided the series' very heavy neutrino and unification sectors do not talk to the Higgs field, which on the series' present readings they do. The same charged scalar would make the Higgs decay to two photons about ten percent rarer than the Standard Model predicts, while the measurements, as recalled here, lean the other way. The route does not explain the size of the weak scale; it moves the question to where a coupling runs through zero. (Since 2 November 2026 this route is recorded as ruled out under the series' reading of how the Higgs field couples to quarks: the two-photon rate now measured lies well above what it predicts, the extra particles would make bottom mesons turn into their antiparticles far faster than is observed, and the forces among them would grow too strong within a few TeV.)

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The hypothesis is the one-loop formula of Gildener and Weinberg (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}): when a scale-free tree potential has a flat direction $\varphi\hat{n}$ on which it vanishes, the one-loop potential along it is $B\varphi^{4}(\ln(\varphi^{2}/\mu^{2}) + \text{const})$ with $64\pi^{2}B v^{4} = \sum_{i}n_{i}M_{i}^{4}$ (vectors $n = 3$, real scalars $n = 1$, Dirac fermions $n = -4N_{c}$, masses at $\varphi = v$), and its minimum gives the scalon mass $m_{S}^{2} = 8Bv^{2}$, which is the displayed formula. It requires every field-dependent mass squared to be proportional to $\varphi^{2}$ and no explicit dimensionful coupling to the scalon; hypothesis (D) secures that for the series' content, and the paragraph \emph{Decoupling} below says why it is a restriction.

\emph{(i).} By \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(2) the gauge mass form at a charge-preserving point is $\tfrac14 \mathsf{N} P$ with $P$ of eigenvalues $g^{2}, g^{2}, g^{2} + g'^{2}, 0$, giving two vectors of mass $M_{W}$, one of mass $M_{Z}$ and the photon, all with $M^{2} \propto \mathsf{N}$; with three polarisations each, $6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4}$. By clause (3) of the same result, the six real directions on the locus are three gauge directions (eaten, massless in Landau gauge, no contribution), the neutral mode (the scalon itself, absent from the sum) and a charged plane of two real directions. On the flat physical ray of a scale-free potential (\claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}, clause (3)) the charged mass squared is $2(2a - e)\mathsf{N}$: along $\alpha = (0, \varepsilon z)$, which keeps $Q = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = 0$ exactly, $\mathsf{N}$ and $m$ both grow by $\tfrac12\varepsilon^{2}|z|^{2}$, and $V = a\mathsf{N}^{2} + bm^{2} + e\mathsf{N}m$ grows by $(2a - e)\mathsf{N}\varepsilon^{2}|z|^{2} + \tfrac14(a + b + e)\varepsilon^{4}|z|^{4}$ at $m = -\mathsf{N}$ with $b = e - a$; the kinetic coefficient is $|z|^{2}$. Under the conjugate reading every tree Dirac entry is $\lambda = |\beta| = \sqrt{2\mathsf{N}}$ on the physical branch (clause (5)), so the fermion masses squared are proportional to $\mathsf{N}$ as well; this holds in the per-sector reading and in its $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion alike, since on the ray $\alpha = 0$ both $c$ and $c^{*}$ have size $|\beta|$. The top quark is a Dirac fermion with three colours, weight $-12$; the bottom and charm likewise, and the tau $-4$.

\emph{(ii) to (iv).} Exact rational arithmetic with the stored masses and brackets: $\pi \in [\tfrac{333}{106}, \tfrac{355}{113}]$; $v \in [246, 247]$ GeV, which contains $246.22$ GeV (the Fermi scale, \claimref{quantity.fermi-scale}) and the tree value $v^{2} = M_{W}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta_{W}\alpha^{-1}/\pi$ from the stored $M_{W}$, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z})$ and $\alpha^{-1}(M_{Z})$, about $246.6$ GeV; $m_{t} \in [162, 173]$ GeV, which contains the stored pole mass $172.57$ GeV, the stored $m_{t}(M_{Z}) = 171.7$ GeV and the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ value $m_{t}(m_{t})$ near $162.5$ GeV (from memory); $m_{h} \in [125, 125.4]$ GeV containing the stored $125.20$ GeV. Solving (i) for $m_{\pm}^{4}$ gives an expression increasing in $\pi$, $v$, $m_{h}$, $m_{t}$ and decreasing in $M_{W}$, $M_{Z}$, so its range over the box is attained at the corners, which the check evaluates exactly: $450^{4} < m_{\pm}^{4} < 456^{4}$. The threshold (iii) is the zero of the right side of (i) at $m_{h} = 0$: the check evaluates its sign at $249, 250$ GeV ($m_{t} = 162$) and $267, 268$ GeV ($m_{t} = 173$). The quartic: $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N} = (2a - e)v^{2}$, and the corners give $3.2 < 2a - e < 3.5$. Because the mass of the charged pair exceeds $m_{t} - m_{b}$ for every top mass in the range, $t \to bH^{+}$ is closed. The tree prediction $m_{\pm}^{2} = M_{W}^{2} + m_{h}^{2} - M_{Z}^{2}$ of $W = \kappa \mathsf{N}^{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(4) with \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-charged-scalar-sum-rule}) is not a flat-direction potential: its flat point has $m_{\pm}^{2} = M_{W}^{2} - M_{Z}^{2} < 0$ (\claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}, clause (4)). The quartic $2a - e \approx 3.4$ is about $1.7$ in the Standard Model normalisation $m_{h}^{2} = 2\lambda v^{2}$: large; its running, and with it the scale of a Landau pole, is not computed here.

\emph{(v).} On the flat ray $m_{\pm}^{2} = (2a - e)\varphi^{2}$, so the scalon-pair coupling is $\partial m_{\pm}^{2}/\partial\varphi = 2m_{\pm}^{2}/v$ and the pair's term in the diphoton amplitude, $(g_{hSS}v/2m_{S}^{2})Q^{2}A_{0}$, has unit weight with $Q = 1$. The loop functions (cited from memory) are $A_{1} = -(2\tau^{2} + 3\tau + 3(2\tau - 1)f)/\tau^{2}$, $A_{1/2} = 2(\tau + (\tau - 1)f)/\tau^{2}$, $A_{0} = -(\tau - f)/\tau^{2}$, $f = \arcsin^{2}\sqrt{\tau}$ for $\tau \le 1$, and the top enters with $N_{c}Q_{t}^{2} = \tfrac43$. The check bounds $f$ by its series $\tfrac12\sum_{n}(4\tau)^{n}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, whose terms are at most $\tau^{n}$, with a rational tail bound and outward rounding, verifies the bracket against $\arcsin^{2}\tfrac12 = \pi^{2}/36$, and obtains $-8.332 < A_{1}(\tau_{W}) < -8.331$, $1.835 < \tfrac43 A_{1/2}(\tau_{t}) < 1.836$, $0.336 < A_{0}(\tau_{\pm}) < 0.337$ and $0.898 < \mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$ for $m_{\pm} \in [450, 456]$ GeV. The measured diphoton signal strength, $1.10 \pm 0.06$ in the Particle Data Group average of the ATLAS and CMS measurements, lies about three standard deviations above; the ATLAS full Run 2 value alone, $1.04^{+0.10}_{-0.09}$ (arXiv:2207.00348), lies about 1.5 standard deviations above. Both values were checked against the published sources.

\emph{Decoupling.} Hypothesis (D) is not a property of the stored content. Under the conjugate reading the neutrino Dirac entries are read like the up-type ones (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)), so order-one Dirac couplings $y$ are allowed for the heaviest family, and the Pati-Salam route stores $v_{R} = M_{I}/g_{R} = 4.15 \times 10^{10}$ GeV (\claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}). Heavy Majorana neutrinos of mass $M_{R}$ then contribute to the rung field a one-loop mass term of order $y^{2}M_{R}^{2}/(4\pi^{2})$, an explicit dimensionful coupling far above $v^{2}$ that lifts the flat direction; requiring it below $v^{2}$ is the Vissani-type naturalness bound (F. Vissani, Phys. Rev. D 57 (1998) 7027, cited from memory, not checked), $M_{R}$ below about $10^{7}$ GeV for order-one $y$. The right-handed gauge bosons of the Pati-Salam stage couple to the rung bidoublet and give the same kind of term, of order $g_{R}^{2}M_{W_{R}}^{2}/(16\pi^{2})$, at one loop. Classical scale invariance removes no physical threshold, so (D) holds only if these couplings are absent or the heavy scales are near the weak scale; argued, not computed.

\emph{Remarks (computed, floating point, one loop, $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$, Landau gauge; not part of the claim).} (a) Per-sector reading (not $\su(2)_{R}$ covariant): for a potential even under $c \mapsto c^{*}$ both rays are flat; in the per-sector reading the fermions read only $|\beta|$, so on the mirror ray they are nearly massless (under the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion their entries there are of order $|\alpha|$ and the comparison below does not apply), and with the bosonic content equal the mirror minimum is deeper (ratio of minimum energies about $1.75$): the conjugation-odd quartic $e$ must be positive for the physical branch to be the vacuum. (b) With $W = 0$ as a boundary condition the physical-branch coefficient equals $(g^{2} + g'^{2})/8 \approx 0.069$, while its slope near the flat point is $m_{h}^{2}/v^{2} \approx 0.26$ per e-fold: the pure D-term boundary sits about $0.27$ e-folds above the transmutation scale, and the charged quartic $2a - e \approx 3.4$ there cannot run from the D-term's $\tfrac14 g^{2} \approx 0.1$ in that interval, so a pure D-term at a high scale is not a boundary for this route. The transmutation scale is therefore an input, in place of the level; under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion it is an input of $v/M_{P}$ type, like the level itself (\claimref{synthesis.constant-d-term-level-fixes-weak-scale-against-planck-under-promotion}).

synthesis.up-down-split-under-conjugate-.technical: The series reads up-type masses through the conjugate of the rung vector, and under that reading one rung coupling gives up and down quarks equal masses. The question here is which dressings of the rung coupling can split them. An up-type mass term and the matching down-type term share the left-handed doublet and differ only in the right-handed singlet: $u^{c}$ and $\nu^{c}$ have right-handed isospin $-\tfrac12$, $d^{c}$ and $e^{c}$ have $+\tfrac12$, and they have the same size of $B - L$. A dressing that does not distinguish the sign of the right-handed isospin therefore gives equal up and down masses; this covers the plain $10$ and every function of $B - L$, including the Georgi-Jarlskog composite. A dressing odd in that isospin gives opposite contributions. The square of the Majorana element contains such odd pieces, because the Majorana element itself points along one direction of right-handed isospin. Adding its degree-four pieces (a truncation of the square that nothing in the stored structure selects; the whole square gives no mass entry), the down-type contributions cancel exactly and the up-type ones add: the result feeds up-type quark and Dirac neutrino masses only, in the ratio $3$ between them. Whether a dynamics selects this piece, and with which family matrix, is not derived.
synthesis.up-down-split-under-conjugate-.lay: In this framework, under its conjugate reading, the up-type quarks (up, charm, top) and the down-type quarks (down, strange, bottom) get their masses from one coupling read in two ways, which at first order makes them equal, against the observed large ratio of top to bottom. This result shows that any correction that does not tell left-right isospin apart keeps them equal, and that the square of the heavy object that gives neutrinos their large mass does tell it apart: one natural part of it feeds only the up-type quarks and the neutrinos. How large that part is, and how it is shared among the three families, is not decided.

proofs.main:
(i) On the sixteen, the even half of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics} (the halving the Pati-Salam stage forces, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(iii); the Dirac-neutrino entries need it), with the pairing of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes}: by Theorem \claimref{standard-model.yukawa-pattern-two-rung-module}, $w_{4}$ couples exactly $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$ and $v_{4}$ exactly $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$, each with symmetric form. For a diagonal $g$ with value $g(\varphi)$ on a basis state, $B(\psi, w_{4}g\varphi) = g(\varphi)B(\psi, w_{4}\varphi)$, so the symmetric part on a coupled pair $\{\psi, \varphi\}$ is $\tfrac12(g(\psi) + g(\varphi))$ times the $10$ entry, and likewise for $v_{4}$. By Proposition \claimref{standard-model.generation-ten-under-pati-salam} and the formula $T_{3R} = \tfrac12(N_{R} - 1)$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}, the doublets $L$, $Q$ have $T_{3R} = 0$, the singlets $e^{c}$, $d^{c}$ have $T_{3R} = \tfrac12$ and $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$ have $T_{3R} = -\tfrac12$, while $B - L$ is $1$ on $e^{c}$ and $\nu^{c}$ and $-\tfrac13$ on $d^{c}$ and $u^{c}$. So for $g = h(T_{3R}, B - L)$ the down-type lepton weight is $\tfrac12(h(0, -1) + h(\tfrac12, 1))$ and the up-type one $\tfrac12(h(0, -1) + h(-\tfrac12, 1))$, and on quarks the same with $(\tfrac13, -\tfrac13)$. Writing $h = h_{e} + h_{o}$ with $h_{e}$ even and $h_{o}$ odd in $T_{3R}$, $h_{o}(0, \cdot) = 0$ and $h_{o}(-\tfrac12, \cdot) = -h_{o}(\tfrac12, \cdot)$, which gives $e + o$ and $e - o$. The magnitudes of the $10$ entries agree in the two sectors under the conjugate reading (Corollary \claimref{standard-model.one-vev-vector-relations-breaking-pattern}: both are $|b|$), so equal weights mean equal masses.

(ii) The split. By Proposition \claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-square-of-majorana-element}(i), $TT^{\dagger} = \prod_{i}(\tfrac12 + \beta_{i})$ with $\beta_{i} = n_{i} - \tfrac12$, and $G_{4} = \tfrac18\sum_{i < l}\beta_{i}\beta_{l}$, each $\beta_{i}\beta_{l}$ a monomial supported on the modes $i$, $l$. The pair-only part is $P_{4} = \tfrac18\sum_{i < l \le 3}\beta_{i}\beta_{l} = \tfrac{1}{16}\bigl((\beta_{1} + \beta_{2} + \beta_{3})^{2} - \tfrac34\bigr) = 4\mu_{P}^{2} - \tfrac{3}{64}$ (using $\beta_{i}^{2} = \tfrac14$), which with $\mu_{P} = -\tfrac{3}{16}(B - L)$ is $\tfrac{3}{64}(3(B - L)^{2} - 1)$, and on pair number $k = 0, 1, 2, 3$ takes the values $\tfrac{3}{32}, -\tfrac{1}{32}, -\tfrac{1}{32}, \tfrac{3}{32}$, equal to $\tfrac{3}{32}(B - L)(-1)^{k}$. The rung-only part is $R_{4} = \tfrac18\beta_{4}\beta_{5} = \tfrac{1}{32}(-1)^{N_{R}} = -\tfrac{1}{32}\chi$, since $(-1)^{n} = -2\beta$ for each mode. The rest is $X_{4}$ (loc. cit. (ii)). The same split is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-is-rung-vector-times-pair-part-of-majorana-square}(i). Weights: $P_{4}$ is a function of $B - L$, with values $\tfrac{3}{32}$ at $|B - L| = 1$ and $-\tfrac{1}{32}$ at $\tfrac13$, the same on both states of each pair, so its weights are those values in both sectors. $\mu_{R} = \tfrac18(\beta_{4} + \beta_{5}) = \tfrac18(N_{R} - 1) = \tfrac14T_{3R}$ is $0$ on doublets and $\pm\tfrac18$ on the singlets, so by (i) its weights are $\tfrac{1}{16}$ down and $-\tfrac{1}{16}$ up on both sectors. $X_{4} = 8\mu_{R}\mu_{P}$ with $\mu_{P} = -\tfrac{3}{16}(B - L)$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-majorana-moment-map}(i)) is $-\tfrac{3}{8}T_{3R}(B - L)$: zero on doublets, $-\tfrac{3}{16}$ on $e^{c}$, $\tfrac{1}{16}$ on $d^{c}$, $\tfrac{3}{16}$ on $\nu^{c}$ and $-\tfrac{1}{16}$ on $u^{c}$; halving gives the stated weights. $R_{4} = -\tfrac{1}{32}\chi$ takes opposite values on the doublet and the singlet of each pair, and $\mu_{P}$, a multiple of $B - L$, opposite values because every pair is $B - L$ neutral (Proposition \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}(iii)); both give antisymmetric forms only.

(iii) Adding (ii): down $(\tfrac{3}{32} - \tfrac{3}{32}, -\tfrac{1}{32} + \tfrac{1}{32}) = (0, 0)$, up $(\tfrac{3}{16}, -\tfrac{1}{16})$. The up-type form of Proposition \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}(iv) has moduli $1$ on $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $\tfrac13$ on $(Q, u^{c})$; on the sixteen $v_{4}P_{4} = -\tfrac{3}{32}v_{4}(B - L)\chi$ by the same parity identity as for $w_{4}$ ($\chi = -(-1)^{N_{P}}$ on the sixteen), and $X_{4}$ has the same up weights as $P_{4}$, so the up entries of $G_{4}$ are $-\tfrac{3}{16}$ times that form. Through degree four, $TT^{\dagger}$ is $\tfrac{1}{32} + \tfrac12(\mu_{P} + \mu_{R}) + G_{4}$ (loc. cit. (i)); by (ii) the down weights are $\tfrac{1}{32} + \tfrac{1}{32} + 0 = \tfrac{1}{16}$ on both sectors and the up weights $(\tfrac{1}{32} - \tfrac{1}{32} + \tfrac{3}{16}, \tfrac{1}{32} - \tfrac{1}{32} - \tfrac{1}{16})$. Finally $TT^{\dagger}$ is the projector onto the full state (loc. cit. (i), with the Majorana element of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), which is odd, so $TT^{\dagger}\varphi = 0$ for $\varphi$ in the sixteen and the whole square gives no entry.

The check computes all of this on the $32 \times 32$ rational module: the sector weights of $w_{4}g$ and $v_{4}g$ against the $10$ forms for four $T_{3R}$-even and two $T_{3R}$-odd weightings with hand-tabulated values, the parts $P_{4}$, $X_{4}$, $R_{4}$ of the expanded square, $\mu_{R}$, $\mu_{P}$, $G_{4}$, the truncation through degree four, and the whole square.
